The 2009 order records a sightseeing trip for five officials budgeted at about RMB 35,000, or $4,227, in December 2002; shoes worth about $500 for four institute officials in January 2004; and the hiring in May 2004 of a former institute official whose wife was an official there in charge of two projects. Two contracts to put graphics on about 15,400 police cars followed. Avery paid $273,213 in disgorgement, $45,257 in interest and a $200,000 penalty.
inside: A materials maker's gifts and a job offer reached officials of China's police research institute, which helped it win the contracts to mark 15,400 police cars.
cite: SEC administrative order 34-60393, In the Matter of Avery Dennison Corporation, 28 July 2009

n: AGCO paid Iraq's agriculture ministry a 10% kickback on UN contracts
rank: the Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture
d: AGCO, an American farm machinery maker, paid kickbacks to the Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture to win United Nations Oil for Food contracts for its equipment. The US Securities and Exchange Commission said the ministry demanded a kickback of ten percent of contract value in December 2000, that AGCO's business manager for Iraq and his supervisor agreed, and that $5,912,393 was paid as 'after sales service fees' across sixteen contracts between 2000 and 2003, with United Nations contract prices secretly inflated by an artificial ten percent and the money routed through a Jordanian agent into Iraqi-controlled accounts in Jordan. AGCO paid $13,907,393 in disgorgement, $2 million in interest and a $2.4 million penalty, plus a $1.6 million US criminal penalty and a Danish confiscation of over $600,000.
inside: A machinery maker paid the Iraqi agriculture ministry the ten percent it demanded, and the ministry then bought its equipment through the UN programme.
cite: SEC litigation release 21229, 30 September 2009

n: Customer liaisons and BRI Kutalimbaru staff ran Rp6.28bn of fictitious KUR
org_label: Habib Mahendra, Rahmayanti and Rahmad Singarimbun, customer liaisons
rank: Unit head, BRI Kutalimbaru
d: KUR is Indonesia's subsidised credit scheme for small businesses, paid out through state-owned banks. On 24 February 2025 prosecutors at the Medan corruption court indicted seven people over KUR lending at the Kutalimbaru unit of the state-owned bank BRI, outside Medan in North Sumatra: two successive unit heads, Moehammad Juned and Erwin Handoko, a field credit officer, a customer-service clerk, and three outside customer liaisons, Habib Mahendra, Rahmayanti and Rahmad Singarimbun. The indictment says they used customers' identity data to raise loan applications, then kept the passbooks and cards and withdrew the money for themselves, costing the state Rp6.28bn. On 3 July 2025 the court convicted the former customer-service clerk, Joshua Adrian Sitompul, of joint corruption and jailed him for two years.
cite: ANTARA Sumut, 24 February 2025 (indictment, defendants, mechanism, Rp6.28bn); Supreme Court decision directory, PN Medan 18/Pid.Sus-TPK/2025, 3 July 2025 (conviction and two-year sentence)
inside: Outside loan liaisons worked with the state bank's own unit heads and clerks, who kept customers' passbooks and drew subsidised credit in their names for themselves.

n: A borrower and BRI Guntung Payung's officer took Rp2.7bn in Kupedes credit
rank: Field credit officer, BRI Guntung Payung unit
d: Kupedes is the state-owned bank BRI's general village credit line. On 12 December 2023 the corruption court in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, convicted two people over 2019 Kupedes lending at BRI's Guntung Payung unit, part of its Martapura branch: Etna Agustiany, a housewife named as the borrower, and Richard Wylson Takaen, a former field credit officer at the unit. The court put the loss to the state at Rp2.7bn and gave each four years in prison, a Rp200m fine and an order to repay Rp308m. Prosecutors said the lending ran through brokers. Her lawyer, OC Kaligis, disputes that, says signatures were forged and says the loss figure came from the bank's supervisors rather than the state audit board.
cite: ANTARA Kalsel, December 2023 (verdict, both defendants, Rp2.7bn, sentences, Rp308m restitution, defence case)
inside: A borrower and the state bank's own field credit officer were convicted together over village credit, each ordered to repay Rp308m of the money the unit paid out.

n: A businessman paid BRI Sunter's branch head in cash and a car for credit
rank: Branch head, BRI Sunter
d: At the corruption court in central Jakarta, prosecutors have charged Mardin Setiawan, former head of the state-owned bank BRI's Sunter branch in north Jakarta, a relationship manager named Riyandi Setiawan, and a private businessman, Franklin Markus Worotikan, over working-capital credit paid to nine linked companies presented as independent businesses. The indictment says the lending was split into facilities of up to Rp5bn each so that the decision stayed with the branch head and escaped BRI's regional review, and that the bank staff took benefits from Franklin: Rp300m to Rp400m in cash as a disbursement fee of about one per cent, a Toyota Alphard worth some Rp700m, flights and hotels for a family holiday, and about Rp100m for entertainment. The alleged loss is Rp40,387,969,856. The trial was running in December 2025.
cite: Dandapala, 24 December 2025 (indictment, defendants, nine companies, the Rp5bn splitting, the fee, Alphard and other benefits, Rp40.39bn loss)
inside: An outside borrower is alleged to have paid the state bank's branch head a one per cent disbursement fee, a car and holidays, and the branch then lent to his nine companies.

n: A developer's 73 fictitious buyers drew Bank Papua's subsidised mortgages
rank: Officer, Bank Papua Teminabuan branch
d: Bank Papua is the development bank owned by Papua's provincial government. On 26 July 2023 the corruption court at Manokwari convicted Syamsul Arief over subsidised housing loans, made in 2016 and 2017 under the state KPR Sejahtera scheme and its FLPP liquidity facility, at the bank's Teminabuan branch; his Bank Papua staff appointment papers are among the case exhibits. The file records 73 fictitious borrowers and a write-off proposal covering Rp12,915,177,078 of principal and Rp622,872,326 of interest. He was jailed for ten years, fined Rp500m and ordered to repay Rp400m, part of it met from a deposit held in his name. The verdict names a developer, Muh. Ramli of the Nani Bilik Group, and two other men as defendants or suspects in separate cases.
cite: Supreme Court decision directory, PN Manokwari 8/Pid.Sus-TPK/2023, verdict 26 July 2023 (defendant, Bank Papua Teminabuan, 73 fictitious debtors, figures, sentence and Rp400m restitution, separate cases)
inside: A developer's fictitious house buyers took subsidised mortgages from the provincial bank through a member of its own staff, who was ordered to repay Rp400m of the proceeds.

n: LPEI directors took 'zakat' fees from the exporters whose credit they signed
rank: Executive directors, Indonesia Eximbank (LPEI)
d: LPEI, Indonesia's state export financing institution, lends to exporters. On 3 March 2025 the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) named five suspects over credit to PT Petro Energy: two of LPEI's executive directors, Dwi Wahyudi and Arif Setiawan, and three company figures, Jimmy Masrin, Newin Nugroho and Susy Mira Dewi Sugiarta. KPK says payments from borrowers of 2.5 to 5 per cent of the credit, coded as 'uang zakat', went to the directors who signed the approvals. About US$60m, some Rp988bn, was paid to the company in three tranches from 2015 to 2017 against what prosecutors call fake contracts, with warnings from LPEI's own analysts overridden. KPK puts the potential loss across 11 borrowers at Rp11.7tn.
cite: Detik, 3 March 2025 (the 'uang zakat' code, 2.5-5 per cent to the signing directors, suspects, Rp11.7tn potential loss); ANTARA, 3 March 2025 (five suspects and roles, US$60m in three tranches, fake contracts, analysts' warnings)
inside: An exporter's money is said to have reached the state export bank's own executive directors as a fee coded 'zakat', and they signed off the credit its analysts had warned against.

n: A BRI partner and a credit officer lent Rp3.2bn in Brebes residents' names
rank: Credit officer, BRI Paguyangan unit
d: The corruption court at Semarang in Central Java convicted two people over lending at the Paguyangan unit of the state-owned bank BRI, at Bumiayu in Brebes regency. Dini Setyowati, a bank partner from outside its staff, gathered credit applications from residents; Hendri Wibowo, a credit officer at the unit, approved the applications she brought in. The court found that applications for hundreds of residents rested on wrong or fictitious data and put the loss to the state at up to Rp3.2bn for 2019 and 2020. Both were jailed for six years, less than the seven and a half years prosecutors sought, and fined Rp300m. She was ordered to repay Rp3.2bn and he was ordered to repay Rp48m.
cite: VOI, report on the Semarang corruption court verdict (both defendants and roles, BRI Paguyangan unit, up to Rp3.2bn for 2019-2020, six-year sentences, Rp300m fine, Rp3.2bn and Rp48m restitution)
inside: An outside bank partner brought in applications in residents' names and the unit's own credit officer passed them; he was ordered to repay Rp48m of the proceeds.

n: Gold traders got Antam's refinery unit to stamp their scrap gold as Antam's
org_label: Private gold customers of Antam's Logam Mulia unit
rank: UBPP Logam Mulia refining unit, PT Antam
d: PT Antam is Indonesia's state-owned mining company. Seven private customers of its precious metal processing and refining unit, UBPP Logam Mulia, had scrap and washed gold cast into bars and stamped with Antam's LM logo, which carries London Bullion Market Association and national accreditation certification meant to show the metal came from legal sources. Six former Antam officers of the same unit were tried in a separate cluster of the case and given eight years each. On 28 May 2025 the Jakarta corruption court convicted all seven traders, with sentences of six to nine years; Lindawati Effendi got nine years and a restitution order of Rp616.9 billion. Prosecutors put the loss to the state at Rp3.3 trillion.
inside: Private gold dealers reached the state miner's own refinery officers, so Antam's hallmark and its legality certification went onto their scrap metal.
cite: Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdict, reported by iNews, 28 May 2025

n: A broker and Antam's Surabaya outlet staff handed a buyer unpaid-for gold
org_label: Broker Eksi Anggraeni and buyer Budi Said
who: A gold broker and a private buyer
rank: BELM 01 Surabaya retail outlet, PT Antam
d: Antam, Indonesia's state mining company, sells gold bars through its own retail outlets. Eksi Anggraeni, a broker, worked with three staff of the BELM 01 Surabaya outlet, Endang Kumoro, Ahmad Purwanto and Misdianto, to offer gold to the Surabaya businessman Budi Said. Invoices were manipulated so that more gold was handed over than each invoice covered, and reports were falsified to hide a shortfall of 152.80 kg, worth Rp92.2 billion, at the outlet between September and December 2018. On appeal the Surabaya High Court gave Eksi 11 years and the three Antam employees nine years each. Budi Said was convicted separately in Jakarta in December 2024 and sentenced to 15 years for corruption and money laundering.
inside: A gold broker and a buyer reached three staff of the state miner's own Surabaya shop, who released bars the invoices did not cover.
cite: Pengadilan Tinggi Surabaya appeal rulings reported by Infobank News, 10 March 2024; Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdict reported by ANTARA Jawa Timur, 27 December 2024

n: PT Netway Utama got PLN's chief to hand it two IT jobs without a tender
rank: president director, PLN
d: PLN is Indonesia's state electricity company. Eddie Widiono Suwondho, its marketing and distribution director and later president director, ordered the direct appointment without tender of PT Netway Utama for the Roll Out CIS-RISI customer information system at PLN's Jakarta and Tangerang distribution unit, and for a further IT-based CMS project at the East Java unit. A law firm was asked to prepare a study that would justify the direct appointment. The Jakarta corruption court sentenced Eddie to five years in December 2011 over a Rp46 billion loss on the first project, and in October 2013 sentenced Netway's president director Gani Abdul Gani to eight years, citing total state losses of Rp116.159 billion and a personal gain of Rp9.686 billion.
inside: A software contractor reached the state power company through the director who ran its distribution business, and was handed two contracts with no tender at all.
cite: Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdicts reported by Hukumonline, 21 December 2011 and 28 October 2013

n: A coal trader drew state asset firm PPA's money on PLN coal invoices
rank: investment manager, PT Perusahaan Pengelola Aset
d: PT Perusahaan Pengelola Aset is a state-owned asset management company. Police say it approved Rp50 billion of invoice financing for the coal trader PT Bintang Abadi Sampurna against invoices for coal supplied to PT PLN Batubara, the coal arm of the state electricity company, but about Rp67.31 billion was paid out over eight disbursements in 2019 and 2020. Due diligence and risk analysis were not done properly, a recommended direct check with PLN Batubara was skipped, invoices went unverified, collateral rules were ignored, and bank statements were allegedly falsified to make the collateral account look funded. Three suspects were detained, named only by initials: an investment manager at PPA and the trader's director and head of operations. A state audit put the loss at Rp38.8 billion.
inside: A coal trader reached the state asset company through its investment manager, who pushed through payments on invoices nobody checked with the power company.
cite: Kortas Tipikor Polri press conference, 20 July 2026, reported by RCTI+

n: Rice traders and Bulog's Bulukumba branch heads took subsidised rice
org_label: CV UF and two rice traders
rank: Bulukumba branch head, Perum Bulog
d: Perum Bulog is Indonesia's state food agency. Its Bulukumba branch in South Sulawesi distributed rice under SPHP, a scheme meant to steady supply and prices. Between January and September 2023 about 710,467 kg of the 1,344,490 kg distributed across the Bulukumba, Sinjai, Bantaeng and Jeneponto areas, worth Rp11.23 billion in all, was handled outside the rules, with distributor and retailer registration misused, warehouse handovers manipulated and personal bank accounts used. On 14 July 2025 the Makassar corruption court convicted the branch head Ervyna Zulaiha, who got three years, her supply chain assistant manager Rajamiddin, and three outsiders: CV UF's director Iskandar Daeng Tiro, a food procurement partner Sonny Sallatu and a rice businessman Sudirman. The loss was put at Rp2.14 billion.
inside: Three private rice traders reached Bulog's branch through its own head and supply manager, and took subsidised rice meant to hold food prices down.
cite: Pengadilan Tipikor Makassar verdicts reported by Detik Sulsel, 14 July 2025

n: Rail providers paid Indonesia's railway infrastructure director for packages
org_label: PT KA Properti Manajemen and other rail providers
rank: Director of Railway Infrastructure, Directorate General of Railways
d: The Directorate General of Railways (DJKA), part of Indonesia's transport ministry, buys and maintains track work. Its director of railway infrastructure, Harno Trimadi, who was also the budget holder, took money from providers so they would win the 2022 level-crossing repair packages for Java and Sumatra. Yoseph Ibrahim and Parjono, president director and a vice-president of PT KA Properti Manajemen, a subsidiary of the state railway company KAI, paid Rp1.125 billion in cash instalments after the firm won a Rp20.75 billion package; a provider, Dion Sugiarto, paid Rp1.5 billion plus foreign currency. KPK arrested the ministry's contracting official Fadliansyah in a sting in April 2023. In December 2023 the Jakarta corruption court gave Harno five years and Fadliansyah four.
inside: Rail contractors, one of them a state railway subsidiary, put money inside the ministry directorate that awards track work, and the packages went to them.
cite: KPK indictment reported by ANTARA Megapolitan, 3 July 2023; Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdict reported by Investor Trust, 11 December 2023

n: Sugar refiners took import work via Indonesia's trade ministry and PPI
rank: Minister of Trade; business development director, PT PPI
d: Indonesia restricts raw sugar imports, and import for market stabilisation is reserved for state companies. Prosecutors charged nine directors of private sugar refiners, among them Tony Wijaya of PT Angels Products and Wisnu Hendraningrat of PT Andalan Furnindo, with acting jointly with trade minister Thomas Lembong and with Charles Sitorus, business development director of the state trading company PT Perusahaan Perdagangan Indonesia, over 2015 and 2016 imports that let the refiners process and sell the sugar. The indictment, read in Jakarta on 19 June 2025, put the loss at Rp578.1 billion. On 29 October 2025 the court sentenced four of them, including Wisnu and Indra Suryaningrat of PT Medan Sugar Industry, to four years each with restitution.
inside: Private refiners reached the trade ministry and the state trading company through a minister and a director, and took the sugar import work reserved for the state.
cite: Kejaksaan indictment reported by CNN Indonesia, 19 June 2025; Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdicts reported by ANTARA Jawa Timur, 29 October 2025

n: A sugar trader paid Indonesia's DPD speaker for Bulog's sugar allocation
rank: Speaker of the Regional Representative Council (DPD)
d: Perum Bulog, Indonesia's state food agency, allocates imported sugar through regional divisions. CV Semesta Berjaya had asked Bulog's West Sumatra division for 3,000 tonnes and heard nothing, so its owner Xaveriandy Sutanto and his wife Memi paid Irman Gusman, speaker of the Regional Representative Council, the country's upper house, for help, at an agreed Rp300 per kg. Irman asked Bulog's president director Djarot Kusumayakti to route the sugar through West Sumatra and recommended the company; the regional head was directed to allocate it, and 1,000 tonnes was delivered between August and September 2016, some diverted to Medan and Pekanbaru. KPK arrested the three in September 2016. The Supreme Court found he received Rp200 million and in September 2019 cut his sentence to three years.
inside: A sugar trader's money reached the speaker of Indonesia's upper house, who then had the state food agency allocate the import to that trader.
cite: Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta verdict reported by Hukumonline, 20 February 2017; Supreme Court review reported by CNN Indonesia, 27 September 2019

n: Vendors billed Telkom Akses for work never done, via two of its managers
who: Partner contractors of PT Telkom Akses
rank: provisioning and migration manager, PT Telkom Akses Tangerang
d: PT Telkom Akses installs and maintains fibre lines for Telkom, Indonesia's state telecoms company. Ari Bastian, provisioning and migration manager for the Tangerang area, had his site manager Rendra Setyo Argo Kusumo supply fictitious new-connection and migration job data. The fake entries were merged with genuine partner records, checked by staff and turned into purchase orders, which partner contractors then used to claim payment: PT Anartel Cipta Cemerlang, PT Rafi Jaya Brothers, PT Jelma Rangga Gading, PT Partner Properti and PT Mega Creative Promosindo. In November 2020 a bank account was opened in another person's name to take the partners' payments. The corruption court at Serang sentenced both men to seven years, over a loss of Rp7.49 billion.
inside: Contractors to the state telecoms installer were paid for jobs that did not exist, because two of its own managers fed the fake job data into its billing.
cite: Pengadilan Tipikor Serang verdicts reported by Dandapala, 10 April 2025

n: Four firms took money from Telkom's Graha Telkom Sigma on dressed-up deals
org_label: Four private construction and property firms
rank: sales director, PT Graha Telkom Sigma
d: PT Graha Telkom Sigma was a property and construction company in the group of Telkom, Indonesia's state telecoms company. Its sales director Taufik Hidayat, with Judi Achmadi and Bakhtiar Rosyidi of the related company Telkom Sigma Caraka, arranged contracts with firms belonging to four outside businessmen: Agus Herry Purwanto of PT Mulyo Joyo Abadi, Tejo Suryo Laksono of PT Granary Reka Cipta, Rusdji Basalamah of PT Wisata Surya Timur and Syarif Mahdi of PT Prima Karya Sejahtera. The work covered housing, crushed stone for Cengkareng airport, an apartment and hotel fitting-out, with procurement documents dressed up and no board approval. State auditors put the loss above Rp324 billion. The Serang corruption court convicted eight in March 2024; the Supreme Court raised Agus's sentence to ten years in January 2025.
inside: Four outside businessmen reached the state telecoms group's construction arm through its own directors, and its money went out on contracts the board never approved.
cite: Kejaksaan indictment reported by Detik, 25 October 2023; Pengadilan Tipikor Serang verdicts and Supreme Court cassation reported by Dandapala, 16 January 2025; company address from Telkomsigma group records (Bumi Serpong Damai, South Tangerang)

n: Nine firms drew fabricated financing from Telkom's enterprise division
org_label: Nine private companies financed by Telkom
rank: Enterprise Service division, Telkom Indonesia
d: Telkom Indonesia is the state telecoms company. Prosecutors say that between 2016 and 2018 its enterprise service division released money to private companies through procurement steps fabricated to produce the paperwork needed for payment. The indictment, read at the Jakarta corruption court on 24 November 2025, names nine outside company directors as enriched, among them Nurhandayanto of PT Ata Energi with Rp113.19 billion and Rudi Irawan of PT Batavia Primajaya with Rp66.57 billion, alongside two Telkom staff: general manager August Hoth Mercyon Purba and account manager Herman Maulana, who also controlled PT Indi & Kei and is said to have taken Rp44.54 billion. The prosecution puts the loss to state finances at Rp464.93 billion.
inside: Private firms took money out of the state telecoms company through its own enterprise division, on procurement paperwork prosecutors say was fabricated for that purpose.
cite: Kejaksaan Agung indictment at Pengadilan Tipikor Jakarta Pusat reported by ANTARA, 24 November 2025

n: CBI: pipeline sub-contractor paid GAIL's projects director 50 lakh rupees
rank: Executive Director (Projects), GAIL (India) Limited
d: GAIL (India) Limited is the state-owned gas pipeline and processing company. The CBI alleges that Advance Infrastructures Private Limited, a Vadodara firm working as a sub-contractor on two GAIL pipeline projects, paid 50 lakh rupees to K B Singh, GAIL's Executive Director (Projects), and that the cash was recovered from him. Prosecutors say its director Surendra Kumar met Singh at his Noida home on 29 June 2023 to ask that a final bill be expedited, that Singh released the payment on 20 July, ordering bills processed offline against GAIL's own rules, and that couriers delivered the cash in September. Chief General Manager Davinder Singh and a MECON Limited manager were also named. Five men were arrested; the case is under investigation.
inside: A sub-contractor's cash allegedly reached the director running GAIL's pipeline projects, who then pushed its bills through outside the state company's own invoice system.
cite: Press Trust of India via Outlook Business, 6 September 2023

n: NTPC safety manager jailed for taking 3 lakh rupees over Covid supply funds
org_label: a supplier of Covid-19 protective equipment
rank: Manager (Safety), NTPC Barkagaon project
d: NTPC Limited is India's largest state-owned electricity generator. Sagar Singh Meena, Manager (Safety) at its Barkagaon project in Hazaribagh district, Jharkhand, demanded 7 lakh rupees from a complainant in connection with the release of funds for Covid-19 materials such as masks, sanitisers and protective kits, and agreed during negotiation to take 3 lakh rupees by cheque. The CBI laid a trap, caught him, and filed its chargesheet on 29 November 2020. After thirteen witnesses and seventeen documents, the Special Judge for CBI cases in Ranchi sentenced him to three years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 1 lakh rupees.
inside: A supplier's money reached the safety manager who controlled the release of NTPC's payments, and a court found the state generator's officer had sold that decision.
cite: Sambad English, report of CBI court judgment, Ranchi

n: Food Corporation quality manager jailed over bribe to clear a rice bill
org_label: a Primary Agricultural Credit Society supplying rice
rank: Manager (Quality Control), Food Corporation of India, Buxar
d: The Food Corporation of India is the state body that buys, stores and moves the country's grain. Liyaqat Ali, its Manager (Quality Control) at Buxar in Bihar, demanded 7,200 rupees to process and release a payment of 4.49 lakh rupees owed to a group of rice suppliers. The man asked for it was the president of a Primary Agricultural Credit Society, a village-level farmers' lending and marketing body, who complained instead. The CBI laid a trap on 13 May 2010 and caught him taking the money. On 8 July 2025 the special CBI court in Patna gave him eighteen months' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 25,000 rupees.
inside: A farmers' society's money reached the Food Corporation officer who certified and cleared its rice bill, and the court convicted him of selling that clearance.
cite: Lokmat Times, report of CBI court sentence, 8 July 2025

n: CBI: drilling supplier paid Oil India deputy general manager 7 lakh rupees

Prosecutors say the firm's managing director Kunal Gupta arranged delivery, and that Chakravorty spent part of the money on gold coins in Noida. Both men were arrested and produced before a CBI court in Ghaziabad.
inside: A drilling equipment supplier's cash allegedly reached the Oil India manager deciding its contract, so a state producer's award was being bought from inside.
cite: The Tribune (India), 6 May 2025

Ashish Kansal, chief executive and director-promoter of SMPP Limited, and Kumar's brother B Harshavardhan were also arrested on 13 October. Searches in Pune recovered about 1.73 crore rupees in cash and about 50 lakh more in Mysuru, Bengaluru and Delhi, some 2.23 crore in all. The investigation continues.
inside: Private ammunition contractors allegedly paid a director inside India's state munitions company for official favours, putting the buyer's decisions in their suppliers' hands.

n: CBI: Bank of Baroda officers in Sultanpur took 35,000 to release an overdraft

The agency registered the case on 13 July 2026, laid a trap the next day and says the credit officer accepted 35,000 rupees, acting at the branch manager's direction. Both were arrested and produced before a court in Lucknow.
inside: A borrower's cash allegedly reached the two bank officers who controlled his credit line, so a state bank's lending decision was settled by payment rather than assessment.

n: CBI: Bank of Baroda manager in Bulandshahr took 1 lakh for an 80 lakh loan

The complainant's wife had applied for the loan at that branch. The bribe was reportedly paid by a signed blank cheque, which the manager is alleged to have encashed. The report does not name the officer. The case was at the stage of arrest and investigation when it was reported the following day.
inside: An applicant's payment allegedly reached the manager who decided her loan, so the state bank's credit went to whoever paid the officer holding the file.
cite: Free Press Journal, 12 December 2024

n: Bank of Baroda manager jailed five years over a held-back scheme loan
org_label: a borrower under the Kamdhenu dairy loan scheme
rank: branch manager, Bank of Baroda, Baskhari branch, Ambedkar Nagar

A borrower had 20.25 lakh rupees sanctioned under the Kamdhenu scheme, which lends for dairy units, but part of the money was held back. Mishra demanded 30,000 rupees to release it and settled for 25,000, taken as a signed blank cheque. The CBI registered the case on 7 March 2017, caught him accepting the cheque in a trap and filed its chargesheet that month. The special CBI court in Lucknow sentenced him on 12 November 2025 to five years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 50,000 rupees.
inside: A dairy borrower's money reached the branch manager holding his loan, and a court found the state bank's officer had sold the release of public scheme credit.
cite: Lokmat Times, report of CBI court sentence, 13 November 2025

org_label: a farmer seeking a Kisan Credit Card loan instalment

d: Baroda UP Gramin Bank was a state-sponsored regional rural bank, one of the publicly owned banks that lend to farmers. Rakesh Chandra Thakur, then branch manager of its Hariharpur branch in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh, demanded 6,000 rupees from a borrower to release the first instalment of a Kisan Credit Card loan of 4.25 lakh rupees. The CBI registered the case on 12 March 2018, laid a trap and caught him taking the money, and filed its chargesheet on 10 May 2018. Charges were framed in December 2020. On 25 August 2026 the special anti-corruption CBI court in Lucknow gave him five years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 25,000 rupees.
inside: A farmer's payment reached the manager controlling his credit instalment, and the court found the public bank's officer had sold access to subsidised farm lending.

The CBI registered the case on 11 August 2016, caught both men in a trap and charged them on 30 September 2016. Charges were framed in March 2019. inside: A farmer's money reached a public bank's assistant manager through a middleman, and the court found that credit meant for farming was being sold at the counter.
cite: Studycafe, report of Lucknow CBI court judgments, 25 August 2026

inside: A solar firm's payments allegedly reached the manager holding its customers' loan files, so disbursement at a state bank branch turned on a per-file fee.

n: CBI: three Indian Bank staff in Eluru took 25,000 to protect a credit limit

According to the complaint, officials told him an auditor had flagged technical problems and warned that his limit would be cut to 20 lakh rupees or the account classified as non-performing; chief manager Banavatu Nagu then asked for 50,000 rupees and settled on 30,000. n: CBI: coal lifters paid Central Coalfields staff at a Hazaribagh colliery
rank: manager and two clerks, Central Coalfields Limited, Giddi-A Colliery, Hazaribagh
d: Central Coalfields Limited is a Coal India subsidiary that mines in Jharkhand. inside: Coal buyers' payments allegedly reached the colliery staff who weighed and cleared their loads, so the state miner's own checks let them take more coal than allowed.

n: CBI: SBI manager in Karimganj gave Xpress Credit loans for bribes
rank: branch manager, State Bank of India, Ramakrishnanagar branch, Karimganj
d: The State Bank of India is the country's largest state-owned bank. Two private individuals are also accused. Searches in Gaya, Hailakandi and Silchar recovered 481 grams of gold, 11.11 grams of diamond and about 1,092 grams of silver from his home in Silchar, along with loan papers and transaction records.
inside: Borrowers' payments, gathered by middlemen, allegedly reached the branch manager who signed their loans, so a state bank lent to people its own rules excluded.

n: Air India doctor jailed for a bribe over a security recruit's medical report
org_label: a candidate for an Air India security agent post

After 27 witnesses and 49 exhibits, a special CBI court in Ahmedabad convicted him on 13 February 2025 and gave him three years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of 1 lakh rupees.
inside: A job applicant's money reached the airline's own doctor, so the medical check that decided who could be hired into a state carrier was sold to the applicant.

Searches at homes and offices in Sitamarhi recovered documents, and both men were to be produced before the special CBI judge in Patna. Neither is named in the report.

inside: A customer's payment allegedly reached the branch manager who decided his credit limit, so a state bank's lending turned on a fee rather than the account.

The case was registered on 5 December 2025 and both men were caught in a trap and arrested the next day. org_label: the proprietor of an HPCL retail outlet and her husband

n: CBI: college staff and a UCO Bank manager opened 118 accounts in Bhopal
rank: senior manager, UCO Bank, Habibganj branch, Bhopal

The CBI alleges that officials of the Academy of Management College, a private business school in Bhopal, and Prema Verma, then senior manager of the bank's Habibganj branch, had 118 accounts opened there in MBA students' names between January 2020 and October 2021 without the students' knowledge, and used them to take about 99.48 lakh rupees of government scholarship money before the students could reach it. n: PNB deputy manager accused of opening a mule account for cyber fraudsters

d: Punjab National Bank is a large state-owned Indian bank. Gurugram police say Vishwas Kumar, a deputy manager at its Kayamganj branch in Uttar Pradesh, acted in connivance with Rohit Sharma to open an account in the name of a firm at a false address, and that Sharma then made it available to cyber fraudsters for 1 lakh rupees. The account was used in a scheme that cost one complainant more than 1.20 crore rupees, which he reported to the Manesar cyber police station on 19 June 2024. Both men were arrested in Gurugram and announced on 20 October 2024; police said eight people had been arrested in the case.
inside: Fraudsters' money allegedly reached a state bank's deputy manager, who opened the account in a firm's name that let them collect what they took from investors.

n: Ajmer: City Union Bank assistant manager held over a forged-ID mule account
rank: assistant manager, City Union Bank branch, Ajmer
d: Police in Rajasthan arrested Shubham Farkya, an assistant manager at a City Union Bank branch in Ajmer, and a second accused, Subhanshu Thakaria, over a savings account opened with a scanned and digitally altered voter identity card in the name of a Tilonia resident who had nothing to do with it. The account-opening form carried forged signatures and another person's photograph, and a mobile number belonging to Thakaria was linked for net banking. The account was sold for 12,000 rupees to a buyer in Ajmer. It received 1.65 lakh rupees on 14 June from a stock trader defrauded of 17,71,480 rupees through a cryptocurrency site; 1 lakh was withdrawn at an ATM in Kishangarh.

n: CBI: ten firms moved 43 lakh rupees to a Bank of India chief manager
org_label: ten firms holding cash credit and overdraft accounts

d: Bank of India is a state-owned bank. The CBI has registered a case alleging that A. Kumar, then chief manager and sanctioning authority at its Itwari branch in Nagpur, obtained 43.42 lakh rupees of undue advantage between February 2024 and March 2025 from ten firms holding cash credit or overdraft accounts there, with the money moved into his savings and personal accounts and said to have been invested in the share market. inside: A small borrower's payments reached the branch manager controlling his credit, and the court found the state bank's officer had charged him for his own loan.
cite: Studycafe, report of CBI court conviction, 4 November 2026

n: CBI: UP Gramin Bank staff in Bijnor took 45,000 over a youth scheme loan

The CBI alleges that one of its relationship managers for medium enterprises in Mumbai, later chief manager, obtained 5 lakh rupees in illegal gratification for facilitating a loan of 17.91 crore rupees sanctioned and paid out to a private company in 2014 on inflated valuations of property. n: Supplier paid a department head at Ukraine's Krasyliv aggregate plant
org_label: Workpiece supplier to the Krasyliv Aggregate Plant
rank: department head, Krasyliv Aggregate Plant
d: The High Anti-Corruption Court convicted a department head of the Krasyliv Aggregate Plant (Krasylivskyi ahrehatnyi zavod), a state-owned defence manufacturer, of taking 1,990,840 hryvnia from a private entrepreneur who supplied the plant with sets of metal workpieces. rank: Berdyansk branch, Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority
d: The Berdyansk branch of the state enterprise Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority (Administratsiya morskykh portiv Ukrainy) paid a commercial company for equipment that was never delivered, costing it about 2.49 million hryvnia on an expert assessment. Prosecutors named Natalia Panchenko, a former director of a private company, and Oleksandr Barchan, head of the branch, as organisers. An engineer at the branch, Oleksandr Dzhembri, pleaded guilty; the High Anti-Corruption Court approved his agreement with the anti-corruption prosecutor in March 2021 and gave him three years in prison, suspended with two years' probation, an 8,500 hryvnia fine and an eighteen-month ban on holding office. Proceedings against the deputy branch head lapsed on time limits.
inside: A private supplier worked with the branch's own managers so the state ports authority paid it for equipment it never delivered.
cite: Slovo i Dilo, 9 March 2021, on the High Anti-Corruption Court ruling

n: Supplier's 2.44m hryvnia kickback to a Ukroboronprom plant director
rank: director of a state instrument-making plant in the Ukroboronprom concern
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau and the anti-corruption prosecutor's office said on 25 October 2022 that people linked to the company Optimumspetsdetal had paid more than 2.44 million hryvnia to the director of a state instrument-making plant belonging to Ukroboronprom, the state defence-industry concern, between September 2016 and January 2017. Investigators say the payment was to cover up unjustified payments the plant made for military goods the company supplied. The report does not name the plant or the director. Nine participants were identified; Ukroboronprom took in goods worth about 165 million hryvnia through the scheme, and over 46 million hryvnia went unpaid in tax. Only the suspicion stage was reported.
inside: Prosecutors allege a defence supplier paid the director of the state plant that bought from it, so unjustified payments for its goods were waved through.
cite: Dengi.ua, 25 October 2022, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Entrepreneur's firms won Ukrzaliznytsia cable tenders through an insider back office
org_label: Cable supplier network around a sitting MP
rank: procurement of JSC Ukrzaliznytsia
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau said on 17 January 2025 that a sitting member of Ukraine's parliament had organised a scheme in which a private entrepreneur's companies won cable tenders at the state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia in 2021 and 2022, mostly at inflated prices. Investigators say a separate organised group that included a Ukrzaliznytsia official worked as an informal back office and, for a percentage of each procurement, made sure those companies won. Losses exceeded 140 million hryvnia and the proceeds were divided among the participants. The bureau did not name the MP; the outlet UNN, citing its own sources and not confirmed by the bureau, identified him as Viktor Bondar. Seven participants had been exposed earlier.
inside: Prosecutors allege a supplier's companies, working with a railway official and an MP, were steered the state railway's cable tenders for a cut of each purchase.
cite: Zaxid.net, 17 January 2025, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Gas traders and Ukrzaliznytsia supply managers split a 206m hryvnia markup
org_label: Gas supplier companies selling to Ukrzaliznytsia
rank: Centre for Production Support, JSC Ukrzaliznytsia
d: On 13 June 2023 the National Anti-Corruption Bureau and the anti-corruption prosecutor's office served four people with suspicion over gas buying at the Centre for Production Support, a branch of the state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia. Investigators say officials bought gas outside tender procedures, favoured two pre-chosen companies, hid better offers from other suppliers, and agreed an extra markup of 200 to 1,000 hryvnia per thousand cubic metres. Losses exceeded 206 million hryvnia, divided among the participants. Two branch heads and the real owner of one supplier company are among the suspects; of those detained the article names Oleksiy Onysymiuk, the branch's deputy director. The scheme is dated December 2016 to January 2020.
inside: Prosecutors allege gas sellers arranged with the railway branch's managers to be chosen without tender and at a markup they shared.
cite: Forbes Ukraine, 13 June 2023, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Equipment suppliers won Kharkivoblenergo tenders 132.5m hryvnia above value
rank: acting chairman of the board, JSC Kharkivoblenergo
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau and the anti-corruption prosecutor's office said in August 2024 that the acting chairman of the board of Kharkivoblenergo, the regional electricity distributor, had made sure two chosen companies won tenders for 11,904 transformers and 79,425 electricity meters at prices about 132.5 million hryvnia above their worth, with some components marked up fivefold. Investigators say the group was organised with a man controlling several commercial companies that supplied energy equipment, and that a Kharkiv Chamber of Commerce department head and a private appraiser inflated the expected contract value. Five people were served suspicion and two detained on 14 August 2024. Losses from the part carried out were about 12.5 million hryvnia.
inside: Prosecutors allege equipment suppliers organised the scheme with the distributor's acting board chairman so its tenders went to them far above value.
cite: Forbes Ukraine, 15 August 2024, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Ukrenergo bought body armour at double price from a chosen supplier
rank: head of the security department, NPC Ukrenergo
d: Ukrenergo, the state electricity transmission company, bought body armour in March and April 2022 at roughly twice the market price from a supplier chosen in advance which, investigators say, lacked the required permits and had never made such goods. Damage is put at over 10.3 million hryvnia. Suspicion was reported on 26 June 2024 against Serhiy Totskyi, former head of Ukrenergo's security department, and the High Anti-Corruption Court later imposed a preventive measure on him. On 21 August 2024 the National Anti-Corruption Bureau served suspicion in absentia on an unnamed accomplice said to have handled dealings with the company and the sale of the armour; he is in hiding. Slovo i Dilo names the supplier as TOP Treiding Lain.
inside: Prosecutors allege an outside supplier and its go-between worked with Ukrenergo's security chief so the state grid company bought its armour at double price.
cite: Slovo i Dilo, 21 August 2024, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Group including a German participant took almost 100m hryvnia from Energoatom
rank: staff of Energoatom
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau's report for 2025 describes an organised group, one of whose participants was in Germany, that colluded with staff of Energoatom, Ukraine's state nuclear generating company, and took almost 100 million hryvnia of money meant for a nuclear fuel storage facility in the Chornobyl exclusion zone. The German participant was extradited to Ukraine, one of two extraditions the bureau records for the period, and the verdict against him has entered into force; it is among the fifty verdicts that became final. The report does not name him and does not say whether he was a supplier or a contractor.
inside: An outside group reached Energoatom through its own staff and took the money set aside for a nuclear fuel store in the Chornobyl zone.
cite: NABU report for 2025 (second half), nabu.gov.ua

n: State dredging firm's Chornomorsk base sold to accomplices at a ninth of value
who: Private buyers and a front company
rank: officials of the state enterprise Chornomorshliakh
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau's 2025 report describes officials of the state enterprise Chornomorshliakh selling its main maintenance base at Chornomorsk to accomplices. The base was valued for the sale at 6.5 million hryvnia, about a ninth of what the bureau puts as its real worth, and was bought for 13.5 million hryvnia, then contributed to a private firm's charter capital. Losses from the sale are put at about 59 million hryvnia. In a second episode 11.5 million hryvnia was paid to a front company for servicing two ships which, the report says, were in India and were not serviced. Together the two episodes come to over 70 million hryvnia. No names or court outcome are given.
inside: Outside buyers took a state marine enterprise's main base through its own officials, at a price the bureau puts at a ninth of its worth.
cite: NABU report for 2025 (second half), nabu.gov.ua

n: Tender terms rewritten at Ukrgasvydobuvannya for the foreign firm that won
org_label: Foreign gas services company that won the tender
rank: officials of JSC Ukrgasvydobuvannya
d: The National Anti-Corruption Bureau said in March 2024 that officials of Ukrgasvydobuvannya, the gas production company of the state Naftogaz group, altered the documents of a fifteen-year tender in 2019 and 2020 in favour of the private foreign company that won it. The changes cut the base production norm by 750 million cubic metres over the contract and tied monthly base figures to 2020 volumes staff had been barred from exceeding, which shifted gas into a higher 'enhanced' rate three to four times the base rate. Damage is put at 211 million hryvnia between October 2020 and November 2023. Two people were served suspicion, one of them a former company official who later became business development head at the winning firm.
inside: Prosecutors allege the winning contractor had the state gas producer's own tender terms rewritten in its favour, and later hired the official involved.
cite: Glavcom, 11 March 2024, reporting NABU and SAPO

n: Drilling Advisor's director charged over Ukrgasvydobuvannya reagent buying
rank: procurement of JSC Ukrgasvydobuvannya
d: Timur Turgunov, director of the company Drilling Advisor (Drilinh Edvaizer), is the central suspect in a case over the buying of drilling reagents and materials by Ukrgasvydobuvannya, the gas producer of the state Naftogaz group and Ukraine's largest. Prosecutors allege intermediary companies inflated the prices of reagents and materials and the state company overpaid through its tenders, with damage of over 295 million hryvnia confirmed by a forensic economic examination. On 29 May 2026 the High Anti-Corruption Court moved the proceedings from the Bureau of Economic Security to the National Anti-Corruption Bureau and the anti-corruption prosecutor's office. Turgunov is on bail of 998,400 hryvnia, barred from leaving the Kyiv region without permission and from contacting witnesses.
inside: Prosecutors allege a drilling supplier and intermediary firms reached the state gas producer's purchasing so it overpaid for reagents by 295 million hryvnia.
cite: Mind.ua, 11 June 2026, on the High Anti-Corruption Court ruling of 29 May 2026

n: Viet A's gifts reached Ca Mau's health department and disease centre
rank: provincial health department director and disease control centre director
d: Viet A Technology, the private Vietnamese firm that supplied much of the country's Covid-19 testing, had Ca Mau province's kit purchases written around its own goods and paid three of the officials who signed. The provincial people's court found they borrowed kits and chemicals from the company first and put the bidding file together afterwards, taking reference prices only from Viet A staff, so the company always had the price advantage. The health department director signed three contracts worth over 37.3 billion dong and the disease control centre director five worth over 6 billion. On 18 June 2024 the court convicted all four of breaking bidding rules, then exempted them from punishment and confiscated gifts of 1.55 billion, 1.155 billion and 120 million dong.
inside: A test kit maker had a province's purchase prices and bid file built around its own product and paid the health officials who signed, so public money bought its kits.
cite: VietnamPlus (Vietnam News Agency), 18 June 2024, report of the Ca Mau Provincial People's Court verdict

n: Viet A's 15% kickback reached Ba Vi district hospital's buyer
rank: deputy head of supplies, Ba Vi District General Hospital
d: Ba Vi District General Hospital, a public hospital on Hanoi's western edge, was told by the city health department in early 2020 to test community samples for Covid-19. Its deputy head of supplies, Chu Vu Nam, copied the technical specifications of Viet A Technology's test kit into the tender documents and drafted the approval submission so the company would qualify and win. Viet A took packages worth over 5.6 billion dong, of which the hospital paid over 4.3 billion. Its deputy general director, Vu Dinh Hiep, said the firm would pay support equal to 15 per cent of what was paid, and handed Nam 400 million dong in early December 2021. Hanoi's people's court jailed Nam for five years on 8 May 2024.
inside: The supplier's own kit specifications went into the hospital's tender, and its deputy director paid the officer who put them there a share of what the hospital paid.
cite: Bao Dau Tu, 8 May 2024; VietnamNet, 8 May 2024 (Hanoi People's Court verdict)

n: Viet A paid Phu Tho hospital's testing chief to steer eight contracts
rank: deputy director of the testing centre, Phu Tho provincial general hospital
d: Tran Gia Phu headed the microbiology unit and was deputy director of the testing centre at Phu Tho provincial general hospital. In 2020 and 2021 the provincial health department told him to set out what Covid-19 test kits were needed and to find suppliers. He already knew staff at Viet A Technology, the private firm that made the kits, and agreed with them on a percentage outside the contract if it was chosen. He gave the department Viet A's details, and it signed eight contracts with the firm by shortened direct appointment, justified by the emergency. Phu Tho's provincial people's court found he had gained more than 2.1 billion dong and jailed him for eight years for taking bribes, reported in November 2023.
inside: The kit maker agreed a percentage with the hospital officer asked to say what the province needed, and the province then signed eight contracts with it.
cite: Bao Phap Luat Viet Nam, 6 November 2023, report of the Phu Tho Provincial People's Court verdict

n: Viet A's eight Tra Vinh kit contracts went through faked bidding files
rank: deputy director of the provincial health department; former disease centre director
d: Tra Vinh provincial police charged four health officials on 25 May 2022 with breaking bidding rules over purchases from Viet A Technology, the private firm that supplied much of Vietnam's Covid-19 testing. Investigators say that from 2021 to 2022 the four worked with the company on eight bid packages worth more than 36 billion dong for equipment, test kits and reagents, five signed by the provincial health department and three by the provincial disease control centre, and gave the bidding process a false appearance of legitimacy. The estimated loss to the state is about 7.6 billion dong, roughly 6.9 billion at the department and 700 million at the centre. Those charged are deputy health director Tran Dac Thanh, former centre director Nguyen Van Lo and two staff, all detained.
inside: Prosecutors say provincial health officials worked with the test kit firm to dress up bidding for eight contracts it was to win, so the province bought from it.
cite: Bao Chinh Phu (Vietnam Government Portal), 25 May 2022, Tra Vinh provincial police charges

n: Viet A's commission reached Ha Dong hospital's testing and pharmacy heads
rank: head of microbiology and deputy head of pharmacy, Ha Dong General Hospital
d: Ha Dong General Hospital is a public hospital in south-west Hanoi. On 4 June 2022 Hanoi police charged two of its officers over test reagents bought from Viet A Technology, the private firm behind Vietnam's Covid-19 kits: the head of the microbiology department, Tran Le Tien, and the deputy head of the pharmacy department, Quach Thi Thu Ha, both accused of breaking bidding rules. Investigators put the loss to the state on their two contracts at more than 3.3 billion dong. Police say that once the hospitals had paid, Viet A transferred about 200 million dong to each as a percentage of the contract value. The same charges were brought the same day against four officers of Ba Vi District General Hospital, and the investigation was continuing.
inside: Prosecutors say the kit supplier paid the hospital a share of its own contract value after two deals its testing and pharmacy heads are accused of rigging.
cite: Thanh Tra (Vietnam Government Inspectorate newspaper), 10 June 2022, Hanoi police charges; Bao Phap Luat Viet Nam, 3 October 2023, for the two officers' names and posts

n: Viet A paid Son La hospital's pharmacy head 150m dong over kit orders
rank: head of the pharmacy department, Son La provincial general hospital
d: Lo Van Chien was head of the pharmacy department at Son La provincial general hospital, in Vietnam's north-west. A round-up of the health officials prosecuted over Viet A Technology's Covid-19 test kits, published on 3 October 2023, reports that he took a bribe of 150 million dong from the company's owner and its staff, with more than 260 million dong further promised, over the hospital's kit purchases. His is one of the local strands tried away from the single consolidated case in Hanoi: he is not among the 38 defendants that city's people's court sentenced on 12 January 2024. The outcome of his own case is not given in the sources read here.
inside: The test kit firm's owner and staff are reported to have paid the hospital pharmacy head who handled its kit orders 150 million dong, with more promised.
cite: Bao Phap Luat Viet Nam, 3 October 2023; Bao Lao Cai, 12 January 2024, for the list of the 38 defendants sentenced in Hanoi

n: Viet A was written into the Military Medical Academy's own kit project
rank: Military Medical Academy research institute; a science ministry department head
d: Viet A Technology, a Vietnamese test-kit maker, was written into a state Covid research project and sold its kits to the body running it. Trinh Thanh Hung, a deputy department head at Vietnam's science ministry, agreed with Viet A's general director Phan Quoc Viet to add the company to a project funded at 18.98 billion dong, and had Ho Anh Son, a senior colonel and deputy director of the Military Medical Academy's research institute, amend the proposal. The academy told the defence ministry it needed 24.6 billion dong but paid Viet A 41.7 billion. Viet paid Hung US$350,000 and Son over 2.5 billion dong, and directed a 20 per cent commission there. On 29 December 2023 the Capital Military Court jailed Viet 25 years, Hung 15 and Son 12.
inside: A test-kit maker was written into a state military research project by the ministry official and the colonel it paid, and the academy then bought its kits for more than the budget it had declared.
cite: Tap chi Toa an nhan dan, 27 December 2023 (the Capital Military Court trial, the defendants' posts, the 18.98bn dong funding and the 24.6bn against 41.7bn figures); Tap chi Toa an nhan dan, 29 December 2023 (the verdict and sentences); Luat su Viet Nam, 29 December 2023 (the US$350,000 and 2.5bn dong payments); Sai Gon Giai Phong, 27 December 2023 (the 20 per cent commission)

n: OceanBank's borrowers paid fees that funded its chief executive's cut
rank: general director, Ocean Commercial Bank (OceanBank)
d: Ocean Commercial Bank (OceanBank) was a Vietnamese commercial bank in which the state oil group PetroVietnam held a fifth of the capital. On 29 September 2017 the Hanoi People's Court found that its chairman Ha Van Tham had used a subsidiary, BSC, to collect service fees from customers who had to sign those contracts in order to obtain loans or foreign currency, and that this money funded payments to the bank's general director Nguyen Xuan Son. About 69 billion dong reached Son that way, and a further 49 billion was treated as embezzlement. Son was sentenced to death and Tham to life. The State Bank had bought OceanBank for zero dong in 2015.
inside: Borrowers had to sign fee contracts with a bank subsidiary to get credit, and about 69 billion dong of those fees went to the bank's own chief executive.
cite: Bao Phap Luat, 29 September 2017

n: OceanBank's off-contract interest bought Vietsovpetro's two top officers
rank: general director and chief accountant, Vietsovpetro
d: Vietsovpetro is the Vietnam-Russia joint venture that pumps much of Vietnam's crude oil. On 22 March 2019 the Hanoi People's Court convicted its former general director Tu Thanh Nghia and its former chief accountant Vo Quang Huy of abusing their positions to appropriate property. The court found that while the two ran the venture they signed ten fixed-term deposit contracts with Ocean Commercial Bank totalling 1,900 billion dong, and that to keep the deposits coming OceanBank's general director Nguyen Thi Minh Thu gave each of them gifts worth billions of dong, which both then used for themselves. Nghia was given three years and six months, and Huy, who received more, seven years. The money was confiscated.
inside: A bank that wanted the state oil venture's deposits paid its general director and its chief accountant personally, and the deposits kept coming.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 22 March 2019

n: A dock supplier's kickback reached Vinalines' chairman and its directors
rank: chairman and general director, Vinalines
d: Vinalines is Vietnam's state shipping corporation. In December 2013 the Hanoi People's Court heard that it had bought the floating dock 83M at many times its real value, losing the state more than 366 billion dong. The court found that general director Mai Van Phuc, deputy general director Tran Huu Chieu and Tran Hai Son, who ran the group's ship repair company, shared a kickback of about 1.666 million US dollars paid by the Singapore company AP, and that chairman Duong Chi Dung took 10 billion dong of it. On 7 May 2014 the appeal panel rejected the appeals of Dung and Phuc, leaving their death sentences for embezzlement and 18-year terms in place; three former customs officers had part of their terms reduced.
inside: The dock supplier's kickback of 1.666 million dollars went to the state shipping corporation's own chairman and directors, who had it buy a dock at many times its value.
cite: VnExpress, 28 December 2013; Bao Dau Tu, 7 May 2014

n: Vu 'nhom' bought into DongA Bank with the bank's own 200 billion dong
rank: shareholding in Dong A Commercial Bank (DongA Bank)
d: Dong A Commercial Bank (DongA Bank) was one of Vietnam's larger private banks. The Da Nang businessman Phan Van Anh Vu, known as Vu 'nhom', obtained shares in it without putting in any money of his own. In an appeal that ended on 7 June 2019 the High People's Court in Ho Chi Minh City upheld the finding that he had signed fabricated vouchers showing 200 billion dong deposited at the bank, which gave him the funds to buy DongA shares, and that the bank then paid him 203 billion dong, the principal plus nearly 3.2 billion in interest. Tran Phuong Binh, its general director and credit council chairman, whose conduct cost the bank more than 3,600 billion dong, was given life; Vu got 17 years.
inside: An outside businessman took a shareholding in a bank by signing fake deposit slips that its chief honoured, and the bank paid him 203 billion dong.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 8 June 2019

n: Enzo Viet's $500,000 bought Agribank's branch and head-office chiefs
org_label: Enzo Viet and the Lifepro Viet Nam joint venture
rank: director, Agribank Nam Ha Noi branch; general director, Agribank
d: Agribank is Vietnam's state-owned agricultural bank. Its Nam Ha Noi branch lent far beyond its limit to Enzo Viet and the Lifepro Viet Nam joint venture for a textile project, partly against six trademarks that were not real or not owned by the seller, and the bank lost nearly 2,500 billion dong. At the trial in December 2015 the court heard that Enzo Viet provided 500,000 US dollars, of which deputy branch director Chu Thi Kim Hien kept 50,000 and branch director Pham Thi Bich Luong passed 310,000 to Agribank's general director Pham Thanh Tan. On 7 January 2016 the panel asked prosecutors to investigate Tan and Luong for bribery. On appeal, on 27 December 2016, Luong's 30 years and Tan's 22 years were upheld.
inside: The borrower's 500,000 dollars reached the branch's director, her deputy and Agribank's own general director, and the lending went on outside the plan.
cite: Bao Thanh Tra, 23 December 2015; Bao Dau Thau, 22 December 2015 and 8 January 2016; An Ninh Thu Do, 27 December 2016

n: A PVC contractor's advance bought Trinh Xuan Thanh's Tam Dao villa land
rank: chairman, PetroVietnam Construction (PVC)
d: PetroVietnam Construction (PVC) is the building arm of Vietnam's state oil group. Its chairman Trinh Xuan Thanh and Do Van Hong, who chaired PVC's part-owned contractor PVC Kinh Bac, discussed buying land for a resort, and Thanh used his position to have PVC advance Hong's company 25 billion dong under an existing contract worth over 131 billion. Hong bought a 3,400 square metre plot in Tam Dao advertised at 23.8 billion dong, and Thanh had a company he set up, registered in his father's name, hold it; the advance was later converted into a capital contribution, leaving PVC more than 13.2 billion dong out of pocket. On 29 September 2021 the appeal court in Hanoi rejected the appeals and gave the plot's use rights to PVC.
inside: A contractor took an improper 25 billion dong advance from the state oil builder and spent it on resort land that ended up with the builder's own chairman.
cite: Tien Phong, 2021; Luat su Viet Nam, 29 September 2021

n: Tan Viet handed back half a dredging contract to Vinawaco's own chiefs
rank: heads of Vinawaco's planning and project management departments
d: Vinawaco, Vietnam's state waterway construction corporation, won the contract in August 2013 to dredge the Hon Gai-Cai Lan shipping channel and gave the work to Tan Viet company. On 21 December 2016 the Hanoi People's Court found that Tan Viet's director Trinh Van Thang and its board chair Vu Thanh Huyen had agreed with Ho Thanh Nghia, who ran Vinawaco's project management department, and Pham Dinh Hoa, head of its planning department, that Tan Viet would do the work for half the contract price and return the other half to the two men. Hoa was given 13 years and Nghia eight years and six months for taking bribes; Thang got 24 years and Huyen 22, partly for billing Vinawaco for dumping sites that were never used.
inside: The subcontractor agreed to hand half the dredging contract's value back to the state corporation's own department heads, who were convicted of taking bribes.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 21 December 2016

n: OceanBank's cash bought PVOil's general director and chief accountant
rank: general director and chief accountant, PVOil
d: PVOil is the oil trading arm that the state group PetroVietnam set up in 2008. From 2009 to 2014 PetroVietnam required its member units to bank with Ocean Commercial Bank, in which it held 20 per cent of the capital, and PVOil placed seven term deposits with a principal of 2,650 billion dong. On 9 October 2020 the Hanoi People's Court found that OceanBank's general director Nguyen Thi Minh Thu and her staff had paid interest outside the contracts to PVOil's own leaders, split between each period's general director and chief accountant: 1.9 billion dong in three payments to general director Nguyen Xuan Son and 2.1 billion in four payments to chief accountant Vu Trong Hai. Both were given three years.
inside: The bank holding the state oil trader's deposits paid its general director 1.9 billion dong and its chief accountant 2.1 billion outside the deposit contracts.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 9 October 2020

n: Contractors' bribes alleged to reach Vietnam's airports corporation board
org_label: contractors bidding to the Airports Corporation of Vietnam
rank: chairman of the board, Airports Corporation of Vietnam (ACV)
d: The Airports Corporation of Vietnam (ACV) is the state company that owns and runs the country's airports. VietnamNet reported on 2 July 2026 that 31 people had been prosecuted in a case at ACV for bidding violations, offering bribes and accepting bribes, and that those indicted include the chairman of ACV's board, Vu The Phiet, and a deputy general director and board member, Nguyen Tien Viet. The report said the authorities were continuing to expand the investigation. It did not name the contractors said to have paid, give any amount, or say which of the 31 people face which charge, and no one has yet been tried.
inside: Prosecutors allege that bribes over ACV's tenders reached the state airports company's own board chairman; 31 people have been prosecuted and none tried yet.
cite: VietnamNet, 2 July 2026

n: Bribery alleged over EVN's 500kV line tenders, 47 people prosecuted
rank: National Power Transmission Corporation (EVNNPT) and its project boards
d: The National Power Transmission Corporation (EVNNPT), part of the state electricity group EVN, built the 500kV circuit-3 transmission line with northern and central power project management boards, contractors and consulting firms. VietnamNet reported on 2 July 2026 that Major General Le Van Tan of the investigation police told a briefing in Hanoi that 47 people had been prosecuted, that investigators had found violations in cost estimates, bidding, contractor selection and acceptance by the investor and the contractors, and that the contractors' offences included embezzlement and the giving and receiving of bribes. Police seized more than 45.8 billion dong and over one million US dollars and froze securities accounts worth about 1,756 billion dong. The case is still under investigation.
inside: Investigators say contractors on the state grid company's 500kV line gave and received bribes around its tenders; 47 people have been prosecuted so far.
cite: VietnamNet, 2 July 2026

n: Valve supplier and a Kenya Pipeline buyer convicted over a rigged tender
rank: Kenya Pipeline Company procurement officer
d: Kenya Pipeline Company, the state firm that moves the country's fuel through its pipelines, bought hydrant pit valves and spares in a tender its own investigators later found had been rigged. The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission said the rules were broken through collusion between KPC officials and private individuals and firms, with a loss of about Kes550 million (about USD 4,354,516). On 24 January 2025 the anti-corruption court at Milimani, Nairobi, convicted KPC procurement officer Fredrick Ogenga of abuse of office for conferring a benefit on Allied Inspection and Testing Company, which had not won the tender, and convicted the supplier Aero Dispenser Valves Ltd and its directors Francis Omondi Obure and Beryl Khasina of fraudulent procurement practice. Ogenga was fined Kes750,000, the company Kes3 million.
inside: A valve supplier and its directors were convicted of colluding with Kenya Pipeline's own buyer, who conferred the tender benefit on a bidding firm; no payment to him is recorded.
cite: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (Kenya), press release, 27 January 2025

n: Oil trader's car gifts to two NNPC chiefs who steered crude to his firms
rank: NNPC group executive directors
d: Victor Briggs and Abiye Membere, former top officials of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, the state oil company, were convicted at the Federal High Court in Abuja on 7 February 2023 of unethically collecting car gifts as public officials. The gifts came from the businessman Olajide Omokore and his firms Atlantic Energy Brass Development Limited and Atlantic Energy Drilling Concept Limited. The anti-graft agency EFCC alleged a conspiracy to induce the Nigerian Petroleum Development Company, NNPC's exploration arm, to let Omokore's companies lift crude oil. A separate charge alleged his firms obtained 7,551,867 barrels of Brass blend crude from NPDC, NNPC and the federal government on a false pretence of having funds. Each was sentenced to two years, with the option of a two-million-naira fine.
inside: An oil trader's gifts reached two serving directors of the state oil company, and prosecutors say its exploration arm was induced to let his firms lift its crude.
cite: EFCC (Nigeria), news release, February 2023

n: Six supply firms and their owners convicted over Kilifi county payments
org_label: Makegra Suppliers, Zohali Services, Kilingi Investments and others
rank: Kilifi County Government officials
d: Kilifi County Government on Kenya's coast paid out Kes51,569,775 of public money between 19 September and 7 October 2016 to six private companies for services never rendered and goods never supplied: Daima One Enterprises, Zohali Services Limited, Makegra Suppliers Limited, Kilingi Investments Limited, Leadership Edge Associates and Jahazi Investments Company Limited. The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuted, and on 17 April 2026 the Malindi anti-corruption court convicted ten parties, five people and five companies, of fraud and money laundering. Chief Magistrate Elizabeth Usui imposed fines matching the benefits each had taken, running from Kes15.21 million to Kes38.29 million, with long default prison terms, and noted the proceeds had not been recovered.
inside: Private supply firms and their owners worked with county officials so that Kilifi's payments went out for goods never delivered, to the firms' benefit.
cite: Capital FM (Kenya), 3 June 2026; EACC prosecution

n: Contractor's three firms took Kes791,385,000 from Kenya's youth service
who: Reinforced Concrete Technologies and two sister firms
rank: NYS director of finance and principal supply chain officer
d: Kenya's National Youth Service, the state body that trains young people and runs public works, paid Kes791,385,000 for a road project at its Kibera site in Nairobi. Prosecutors said the materials were worth Kes78,857,835. The money went to three firms owned by Josephine Kabura Irungu, the supposed contractor: Reinforced Concrete Technologies took Kes320,160,000, Form Homes Builders Kes218,925,000 and Roof and All Trading Kes252,300,000. About Kes77,000,000 moved from a Form Homes account to an account linked to the accused. In November 2024 the Milimani anti-corruption court found NYS finance director Samuel Wachenje and principal supply chain officer Hendrick Nyongesa Pilisi guilty of forgery, fraud and conspiracy for approving payments without tender committee approval. Sentencing was set for 6 November 2024. Kabura's own case continues.
inside: A contractor's three companies were paid by the state youth service through its own finance and procurement officers, who approved the money without tender approval.
cite: Business Today (Kenya), 4 November 2024, on the Milimani anti-corruption court verdict

n: Equipment supplier charged with paying for contracts at a Nigerian university
rank: Vice-Chancellor, Federal University Dutsinma
d: Armayau Bichi, former Vice-Chancellor of Federal University Dutsinma in Katsina State, was arraigned with Lawal Mani and Aliyu Jari at the Katsina State High Court on 5 February 2026 on five counts of bribery over N19.7 million in alleged kickbacks. One count alleges that Theophilus Ilechukwu of Goezek International Agency Nigeria Limited paid a N5 million bribe in 2023 as a reward for the award of contracts for medical equipment and laboratory furnishing, into Jari's bank account. The EFCC, Nigeria's financial crimes agency, brought the charges. All three pleaded not guilty and were granted bail of N5 million each with one surety, with trial set for 12 March.
inside: Prosecutors allege a medical-equipment supplier paid for contract awards at a federal university, with the money reaching an account tied to its vice-chancellor's circle.
cite: AllAfrica/Daily Trust report of the EFCC arraignment, 6 February 2026

n: Contractors paid Egypt's irrigation administrators to sign off canal works
org_label: canal and drainage contractors (unnamed in the ruling report)
rank: heads of central irrigation and drainage administrations
d: Egypt's Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation runs canal rehabilitation and drainage works through regional central administrations. On 20 January 2026 the Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in New Cairo, sentenced six defendants to ten years' aggravated imprisonment and exempted six others in the case the Egyptian press calls the irrigation ministry bribery case. Prosecutors said contractors and their intermediaries paid officials to clear work for payment: the head of the central irrigation administration in Menoufia allegedly took 50,000 Egyptian pounds through an intermediary and 24,000 from two company owners; the head of the Western Delta drainage region allegedly took 100,000 after approving final payment statements at Nubaria; and a drainage director allegedly received 70,000 of a promised 150,000 over a culvert project in Beni Suef.
inside: Canal and drainage contractors paid the irrigation ministry's own regional administrators, who then certified their work and released the payments due to them.
cite: Masrawy (Egypt), 20 January 2026, on the Cairo Criminal Court verdict

n: Tubular's Lomas paid Eskom managers' rent to win Kusile upgrade work
rank: senior Eskom managers, Kusile project
d: Eskom is South Africa's state electricity company. On 6 August 2026 the Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg convicted Michael Lomas, a former Eskom contractor, on 34 counts of corruption under a plea agreement. Between February 2015 and April 2017 he paid more than R2.6 million into a company owned by a co-accused, and funded 24 rental payments of more than R396,000 on a Midrand flat benefiting two former senior Eskom employees, to influence an Eskom contract award to Tubular Construction Projects, the company he worked for. He was given 15 years, wholly suspended. Hudson Kgomoeswana pleaded guilty to routing more than R6 million from the Tubular group to a former senior Eskom employee, and must serve five years. The charges concern about R1.4bn for upgrading the Kusile power station.
inside: A construction contractor paid rent and cash to senior Eskom managers so the state power company's Kusile contract award went to the firm he worked for.
cite: TimesLIVE (South Africa), 6 August 2026, on the Gauteng High Court plea and sentence agreements

n: Boss Engineering convicted of bribing officials for a Nigerian works contract
rank: officials of the Federal Ministry of Works
d: On 14 July 2025 the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory at Apo, Abuja, before Justice A. O. Otaluka, convicted the contractor Kenneth Okezie Samuel, his firm Boss Engineering Nigeria Ltd, Collins Ugwu and Cosmas Eze on six counts brought by Nigeria's Independent Corrupt Practices Commission. The court found that a bribe of six million naira was offered to officials of the Federal Ministry of Works to facilitate a contract award, and that a forged tax clearance certificate was put in Boss Engineering's prequalification papers. The officials are not named in the commission's account. Samuel and Ugwu were given two years on each count, concurrent, with a one-million-naira fine as an option; the company was fined one million naira on three counts. The commission said the fines were paid.
inside: A construction contractor paid a bribe to officials of the federal works ministry so that a public contract would be awarded to his company.
cite: Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (Nigeria), 19 November 2025

n: Eutaw's man paid UNRA officers to clear a bogus Katosi road bid
rank: UNRA director of finance and administration
d: The Uganda National Roads Authority (UNRA), the state body that builds and maintains the country's roads, gave the Mukono-Katosi road contract to Eutaw Construction Company. On 30 August 2018 the Anti-Corruption Court at Kololo, Kampala, before Justice Lawrence Gidudu, convicted Eutaw's country representative Apollo Senkeeto of theft of Shs24.7 billion, six counts of uttering false documents and obtaining execution of a security by false pretence, and jailed him for ten years. UNRA's former director of finance and administration Joe Semugooma and his junior Wilberforce Senjako each got five years for corruption jointly with Senkeeto; the judge held they were gatekeepers who could have blocked the bogus bid and instead sided with him. The former works minister Abraham Byandala and three others were acquitted.
inside: A road contractor's representative worked through UNRA's own finance chief and his junior, who passed a bogus bid and let the firm draw Shs24.7 billion.
cite: Daily Monitor (Uganda), 30 August 2018, on the Anti-Corruption Court judgment

n: Court voids a Trans Nzoia stadium tender and orders Kes25 million repaid
rank: Head of Supply Chain Management, Trans Nzoia County
d: Trans Nzoia County Government in western Kenya awarded tenders to renovate the Kenyatta Municipal Stadium in Kitale and build spectator sheds. The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission said its investigation found bid rigging and no tender evaluation minutes for the two tenders. On 30 April 2025 Justice Nixon Sifuna of the High Court in Nairobi declared the tender null and void for fraud and procurement irregularities, calling the transaction an execution of illegality rather than a paid service. He ordered the county's former Head of Supply Chain Management and the contractor to refund the Kes25 million paid, with interest from the filing of the suit, and said liability in tainted tendering should fall on the awardee and the facilitators within the procuring entity. The report does not name the contractor.
inside: A contractor and the county's own supply chain chief rigged the stadium bid together, so Trans Nzoia's award and its Kes25 million served the awardee.
cite: Kenyans.co.ke, 1 May 2025, on the High Court ruling in the EACC suit

n: NDDC consultant's payments to the MP who chaired the committee over it
rank: Chairman, House Committee on the NDDC
d: Nicholas Mutu, a six-term member of Nigeria's House of Representatives for Bomadi/Patani in Delta State, chaired the House Committee on the Niger Delta Development Commission. The EFCC alleges that Starline Consultancy Services, an NDDC consultant, asked the committee to help recover debts oil and gas companies owed the commission, and that after the committee issued payment demands and recoveries of over N100 billion followed, Starline paid Mutu kickbacks totalling N400,159,689.63 through Heritage Bank accounts of his firms Airworld Technologies and Oyien Homes, concealed by a subcontract letter under which, the consultant later said, no work was done. In April 2026 Justice Folashade Giwa-Ogunbanjo acquitted Mutu of 13 counts; the EFCC has appealed. On 2 July 2026 Justice Joyce Abdulmalik ordered final forfeiture of N150 million he had refunded.
