inside: Prosecutors allege a commission's own consultant paid the MP who chaired the committee supervising it, and the committee then pressed debtors to pay the consultant's client.
cite: Premium Times via AllAfrica, 3 July 2026, on the Federal High Court forfeiture order

n: Consortium chief charged with paying Ghana's Northern Development Authority
rank: Chief Executive and two deputies, Northern Development Authority
d: Ghana's Office of the Special Prosecutor charged four men over the Northern Development Authority, the state body that funds development in Ghana's north. They are Sumaila Abdul Rahman, Stephen Yir-Eru Engmen, Patrick Seidu and Andrew Kuundaari; the report lists their roles as the authority's former Chief Executive, two former Deputy Chief Executives, and the Chief Executive of A&QS Consortium Limited, without saying which name holds which role. The eleven counts include corruption of a public officer and conspiracy to influence a procurement award. On 26 April 2024 the High Court, Criminal Division, in Tamale rejected a no-case-to-answer submission and ordered the accused to open their defence. The Special Prosecutor's report gives no sums.
inside: Prosecutors say a consortium's chief executive corrupted officers of the state development authority so that a procurement award would go his way.
cite: Office of the Special Prosecutor (Ghana), 2024 half-yearly report

n: Borrower's bribe reached the head of NEXIM Bank's Lagos region
org_label: Obi Ogoh and Sevirg AgroAllied Mills Ltd
rank: Head of Lagos Region, Nigerian Export-Import Bank
d: The Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM) is a state-owned development bank that lends to exporters. Ugenyi Kalu, head of its Lagos Region, was convicted on 12 February 2025 by Justice Rahman Oshodi at the Special Offences Court in Ikeja, Lagos, on four counts of official corruption and gratification. The court found that Obi Ogoh had paid Kalu a four-million-naira bribe, which the report ties to a NEXIM loan to Sevirg AgroAllied Mills Ltd; it does not say what favour Ogoh sought. Kalu had pleaded not guilty to a five-count charge, and the court held the prosecution had proved its case beyond doubt. He was sentenced to four years and two months in prison, with the option of a fine of 20.85 million naira.
inside: A borrower's money reached the state export bank's regional head, the payment the court found proved in the lending relationship he was there to judge.
cite: Leadership (Nigeria), February 2025, on the Lagos Special Offences Court judgment

n: Exporter and broker paid an Egyptian customs director to clear shipments
org_label: an import-export trading agency and a customs broker
rank: Director General of Deposits and Customs Affairs, Egyptian Customs Authority
d: The Egyptian Customs Authority collects duty and clears goods at the country's ports. On 12 June 2024 the Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in New Cairo under Judge Modaboly Kassab, sentenced its Director General of Deposits, Customs Affairs and External Annexes, named in the press as Mohamed R., to ten years' hard labour, a fine of 3,782,000 Egyptian pounds and dismissal. Prosecutors said that between May 2018 and October 2023 he demanded 1,510,000 pounds from the owner of an import-export trade agency in return for using his influence with Badr port customs staff to complete his shipments' export procedures, and 338,000 from a customs broker at Tenth of Ramadan port through intermediaries. A justice ministry illicit-gains official got three years for leaking the inquiry into him; the other defendants were acquitted.
inside: An exporter and a customs broker paid the customs authority's own director general, who then used his influence over port staff to clear their shipments.
cite: Masrawy (Egypt), 12 June 2024, on the Cairo Criminal Court verdict

n: Businessmen's cash and flats got 285 feddans from Egypt's land officials
org_label: businessmen and lawyers seeking state land
rank: director of property management, Agriculture Directorate
d: On 30 September 2025 the Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in New Cairo under Judge Mohamed Ahmed El-Gendy, convicted officials of an Egyptian Agriculture Directorate, the provincial office that allocates state farmland, with businessmen and lawyers who sought that land. Between 2004 and 2008 the officials issued allocation and payment permits for 285 feddans along the Qatamiya-Ain Sokhna and Cairo-Ismailia desert roads without the legal requirements being met, and had the use changed from agricultural reclamation to investment. The property management director, named in the press as Anwar M., took cash and residential units, including 50,000 Egyptian pounds for allocating 170 feddans. He received ten years and a fine of 94.48 million pounds; the businessman Ahmed Y. got ten years and must repay 44.88 million.
inside: Businessmen and lawyers paid cash and flats to the land officials who signed their permits, and 285 feddans of state farmland was reallocated to them.
cite: Youm7 (Egypt), on the Cairo Criminal Court verdict of 30 September 2025

n: Contractor charged with paying an Osun college council for an amphitheatre
rank: members of the Governing Council, Osun State College of Education
d: Nigeria's Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) pays for building work at state colleges. The contractor John Ojekorede Ojemuyiwa and his firm Digitpro Engineering Technology Limited held a contract worth N228,298,302 for an amphitheatre at the Osun State College of Education, Ila Orangun. The EFCC's charge alleged that they corruptly gave N43,093,694.36 to members of the college's Governing Council through David Olayinka Olajede of De Capstone Ltd, and complained of an overpaid mobilisation fee. Justice Akin-David Oladimeji of the Osun State High Court at Ede found the pair guilty on counts one and three of an amended three-count charge and imposed three years on each, concurrently. The report does not say which count carried the bribery allegation.
inside: Prosecutors allege a building contractor paid the governing council of a state teacher-training college, which held the contract he was performing for it.
cite: PRNigeria, 11 June 2018, on the EFCC prosecution at the Osun State High Court

n: Two Kampala city officials convicted over a UGX 300,000 facilitation fee
rank: ward administrator and administrative officer, Kampala Capital City Authority
d: Beatrice Nakibuuka, a former ward administrator at the Kampala Capital City Authority, and Jocelyn Wagaba Twemanye, a former administrative officer there, demanded UGX 300,000 from Edul Misaki on 22 December 2020 as facilitation for organising a family meeting about his late brother's estate. The Chief Magistrate's Court, Anti-Corruption Division at Buganda Road, convicted both of corrupt solicitation in 2021, and Nakibuuka also of receiving gratification. Each was fined UGX 1.5 million, Nakibuuka a further UGX 1 million, and both were barred from public office for ten years. The High Court dismissed their appeal on 25 March 2024, and on 31 March 2026 the Court of Appeal in Kampala dismissed a second appeal and upheld the convictions, fines and ban in full.
inside: A man with business before the city authority paid its own officials to arrange the estate meeting he wanted, and they were convicted of soliciting it.
cite: PlusNews (Uganda), on the Court of Appeal judgment of 31 March 2026

n: Land seller's money reached the Nairobi council lawyer who ran the tender
org_label: Henry Musyoki Kilonzi, the land's seller
rank: Director of Legal Services and tender evaluation chair, City Council of Nairobi
d: The defunct City Council of Nairobi paid Kes283,000,000, money from the Ministry of Local Government, for about 120 acres at Athi River to use as a cemetery. Mary Ngechi Ngethe was the council's Director of Legal Services and chaired the technical evaluation committee for the tender. On 24 March 2026 Justice Benjamin Mwikya Musyoki, in the High Court's anti-corruption division at Milimani, found she had received Kes13,000,000 out of the sale proceeds, transferred on her instructions by the seller's advocates and passed to her through the firm acting for the council. The seller, Henry Musyoki Kilonzi, was paid Kes110,000,000; the commission valued the land at about Kes30,000,000. She was ordered to repay the Kes13,000,000 with interest and the costs of the suit.
inside: The seller's money reached the council lawyer who chaired the committee evaluating the tender, and the council paid Kes283,000,000 for land valued far lower.
cite: Ethics & Anti-Corruption Commission v Mary Ngechi Ngethe, HC.ACEC/35/2018, High Court of Kenya, 24 March 2026

n: PPE supplier found 'in cahoots' with a Matzikama municipal manager
rank: Acting Municipal Manager, Matzikama Local Municipality
d: Matzikama Local Municipality in South Africa's Western Cape paid Duneco CC R400,027.50 for personal protective equipment around 21 April 2020, early in the Covid-19 pandemic. The Special Tribunal, a court set up to recover money lost to state corruption, gave judgment on 23 June 2023. Judge JP Daffue found that the acting municipal manager, Aldrich Hendricks, had a financial link with Duneco's sole member Nicolaas Klazen: Klazen had been given the bank details of Hendricks's wife, and a deposit to her account was tied to a private transaction in 2019. The tribunal rejected both men's explanations as false and found Hendricks, the Covid-19 coordinator Isak Jenner and Klazen were in cahoots, without expressly finding a proven kickback. Hendricks, Jenner and the chief financial officer must repay the money.
inside: A PPE supplier had a money link to the acting municipal manager who chose it, and the tribunal found the two were in cahoots over the purchase.
cite: Special Investigating Unit and Another v Duneco CC and Others (WC/05/22) [2023] ZAST 9, 23 June 2023

n: Power-bypass customer paid two ZESCO staff to keep him out of court
rank: senior electrician and general worker, ZESCO Mongu
d: ZESCO Limited is Zambia's state-owned electricity company. Brian Monde Lupasa, a former senior electrician at its Mongu operation in Western Province, and Kwalombota Kwalombota, a former general worker there, were convicted of corrupt practices by public officers after Zambia's Anti-Corruption Commission charged them. During November 2022 they solicited K10,000 and received K3,000 in cash from an individual, to keep him from being prosecuted for bypassing his electricity meter. The commission's release describes the payer only as an individual. Magistrate Kalifano Manyepa, in the Mongu Subordinate Court, sentenced each to 18 months with hard labour under the Anti-Corruption Act of 2012, ordered the K3,000 forfeited to the state and remanded both men in prison.
inside: A customer caught bypassing his meter paid two of the state power company's own staff so that it would not take him to court.
cite: Anti-Corruption Commission (Zambia), release of 29 May 2024, reported by Efficacy News Africa

n: Rudkop won a REK Bitola overburden tender through the plant's own officers
rank: director of REK Bitola and its tender commissions
d: REK Bitola, the lignite mine and power plant of North Macedonia's state electricity company ESM, ran a 2022 tender for excavating overburden worth more than 11 million euros. It chose the private firm Rudkop of Bitola and excluded the Skopje builder Granit. On 12 November 2026 the Basic Court in Bitola convicted the plant's then director Pece Matevski and sentenced him to two years, gave suspended terms to three members of its expert commission and to three staff of the Public Procurement Bureau, and acquitted three procurement commission members. The court found they obtained a benefit for Rudkop and caused REK Bitola damage of 178,370,319 denars, about 2.9 million euros. Rudkop's frozen assets of about 3.5 million euros stay frozen until the verdict is final.
inside: A private contractor got the state power plant's excavation contract through its director and tender panels, who were convicted of rigging the award in Rudkop's favour.
cite: Nezavisen Vesnik and Denesen.mk, 12 November 2026

n: Termoelectrica section head accused of monthly payments from a bidder
org_label: an unnamed business favoured in Termoelectrica's tenders
rank: head of a section at Termoelectrica
d: Termoelectrica is Moldova's state heating and power company, which supplies most of Chisinau. In June 2026 the National Anticorruption Centre (CNA) and prosecutors detained one of its section heads, saying he had repeatedly demanded and taken money he was not entitled to from a representative of a business, in exchange for favouring that business in the company's tenders. Preliminary figures put the payments at about 10,000 lei a month. Investigators searched his office and the businessman's premises and seized cash said to be meant for May 2026, along with storage devices and documents. A court placed him in custody for 20 days. The investigation continues, CNA says others may be involved, and he is presumed innocent until a final judgment.
inside: A supplier bidding for the state heating company's contracts allegedly kept one of its section heads on a monthly payment so its bids were favoured.
cite: Telegraph.md, 3 June 2026; Timpul.md on CNA's weekly report, 8 June 2026

n: Serbian rail infrastructure chief took 10,000 euros over lawyer hirings
rank: acting director, Infrastruktura zeleznice Srbije
d: Infrastruktura zeleznice Srbije is the state company that manages Serbia's railway network. On 21 October 2021 the Higher Court in Belgrade, through its special organised-crime department, sentenced its former acting director Miroljub Jevtic to one year in prison for accepting a bribe, and ordered the 10,000 euros he received confiscated as a gift. Prosecutors from the Prosecutor's Office for Organised Crime said that between August 2018 and May 2019 he engaged lawyers for land expropriation along high-speed rail routes without need or grounds, and that part of the money from that work was paid back through an intermediary. His detention from 10 January to 6 March 2020 counted towards the sentence. The verdict was not final and could be appealed in Belgrade.
inside: Outside lawyers paid for unnecessary expropriation work at the state rail company returned part of the fees, through an intermediary, to the director who hired them.
cite: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty Balkan Service, 21 October 2021

n: Businessman bribed staff of Bulgaria's state irrigation company
rank: employees of Napoitelni Sistemi EAD
d: Napoitelni Sistemi EAD is the Bulgarian state company that runs the country's irrigation canals and dams. The businessman Stoyan Komitov offered bribes to its employees so that they would accept construction sites where no work had been done. The Supreme Court of Cassation upheld his conviction in a final decision reported in July 2022, and he received a suspended sentence; the report does not give its length, name his company, or say which employees were involved. Ivaylo Parvanov, the company's former executive director, was a defendant in the same case, but the proceedings against him were terminated because he died before the verdict was delivered.
inside: A contractor paid employees of the state irrigation company to certify sites where no work had been done, and his conviction is now final.
cite: 24 Chasa, 20 July 2022

n: Nesebar water utility manager charged over 8,000 euros for a connection
org_label: the owner of a property in Kosharitsa
who: a property owner seeking a water connection
rank: manager at ViK Nesebar
d: ViK Nesebar is the municipal water and sewerage company on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. Prosecutors in Burgas charged Svilen Stanchev, a manager there, with demanding and taking a bribe of 8,000 euros from the owner of a property in the holiday zone of Kosharitsa village so that it would be connected to the water and sewerage network. He was detained in late June 2026 after taking marked notes; police also found 30,000 euros at his home and notebooks of names, which prosecutors said they had not yet linked to the payment. A district court ordered custody, then released him to house arrest, and on 18 August 2026 the Burgas Appellate Court returned him to custody. He said the cash at his home belonged to the woman he lives with.
inside: A property owner paid a manager of the municipal water company 8,000 euros for the connection his project needed, prosecutors say.
cite: PressTV.bg, 30 June 2026; DeFakto.bg, 18 August 2026

n: Interholding won Macedonian post and rail privatisation work without tender
rank: Secretary General of the Government
d: Muhamed Zeqiri was Secretary General of North Macedonia's government, the civil servant who runs its central office. Prosecutors said he awarded consultancy contracts to the firm Interholding, for analysing the state of Makedonska Posta and Makedonski Zeleznici and the options for privatising them, without a proper public procurement procedure, causing the state budget more than 1.1 million euros of damage. He was sentenced in December 2023 to two and a half years for abuse of official position. That judgment was annulled and the case retried, and the Court of Appeal in Skopje then set the sentence at one year and seven months, reported on 20 October 2026. The court ordered Interholding's property confiscated but imposed no such measure on Zeqiri, who may appeal to the Supreme Court.
inside: A consultancy obtained government contracts on privatising the state post and railways through the government's own secretary general, outside procurement rules, and had its property confiscated.
cite: Skopje Info, citing Koha, 20 October 2026

n: Chisinau housing directorate accused of taking cuts from winning bidders
org_label: three businessmen whose firms won city contracts
rank: head of the General Directorate for Housing and Communal Services
d: The General Directorate for Housing, Communal Services and Landscaping is the arm of Chisinau City Hall that buys road, lighting and maintenance work. On 4 December 2025 the National Anticorruption Centre detained seven people: four public officials, among them the directorate's head Ion Burdiumov, and three businessmen. Investigators say that since 2024 the officials systematically demanded commissions calculated on the value of contracts those businessmen's companies won, and in exchange favoured the firms in procurement procedures. Searches seized cash worth about 5 million lei, whose origin is still to be established, and intercepts released by the Centre discuss commissions that in some cases passed 1 million lei. A court jailed five of the seven for 30 days and placed two under house arrest or judicial control.
inside: Contractors paid the Chisinau housing directorate's managers a share of each contract they won, and prosecutors say its tenders were steered to them.
cite: Radio Moldova, 8 December 2025; Ziar.md, December 2025

n: Sinohydro commissions alleged over Macedonian motorway contract award
rank: Prime Minister, deputy PM, transport minister, state roads director
d: The Special Public Prosecutor's Office charged four men over the choice of a builder for the Miladinovci-Stip and Kicevo-Ohrid motorways: prime minister Nikola Gruevski, deputy prime minister Vladimir Peshevski, transport minister Mile Janakieski, and Ljupco Georgievski, director of the Public Enterprise for State Roads. Prosecutors said Gruevski agreed commissions with the Chinese contractor Sinohydro and took a reward for illegal influence, while the other three abused their positions, in a period running from November 2012 to 10 October 2013. They put the loss to the state budget at 155,117,256 euros, the gap between what the state pays Sinohydro and what Sinohydro pays its subcontractors. The trial opened in 2018 and reached no verdict: in November 2023 the prosecutor withdrew the charges as time-barred.
inside: A Chinese state contractor allegedly agreed commissions with the prime minister and got the motorway award through the ministers and state roads director who made it.
cite: IRL.mk, 16 September 2019; Off.net.mk and RFE/RL Macedonian Service, 3 November 2023

n: Indjija road company paid a pre-agreed bidder for work not done
rank: directors of JP Indjija put
d: JP Indjija put is the public road company of Indjija municipality in northern Serbia. The Higher Public Prosecutor's Office in Novi Sad says that between 2023 and 2025 Marko Gasic, now president of the municipality and formerly the company's director, and Uros Trifunovic, its current director, enabled tenders for road marking and traffic signs in which the bidder was agreed in advance and contracts were awarded against procurement criteria, and then ordered payments totalling 26,961,059 dinars although they knew the work had not been done. Three further suspects are accused of certifying false technical documents used to release the money, and one of laundering it. In November 2026 the Higher Court in Novi Sad ordered the two directors held for up to 30 days.
inside: A contractor chosen before the tender was run took payments from the municipal road company for work never carried out, prosecutors in Novi Sad allege.
cite: Kurir, citing Tanjug and the Higher Court in Novi Sad, November 2026

n: Security firm billed Macedonia's state roads for guards it did not post
rank: director of the Public Enterprise for State Roads
d: The Public Enterprise for State Roads runs North Macedonia's motorways and its 14 toll stations. On 8 August 2022 it signed a two-year contract with the private agency 2SS of Kicevo, owned by Dzemal Bilbilovski, for continuous security at all 14 stations. Prosecutors say the agency usually provided only the first shift but billed for round-the-clock cover until the contract was ended, making an unlawful gain of 46,918,079 denars and costing the state budget over 760,000 euros. They suspect the enterprise's director Ejup Rustemi, its collection and controls head Drilon Ziberi and assistant director Ejup Latifi of abuse of office and forgery for not acting although they knew the guards were absent, and Bilbilovski of abuse of the tender procedure.
inside: A security contractor kept the state roads enterprise paying for guards it never posted, with the enterprise's director and two sector heads suspected of letting it.
cite: Libertas.mk, on the Skopje Criminal Court's measures against Ejup Rustemi

n: Signas-Argo bribed Macedonian farm payments agency staff for IPARD money
rank: director and staff of the Agency for Financial Support in Agriculture
d: The Agency for Financial Support in Agriculture and Rural Development pays out IPARD money, EU funds for farmers, in North Macedonia. Prosecutors say the company Signas-Argo, headed by the former minister Dzevdet Nasufi, applied for support, was ranked low because it did not meet the conditions, and then paid to be moved up: a senior official was promised 50,000 euros and three other people received 5,000 euros each. On 5 May 2026 the civil servant Jasmina Kostadinova was sentenced to ten months after admitting she took a 2,000-euro bribe to manipulate the ranking list. The agency's former director Ilija Stoilev, charged with taking a bribe, was caught with 50,000 euros in cash; four other staff face abuse-of-office charges, and the company is charged with giving a bribe.
inside: A company that failed the conditions for EU farm funds paid staff of the paying agency to lift its ranking, and one official has been convicted.
cite: Sakam Da Kazam (sdk.mk), 5 May 2026

n: Farmers paid Serbia's agrarian payments chief a cut of their subsidies
rank: director, Administration for Agrarian Payments
d: The Administration for Agrarian Payments, part of Serbia's agriculture ministry, decides who receives farm subsidies. On 26 October 2021 the Higher Court in Belgrade convicted its former director Zarko Radat of accepting bribes as a continuing offence, sentencing him to three years and six months and barring him for four years from posts linked to the agriculture ministry. Valentin Drazilov got one year and three months, and Bora Zivic, a former bank employee, two years. A former Administration employee, Dunja Vasic, received a suspended term for helping. Two farmers, Vladimir Hedji and Milenko Sikimic, got suspended terms of ten months each for giving bribes. The officials took a percentage of subsidies claimed by six farmers from Vojvodina, about 1.6 million dinars in all, for letting the applications through.
inside: Farmers paid officials of the state farm-payments body a share of their subsidies so their claims went through, and a court convicted the body's director.
cite: RTS, citing Tanjug, 26 October 2021

n: Shell companies supplied Moldova's state railway with parts in fake deals
org_label: over 20 shell companies supplying railway parts
rank: director and a department head of Calea Ferata
d: Calea Ferata din Moldova is the state railway. At a press conference on 11 February 2014 the Prosecutor General's Office said more than 20 shell companies, registered in the names of people paid to do so, had been used for fictitious transactions in which train and wagon parts worth over 75 million lei were supplied to the railway. Ten companies and five people were accused of harming the state by about 12 million lei between 2010 and 2013, and ten cases had reached court. Vitalie Struna, the railway's director from November 2011 until his dismissal in 2013, and an unnamed former department head were accused of taking 400,000 euros from its account, sent through banks to a company abroad.
inside: Suppliers set up as shell firms sold the state railway parts in fictitious deals, and its director and a department head were accused alongside them.
cite: Radio Europa Libera Moldova, 11 February 2014

n: ESO's chief came from supplier EMU, which then won its grid contracts
rank: executive director, Electricity System Operator (ESO)
d: ESO, Bulgaria's state electricity transmission operator, buys the work that builds and rebuilds the grid. Angelin Tsachev worked for the contractor EMU, owned by Tanyu Tanev, from 2007 to 2011, and in 2018 the then energy minister Temenuzhka Petkova appointed him ESO's director although he was a mid-level manager at the state company. Mediapool, citing Kapital, reported in May 2021 that EMU's large orders from ESO began around 2018: soon after taking office Tsachev halted a 119-million-leva tender for a Maritsa East to Burgas power line, re-announced it with stricter requirements, and EMU won it. EMU and the nearby firm Impuls Ko then signed a four-year framework agreement worth 70 million leva, under which about 220 million leva has been paid. ESO said it follows the procurement law.
inside: A contractor's former employee was made head of the state grid operator, and its procurement then went to that contractor on a growing framework agreement.
cite: Mediapool, citing Kapital, 28 May 2021

n: Global Saude's payments reached a Correios executive over a staff medicine plan
org_label: Global Gestao em Saude (Global Saude) and Precisa Medicamentos
rank: Correios executive and the postal workers' federation
d: Federal prosecutors charged five people with criminal organisation, corruption and money laundering over a scheme they say favoured Global Gestao em Saude in a contract with Correios, Brazil's state post office. The MPF alleges Global paid R$2.5 million in bribes between 2011 and 2014 to sell a medicine insurance service to Correios staff, with the contract routed through Fentect, a private workers' federation that receives Correios funds, to avoid public bidding. Those charged are Precisa Medicamentos owner Francisco Maximiano, his sister Michelli Maximiano Goncalves, former Correios executive Nelson Luiz Oliveira de Freitas, former Fentect president Jose Rivaldo da Silva and lawyer Alexandre Romano. Monthly payments allegedly rose from R$50,000 to R$200,000 once the plan became compulsory in 2014. The case began with Romano's plea deal; no ruling is reported.
inside: A medicines supplier allegedly paid a Correios executive and a union chief so the post office bought its insurance plan without a public tender.
cite: Correio 24 Horas, reporting the MPF charges

n: Lobbyists paid Correios engineering staff for inside bid information
org_label: Atrium Tecnologia e Servicos de Engenharia / Aerotecnica Uniao
rank: head and deputy head of the Correios engineering department
d: Federal prosecutors in the Federal District charged eleven people in September 2008 with embezzling money from Correios, Brazil's state post office, in 2004 and 2005. Prosecutors say the businessmen Jose Santos Fortuna and Clauzer Esteves paid public employees for inside information on Correios tenders, and that Washington Pavan and Jose Cacao ran the winning firm Aerotecnica Uniao, described as a partner of Atrium Tecnologia, which Fortuna and Esteves allegedly controlled. The contract was for an air treatment system at the letter and parcel sorting centre in Benfica, Rio de Janeiro, and about R$2 million is alleged to have been diverted. Four Correios officers were charged: engineering department head Jorge Dantas, his deputy Carlos Tormim, projects division head Edilson Louzada and works inspector Antonio Winter.
inside: Two businessmen allegedly bought inside tender information from the Correios engineering department, whose own officers then oversaw and authorised payments on their firm's contract.
cite: Congresso em Foco, 12 September 2008, on the MPF/DF charges

n: Codesp's president and directors tried over a R$12m no-bid port contract
rank: president and directors of Codesp
d: On 11 April 2023 a judge of the 5th Federal Court of Santos accepted a prosecution complaint against seven people over a R$12 million contract signed in April 2016 between Codesp, the state company that ran the Port of Santos, and the microcompany N2O Tecnologia da Informacao. Two are businesspeople and five are former Codesp executives, including its president and directors, who are not named in the report. The charges are improper waiver of bidding and peculato, and prosecutors asked for minimum reparation of R$12,393,656.00. The defendants denied irregularities during the police inquiry. The case belongs to Operacao Tritao, covering Codesp tenders from 2013 to 2016; in a separate Tritao case the same judge acquitted eleven people, eight of them senior Codesp officials, over a drone-monitoring contract.
inside: A small IT supplier obtained a R$12 million Santos port contract without a tender through Codesp's own president and directors, who are now on trial over it.
cite: Consultor Juridico, 13 April 2023; Consultor Juridico, 13 August 2023 (acquittal in the Vert case)

n: A digitisation firm paid Codesp directors as an ex-deputy named its board
org_label: Mario Jorge Paladino's document digitisation firm
rank: Codesp financial and logistics directors
d: Operacao Circulo Vicioso, launched on 22 August 2019, targeted former federal deputy Marcelo Squassoni and twenty others, among them businesspeople and former executives of Codesp, the state company running the Port of Santos. Prosecutors say bid and contract fraud cost Codesp more than R$100 million, that Squassoni took R$1.6 million in bribes and loans from firms in the scheme, and that he nominated the Codesp board members who enabled it. The businessman Mario Jorge Paladino, in a plea deal, said his digitisation firm was later hired by Codesp and paid bribes to Squassoni and to the directors Francisco Jose Adriano and Carlos Henrique de Oliveira Poco. Nineteen people had been arrested by late morning. No verdict is reported.
inside: A supplier allegedly paid the Codesp directors a former deputy had placed on the board, and was then hired by the port company it had paid.
cite: ABCdoABC, 22 August 2019, on the MPF and Federal Police operation

n: A railway cartel paid Valec's president over Norte-Sul contracts
org_label: Camargo Correa, Queiroz Galvao, Evolucao Engenharia and Elccom Engenharia
rank: president and engineering director of Valec
d: Operacao O Recebedor, launched on 26 February 2016 as a spin-off of Car Wash after a leniency deal with Camargo Correa, alleged a cartel in railway works run through Valec, the federal state company that built the Norte-Sul and Integracao Oeste-Leste lines. Prosecutors in Goias charged eight people on 11 May 2016, among them former Valec president Jose Francisco das Neves, known as Juquinha, former engineering director Ulisses Assad, Camargo Correa director Joao Ricardo Auler and Queiroz Galvao superintendent Jose Ivanildo Santos Lopes. The cartel is said to have run from about 2000 to the last tenders in 2011, with overpricing of more than R$230 million and losses above R$600 million. Juquinha allegedly received more than R$2.24 million. Camargo Correa agreed to repay R$75 million.
inside: Builders in a cartel paid Valec's own president and engineering director, so the state railway company's tenders were shared out among them for a decade.
cite: Rota Juridica, May 2016, on the MPF/GO charges in Operacao O Recebedor

n: Brazil's anti-corruption office barred four builders over rigged Valec tenders
org_label: Pedrasul Construtora, Construtora Barbosa Mello, CR Almeida and Galvao Engenharia
rank: former Valec executives
d: On 17 October 2023 the Comptroller General of the Union, Brazil's federal anti-corruption office, declared Pedrasul Construtora unfit to bid for or hold public contracts, and rejected appeals by Construtora Barbosa Mello, CR Almeida and Galvao Engenharia, which keep the same ban. The office found that the firms took part in rigging tenders at Valec, the state company that built the Norte-Sul and Integracao Oeste-Leste railways, and that Pedrasul fixed prices with other firms to simulate competition and formed consortia through arrangements with former Valec executives. The finding drew on a leniency agreement with companies in the scheme. The report notes that a 2016 police operation found about R$630 million diverted from Norte-Sul work in Goias. Valec closed in 2022, its work passing to the state planning company EPL.
inside: Builders arranged consortia and prices with Valec's own former executives, so the state railway company's tenders only looked competitive; the anti-corruption office barred them.
cite: Gazeta do Povo, 17 October 2023, on the CGU's sanctions

n: Queiroz Galvao suspected of rewarding an Infraero adviser with a flat
rank: adviser to the presidency of Infraero
d: The federal police suspected that Eurico Bernardo Loyo, a civil engineer and former adviser to the presidency of Infraero, the state company that ran Brazil's airports, was rewarded by the Queiroz Galvao group through its property arm. In 2007 Loyo declared buying a four-bedroom flat in a prime part of Recife for R$281,000, trading in a property valued at R$230,000 that he had declared the year before at R$110,000; police suspected the overvaluation was a prize for his part in rigged Infraero tenders. Phone records showed 94 calls to Queiroz Galvao mobiles and 47 to a number of Consbem Construcoes. The inquiry covered works at ten airports contracted between 2003 and 2006 and R$991.8 million the police attributed to fraud and overpricing. Loyo said he bore no responsibility.
inside: A builder allegedly paid an Infraero presidency adviser through an overvalued property swap for his part in the airport tenders it was winning.
cite: A Tarde, reporting the Federal Police inquiry into Infraero airport works

n: Toshiba's slush fund paid Furnas directors, a former manager told police
who: Toshiba and a power equipment cartel
rank: directors of Furnas
d: In March 2006 Jose Antonio Csapo Talavera, a former administrative superintendent of Toshiba, told Brazil's federal police that the company had used an off-the-books fund, known as caixa dois, to pay bribes to politicians and to directors of Furnas, the federal power generation company. He said Toshiba belonged to a cartel that rigged Furnas tenders, naming WEG, ABB and GE among the members, along with the Gevisa consortium of GE, Villares and Banco Safra. The lobbyist Pedro Terra allegedly offered contracts to build five or six thermoelectric plants, including two at Campos and Sao Goncalo, and charged US$5 million to secure Toshiba's contract. Furnas had R$8.6 million of business with Toshiba over the previous two years. No Furnas director is named in the account.
inside: An equipment maker's own former manager said its secret fund paid directors of the state generator Furnas, whose power plant tenders the cartel then shared out.
cite: Congresso em Foco, 4 March 2006, on the former Toshiba superintendent's statement to the Federal Police

n: A Caixa manager approved 38 housing loans for his partner's units in Para
org_label: a builder selling 38 housing units, and four accredited engineers
who: a housing builder and bank-accredited engineers
rank: manager of the Caixa branch in Marituba
d: On 27 November 2025 a federal court convicted Joao Helio Vieira, former manager of the Marituba branch of Caixa Economica Federal, Brazil's federal savings bank, of peculato, together with his partner, who built and sold 38 housing units, and four bank-accredited engineers. The court described the conduct as intentional improper granting of credit: the bank accepted payslips and income statements with visible signs of falsity to inflate borrowers' incomes, loan money was credited to the partner's account, and the engineers issued false valuations describing properties at Sao Domingos do Capim as isolated units although they belonged to a development of more than twelve. More than R$1.5 million was diverted in 2013 and 2014, and 26 of the 38 contracts defaulted. They were acquitted over Santa Maria do Para.
inside: A builder and the bank's own accredited engineers got housing credit out of Caixa through its branch manager, whose partner was the seller taking the money.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal (MPF/PA), 28 November 2025

n: A document agency paid a Detran-SP officer to wave vehicle papers through
org_label: a vehicle document agency (despachante) in the Campinas region
rank: administrative officer of Detran-SP
d: An administrative officer of Detran-SP, the Sao Paulo state traffic authority, who worked at its office in Saltinho in the interior of the state, was convicted of corruption and lost his public post, as were three people linked to a vehicle document agency, a despachante office in the Campinas region that the report does not name. Prosecutors alleged he used his system access to speed up vehicle paperwork in exchange for bribes, taking R$168,250 between January 2022 and January 2023 for authorisations and registrations that should have gone through normal review. About R$170,000 was found at his home in a police search in January 2023 and he could not explain it. Detran dismissed him in April 2024. His sentence of two years and eight months became community service.
inside: A paperwork agency paid a Detran officer to push its clients' vehicle registrations through the state traffic authority without the checks they needed.
cite: Metropoles, 17 October 2025

n: A builders' standing levy reached Rio's state works bodies over favela works
org_label: OAS, Camargo Correa, Queiroz Galvao, Caenge, Camter and EIT
rank: state governor, government secretary and president of the works company EMOP
d: On 27 May 2026 the federal appeal court for Rio de Janeiro convicted former state governor Sergio Cabral and 22 others of administrative improbity over the PAC-Favelas urban works in Manguinhos, Rocinha and Complexo do Alemao, reversing acquittals by four votes to one. Among the defendants are Icaro Moreno Junior, then president of the state works company EMOP, the then government secretary Wilson Carlos Cordeiro da Silva Carvalho, the public works undersecretary Hudson Braga, and executives of OAS, Camargo Correa, Queiroz Galvao, Caenge, Camter and EIT. Prosecutors said the firms rigged bids and ran a cartel, and that a 5 per cent kickback on state contracts, called the taxa de oxigenio, was demanded; payments in these works are estimated at more than R$162 million. The 23 must pay R$242.4 million.
inside: Construction firms paid a standing 5 per cent levy to Rio's governor, his secretary and the state works company's president, who then awarded them the favela contracts.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal (PRR2), 29 May 2026, on the TRF2 ruling

n: Aegea admitted paying officials to win water concessions in six states
rank: counselors of Santa Catarina's court of accounts, mayors and secretaries
d: Aegea Saneamento, a private water and sewage group, signed a leniency agreement with Brazil's federal prosecutors on 21 April 2021, under which Montese Engenharia, now Aegea Engenharia, is principal debtor for R$439,089,117.67 payable in fifteen annual instalments, and admitted irregularities before 2018. Plea deal annexes, still sealed and reported by UOL, allege at least R$63 million in bribes between 2010 and 2018, across six states and twenty municipalities, to win or keep water and sewage concessions, paid in cash, through sham contracts and purchases of property and vehicles. They describe influence over state courts of accounts, including counselors of Santa Catarina's court, and dealings with mayors and secretaries. Hamilton Amadeo, Aegea's president until 2020, admitted coordinating payments. The superior court approved the plea deals in 2025; politicians named deny wrongdoing.
inside: A water company's money allegedly reached the auditors and mayors who decide sanitation concessions, and it has admitted paying officials before 2018.
cite: Plural (Curitiba), on the MPF leniency agreement; Times Brasil, on the sealed plea deals reported by UOL

n: Cachoeira's emissaries negotiated a bus station contract with a state firm
rank: president of SCPar, Santa Catarina's partnerships company
d: Agencia Publica reported in January 2016 that Enio Andrade Branco, then a director of Celesc, Santa Catarina's state power company, had headed SCPar, the state company for public-private partnerships, under governor Raimundo Colombo, and that according to O Estado de S. Paulo he negotiated in 2011 with emissaries of the gambling boss Carlinhos Cachoeira to secure a contract for a bus station in Florianopolis. The federal police named Branco in Operacao Monte Carlo, the investigation of Cachoeira's network that also reached former senator Demostenes Torres. Branco said he had known Torres since 2007 and that his contacts with Cachoeira were rare and social. No conviction is reported. Earlier, as president of the Goias power company Celg, his assets were frozen over a 2008 outsourcing contract.
inside: A gambling network's emissaries dealt directly with the head of a Santa Catarina state company over a public contract, according to reporting he disputes.
cite: Agencia Publica, January 2016, citing O Estado de S. Paulo and the Federal Police

n: A western Parana firm paid Sanepar insiders for sewage tenders, police say
org_label: a construction firm based in western Parana
rank: a retired Sanepar employee and a former company president
d: On 13 December 2019 Brazil's federal police ran Operacao Aguas Claras, executing eight search warrants authorised by the 9th Federal Court of Curitiba at the homes of current and former employees of Sanepar, Parana's state water and sewage company, and of businesspeople in Curitiba and Cascavel. Police suspect a firm based in western Parana, which they did not name, paid bribes to win rigged sewage works tenders between 2011 and 2016: about R$700,000 to a retired Sanepar employee in Curitiba who allegedly offered to steer tenders in exchange for benefits, and about R$200,000 more requested by a former company president through an assistant and booked as advertising or sponsorship. Cash in several currencies was seized. No arrests were reported, and Sanepar said it was cooperating.
inside: A contractor allegedly paid a retired Sanepar insider and, through an assistant, a former company president, to have the state water firm's sewage tenders steered its way.
cite: Tribuna do Parana, 13 December 2019, on the Federal Police operation

n: Businessmen bribed Sanepar staff for rigged tenders, Parana prosecutors say
org_label: five companies led by a group of businessmen
rank: Sanepar staff handling tenders and measurements
d: On 20 July 2020 the organised crime unit of Parana's state prosecutors, Gaeco, ran Operacao Ductos against bid rigging at Sanepar, the state water and sewage company, carrying out 16 temporary arrest warrants and 50 searches, including at eight Sanepar units and at five companies in Ponta Grossa, Cornelio Procopio, Telemaco Borba and Curitiba, and freezing the assets of 22 people and companies. Prosecutors say a group of businessmen led the fraud and set up further companies to receive the illegal payments, that Sanepar staff took bribes and gave them internal information, and that services were not fully carried out or were overpriced, with measurements falsified or unchecked. The offences under investigation are bid fraud, peculato, money laundering, corruption and forgery. Sanepar said the staff involved were suspended.
inside: Contractors allegedly paid Sanepar's own staff for internal information and signed-off measurements, so the state water company's tenders and payments followed their arrangement.
cite: Gazeta do Povo, 20 July 2020, on the Gaeco operation

n: Operation Fiat Lux found bribes in at least six Eletronuclear contracts
org_label: service companies and offshore firms used for fictitious subcontracting
rank: president of Eletronuclear when payments began
d: Operacao Fiat Lux, reported on 25 June 2020, was a Car Wash spin-off following the earlier operations Radioatividade, Pripyat, Irmandade and Descontaminacao, with arrest warrants carried out in Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, Brasilia, Barueri, Petropolis and Niteroi. Investigators say bribes were found in at least six contracts of Eletronuclear, the state company that runs Brazil's nuclear power stations, and that money moved through fictitious subcontracting of service companies and offshore firms, which then shared it among the suspects. The scheme emerged from plea deals by businessmen arrested in Operacao Blackout in 2017, and part of it involved companies in Canada, France and Denmark, which the report does not name. Admiral Othon Pinheiro was Eletronuclear's president when the payments began; former minister Silas Rondeau was also a target.
inside: Contractors' money, routed through sham subcontracts and offshore firms, reached inside Eletronuclear across at least six of the state nuclear company's contracts.
cite: O Antagonista, 25 June 2020, on the MPF's Operacao Fiat Lux

n: Contractor paid KTZ railway branch chiefs to sign off work at Aksu-1 station
org_label: an electrical installation contractor at Aksu-1 station
rank: heads of a Pavlodar branch of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy
d: Two former heads of a Pavlodar branch of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, the state railway company, were convicted of extorting money from a contractor doing electrical installation work at Aksu-1 station. The interdistrict criminal court of Pavlodar found that between February and April 2025 they took 2.7 million tenge in total, promising in return the signing of acts of completed work and unobstructed acceptance of services. The evidence came from covert investigative measures and witness testimony. Each was given seven years in prison and barred for life from state posts. The court also considered a 2021 episode in which the main-network head received an office chair worth 57,000 tenge from a subordinate. The verdict was not yet in force and could be appealed.
inside: A contractor's payments reached the officers who accepted its work, so the state railway's sign-off on electrical installation served the firm being paid.
cite: Azattyq Ruhy, citing the Pavlodar interdistrict criminal court

n: Haulier Vadisa M bribed the Kostanay head of Kazakhstan's state wagon firm
rank: director of the Kostanay branch of Qaztemirtrans
d: B. Usabekov, director of the Kostanay branch of Qaztemirtrans, the wagon-owning arm of Kazakhstan's state railway company Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, was convicted of taking a bribe from S. Tairov, director of the firm Vadisa M LLP. Court No. 2 in Kostanay found on 3 October 2022 that the money was paid for unhindered and expedited supply of freight wagons. Usabekov was sentenced to six years in a medium-security prison and barred for life from public office. Tairov was fined 24 million tenge, which the report says is twenty times the amount of the bribe. The case was published by the press service of Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Agency. The verdict had not yet entered into legal force when reported.
inside: An outside firm paid the branch director who allocated freight wagons, so a state company's wagon supply was arranged to serve the customer paying.
cite: Kazpravda, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency of Kazakhstan, October 2022

n: Entrepreneur paid Prodkorporatsiya officers over a grain commodity credit
rank: director of the financial department, NC Prodkorporatsiya
d: The director of the financial department of Prodkorporatsiya, Kazakhstan's state grain trading and food contract company, and a chief specialist were convicted of taking a bribe from an entrepreneur who is not named. The interdistrict criminal court of Astana found on 16 May 2024 that N. G. Zhumadilov and G. Zh. Abenov were paid for help in collecting documents and for assistance in signing a grain commodity credit agreement, under which the company lends grain rather than money. The report puts the payment at 800,000 tenge for issuing a wheat commodity credit, a figure given in a background note rather than in the account of the verdict. Both were fined 48 million tenge and barred for life from state and quasi-state posts. The city prosecutor appealed for prison instead.
inside: A borrower's money reached the officers handling his grain credit, so the state grain company's lending decision was worked through for the man paying.
cite: Bizmedia.kz, 16 May 2024, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency

n: Astana LRT tram project: contractors and city officials jailed over billing
org_label: MG-Pro, Nur Trade Astana, Geobur and Rimteks
rank: Astana LRT management and city departments
d: Officials of the Astana city administration and of Astana LRT, the municipal company building a light rail line in Kazakhstan's capital, were convicted of taking money allocated to the project together with the directors of private firms. The court found officials approved inflated costs for design documentation, technical supervision and consultancy, while contractor directors signed sham contracts with subcontractors at inflated prices and cashed budget money through shell companies, for services largely not delivered. Seven defendants were convicted in May 2021, among them the directors of MG-Pro, Nur Trade Astana, Geobur and Rimteks. On 18 July 2023 the Astana city court upheld a verdict of 3 May 2023 giving nine defendants, including Talgat Ardan and Kanat Sultanbekov, seven years each, with over 5 billion tenge recovered for the state.
inside: Private contractors reached a city rail company and the city's own departments through their officers, so approvals and estimates served firms billing for work largely not delivered.
cite: Nur.kz, 28 May 2021 and on the 18 July 2023 appeal ruling

n: Bazis Construction paid Kazselezashchita chiefs to sign off unbuilt work
rank: head of the republican state enterprise Kazselezashchita
d: Karim Kokrekbaev, former head of the republican state enterprise Kazselezashchita, which builds and maintains mudflow defences in Kazakhstan, was convicted of taking a bribe on a particularly large scale from the director of the construction company Bazis Construction, who is not named. A jury trial in Almaty Region found the money was paid so that officials would sign acceptance acts for work either not done at all or done only formally, leaving the state with damage of almost 2 billion tenge. His former deputy Adilet Akhataev and the businessman Andrey Poplavsky, who the court found arranged the forged documents, were also convicted. Kokrekbaev was given 12 years and the other two 11 years each. The verdict was reported on 3 July 2025 as not yet in force.
inside: A construction company's bribe reached the state enterprise's own chiefs, so acceptance acts were signed for mudflow defence work the court found not done or done only formally.
cite: Bizmedia.kz, 3 July 2025

n: Astana state builder's department head sought 103m tenge from a contractor
org_label: a contractor organisation building an Astana housing complex
rank: head of a department, Elorda Qurylys Kompaniyasy
d: B. K. Bazarbek, head of a department at Elorda Qurylys Kompaniyasy, a construction company subordinate to the Astana city administration, was convicted of fraud and of inciting a bribe. According to Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Agency he demanded 103 million tenge from the director of a contractor organisation, to be paid to the company's leadership in exchange for an advance payment and an increased estimate under a contract to build a multi-apartment residential complex in Astana. A specialised interdistrict criminal court in Astana, sitting with a jury, sentenced him to ten years in prison. The case was reported on 19 March 2025, and the verdict had not then entered into legal force. The report gives no dates for the offence and names no other official.
inside: A contractor was asked for 103 million tenge so a city-owned builder would raise its estimate and advance its money, putting the payer inside its pricing.
cite: Finratings.kz, 19 March 2025, citing Antikor; Kazpravda

n: Builder fined for paying Ust-Kamenogorsk's construction chief to sign work
rank: head of the Ust-Kamenogorsk city construction department
d: An entrepreneur in Ust-Kamenogorsk, in eastern Kazakhstan, was convicted of bribing the head of the city's construction department. The regional court's press service said he handed over 5 million tenge in a hotel car park on 17 October 2025 so that acts of completed work would be signed more quickly, allowing companies he controlled, including a firm identified only as TOO K, to be paid sooner for building projects. The interdistrict criminal court fined him 100 million tenge, twenty times the bribe, and barred him for life from public service, the National Bank and the quasi-state sector. He did not contest the charge, and the verdict was reported on 14 May 2026 as not yet in force.
inside: A builder's 5 million tenge reached the city official who certified his work, so municipal sign-off on his projects served the companies he controlled.
cite: Azattyq Ruhy, 14 May 2026, citing the regional court press service

n: Uzagrolizing chief took $1.18m over repainted Chinese cotton harvesters
org_label: Xinjiang Boshiran Intelligent Agricultural Machinery and Inter Agromash
who: A Chinese machinery maker and the importer Inter Agromash
rank: chairman of the board of Uzagrolizing
d: Nodir Otajonov, former chairman of the board of Uzagrolizing, the Uzbek state company that leases farm machinery to farmers, was sentenced to six years over the import of used Chinese cotton harvesters presented as new. According to the court document reviewed by Kun.uz, in spring 2024 he approached Xinjiang Boshiran Intelligent Agricultural Machinery and proposed refitting 100 cheap used three-row harvesters to look like new two-row models priced at $80,000 each, agreeing orally on a 15 per cent share; he received $1.18 million for securing the $8 million order. Unable to import directly, he brought in Khaydar Abdushukurov, founder of Inter Agromash, whose company offered the state firm 100 new combines on 5 July 2024. Abdushukurov was also convicted.
inside: A Chinese manufacturer and a local importer reached the state leasing company through its chairman, who took $1.18 million so it bought their refitted machines as new.
cite: Kun.uz, 19 September 2026, citing the court document

n: Uzbekneftegaz chiefs charged with Enter Engineering and Eriell men
rank: chairman, deputy chairman and procurement head of Uzbekneftegaz
d: Prosecutors in Uzbekistan charged the former chairman of Uzbekneftegaz, the state oil and gas company, along with representatives of two large private contractors in the country's energy industry. The defendants include Bakhodir Siddiqov, who led the company from March 2023 to December 2025, his former deputy Bakhtiyor Anarkulov, the head of the company's procurement department Dilmurod Burkhanov, Ulugbek Usmonov of Enter Engineering and Nodirjon Boboev of Eriell Management. The charges are large-scale embezzlement, abuse of official authority, official forgery and laundering. The case went to the Yashnabad district criminal court in Tashkent in July 2026; reports in November 2026 put the number of defendants at 25. No particular contract has been identified publicly, and the allegations have not been proven.
inside: The charges place two energy contractors' representatives inside the state oil company's procurement alongside its chairman and purchasing head; prosecutors' allegations have not been proven.
cite: Intellinews, 23 July 2026; Anhor.uz, 4 November, citing Gazeta.uz and court data

n: Agency annulled Uzbekistan Airports camera tender over affiliated bidders
rank: procurement commission of Uzbekistan Airports
d: Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency found that Uzbekistan Airports, the state company that runs the country's airports, had carried out a public procurement worth 6.8 billion sums in breach of legal requirements. The tender covered the supply, installation and commissioning of body cameras. The Agency said the bids were not fully and objectively evaluated against the criteria in the tender documents, that people with mutual affiliations, meaning interconnections and conflicts of interest, took part in the process, and that several errors were made during evaluation. After the Agency's submission, the procurement commission's decision naming the winning bidder was annulled, and the documents gathered during the inquiry were sent to law enforcement agencies. The announcement, dated 23 August 2025, named no bidder and no official.
inside: People with undisclosed links to bidders took part in a state airport company's tender, and the winner it chose was annulled once the anti-corruption agency intervened.
cite: Kun.uz, 23 August 2025, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency

n: Customers paid Samarkand state power staff to drop electricity violations
org_label: private electricity customers in Kattakurgan district
rank: staff of the Qoradaryo electricity supply company
d: Seven employees of the state electricity and gas supply companies in Samarkand region, Uzbekistan, were put in preventive detention for corruption at a meeting on 14 February 2025 attended by the deputy prosecutor general, Sh. Aminov. The next day the Kattakurgan district court ordered preventive detention for four employees of the Qoradaryo electricity supply company, named by initials only. Prosecutors allege that an inspector, a supervisor and an engineer acted together to settle a violation report against a resident of the Valijon neighbourhood for breaking electricity-use rules, in exchange for 7 million sums and $200, and that a company lawyer asked another resident, whose illegal grid connection had created a debt of 27 million sums, for 2.7 million sums. The allegations are not established.
inside: Customers' payments allegedly reached the staff who recorded their meter offences, so a state supply company's enforcement decisions were settled for the people paying.
cite: Kun.uz, 17 February 2025, citing the Ministry of Energy and the Kattakurgan district court

n: Rolls-Royce's US arm paid $7.8m for SOCAR turbine orders
rank: SOCAR, the state oil and gas company
d: Rolls-Royce's American affiliate Rolls-Royce Energy Systems paid more than $7.8 million through an intermediary, between 2000 and 2009, to win large turbine orders from SOCAR, Azerbaijan's state oil and gas company. The payments were part of a $170 million settlement with the United States government, reported in December 2016, covering bribery in six countries under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. The Justice Department took the case because an American company was involved and because it considered SOCAR government-controlled and performing government functions. US prosecutors put the affiliate's profits from Azerbaijani turbine deals at over $50 million, which included a 120 million euro service contract covering 28 turbines in 2007. SOCAR had not answered questions when the report was published, and no SOCAR official was named.
inside: A turbine maker's payments through an intermediary bought orders from the state oil company, so SOCAR's equipment purchasing served the supplier paying for it.
cite: Meydan TV, 2018, on the US Department of Justice settlement; Baku Research Institute survey

n: Bombardier tried over Azerbaijan Railways signalling deal, staff acquitted
rank: a mid-ranking official of Azerbaijan Railways
d: Swedish prosecutors alleged that Bombardier Transportation won a $340 million signalling systems contract from Azerbaijan Railways in 2013 by bribing at least one mid-ranking railway official, who also represented the local partner Trans-Signal-Rabita, and that the two sides rigged the tender specifications. Prosecutors treated the roughly $100 million that Trans-Signal-Rabita was expected to receive from the deal as the bribe. The Stockholm district court acquitted Thomas Bimer, a former business area manager at Bombardier Transportation AB, finding that prosecutors could not prove beyond reasonable doubt that the benefit was improper and that there could have been legitimate reasons to use a local partner. Swedish prosecutors appealed the acquittal of another Bombardier employee, Evgeny Pavlov, on 25 October 2017.
inside: Prosecutors said a train maker reached the state railway through an official who also sat on its local partner, so the tender was written to suit them; the court acquitted.
cite: OCCRP on the Stockholm acquittal; Manufacturing.net, 25 October 2017, on the appeal

n: Austrian banknote printer's kickbacks on Azerbaijan's manat orders
rank: Central Bank of Azerbaijan, banknote printing orders
d: Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicherheitsdruck (OeBS), the Austrian National Bank's banknote printing subsidiary, overcharged its contracts with Azerbaijan by 20 per cent and with Syria by 14 per cent, and the kickbacks went to local decision makers. On 3 October 2014 a Vienna court convicted seven defendants and acquitted two, among them the former OeBS chairman Wolfgang Duchatczek, for lack of clear evidence. The former executive director Johannes Miller, who confessed, and another manager were each given two years' probation and fines of 800,000 euros; two lawyers who moved the money were also convicted. A Baku Research Institute survey records the affair as the raising of the price of printing new manat notes, treated as a commission, and names the Central Bank of Azerbaijan's then chairman Elman Rustamov.
inside: A state printing firm's kickbacks on manat banknote orders went to decision makers on the Azerbaijani side, so the central bank paid a fifth more than the work was priced at.
cite: CoinsWeekly on the 3 October 2014 Vienna verdicts; Baku Research Institute survey of corruption cases

n: CBI: KEC International executive paid a Power Grid senior general manager
rank: senior general manager, Power Grid Ajmer
d: Power Grid Corporation of India is the state-owned company that runs the national electricity transmission grid. On 20 March 2025 the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) says it caught Uday Kumar, a senior general manager posted at Ajmer, taking 2.4 lakh rupees at Sikar in Rajasthan from Suman Singh, an executive of the Mumbai contractor KEC International. The CBI alleges the money was to get KEC's contract bills cleared smoothly. Its first information report also names KEC's vice-president for northern transmission and distribution, Jabraj Singh, a finance manager and another employee. Premises were searched at Sikar, Jaipur and Mohali. The investigation continues; KEC had issued no response when the arrest was reported.
inside: A transmission contractor's executive paid the Power Grid manager who processed its bills, so a state grid company's payment decisions, prosecutors allege, served the supplier.
cite: Free Press Journal (PTI), 21 March 2025

n: CBI: Tata Projects staff paid a Power Grid executive director over grid bills
rank: executive director, Power Grid Corporation of India
d: Power Grid Corporation of India is the state-owned operator of the country's electricity transmission grid. In July 2022 the CBI arrested Bimlendu Shekhar Jha, an executive director posted at Itanagar, with five Tata Projects employees: executive vice-president Desh Raj Pathak, assistant vice-president R N Singh, regional project manager Nafeez Hussain Khan and two junior staff. The CBI alleges Jha took illegal gratification from the company and favoured it by preparing inflated bills, clearing bills early and allowing price variation clause benefits on contracts under the World Bank-funded North Eastern Region Power System Improvement Project in Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim. More than 93 lakh rupees was recovered from Jha's home. All six were remanded to custody until 15 July 2022. Tata Projects said it had zero tolerance for compromise.
inside: A large construction contractor's executives allegedly paid the Power Grid director who approved their bills, so the state grid company's payments and price adjustments served the firm.
cite: The Tribune (India), 7 July 2022

n: CBI: Delhi municipal engineers took 10 lakh rupees from a contractor
rank: junior and executive engineers, MCD Najafgarh zone
d: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is the city's elected civic body, responsible for roads, drains and sanitation. On 11 November 2025 the CBI laid a trap and caught Ajay Babbarwal, a junior engineer in the corporation's Najafgarh zone, allegedly accepting 10 lakh rupees from a contractor whose bills were pending. The CBI says Babbarwal, executive engineer R C Sharma and assistant engineer Navin Kaul together sought 25.42 lakh rupees to clear bills worth about 3 crore rupees. All three were named in the first information report, and the CBI searched their premises and says it recovered cash, jewellery and property papers. The contractor is identified only as the complainant. The matter is under investigation.
inside: A municipal contractor's money allegedly reached the engineers who certify his bills, so the corporation's payment decisions turned on what he paid them.
cite: Deccan Herald (PTI), 13 November 2025

n: Maharashtra ACB: CIDCO estate officer took 2 lakh over a Sanpada flat transfer
org_label: a Navi Mumbai society transfer agent
rank: assistant estate officer, CIDCO
d: The City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) is the Maharashtra state company that built and administers Navi Mumbai, and its estate office approves transfers of the flats it allotted. A contractor who handles housing society registrations and transfers, holding power of attorney for a flat in Sanpada, applied for a transfer on 11 June 2025 and says the file then stalled. He complained to the state Anti-Corruption Bureau on 22 January 2026. The bureau says a 57-year-old assistant estate officer first demanded 4 lakh rupees and settled for 2 lakh, and that an associate was caught taking the money at a hotel near Nerul station. Both were arrested and booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act; neither has been named.
inside: An outside transfer agent's 2 lakh rupees allegedly bought the CIDCO estate officer's signature, so a state housing company's transfer decision served whoever paid for it.
cite: ThePrint (PTI), 29 January 2026

n: Maharashtra ACB: MHADA engineer took 40,000 to drop action on a row house
rank: assistant engineer, MHADA Bandra office
d: The Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) is the state body that builds and regulates public housing, and it can act against unauthorised use of the homes it oversees. MHADA's Bandra office told a Mumbai man that his wife's row house was being used for paying guests and that action would follow. The state Anti-Corruption Bureau says Ranjit Chavan, an assistant engineer at that office, demanded 4 lakh rupees to drop the action, agreed to 2 lakh in instalments, and was caught red-handed in October 2025 taking 40,000 rupees of it. A case was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The bureau's account is an allegation, and no later outcome was reported.
inside: A property owner facing enforcement allegedly paid the state housing authority's own engineer, so the decision whether to act on his house turned on the money.
cite: Free Press Journal, 10 October 2025

n: CBI: Megha Engineering paid NMDC officers to clear Bastar steel plant bills
rank: NMDC directors and finance officers
d: NMDC is India's state-owned iron ore miner, and it built an integrated steel plant at Nagarnar in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. In April 2024 the CBI registered cases alleging that the Hyderabad contractor Megha Engineering and Infrastructure (MEIL) offered 78 lakh rupees in bribes to NMDC officers and others to get bills cleared under a 314 crore rupee construction contract, and that the officers received 73.85 lakh rupees. NMDC had paid MEIL 174 crore rupees against 73 invoices. Those booked include retired executive director Prashant Dash, production director Dilip Kumar Mohanty, finance officers L Krishna Mohan and K Rajshekar, three Nagarnar Ispat staff, two MECON officers and MEIL general manager Subash Chandra Sangras. The charges include conspiracy, forgery and bribery.
inside: A large infrastructure contractor's money allegedly reached NMDC's own directors and finance officers, so the state miner's payments on its steel plant contract served the builder.
cite: Deccan Chronicle, 13 April 2024

n: CBI: Indian Oil managers in Nagpur sought 1 lakh over a petrol outlet transfer
rank: general manager and chief manager, retail sales, IOCL Nagpur
d: Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) is India's largest state-owned oil refiner and fuel retailer, and it must sign off when a petrol station's dealership changes hands. In March 2022 the CBI booked N P Rodge, general manager for retail sales at IOCL Nagpur, alleging he demanded 1 lakh rupees to execute an agreement transferring ownership of a retail outlet, and directed the complainant to pay chief manager Manish Nandle. The CBI says it set a trap and caught Nandle demanding and accepting the money. Officers searched the two men's offices and homes. The complainant, who sought the outlet transfer, was not named, and the investigation was continuing when the case was reported.
inside: An outsider seeking a fuel dealership allegedly paid the state refiner's own retail sales managers, so IOCL's decision on who held the outlet turned on the payment.
cite: ThePrint (PTI), 25 March 2022

n: CBI: Indian Oil sales officer in Gondia sought 1 lakh from a pump dealer
rank: sales officer, IOCL Gondia
d: Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) is the state-owned refiner that supplies the petrol pumps carrying its brand, and its sales officers control the flow of stock to them. In March 2022 the CBI said Sunil Golar, a sales officer at IOCL's Gondia office in Maharashtra, demanded 1 lakh rupees from a dealer so that his pump would run smoothly without the company delaying its stock supply, and in return for earlier favours. The CBI laid a trap and caught Golar demanding and accepting the money, then searched his office and home. The dealer was not named. The case was still under investigation when it was reported, and the allegations have not been tested in court.
inside: A fuel dealer allegedly paid the state refiner's own sales officer, so IOCL's decisions on supplying his pump served him rather than the company's rules.
cite: ThePrint (PTI), 25 March 2022

n: CBI: cargo handlers paid Paradip Port's chief mechanical engineer
rank: chief mechanical engineer, Paradip Port Trust
d: Paradip in Odisha is a state-owned major port. In August 2022 the CBI arrested its chief mechanical engineer, Saroj Kumar Das, his aide Sumanta Rout, Sankha Subhra Mitra, a port operations manager with the KCT Group, and Surya Narayan Sahoo, an operations deputy general manager at Orissa Stevedores. The CBI alleges Rout collected bribes from cargo companies for Das, and that 60 lakh rupees was demanded, of which 25 lakh was collected at Cuttack; Rout kept 10 lakh and passed 10 lakh to a Bhubaneswar developer with whom Das had booked a property. The alleged favour was having a conveyor belt damaged by a private firm while unloading cargo repaired at the port's expense. About 84.5 lakh rupees in cash was recovered across 15 searches.
inside: Cargo handling firms allegedly paid the port's own chief engineer through a middleman, so the state port carried repair costs their work had caused.
cite: Deccan Chronicle (PTI), 5 August 2022

n: CBI: a Delhi medicine supplier paid ESIC doctors 1 crore for a rate contract
rank: ESIC medical officers, Delhi
d: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) runs India's hospitals and dispensaries for insured workers, and buys medicines through a Central Rate Contract. In May 2019 the CBI booked two ESIC medical officers, Vikas Gupta and Kajal Goldar, alleging that Basant Goel, a Delhi medicine supplier linked to the empanelled chemist Goel Medicos, paid them about 1 crore rupees in instalments during 2016-17 to secure a place in that contract by being appointed agent of a reputed manufacturer during the tender. The alleged payments were 38 lakh rupees into Gupta's account, 10 lakh into his wife's and 52 lakh in cash for Goldar. ESIC's own vigilance inquiry confirmed 48 lakh rupees reaching Gupta and his wife.
inside: A medicine supplier's money allegedly reached two ESIC medical officers, so the state insurer's rate contract for drugs and dressings was shaped to admit his business.
cite: Medical Dialogues, 4 May 2019

n: CBI: device suppliers paid cardiologists at Delhi's RML Hospital
org_label: Nagpal Technologies, Scienmed, Biotronics and Bharati Medical Technology
rank: cardiologists and technical staff, RML Hospital
d: Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital is a large central government hospital in New Delhi. On 8 May 2024 the CBI registered a case naming eleven people, including two cardiologists, hospital staff, supplier representatives and their firms, and arrested nine. The first information report alleges that Dr Parvathagouda Channappagouda sought payments totalling about 2.48 lakh rupees for permitting the use of implant devices and promoting equipment, from Nagpal Technologies, from Scienmed, which allegedly transferred 1,95,000 rupees to his father's account, and from Biotronics. It alleges Dr Ajay Raj demanded 25,000 and then 35,000 rupees from Bharati Medical Technology for promoting equipment, and that a senior technical in-charge sought 1 lakh rupees from Scienmed. A special court remanded the nine to CBI custody.
inside: Device and equipment suppliers allegedly paid the hospital's own cardiologists and technical staff, so which implants went into public patients followed the payments.
cite: The Tribune (India), 9 May 2024

n: CBI: a railway contractor's 32 lakh rupees reached a chief engineer's family
org_label: a South East Central Railway works contractor
rank: chief engineer, South East Central Railway
d: South East Central Railway at Bilaspur is a zone of Indian Railways, the state-owned rail operator, and its construction wing awards work on bridges, road over- and under-bridges, capacity enhancement and track lining. On 25 April 2025 the CBI laid a trap and caught the zone's chief engineer after a relative accepted about 32 lakh rupees at Ranchi, the officer's native town. The CBI alleges the money came from the managing director of a private firm holding such work orders, delivered through an employee, to favour the firm in contracts and to settle pending matters in its favour. Four people were held, including the managing director. Neither the officer nor the firm was named, and the investigation continues.
inside: A works contractor's managing director allegedly routed 32 lakh rupees to the railway chief engineer's relative, so the zone's contract decisions served the firm.
cite: Free Press Journal, 25 April 2025

n: CBI: an advertising firm paid an NTPC manager 8 lakh to pass a 40 lakh bill
rank: senior manager, corporate communications, NTPC
d: NTPC is India's largest state-owned electricity generator. In May 2024 the CBI arrested a senior manager in its corporate communications department at New Delhi after a trap. The complainant, a vice-president of an advertising company whose booths had been installed in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Pondicherry for NTPC in January and February 2024, said the manager refused a proforma invoice of about 40 lakh rupees because a work completion certificate was missing, and said he would get the bill passed if he were paid. The CBI says he first sought 6 lakh rupees, raised the demand to 9.25 lakh, and took 8 lakh, flying to Mumbai for the handover. His premises at Noida were searched.
inside: An advertising contractor paid the NTPC manager who controlled its invoice, so a state power company's payment went through on the strength of 8 lakh rupees.
cite: Free Press Journal (PTI), 3 May 2024

n: Maharashtra ACB: BMC engineer took 3 lakh to approve a Mumbai toilet project
rank: assistant engineer, Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
d: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is India's richest civic body and approves the public toilets built under its 'Pay and Use' scheme. A contractor of 25 years' standing complained to the state Anti-Corruption Bureau on 29 November that Ranjan Bagwe, an assistant engineer, had demanded 10 lakh rupees in October 2024 to approve a toilet near Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Road and Reay Road station in E Ward, later reducing the demand to 6 lakh. The bureau says Bagwe was arrested in his office cabin after accepting 3 lakh rupees as a first instalment. The case was reported on 10 December 2024 and the report gives no later outcome.
inside: A civic contractor's 3 lakh rupees allegedly bought the BMC engineer's approval, so whether a public toilet project went ahead turned on the payment.
cite: Free Press Journal, 10 December 2024

n: Telangana ACB: GHMC engineer took 15 lakh to process a contractor's bill
rank: superintending engineer, Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation
d: The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) is the city's civic body and pays the contractors who build its works. On 4 February 2026 the Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau said it had caught P Chinna Reddy, a superintending engineer in GHMC's Kukatpally zone, and a computer operator, B Praveen Kumar, who took the money on his behalf, accepting 15 lakh rupees from a contractor. The bureau says the payment was sought for verifying the works and processing the contractor's bill of 1.40 crore rupees. Both men were arrested and produced before the Anti-Corruption Bureau court in Hyderabad. The contractor, who complained to the bureau, was not named, and no later outcome was reported.
