inside: A contractor's 15 lakh rupees allegedly reached the municipal engineer who verifies his work, so the corporation's own check on the job served the man being checked.
cite: Telangana Today, 4 February 2026

n: Karnataka ACB: a BBMP corporator and engineers took 15 lakh over a bill
rank: corporator and engineers, Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike
d: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) is Bengaluru's municipal corporation. In March 2017 Karnataka's Anti-Corruption Bureau acted on a complaint by a civil contractor who had renovated the regional transport office at Rajajinagar and whose bill of 2.74 crore rupees had been pending about eighteen months. The bureau says corporator Krishnamurthy, assistant engineer Krishna and assistant executive engineer Arun Kumar first demanded 38.5 lakh rupees to release the bill, then settled on 15 lakh, split 10 lakh for the corporator and 5 lakh for the engineers. Krishnamurthy was caught taking 10 lakh at his house and Krishna 5 lakh; Arun Kumar was arrested later. The report records the arrests only.
inside: A civil contractor's 15 lakh rupees was allegedly split between a BBMP corporator and its engineers, so the corporation released his pending bill.
cite: Deccan Herald, 31 March 2017

n: CBI: a Singrauli middleman's 5 lakh rupees went to the CBI's own Jabalpur DSP
rank: deputy superintendent of police, CBI anti-corruption branch, Jabalpur
d: Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) is a state-owned coal producer at Singrauli in Madhya Pradesh. In August 2024 the CBI arrested five people, including Joy Joseph Damle, a deputy superintendent of police in its own anti-corruption branch at Jabalpur, alleging that 5 lakh rupees was being delivered to him to secure a favourable report on complaints and investigations the CBI was conducting against the payers. The CBI says Ravi Shankar Singh, a director of Sangam Engineering at Singrauli, acted as a conduit between contractors, businessmen and NCL officials, that an associate was arrested while delivering the money, and that an NCL chief manager of administration provided it. All five were produced before a special court at Jabalpur.
inside: A contractors' middleman allegedly paid the CBI officer investigating them, so the agency's own report on coal company contracts was to be written to suit the payers.
cite: ThePrint (PTI), 19 August 2024

n: CBI: a signalling joint venture paid for a 7 crore rupee railway bonus
rank: senior section engineer, South Central Railway signal projects
d: South Central Railway is a zone of Indian Railways, the state-owned rail operator. On 16 August 2026 the CBI arrested a senior section engineer in the office of its chief signal and telecommunications engineer (projects) at Vijayawada, with a private person reported to be the son of a company managing director. The CBI alleges 15 lakh rupees was paid to sanction and release a bonus of about 7 crore rupees to a joint venture of two private firms for automatic block signalling work said to have been finished ahead of schedule under a 179.50 crore rupee contract, and that dates in the bonus file were altered to favour the venture. A case was registered against the engineer, four company representatives and unidentified others.
inside: A signalling joint venture allegedly paid the railway engineer handling its bonus file, so the state operator's own records were altered to pay out 7 crore rupees.
cite: Deccan Chronicle, 16 August 2026

n: MP Lokayukta: West Discom engineer took a bribe for a godown power connection
rank: junior engineer, Madhya Pradesh West Discom
d: West Discom, formally the Madhya Pradesh Paschim Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company, is the state-owned electricity distributor for western Madhya Pradesh. In August 2025 the Lokayukta Special Establishment police at Indore said they had caught a junior engineer of the company red-handed taking a 10,000 rupee bribe from Suryakant Sonone, an Indore resident who needed a 10-kilowatt connection for a godown at Naliya Bakhal to run a steam machine business. The engineer, who was not named, had also asked for 40,000 rupees described as government charges. A case was registered under section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act and further investigation was under way.
inside: A business owner paid the state power company's own engineer, so whether his godown got an electricity connection depended on the 10,000 rupees rather than the rules.
cite: Free Press Journal, 8 August 2025

n: CBI: Western Coalfields supervisor took 40,000 of a contractor's bill
rank: senior supervisor (civil), Western Coalfields Umred area
d: Western Coalfields Limited is a state-owned coal producer, a subsidiary of Coal India, with mines around Nagpur. On a written complaint received on 29 September 2026, the CBI's anti-corruption branch says a contractor who had been awarded work was asked for 50,000 rupees, described in the complaint as about two per cent of his bill, to get a payment bill released. Pawan Nakhate, a senior supervisor (civil) at the Gokul Murpar sub-area of the company's Umred area, was arrested on 30 September 2026 after allegedly accepting 40,000 rupees. The contractor was not named, and the report carries the allegations only, with no charges or court proceedings described.
inside: A mine contractor's 40,000 rupees allegedly reached the coal company supervisor who releases his bills, so a state miner's payment decision followed the cut he paid.
cite: United News of India, 30 September 2026

n: CBI: a Meerut broadband contractor paid BSNL's Faridabad general manager
rank: principal general manager, BSNL Faridabad
d: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) is India's state-owned telephone company. In April 2018 the CBI arrested its principal general manager at Faridabad, Adesh Gupta, an assistant general manager, Kamal Mewani, and a junior telecom officer, Shankar Verma. Ashok Kumar Tomar, a Meerut businessman given work to install and maintain new broadband connections through the general manager's office, said Gupta demanded 51,000 rupees to pass his bills and agreed to 45,000. The CBI says Mewani accepted the money and handed it to Gupta. Tomar had submitted 32 bills totalling 7,99,877 rupees. Searches of Gupta's home turned up about 42.68 lakh rupees in cash, insurance policies of about 1.5 crore rupees and property papers.
inside: A broadband contractor paid BSNL's own general manager to pass his bills, so the state telephone company's payments to him turned on 45,000 rupees.
cite: The Tribune (India), 21 April 2018

n: CBI: a Jabalpur firm paid BSNL's Bhopal chief engineer 1.5 lakh over its bills
rank: chief engineer (electrical), BSNL Bhopal
d: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) is India's state-owned telephone company. On 27 August 2026 the CBI registered a case and the same day trapped Awanish Kumar Shukla, chief engineer (electrical) at BSNL Bhopal, and V B Chakrapani, a superintending engineer. The CBI alleges the two demanded 4 lakh rupees from a Jabalpur firm that carried out operation and comprehensive maintenance and electrical installation work for BSNL, to process its pending bills for fourteen different works, and were caught accepting 75,000 rupees each, 1.5 lakh in total. Both were arrested, and searches followed at their premises in Bhopal, Lucknow and Kanpur. The firm was not named and the allegations have not been tested in court.
inside: A maintenance contractor allegedly paid BSNL's own chief and superintending engineers, so the state telephone company's bills for fourteen jobs moved for 1.5 lakh rupees.
cite: Free Press Journal, 28 August 2026

n: CBI: New India Assurance manager took a tenth of a 1 lakh accident claim
rank: senior branch manager, New India Assurance Sivasagar
d: New India Assurance is a state-owned general insurer. In March 2018 the CBI arrested Debabrata Rakshit, senior branch manager of its Sivasagar branch in Assam, after a trap at the branch office at KP Chariali. Parikshit Baruah, a customer whose commercially registered vehicle had been in an accident, complained that Rakshit sought a payment to process his claim. The CBI says 10,000 rupees was taken, which the report describes as ten per cent of the 1 lakh rupee claim. Rakshit was caught red-handed and was to be produced before the CBI special court at Guwahati the next day. The report gives no later outcome.
inside: A policyholder paid the state insurer's own branch manager, so whether his accident claim was processed depended on a tenth of the claim going to the manager.
cite: North East Now, 31 March 2018

n: CBI: a railway contractor paid West Central Railway's deputy chief engineer
rank: deputy chief engineer (construction), West Central Railway
d: West Central Railway is a zone of Indian Railways, the state-owned rail operator, with headquarters at Jabalpur. The CBI registered a case on 4 June 2026 and arrested Narayan Singh Bundela, deputy chief engineer (construction), the same night after a trap at a hotel in Sagar. The CBI says a contractor paid him 1 lakh rupees to release his security deposit, pending bills and price variation clause dues of nearly 1 crore rupees for completed contract work. Investigators also found 62,000 rupees in unaccounted cash in his guest house room, and documents on real estate investments at his home. Bundela, posted at Bhopal, was taken to Jabalpur for court. The CBI is checking whether similar demands were made in other railway contracts.
inside: A railway contractor paid the deputy chief engineer who held his deposit and dues, so the state operator released nearly 1 crore rupees owed to him for 1 lakh.
cite: The Hitavada, 6 June 2026

n: CBI: a Bhopal construction firm paid NHAI project directors 20 lakh rupees
rank: general manager and project directors, National Highways Authority of India
d: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is the state body that builds and pays for the national road network through project implementation units. In March 2024 the CBI arrested six people: a general manager and project director at the NHAI unit in Nagpur, a deputy general manager and project director at NHAI Harda in Madhya Pradesh, and two directors and two employees of a Bhopal construction company. The CBI says it expected a 25 lakh rupee payment and that 20 lakh was delivered, allegedly for completion certificates, processed bills and keeping awarded road works moving, including pending bills and a completion certificate on an Outer Ring Road project. About 1.10 crore rupees in cash was recovered. None was named.
inside: A road contractor's directors allegedly paid NHAI's own project directors through employees, so the authority's completion certificates and payments followed the firm's money.
cite: Free Press Journal, 4 March 2024

n: Maharashtra ACB: a developer paid CIDCO staff to spare a Navi Mumbai building
org_label: a Thane and Navi Mumbai land developer
rank: development officer and surveyor, CIDCO
d: The City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) is the Maharashtra state company that built Navi Mumbai, and its controller of unauthorised construction can order buildings demolished. On 10 June 2019 the state Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested CIDCO development officer Pritamsingh Rajput, 39, surveyor Vikas Khadse, 52, and Pradip Patil, a waiter at a CIDCO canteen who took the money for them. A real estate businessman who buys and develops land in Thane and Navi Mumbai complained that the officials demanded 10 lakh rupees, reduced to 8 lakh in instalments, so that a 2,178 square foot structure built by his associate would not be demolished. Patil was caught taking the first instalment of 2.50 lakh rupees.
inside: A developer allegedly paid the CIDCO officers who police unauthorised building, so a state housing company's demolition decision turned on 8 lakh rupees in instalments.
cite: Housing.com News (PTI), 11 June 2019

n: CBI: a Reliance consultant paid a DGCA deputy director general over drone files
org_label: Reliance Industries consultant and Asteria Aerospace
rank: deputy director general, Directorate General of Civil Aviation
d: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is India's aviation regulator and clears drone imports. In April 2026 the CBI arrested Mudavath Devula, a DGCA deputy director general, and Bharat Mathur, described as a senior vice-president at Reliance Industries and by Reliance as an engaged consultant. The applications concerned Asteria Aerospace, a subsidiary of Reliance's Jio Platforms. The CBI seized 2.5 lakh rupees at the handover near the IIT Delhi flyover on 18 April and says the first information report puts the bribe at 5 lakh rupees per application file, for three pending drone import approvals. Searches recovered 37 lakh rupees in cash, gold and silver. Reliance said it was unaware of any such transaction and had not authorised one.
inside: A consultant acting for a Reliance subsidiary allegedly paid the regulator's deputy director general, so the DGCA's drone import approvals were to be cleared for the firm.
cite: Outlook Business, 20 April 2026

n: Lintasarta paid Indonesia's informatics director-general Rp6.5bn for contracts
rank: Director General of Informatics Applications, Ministry of Communication and Informatics
d: Lintasarta, a private telecoms and data-centre firm, paid the civil servant who decided who built Indonesia's temporary national data centre. On 10 March 2026 the Jakarta corruption court found Semuel Abrijani Pangerapan, Director General of Informatics Applications at the communications ministry from 2016 to 2024, guilty of taking a Rp6.5 billion bribe from Lintasarta's business director Alfi Asman as a reward for appointing the company to several projects. He was given six years, a Rp500 million fine and a Rp6.5 billion restitution order. Alfi Asman got six years, a ministry director nine years, and a Dokotel Teknologi account manager six years. The court put the state's loss at Rp140.86 billion.
cite: ANTARA, 10 March 2026 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict)
inside: A data-centre contractor paid the official who awarded its contracts, so the ministry's procurement of the national data centre served the company that paid.

n: A convicted man's lawyer paid Surabaya court's chief to pick his judges
org_label: Lisa Rachmat (defence lawyer for Ronald Tannur)
rank: Chief judge of Surabaya District Court
d: A defendant's own lawyer bought the choice of the judges who would try him. On 22 August 2025 the Jakarta corruption court sentenced Rudi Suparmono, former chief judge of the Surabaya District Court and in 2024 chief judge of the Central Jakarta District Court, to seven years and a Rp750 million fine. Prosecutors said Lisa Rachmat, defence lawyer for Ronald Tannur, paid him 43,000 Singapore dollars, about Rp541.8 million, and that he then appointed the three judges she asked for. He was also charged with taking gratuities of about Rp21.85 billion while holding those two posts. The sentence matched the prosecution's demand.
cite: ANTARA Megapolitan, 22 August 2025 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict)
inside: A litigant's lawyer paid the judge who ran the court, so the panel that decided her client's case was the one she had chosen.

n: A failing gas distributor got PGN's directors to prepay it for gas
rank: commercial director and president director, PT Perusahaan Gas Negara
d: PT Inti Alasindo Energy, an East Java gas distributor in financial difficulty, obtained an advance-payment arrangement from Indonesia's state gas company PGN. On 12 January 2026 the Jakarta corruption court convicted PGN's commercial director for 2016 to 2019, Danny Praditya, of joint corruption over gas sale-and-purchase deals between 2017 and 2021, giving him six years and a Rp250 million fine; it found he received none of the money, and put the loss at US$15 million, about Rp246 billion. Inti Alasindo's former commissioner Iswan Ibrahim was tried with him. On 20 August 2026 the same court convicted PGN's president director for 2008 to 2017, Hendi Prio Santoso, and ordered him to repay 500,000 Singapore dollars.
cite: Katadata, 12 January 2026; EmitenNews, 20 August 2026 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdicts)
inside: A private gas buyer in trouble reached the state gas company through its own directors, and PGN's payment terms were rewritten to carry it.

n: A safety contractor paid Indonesia's manpower ministry Rp4.7bn for certificates
rank: officials of the Ministry of Manpower
d: A company paid officials of Indonesia's manpower ministry to get occupational safety and health certificates, known as K3, issued for its clients. On 4 June 2026 the Jakarta corruption court convicted two businessmen of PT KEM, Temurila and Miki Mahfud, of joint corruption and gave each 18 months and a Rp200 million fine. The court found they paid Rp4,786,460,000, about Rp4.7 billion, described in the case as 'non-technical' money, and that it did not come back to them or to PT KEM. The judge said they had admitted knowing of the practice at a previous company and continued it. The article does not name the officials who took the money.
cite: Detik, 4 June 2026 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict)
inside: A contractor paid staff of the ministry that issues workplace safety certificates, so the ministry's certification decisions followed the money.

n: Blueray Cargo's owner and staff paid Indonesian customs officials over imports
rank: officials of the Directorate General of Customs and Excise
d: A freight forwarder paid officials of Indonesia's customs service over the importing of goods. On 17 July 2026 the Jakarta corruption court sentenced Blueray Cargo's owner John Field to two years, its operations manager Deddy Kurniawan Sukolo to 18 months and the head of its document team, Andri, to 18 months, for bribing officials of the Directorate General of Customs and Excise. The Corruption Eradication Commission, which brought the case, said it accepted the verdicts. The report does not name the customs office or the officials who took the money, give the amounts, or say whether any customs officer has been convicted.
cite: RCTI+, 17 July 2026 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict; KPK statement)
inside: A freight company paid customs officials so that the service deciding what entered the country was working for the importer's agent.

n: A tax consultant's money reached Indonesia's tax examination director
rank: Director of Examination and Collection, Directorate General of Taxes
d: Money from outside the tax office reached the officials who ran Indonesia's tax audits. On 4 February 2022 the Jakarta corruption court convicted Angin Prayitno Aji, Director of Examination and Collection at the Directorate General of Taxes from 2016 to 2019, and Dadan Ramdani, head of its sub-directorate for cooperation and examination support, of joint and continuing corruption. Angin was given nine years, Dadan six, each with a Rp300 million fine, and each was ordered to repay Rp3.375 billion and 1.095 million Singapore dollars. The page records that the judge identified tax consultant Agus Susetyo as the person who began the payments; it does not name the companies that paid.
cite: Hukumonline, 4 February 2022 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict)
inside: Consultants acting for taxpayers paid the officials who set and checked tax bills, so audit decisions inside the tax directorate served their clients.

n: Cart suppliers paid Indonesia's trade ministry finance chief to win a tender
org_label: PT Piramida Dimensi Milenia and its associates
rank: Head of the Finance Section, Directorate General of Domestic Trade, Ministry of Trade
d: Suppliers of market carts were steered a trade ministry tender by the official who held its purse strings. Putu Indra Wijaya, head of the finance section at the Ministry of Trade's domestic trade directorate, met prospective bidders Bambang Widianto and Mashur, asked them for Rp835 million and promised they would win the 2018 contract for 7,200 small-trader carts worth Rp54 billion. He then steered the award to PT Piramida Dimensi Milenia, which the court said lacked the required qualifications. The reported loss was about Rp17 billion. The Supreme Court raised his sentence to ten years on 9 December 2024, with restitution of Rp16,935,000,000. The report does not confirm how much he actually received.
cite: Dandapala (Supreme Court), 2 January 2025, on cassation decision of 9 December 2024
inside: Bidders' money reached the ministry official who controlled the tender, and the contract went to a firm the court said was not qualified.

n: A contractor paid Langkat's regent a 15.5% fee for district works
rank: Regent of Langkat, North Sumatra
d: A small contractor bought work packages from the head of a North Sumatran district by paying a percentage of each contract. On 20 June 2022 the Jakarta corruption court sentenced Muara Perangin Angin, director of CV Nizhami, to two years and six months and a Rp200 million fine for bribing the suspended Langkat regent, Terbit Rencana Perangin Angin. The court found a commitment fee was set at 16.5 per cent of contract value and negotiated down to 15.5 per cent, giving Rp572,221,414 handed over in black plastic on 18 January 2022 through four of the regent's associates. Muara had obtained road, embankment and school jobs by direct appointment. The article does not report the regent's own verdict.
cite: ANTARA Sumut, 20 June 2022 (Jakarta Corruption Court verdict; KPK)
inside: A contractor's percentage payments reached the elected head of the district, and the district's public works and school contracts were handed to him without tender.

n: A tax consultant and a mining firm are accused of paying a Jakarta tax office
org_label: tax consultant Abdul Kadim Sahbudin and PT Wanatiara Persada staff
who: a tax consultant and a company's staff
rank: head of the North Jakarta medium taxpayers' office, Directorate General of Taxes
d: The Corruption Eradication Commission says money from outside reached the tax office that examines larger Jakarta taxpayers. On 18 February 2026 it said five people were suspects over bribery linked to tax examinations at the Directorate General of Taxes: as alleged recipients, Dwi Budi, head of the North Jakarta medium taxpayers' office, his supervision and consultation section head Agus Syaifudin, and an assessment team member, Askob Bahtiar; as alleged payers, tax consultant Abdul Kadim Sahbudin and Edy Yulianto, a staff member of PT Wanatiara Persada. The commission was still questioning witnesses to complete the file. The report gives no amounts and names no specific tax decision.
cite: Metro TV (medcom.id), 18 February 2026 (KPK statement)
inside: A consultant and a company employee are accused of paying the officials who examine their tax, so the tax office's audits would go their way.

n: A miner paid East Kalimantan's governor and energy office for six licences
rank: Governor of East Kalimantan; head of the provincial energy and mineral resources office
d: A mining businessman paid to have six of his mining permits extended by East Kalimantan's provincial government. On 30 January 2026 the corruption court in Samarinda convicted Rudy Ong Chandra and sentenced him to two years and four months with a Rp200 million fine. The case says he prepared Rp3 billion for Amrullah, the former head of the provincial energy and mineral resources office, who was said to have helped with the six permits, and paid Rp3.5 billion, in Singapore dollars, to Dayang Donna Walfiarties Tania, head of the provincial chamber of commerce, acting as intermediary for her father, former governor Awang Faroek Ishak, who has since died.
cite: Metro TV (medcom.id), 30 January 2026 (Samarinda Corruption Court verdict; KPK)
inside: A permit holder's money reached the provincial governor through his daughter and the official who handles mining permits, and six of the firm's licences were pushed through.

n: A finance company's notes were bought by Bank NTT's treasury for Rp50bn
rank: head of the treasury division, later president director, Bank NTT
d: Prosecutors in East Nusa Tenggara say a troubled finance company got the province's own bank to buy its paper. On 9 December 2025 the provincial prosecutor's office named Hari Alexander Riwu Kaho, head of Bank NTT's treasury division in 2018 and later its president director, a suspect, and detained him on 12 December. They say he approved the purchase of Rp50 billion of medium-term notes issued by PT Sunprima Nusantara Pembiayaan on 22 March 2018 without due diligence or the bank's required proposal process, and that the issuer's accounts contained fictitious receivables. SNP is alleged to have paid unofficial fees of 3.5 to 4 per cent into an account presented as a sales agent. It defaulted in 2020.
cite: Detik, 12 December 2025 (Kejati NTT; BPK investigative audit)
inside: A finance company allegedly reached the provincial bank through its treasury chief, and the bank's investment decision put Rp50 billion into the issuer's notes.

n: Roma Energy owner convicted of bribing Pemex and PEP officials for contracts
rank: officials of Pemex and Pemex Exploracion y Produccion
d: Pemex is Mexico's state oil company and Pemex Exploracion y Produccion (PEP) is its exploration and production arm. US prosecutors said Ramon Alexandro Rovirosa Martinez, who runs the Texas firm Roma Energy, and Mario Alberto Avila Lizarraga paid more than $150,000 in cash and luxury goods to at least three Pemex and PEP officials between 2019 and 2021, so that companies linked to Rovirosa would win and keep contracts worth at least $2.5 million. A Houston jury convicted Rovirosa on three counts in December 2025 and acquitted him on a fourth; Avila remains a fugitive. Mexico's anti-corruption secretary said three former Pemex staff were under investigation and five audits reopened.
inside: A contractor paid officials inside the state oil company so its purchasing decisions handed his own firms at least $2.5 million in work.
cite: US Department of Justice via Mexico News Daily, 12 Aug 2025; Animal Politico, 6 Dec 2025; Zeta (Buenrostro announcement), 29 Aug 2025

n: Recordings allege pay-to-play bribery for Pemex contracts under Lozoya
rank: Pemex drilling and exploration directorates
d: Oro Negro, a Mexican oil-services firm, hired the Israeli investigation company Black Cube after Pemex, the state oil company, cancelled its contracts. Two former Mossad agents posed as investors and recorded Jose Carlos Pacheco Ledesma, a former Pemex drilling and services chief, and Luis Sergio Guaso Montoya, a former exploration and production deputy director, at a Mexico City dinner in 2017. El Universal and the Wall Street Journal reviewed the recordings, which describe contractors paying up to US$5 million a contract and up to US$100,000 for a meeting with the Pemex chief, with money routed through companies run by officials' relatives. Pacheco denied discussing bribery; Emilio Lozoya, then Pemex's chief, denied the accusations.
inside: Contractors are recorded describing a going rate for Pemex contracts, paid through officials' relatives, so the state oil firm's awards followed the payments.
cite: Mexico News Daily, 14 Oct 2019, citing El Universal and the Wall Street Journal

n: IMSS bought from Marzam while the owner's father sat on its board
rank: IMSS governing board
d: The IMSS is Mexico's state social-security institute and the country's largest buyer of medicines. Mexicans Against Corruption and Impunity reported in 2019 that the drug distributor Marzam, bought in 2015 by Luis Doporto Alejandre, won IMSS contracts worth more than 526 million pesos between 2015 and 2018, more than five times its IMSS sales from 2002 to 2014, while his father Hector Doporto Ramirez had sat on the IMSS governing board since 2010. The group said federal authorities were investigating Marzam for financial crimes over the same period. Luis Doporto told the group his father was a substitute board member who was never involved in purchasing. No sanction was reported.
inside: A supplier's owner had his father seated on the state institute's governing board while its medicine contracts with that institute grew more than fivefold.
cite: Mexicans Against Corruption and Impunity via Mexico News Daily, 11 Mar 2019, citing El Financiero

n: Two firms paid by Segalmex and Liconsa for milk work they did not do
rank: Segalmex, Liconsa and Diconsa contracts
d: Segalmex was a federal food company created in 2019 to coordinate Liconsa, which supplies milk, and Diconsa, which supplies rural shops. Reporting drawn from the book Licencia para robar says the FGR, Mexico's federal prosecutor, found that Segalmex gave simulated or irregular contracts to Comercializadora de Productos Lacteos de La Laguna (Coprolac), paid about 1,228.4 million pesos, and to Grupo Vicente Suarez 73, a construction firm paid about 488.6 million pesos. Neither is said to have had the experience to fortify and dry the milk, which Liconsa had already delivered, and the powdered milk and cream were not returned. The FGR has named senior Segalmex officials, among them Rene Gavira, as an alleged criminal organisation.
inside: Outside suppliers took Segalmex and Liconsa contracts to process milk they never returned, awarded by the state food company's own senior officials.
cite: La Cronica de Hoy, 25 Sep 2025, drawing on Licencia para robar by Zedryk Raziel and Georgina Zerega

n: Front firm paid 142m pesos for a simulated Diconsa sugar purchase
rank: Diconsa purchasing
d: Diconsa is the Mexican state company that supplies food to rural shops, and was run under Segalmex. The FGR, the federal prosecutor, says Diconsa paid Servicios Integrales Carregin in advance for 25,000 tonnes of sugar without receiving the full product, and that 142 million pesos were diverted; it says Carregin dispersed 82% of that sum within two months through 18 people and companies. In August 2024 a judge bound over Luis Fernando Zurita Mora, a wholesaler known as El Rey del Abarrote, on organised-crime and illicit-funds charges for allegedly receiving 1,680,000 pesos from the firm. He is held at Altiplano prison, with five months allowed for further investigation.
inside: A supplier company took an advance from the state food distributor for sugar it did not fully deliver, then dispersed 142 million pesos onward.
cite: Vanguardia, 22 Aug 2024, on the FGR case

n: ISSSTE hospital official charged over 20.3m pesos from a supplier
rank: administration of the ISSSTE's 20 de Noviembre hospital
d: The ISSSTE is Mexico's social-security institute for state employees, and its 20 de Noviembre hospital is in Mexico City. In October 2026 the FGR, the federal prosecutor, filed charges against Javier Tapia Santoyo, a former official of that hospital, saying he had business interests with Interaccion Biomedica, a company the FGR describes as an invoice mill that simulates operations and which has been on the tax authority's final list since 2017. The firm was given three contracts worth 11.1 million pesos in April 2018, for nerve-conduction studies, portable X-ray leasing and specialist dressings, while Tapia received 20.3 million pesos in transfers, directly or through third parties, between October 2017 and January 2019. The FGR seeks 18 years.
inside: A supplier listed as an invoice mill won hospital contracts from a state institute official who, prosecutors say, took 20.3 million pesos from it.
cite: Reforma via Plano Informativo, 30 Oct 2026

n: Finance firm Corafi took 800m pesos of Segalmex and Liconsa funds
rank: Segalmex administration and finance unit
d: Segalmex and Liconsa are Mexican state food companies. The FGR, the federal prosecutor, says about 800 million pesos of their public money was moved between February 2019 and June 2020 into a trust whose settlor was Corporacion en Asesoria Financiera (Corafi), a non-bank finance company, on instruction letters signed by Rene Gavira Segreste, head of Segalmex's administration and finance unit, against a fixed 11% annual yield. The FGR says Corafi was not authorised to take in funds this way. A federal judge bound over its shareholders Rene Davila de la Vega and Rene Davila Diaz in December 2023; an appeal failed in 2025, and in August 2026 a court refused to strike 15 pieces of evidence. There is no verdict.
inside: An unauthorised finance company drew about 800 million pesos of state food-company money through the finance chief who signed the instructions.
cite: El Imparcial, 31 Aug 2026, on the FGR case and the appeal ruling

n: De Vido convicted over gas pipeline works awarded to Odebrecht
rank: Ministry of Federal Planning and Secretariat of Energy
d: Odebrecht is the Brazilian construction group that has admitted paying bribes across Latin America. On 24 June 2026 Argentina's Federal Oral Court No. 2 convicted Julio De Vido, former minister of federal planning, and Daniel Omar Cameron, former national energy secretary, of negotiations incompatible with public office, giving each three years' conditional prison and permanent disqualification; Cristian Folgar, a former fuels under-secretary, got two years and six months as a necessary accomplice. The works, between 2006 and 2008, expanded pipelines operated by Transportadora Gas del Norte and Transportadora Gas del Sur, with the state market administrator CAMMESA used as a bridge for treasury money. The prosecutor put the investment above US$2.3 billion. Two CAMMESA managers were acquitted.
inside: A construction group obtained pipeline expansion works through the planning ministry and energy secretariat, whose officials a court found had negotiated incompatibly with it.
cite: Procuraduria de Investigaciones Administrativas (MPF Argentina), 24 Jun 2026 verdict of TOF No. 2

n: Enarsa's LNG cargoes bought without tender through Diligentia
rank: Ministry of Federal Planning, over Enarsa's contracting
d: Enarsa is Argentina's state energy company. On 2 October 2025 Federal Oral Court No. 7 convicted Julio De Vido, former minister of federal planning, of fraudulent administration over the purchase of 11 liquefied natural gas cargoes in 2008 and 2009, sentencing him to four years with permanent disqualification; Roberto Baratta, a former under-secretary, received three years and six months, and the businessman Nicolas Dromi San Martino three years, suspended, as a necessary accomplice. Payments were made without public tender through intermediary companies, among them Diligentia S.A., which Dromi San Martino chaired, under the Programa Energia Total. The court said Enarsa was given operational management without adequate rules and had no control over contracting. Restitution of US$5,523,345 plus interest was ordered.
inside: An intermediary company chaired by a businessman collected payments for the state energy firm's gas cargoes, arranged without tender by the ministry officials above it.
cite: El Economista (Argentina), 2 Oct 2025, on the TOF No. 7 verdict

n: ARSAT purchasing manager allegedly paid by supplier Argentina Logistic Services
rank: ARSAT purchasing and contracting sub-management
d: ARSAT is Argentina's state satellite and telecommunications company. A federal investigation in San Isidro, under judge Lino Mirabelli and prosecutor Fernando Dominguez, alleges that Gerardo Boschin, ARSAT's deputy manager for purchasing and contracting, leaked tender details to the supplier Argentina Logistic Services and took cash at ARSAT's offices; one seized message says US$6,000 would be handed to him. Reporting by La Nacion says he could award contracts of up to US$2 million without tender, and between 2021 and 2024 signed about ten purchase orders worth over US$2 million and 16 million pesos, and that the former ARSAT head Facundo Leal transferred a pick-up truck to him. The allegations are unproven; his homes were raided and he has not been detained.
inside: A supplier allegedly paid the state satellite company's purchasing manager in cash for tender details, and collected purchase orders worth over US$2 million.
cite: Perfil, on a La Nacion investigation and court material, federal court of San Isidro

n: Odebrecht-led consortia won AySA plant works amid bribery charges
rank: AySA presidency and infrastructure directorate
d: AySA is Argentina's state water and sewerage utility. In 2019 federal judge Sebastian Casanello indicted contractors and officials over two of its plants: the Parana de las Palmas water treatment works, awarded to a consortium of Odebrecht, Benito Roggio e Hijos, Supercemento and Jose Cartellone, and the Berazategui sewage plant, awarded to Esuco and Camargo Correa. Prosecutors allege the firms paid public works ministry officials to win contracts and to unblock overdue payments, and the judge found the two jobs were divided between Odebrecht and Camargo Correa. Those indicted include the businessmen Carlos Wagner, Aldo Benito Roggio and Tito Biagini, and AySA's former president Carlos Ben. The works, tendered in October 2007, were delivered only partly from April 2015 at more than twice the tender price.
inside: Contractors allegedly paid public works officials to win and be paid for the state water utility's plants, and the utility's own former president was indicted.
cite: Procuraduria de Investigaciones Administrativas (MPF Argentina), 1 Mar 2019, on judge Casanello's ruling in case 1614/2016

n: FAdeA buyers charged with taking payments from aircraft parts suppliers
org_label: K1 Technologies and Laboratorio Integral Aeronautico
who: K1 Technologies and Laboratorio Integral Aeronautico
rank: FAdeA purchasing department
d: FAdeA is Argentina's state-majority aircraft factory in Cordoba. A federal judge there, Alejandro Sanchez Freytes, indicted three of its purchasing staff, Gustavo Alonso Ferrero, Maria Carolina Villarruel and Cesar Frances, for passive bribery. A March 2020 email from the US defence supplier K1 Technologies offered Alonso Ferrero commissions of 1% on orders up to US$50,000 and 2% above that, in exchange for competitors' quotes and the maximum price FAdeA would pay, and suggested Western Union because it leaves no trail. He received 20 transfers totalling US$12,000 between 2020 and 2023; Villarruel one of US$550; Frances 252,271 pesos from the supplier Laboratorio Integral Aeronautico. A union official found the email in 2023. Frances denied taking bribes; the suppliers' executives settled through reparation agreements.
inside: Two suppliers paid buyers inside the state aircraft factory for rivals' quotes and its price ceiling, so their own bids could be set to win.
cite: Perfil Cordoba, on the ruling of Juzgado Federal de Cordoba 2 and the Oficina Anticorrupcion complaint

n: Enarsa power plant contracts steered to the Isolux-IECSA venture
rank: Enarsa presidency and project management
d: Enarsa is Argentina's state energy company. In May 2020 federal judge Sebastian Casanello indicted its head from 2003 to 2013, Exequiel Espinosa, and its manager for the project, Santiago Pierro, together with five executives of the Isolux-IECSA joint venture, for fraudulent administration against the public administration. Enarsa's 2007 public tender covered five power stations; only Ensenada de Barragan and Brigadier Lopez were awarded, both to Isolux-IECSA. The judge said the contracts were steered to the venture through coordination between officials and executives, that bids were priced above budget, and that addenda raising prices were granted without competitive procedures, with irregular payments of 792,651,795.48 pesos by October 2011. He said it was unknown whether the venture gave anything in return. All denied the allegations.
inside: An outside joint venture obtained the state energy company's power station contracts and price-raising addenda through its president and project manager, prosecutors allege.
cite: Infobae, 12 May 2020, on judge Casanello's processing order

n: Enarsa reserved fuel depots for firms without tender or board approval
rank: Enarsa presidency
d: Enarsa is Argentina's state energy company. In July 2021 federal judge Sebastian Casanello indicted Exequiel Espinosa, its former president, for aggravated fraudulent administration and attached 800 million pesos of his assets, after a complaint by the Oficina Anticorrupcion, the national anti-corruption office. In 2012 he contracted fuel storage depots from three firms without tender and without board authorisation, and his offer letters wrongly stated that a required framework agreement with the state market administrator CAMMESA had been signed. The fuel was never used or paid for. One depot belonged to Pobater, owned by Horacio Sambucetti, a businessman close to the planning minister Julio De Vido; Enarsa paid 899,200 dollars plus VAT to end that contract, and Chenyi and Generacion Independencia have claimed more than 15 million dollars in arbitration.
inside: Three storage firms, one owned by a businessman close to the planning minister, got no-tender reservations pushed through by the state energy company's own president.
cite: EconoJournal, 19 Jul 2021, on judge Casanello's indictment

n: Housing developer and GSIS Tarlac officers convicted over P293m loans
rank: GSIS Tarlac City division chief, appraiser and insurance specialist
d: The Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) is the state pension fund for Philippine public workers, and it lends to its members. On 3 March 2023 the Sandiganbayan, the country's anti-graft court, convicted three GSIS Tarlac City officers and Jose de Guzman, president of the private developer JQG Homes Development, over housing loans worth P293.16 million. The Ombudsman's 2012 indictment says they conspired to approve 491 ineligible applications under the 2001 Bahay Ko scheme for public school teachers, losing GSIS P241.053 million, and that commercial lots were over-appraised by P33.243 million. Houses were unfinished or uninhabitable. The court said the accused showed manifest partiality and bad faith. Each got six to 10 years a count.
inside: A private developer worked through the pension fund's own branch officers, who approved 491 ineligible housing loans so that GSIS lending and appraisals served his company.
cite: Rappler, 8 March 2023; Manila Bulletin, 8 March 2023

n: Fire truck supplier and Cebu airport authority officers convicted
rank: General manager and bids and awards committee, Mactan-Cebu airport authority
d: The Mactan-Cebu International Airport Authority (MCIAA) is the state corporation that ran the Philippines' second-busiest airport. In a decision dated 14 February and reported in 2025, the Sandiganbayan convicted its former general manager Adelberto Yap, three bids and awards staff, and Marlon Barillo, president of the supplier Asiaborders Philippines Inc., over a 1 March 2006 contract for an aircraft rescue fire-fighting truck. The committee cut the minimum operating experience from five years to one; Asiaborders had been trading under two years and was the only bidder left. P6 million was released in advance for an undelivered truck, and Yap agreed to pay $732,000 where fair value was $616,836.86. Yap got 12 to 18 years.
inside: The supplier's own president was convicted with the airport corporation's officers, who lowered the bidding rules and paid in advance so the contract went to his firm.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 1 October 2025

n: Aircraft parts dealer got cut-price sales from state aerospace firm
rank: President and senior vice-president, Philippine Aerospace Development Corporation
d: The Philippine Aerospace Development Corporation (PADC) is a state-owned aviation company. Its president Danilo Crisologo and temporary senior vice-president Roberto Manlavi were convicted of graft over seven negotiated sales of aircraft parts to the private dealer Wingtips Parts Corporation in 2008. A 2006 PADC policy set a 30 per cent mark-up on local parts; in 2007 Manlavi issued a memorandum cutting selling prices, which Crisologo approved although neither the pricing committee nor the board had authorised it. The government received P849,510.22 and lost over six million pesos. The Supreme Court's Second Division affirmed the Sandiganbayan on 27 June 2022, and both men were sentenced to six years and one month to 10 years.
inside: A private parts dealer bought from the state aerospace company at prices two of its own executives cut without board authority, so PADC's selling decisions served the buyer.
cite: Supreme Court of the Philippines, 7 September 2022 (G.R. No. 253327)

n: State bank officer undervalued foreclosed plant for the winning bidder
rank: Senior assistant vice-president, Development Bank of the Philippines
d: The Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP) is a state-owned development bank. In a decision reported on 25 March 2026 the Sandiganbayan convicted Romeo A. Aguilar, its senior assistant vice-president and head of the remedial management department, of graft for approving a wrong valuation in 2013 of a foreclosed property in Cabuyao, Laguna owned by Milestone Paper Products. Aguilar approved an appraised value of P56,269,000 and a maximum bid price of P45,817,766.25; prosecutors say the correct figures were about P116,896,000 and P89,300,000, and that the winning bidder JRK Holdings Corporation gained P43,452,000. He was sentenced to six to 10 years and ordered to repay DBP P43,452,000 with interest.
inside: A private bidder bought a foreclosed plant from the state bank at a price the bank's own department head understated, and the court put the bidder's gain at P43,452,000.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 25 March 2026

n: State railway chief signed rail supply deals without the needed approval
rank: General manager, Philippine National Railways
d: The Philippine National Railways (PNR) is the state rail corporation. In a Fourth Division decision dated 22 January the Sandiganbayan convicted its former general manager Manuel Andal on two counts of graft for contracting two suppliers in 2009 without the prior approval of the transport secretary: Pandrol Korea, for 170,000 sets of rail fastenings and 50,000 clips and insulators, and Nikka Trading, for 50,000 sets of anti-vandal concrete sleepers. The Nikka contract was signed on 12 August 2009, before the PNR board passed the resolution covering it on 10 September 2009. The court found evident bad faith, manifest partiality and gross inexcusable negligence, gave him eight years and one month to 12 years a count, and ordered him to indemnify the government P86.50 million.
inside: Two named suppliers got PNR orders from the railway's own general manager, who signed for them before the board or the transport secretary had approved, in what the court called manifest partiality.
cite: Philippine Daily Inquirer, report on Sandiganbayan Fourth Division decision

n: Foundation chairman and state training centre staff took a lawmaker's fund
rank: Group head and legislative liaison officer, Technology Resource Center
d: The Technology Resource Center (TRC), now defunct, was a state-owned corporation that implemented livelihood projects. In a 61-page decision promulgated on 14 October 2022, a five-justice special division of the Sandiganbayan convicted Edison Sabio, chairman of the private Aksyon Makamasa Foundation Inc., of two counts each of graft and malversation, and with him two TRC officers, group head Maria Rosalinda Lacsamana and legislative liaison officer Belina Concepcion. P20.06 million from the Priority Development Assistance Fund of then Isabela representative Anthony Miranda was routed to the foundation through TRC in 2007. Sabio received 36 years and was ordered to indemnify the government P40.12 million; the two officers got 18 years each. Three other TRC officials were acquitted.
inside: An outside foundation's chairman worked through the state corporation's own officers, so TRC released P20.06 million of a lawmaker's development fund to his foundation.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 27 September 2025

n: Napoles and state centre officers convicted over a senator's fund release
rank: Deputy director general and group manager, Technology Resource Center
d: In a decision dated 5 June 2025 the Sandiganbayan convicted the businesswoman Janet Lim Napoles, two officers of the state-owned Technology Resource Center (TRC) — deputy director general Dennis Cunanan and group manager Maria Rosalinda Lacsamana — and Evelyn de Leon, an officer of the private Masaganang Ani Para sa Magsasaka Foundation. The court found Napoles created the foundation as a conduit and ended up with the money, part of Senator Joel Villanueva's Priority Development Assistance Fund; the report's headline gives P1.7 million and its text a total of P1,170,000. None reached a legitimate project. Each got six to 10 years, Napoles was ordered to return the full amount, and all four were acquitted on two malversation counts. Villanueva was not charged.
inside: Napoles's foundation reached the state corporation through two of its own senior officers, who released a senator's development fund to a conduit that kept it.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 1 October 2025

n: Aaron Foundation took P9.8m of a Laguna fund through state centre officers
rank: Deputy director general, group manager and chief accountant, TLRC
d: The Technology and Livelihood Resource Center (TLRC), later the Technology Resource Center, was a state-owned corporation. In a 108-page Sixth Division decision dated 4 February 2024 the Sandiganbayan convicted three of its officers — deputy director general Dennis Cunanan, group manager Maria Rosalinda Lacsamana and chief accountant Marivic Jover — over the 2007 Priority Development Assistance Fund of then Laguna representative Danton Bueser. The budget department released P10 million; TLRC kept two charges of P100,000 and passed P9.8 million to the private Aaron Foundation Philippines Inc. Sixteen officials from seven Laguna towns certified that no projects were carried out. The court called them ghost projects. The three were fined P9.8 million and ordered to repay P9.8 million. The foundation's president, Alfredo Ronquillo, died while the case ran.
inside: An unaccredited private foundation obtained P9.8 million of a lawmaker's fund because the state corporation's own senior officers certified and released the money to it.
cite: Philippine News Agency, 7 February 2024; Malaya Business Insight, 1 October 2025

n: Molugan Foundation head convicted with state centre officers over P9.6m
rank: Deputy director general, chief accountant and liaison officer, TLRC
d: The Sandiganbayan convicted Samuel Bombeo of the private Molugan Foundation Inc., three officers of the state-owned Technology and Livelihood Resource Center (TLRC) — deputy director general Dennis Cunanan, chief accountant Marivic Jover and legislative liaison Belina Concepcion — and Hiram Diday Pulido, former chief of staff of the late Negros Oriental representative Herminio Teves. P10 million of Teves's 2007 Priority Development Assistance Fund went to projects the court found did not exist: Bombeo received P9.6 million and TLRC kept a P400,000 service fee. State auditors found the foundation neither accredited nor qualified. Sentences run six to 10 years for graft and 12 to 18 for malversation, with joint indemnity of P9.6 million. Teves died in 2019 and his case was dismissed.
inside: An unqualified foundation's principal was convicted with the state corporation's own officers, who routed P9.6 million of a lawmaker's fund to him for projects that did not exist.
cite: Philippine News Agency, 18 September 2023; Manila Bulletin, 18 September 2023

n: Napoles and NLDC president convicted over a senator's livelihood fund
rank: President, National Livelihood Development Corporation
d: The National Livelihood Development Corporation (NLDC) was a state-owned corporation that financed livelihood projects. In a decision promulgated on 24 October 2025 the Sandiganbayan convicted its former president Gondelina G. Amata, the businesswoman Janet Lim Napoles and Michael Lim Benjamin, then a Senate political officer, over P14.5 million of then senator Gregorio Honasan's 2009 Priority Development Assistance Fund, meant for livelihood work in San Agustin, Surigao del Sur. The partner under Amata's memorandum of agreement was the Agri & Economic Program for Farmers Foundation; the prosecution said Napoles created it to divert the fund. Sentences run six to 10 years for graft and up to 17 years for malversation, with fines and restitution of P7.5 million and smaller sums carrying 6 per cent interest.
inside: Napoles's foundation was made the NLDC's project partner by the state corporation's own president, so a senator's P14.5 million livelihood fund was paid out to it.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 24 October 2025

n: Two foundations drew P65m through three state corporations' officers
org_label: Kabuhayan at Kalusugang Alay sa Masa Foundation and Aaron Foundation Philippines
rank: Officers of NABCOR, NLDC and TLRC
d: On 2 July 2024 the Sandiganbayan's Third Division convicted 15 former officers of three now-dissolved state-owned corporations — the National Agribusiness Corporation, the National Livelihood Development Corporation and the Technology and Livelihood Resource Center — and two members of the partner non-governmental organisations, over the P65 million Priority Development Assistance Fund of former Misamis Occidental representative Marina Clarete. The court held that a conspiracy to embezzle the funds was proved beyond reasonable doubt. The foundations named are Kabuhayan at Kalusugang Alay sa Masa Foundation and Aaron Foundation Philippines. Sentences range from a few years to 175 years for NABCOR's former vice-president Rhodora Mendoza, with fines and reimbursements to the treasury. Clarete, who the report says remains in hiding, is not yet before the court.
inside: Two outside foundations were written in as project partners by officers of three state corporations, which then paid out P65 million of a lawmaker's fund for bogus livelihood projects.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 2 July 2024; The Star (Malaysia), 4 July 2024

n: Drinks distributor won a P6m transport ministry phone order without bidding
org_label: West Island Beverages Distributor (Samuel Jonathan Ng)
rank: Directors and legal officer, Department of Transportation and Communications
d: The Sandiganbayan convicted four officers of the Department of Transportation and Communications — directors Ildefonso Patdu Jr., Elmer Soneja and Rebecca Cacatian, and legal officer Geronimo Quintos — and the businessman Samuel Jonathan Ng, over the purchase of P6 million worth of mobile telephones in 2005. The contract went to Ng's company, West Island Beverages Distributor, without public bidding, and state auditors found the firm was not an authorised mobile phone dealer. The officials were sentenced to five to 10 years for manifest partiality towards his company. Former Iloilo representative Judy Syjuco, the main accused, pleaded guilty under a plea bargain to defrauding the public treasury. On 11 September 2024 the court denied motions for reconsideration and affirmed its 7 June 2024 decision.
inside: A drinks distributor with no phone dealership got a ministry supply contract without bidding, through four of the ministry's own officers whom the court found partial towards his firm.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 11 September 2024

n: Textile firm drew P103m in tax credits from the finance department's centre
rank: One-Stop Shop Inter-Agency Tax Credit and Duty Drawback Center, Department of Finance
d: The One-Stop Shop Inter-Agency Tax Credit and Duty Drawback Center, set up inside the Philippine finance department in 1992 and now defunct, issued tax credit certificates that firms could use to pay taxes or sell on. The Ombudsman charged its staff and officers of Scope Industries Inc. in 1999, alleging Scope obtained certificates on spurious export papers although it did not export textiles; the certificates were used or transferred to firms including Dragon Textile Mills, Filsyn and Pilipinas Shell. Forty certificates worth P103,042,663 were issued between 1995 and 1998. The Sandiganbayan convicted ten former centre personnel on 24 counts and acquitted on 16, putting the loss at P61.508 million. Scope's named officers have not been arraigned and are at large.
inside: A textile company obtained tax credit certificates worth P103,042,663 through the finance department's own evaluators, who approved its spurious export papers without verification.
cite: Rappler, August 2023; Sandiganbayan Third Division, People v. Belicena et al., Crim. Cases 25596-25636

n: Van dealer and Mountain Province officials convicted over hospital purchase
rank: Provincial bids and awards committee, Mountain Province
d: The Sandiganbayan's Third Division convicted ten officials of Mountain Province, in the northern Philippines, and Ronaldo Kimakim, owner of the supplier Ronhil Trading Incorporated, over a simulated and overpriced purchase of a Mitsubishi L-300 van for Bontoc General Hospital in 2006. The officials specified the brand and model, which the court said gave the supplier an unwarranted advantage under the procurement law. The province paid P843,700.91; Kimakim had bought the same vehicle, with the same plate, chassis and engine numbers, from a dealership on 29 March 2006 for P756,000 and resold it the same day, a difference of P87,700.91. He admitted taking a P10,000 fee. All eleven were given six to eight years. The case was filed in 2017.
inside: A trader supplied a van to a provincial hospital at a mark-up after the province's own bids committee wrote his chosen brand and model into the specification.
cite: Rappler, report on Sandiganbayan Third Division decision

n: Medicine supplier and Maripipi officials convicted over unbid deal
rank: Mayor and bids and awards committee, Maripipi, Biliran
d: On 31 January 2023 the Sandiganbayan convicted thirteen people of graft over the purchase of medicines and medical supplies worth P7,998,777.26 by the town of Maripipi in Biliran province in 2010. They include the former mayor Noel Albelda, the bids and awards committee and technical working group, the municipal accountant and health officer, a state auditor of the Commission on Audit, and two people from the supplier SUREMEDS: its proprietor Jerome Capuyan and its authorised representative Cherel Serato. No public bidding was held, and payment was approved without the signature of the official who was to accept the medicines. The court found gross inexcusable negligence and manifest partiality. Each was sentenced to six to 10 years.
inside: A medicine supplier's proprietor and agent were convicted alongside the town's own mayor and bids committee, who awarded the contract to them without any bidding.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 31 January 2023

n: Land claimant's P50,000 bought a land registry examiner's order
rank: Examiner, Land Registration Authority
d: The Land Registration Authority is the Philippine agency that issues the orders needed to process land titles. Giovanni Purugganan, one of its examiners, was convicted of direct bribery by a Quezon City trial court on 8 February 2017 for demanding P300,000 from Albert Avecilla to speed up an order on his uncle's property, a process that normally takes six to eight months. Avecilla paid P50,000 in marked notes in a National Bureau of Investigation entrapment on 23 August 2011. In a 46-page resolution the Sandiganbayan affirmed the bribery conviction, two years and four months in prison and a P100,000 fine, but reversed a separate graft conviction, holding that a titling order is not a contract or transaction under the anti-graft law.
inside: A man seeking a land title paid P50,000 to an examiner inside the registry, so the agency's own order on his family's property was issued for money.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 16 September 2025

n: Servicing firms paid a PGNiG engineer in Zielona Gora for gas-plant contracts
org_label: Electrical servicing contractors in six Polish voivodeships
rank: Electrical and Automation Department, PGNiG Zielona Gora branch
d: Poland's Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA), its anti-graft police force, says an employee of the Electrical and Automation Department at the Zielona Gora branch of PGNiG, then the state gas company, made informal arrangements with the owners of outside servicing firms during tender procedures and passed them sensitive information. From March 2020 to April 2021 he allegedly inflated the value of the services ordered by at least 588,000 zloty and took the money as a bribe, disguised as invoices for design services that did not reflect real work. The contracts were framework agreements to service electrical equipment at gas mines and storage sites. In June 2022 the CBA detained eight people, the employee and seven owners or staff of outside firms, and all eight were charged.
inside: Outside servicing firms reached the state gas company through the branch engineer who ran its tenders, so framework contracts and inflated service bills went to the firms that paid him.
cite: CBA (Centralne Biuro Antykorupcyjne) press release, 27 June 2022

n: Bidders paid a Polska Spolka Gazownictwa manager for pipeline tenders
org_label: Construction firms bidding for gas network work
rank: Head of Investments and Renovations, Gorzow Wielkopolski gas division
d: The CBA, Poland's anti-corruption police, says the former head of the Investments and Renovations Department at the Gorzow Wielkopolski gas division of Polska Spolka Gazownictwa, the state-owned gas distribution company, accepted at least 160,000 zloty from entrepreneurs for favouring certain bidders in tenders for construction services and for a study on gas pipeline development. The payments were allegedly disguised as fees for consulting work he supposedly did for bidders through his own business, and he allegedly extended bid deadlines, prepared cost estimates for bidders and allowed extra work. He and a Mazovian businessman were charged in May 2022; three more entrepreneurs were detained that October and two held for three months.
inside: Firms bidding for the state gas distributor's work bought its branch tender chief, who then shaped deadlines and estimates so that their offers looked the best.
cite: CBA press releases, 19 May 2022 and 21 October 2022

n: Fuel trader paid Szczecin power plant staff to pass bad fuel off as biomass
org_label: Transport company supplying fuel to Elektrownia Szczecin
rank: Chief engineer and fuel quality staff, Elektrownia Szczecin
d: The CBA, Poland's anti-corruption police, detained twelve people in February 2017 over deliveries to Elektrownia Szczecin, a power station in the Dolna Odra group owned by the state electricity company Polska Grupa Energetyczna (PGE). A businessman whose transport company supplied the plant allegedly paid staff responsible for checking fuel quality to confirm that lorries carried suitable biomass when they did not, so the plant burned poor-quality fuel. The plant's chief engineer was caught taking a 50,000 zloty bribe. Searches turned up about 1 million zloty in cash, including over 100,000 zloty in plant offices. The CBA put PGE's losses in the millions and said the case was still developing.
inside: A fuel supplier bought the power station's own quality inspectors, so the state utility accepted and paid for deliveries its rules should have rejected.
cite: CBA press release, 3 February 2017

n: Mining contractors paid executives of Poland's state mine closure company
org_label: Mining support companies contracted by Spolka Restrukturyzacji Kopaln
rank: Vice-president and unit directors, Spolka Restrukturyzacji Kopaln
d: Spolka Restrukturyzacji Kopaln (SRK), the state company in Bytom that closes and drains Poland's exhausted coal mines, was investigated by the CBA for 2016 and 2017. In June 2017 its vice-president Miroslaw S., who also ran its mine liquidation and environmental office, was caught taking a 30,000 zloty bribe for favouring a Katowice mining support company in public tenders; that company's president, Grzegorz G., was detained too, and it held multi-million zloty orders from SRK. A manager monitoring mine liquidation, Marek C., allegedly received cash and a luxury car with a fuel card, spending 16,000 zloty on fuel in a few months. In February 2018 a former dewatering plant director and three mining firm representatives were detained.
inside: Contractors living off mine closure work paid SRK's own vice-president and managers, so the state company's tenders went to the firms that were paying.
cite: CBA press release, 14 February 2018

n: Coal trading agency paid vice-presidents of two Polish state coal companies
rank: Vice-presidents of Rudzka and Nadwislanska Spolka Weglowa
d: A coal trading agency run by Barbara Kmiecik paid the vice-presidents of two Polish state coal companies, Rudzka Spolka Weglowa and Nadwislanska Spolka Weglowa, for steady coal supplies, which it exported to a Czech buyer, and for approval of multi-party compensation agreements that let it buy coal more cheaply because creditors gave up interest and part of their claims. The charges covered 1994 to 1998. The district court in Ruda Slaska convicted Wieslaw K. of Rudzka, who took 420,000 zloty, giving him two and a half years in prison and a 90,000 zloty fine; Jerzy H. of Nadwislanska, who took 140,000 zloty, received a suspended term. Jacek W., who handed over the bribes, got two and a half years. The Gliwice regional court upheld the verdicts.
inside: A private coal trader bought the men who decided supply at two state coal companies, so its deliveries and its debt write-off deals were approved on its own terms.
cite: Gazeta Prawna / PAP, 'Gliwice: Kary wiezienia za korupcje w gornictwie sa prawomocne'

n: Subcontractors paid buyers at PIT-RADWAR, a plant of Poland's arms group
org_label: Electrical and electronics subcontractors of PIT-RADWAR
rank: Logistics and ordering staff, PIT-RADWAR SA
d: PIT-RADWAR SA, a radar and electronics maker belonging to Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa, the Polish state armaments group, was investigated by the CBA with help from the military police over purchases of machines, devices and parts handled by its logistics staff. Two logistics employees were detained in Warsaw just after taking cash described as an illegal commission on a parts purchase, and were charged and held. An entrepreneur allegedly inflated the value of goods supplied to the company by a few per cent and passed the mark-up back to an employee once the invoices were paid. Lukasz M., an employee of a Wroclaw electrical firm that subcontracted to PIT-RADWAR, allegedly paid bribes from 2010 to 2014. Ten people had been detained by August 2018.
inside: Suppliers to a state arms plant paid its logistics buyers a share of inflated invoices, so orders and prices at PIT-RADWAR were set to suit the sellers.
cite: CBA press release, 24 August 2018

n: Contractor Radekov bribed a Czech Post deputy director over renovation tenders
org_label: Radekov and other contractors bidding for Czech Post work
rank: Deputy general director, Ceska posta (Czech Post)
d: Prague City Court ruled in September 2020 on rigged contracts at Ceska posta, the Czech state postal company. Richard Soldan, its former deputy general director, received a two-year suspended sentence and a 150,000 crown fine over five tenders issued between 2012 and 2014 for post office interiors and counter modernisation, in which pre-arranged firms were allowed to win. Antonin Hadac, managing director of the contractor Radekov, was convicted over a window replacement contract at the Znojmo post office and fined 50,000 crowns, and Radekov itself was fined 250,000 crowns. The court acquitted Agrotec, a company held in trust for then prime minister Andrej Babis, whose employees had been accused over tyre supplies. The ruling could be appealed.
inside: A building contractor reached the state postal company through its deputy general director, and renovation tenders were steered to firms arranged in advance.
cite: Novinky.cz / CTK, 2 September 2020

n: Medical suppliers rigged Central Bohemian hospital tenders with their managers
org_label: Puro-Klima, Hospimed and B. Braun Medical
rank: Head of Kladno hospital and deputy head of regional hospitals
d: A regional court convicted nine defendants in April 2015 over rigged public tenders in the Czech Central Bohemian Region. The prosecutor said the main organisers were Katerina Kottova, who headed the Kladno hospital, and Petr Kott, deputy head of the region's hospitals; the suppliers Puro-Klima, Hospimed and B. Braun Medical repeatedly won the health tenders. B. Braun allegedly tailored a Kladno tender for a dental robot with Kott's help and supplied other bidders. At Mlada Boleslav hospital a rival was removed on a formal defect. The Kotts each received seven and a half years; managers of Puro-Klima and Hospimed got five and a half years, and a B. Braun manager a suspended term. The verdict was not final and appeals were lodged.
inside: Equipment suppliers worked through the managers running the region's hospitals, so hospital tenders were written and awarded for the suppliers that were in on them.
cite: Czech Television (CT24) / CTK, 7 April 2015

n: Suppliers paid 27.8m crowns to the director of Prague's Na Homolce hospital
org_label: Suppliers and front companies of Na Homolce hospital
rank: Director, Nemocnice Na Homolce
d: Vladimir Dbaly, a neurosurgeon who ran the state hospital Na Homolce in Prague from October 2006 to March 2012, was finally sentenced by the Prague High Court in June 2021 to ten years in prison with forfeiture of property. Investigators say bribes of about 27.8 million crowns reached him over 2009 tenders for digitising medical records and buying a Leksell Gamma Knife; the first-instance verdict found that he and his deputy approached only Jozef Kalavsky's firm, which they knew did not meet the conditions, and that the digitisation tender was to favour a front company, Disol. Earlier convictions covered 2008 to 2011 tenders for consulting, accounting and legal services. He and co-defendants must pay the hospital 112 million crowns.
inside: Suppliers and front companies reached a large state hospital through its own director, and its equipment and service tenders were arranged so that they won.
cite: CNN Prima News / CTK, 17 June 2021

n: Builder ESB and the head of the Lany state forest rigged a reservoir contract
who: ESB, a construction and mining firm
rank: Head of Lesni sprava Lany
d: Lesni sprava Lany is the state forest administration that manages the Lany game reserve for the Czech president's office. In May 2021 the district court in Kladno found its head, Milos Balak, guilty of influencing a public tender for the second stage of securing and draining slopes around the Klicava reservoir, about five years earlier. The judge said the defendants shaped the preparation of the project and breached procurement rules on equal treatment and transparency, calling the consultations fraudulent. Balak received three years in prison, a four-year ban on activity and a 1.8 million crown fine; Libor Tkadlec, a manager of the firm Energie - stavebni a banska, got a suspended term, and the firm was penalised over 5 million crowns. All denied wrongdoing and appealed.
inside: A building firm worked with the head of the state forest administration on the preparation of its tender, so the reservoir contract was shaped around the firm.
cite: Czech Television (CT24) / CTK, 7 May 2021

n: Builders and a laundry firm accused of buying Motol hospital's directors
org_label: Geosan Group, Pragoperun and other hospital contractors
rank: Director and operations deputy director, Motol University Hospital
d: Czech organised crime police raided Motol University Hospital in Prague on 24 February 2025 after about two years of investigation and charged at least 17 people with damaging the European Union's financial interests, subsidy fraud, bribery and money laundering. Miloslav Ludvik, the hospital's long-serving director, and Pavel Budinsky, his operations deputy, were charged and Ludvik was dismissed. Police allege a bribe of 8 million crowns, 5 million of it meant for Ludvik and 3 million for Budinsky. Geosan Group, which rebuilt the hospital's Blue Pavilion with a subsidy of almost 1.5 billion crowns, had its commercial director detained; according to reports Budinsky demanded 1 million crowns from the head of Pragoperun in 2023 to keep the laundry contract.
inside: Contractors holding the hospital's building and laundry work are alleged to have paid its director and his deputy to keep billion-crown contracts flowing to them.
cite: CNN Prima News, 25 February 2025, citing NCOZ and police

n: IT firms and the Lesy CR computing chief indicted over a billion-crown system
who: Dynn and Time Import, IT suppliers
rank: Head of information technology, Lesy CR
d: The Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office in Prague indicted five people in May 2017 for collusion in public tenders at Lesy CR, the Czech state forestry enterprise, over conduct between 2008 and 2012. They were Jan Pribyl, the enterprise's former head of information technology, and four businessmen, Jiri Hart, Jiri Pantoflicek, Michal Kriz and Martin Stufi, whom reporting linked to the firms dynn and Time Import. Those two firms won an information system contract worth over 1 billion crowns from Lesy CR in 2008 and 2009. About 300 million crowns was allegedly taken out for fictitious services, with 287 million crowns sent to British companies for consulting that was never delivered and further money to Samoa before returning to the accused.
inside: IT suppliers worked with the state forestry enterprise's own computing chief on its tenders, won a billion-crown system contract and drained part of the money as fictitious services.
cite: Czech Television (CT24) / CTK, 2 May 2017

n: Construction firms rigged repair tenders at the Kladruby state stud farm
org_label: Cettus, Chladek a Tintera and other builders
rank: Deputy director, Narodni hrebcin Kladruby nad Labem
d: The Prague High Court finally punished twelve people and one company in February 2023 for manipulating tenders to restore the national stud farm at Kladruby nad Labem, a state enterprise and national cultural monument. Vladimir Novy, former director of the construction firm Cettus, acted as the investor's representative in 2013 and rigged the tenders for design documentation and technical supervision; he received a three-year suspended sentence and a 200,000 crown fine. Simona Vonkova, the stud farm's former deputy director, also received a three-year suspended sentence. Petr Pejcha of Chladek a Tintera got a suspended term and his firm was fined 2 million crowns. The companies DOP Construction and Strabag were acquitted on appeal. Prosecutors said a 250 million crown subsidy was put at risk.
inside: Builders took over the preparation of a state stud farm's restoration tenders, with its deputy director convicted alongside them, so the work was awarded on their terms.
cite: Czech Television (CT24) / CTK, 14 February 2023

n: Czech rail infrastructure chief charged after 80m crowns found in his safe
org_label: Trojek and other suppliers of Sprava zeleznic
rank: Director general, Sprava zeleznic
d: Czech police opened a prosecution of five people in 2026 for securing an advantage in awarding a public contract at Sprava zeleznic, the state railway infrastructure manager, and the supervising prosecutor confirmed it. Jiri Svoboda, its former director, is among the accused; organised crime police raided the company in November 2025 and its board removed him on 1 December 2025. In a search of his home officers found cash equivalent to 80 million crowns and a collection of expensive watches. About 20 billion crowns of contracts were examined, including a 7 billion crown rebuild of the Pardubice rail junction. As director he signed long-term scrap metal sale contracts with the firm Trojek, which owns the flat next to his and has not been charged. He has denied wrongdoing.
inside: Prosecutors allege contracts at the state rail infrastructure company were steered for outside firms through its director, who was found with 80 million crowns in cash at home.
cite: Ekonomicky denik, 7 August 2026, citing Seznam Zpravy and Odkryto

n: Notary and land registry chief moved 6,500 hectares out of a state forest firm
org_label: Slanske lesy s.r.o. and the businessman Milan Ico
rank: Director of the Land Registry Office in Trebisov
d: In 1998 about 6,500 hectares of forest and some 500 hectares of arable land disappeared from the ownership records of Vychodoslovenske lesy, a Slovak state forestry enterprise. The land was transferred on a notarial certificate issued by the notary Ferdinand Ontko to Maria Dusickova, then 85, described as an alleged illegitimate daughter of Count Ladislav Karolyi, who put it into the company Slanske lesy; the businessman Milan Ico became its executive. Pavol Pacuta, then director of the Land Registry Office in Trebisov, was also involved. In March 2022 the Supreme Court set aside the sentencing part of an earlier ruling and jailed Ico for three years and Ontko and Pacuta for two and a half years each, citing a loss to the state of about 42 million euros.
inside: A private company got the land registry's own district director and a notary to sign state forest land over to it, stripping 6,500 hectares from the state enterprise's records.
cite: TASR / TERAZ.sk, 17 March 2022

n: Intermediaries paid judges in Zilina for verdicts in their clients' cases
rank: Judges of the regional and district courts in Zilina
d: Slovakia's Special Prosecutor's Office indicted five men in August 2020 for bribery and laundering the proceeds of crime, saying they handed over money from 2015 to 2019 to influence decisions by judges at the regional and district courts in Zilina, so that clients would be discharged from charges, released on parole or given suspended sentences. The alleged payments were of 5,000, 7,000, 10,000, 22,000 and up to 100,000 euros. The main defendant was Frantisek T.; another defendant was a lawyer, and one was already serving a sentence. The Specialized Criminal Court accepted the indictment in November 2020 and the defendants admitted guilt. In the related operation Plevel that September, police detained eleven people including a former regional judge and a Zilina district judge.
inside: Underworld intermediaries paid their way into two Slovak courts, so judges decided their clients' cases the way the money asked.
cite: TASR / TERAZ.sk, 30 November 2020

n: Subcontractor paid the Bardejov hospital director over rebuilding contracts
rank: Director and supervisory board member, St James hospital, Bardejov
d: The trial of five people opened at Slovakia's Specialized Criminal Court in Banska Bystrica in March 2022 over the reconstruction of the St James hospital in Bardejov, a state-funded hospital in eastern Slovakia. The prosecutor alleges that its director, Marian P., who also chaired the Slovak Hospitals Association, and Jan P., a member of the hospital's supervisory board, took bribes from a subcontracting firm in 2008 and 2009, and that two companies won construction contracts at the hospital in return. The money was allegedly used to build, renovate and furnish their own and other properties, and part of the European Union funds for the project went to private use. The director denies the charges. The ministry overseeing the funds claims more than 621,000 euros.
inside: A building subcontractor is alleged to have paid the hospital's own director and a board member, so the hospital's reconstruction contracts went to the firms that paid.
