cite: SITA, 30 March 2022

n: Businessman Jozef Brhel convicted over IT tenders at Slovakia's tax authority
rank: Financial Administration of Slovakia and the finance ministry
d: The Specialized Criminal Court in Banska Bystrica ruled on 17 February 2026 in the Mytnik case, about overpriced information technology tenders at Slovakia's Financial Administration, the body that collects tax and customs, between 2013 and 2018. The businessman Jozef Brhel received three years suspended and a 1.5 million euro fine, and his son three years suspended and a 1.2 million euro fine. Radko K., a former state secretary at the finance ministry, received 28 months suspended and a 60,000 euro fine, and a second businessman a shorter suspended term. A lawyer and a former Financial Administration official were acquitted. The court found guilt on three corrupt acts linked to the IT contracts. All denied guilt and announced appeals, so the ruling is not final.
inside: A businessman's group reached the state tax and customs authority through a finance ministry state secretary and its own staff, and its IT contracts were awarded at inflated prices.
cite: Noviny.sk / TASR, 17 February 2026

n: Cigarette factory owner paid Slovakia's tax crime chief 490,000 euros
rank: Director, Criminal Office of the Financial Administration
d: Prosecutors said the businessman Jozef Kertesz paid cash bribes totalling 490,000 euros between 2016 and 2019 to Ludovit Mako, then director of the Criminal Office of the Financial Administration, Slovakia's tax crime investigators, passing the money through the late Frantisek Bohm. The aim was unlawful advantages, including over the running of a cigarette factory and a tax warehouse and the size of a required tax security deposit. The Specialized Criminal Court in Banska Bystrica convicted Kertesz of continued bribery in June 2023 and jailed him for six years. On 15 October 2025 the Supreme Court annulled that sentence, dropping one act it could not confirm, and imposed three years suspended with a 25,000 euro fine. That ruling is final. His defence argued he had been pressured and extorted.
inside: A cigarette and tax warehouse businessman bought the head of the tax crime office, so decisions on his factory, his warehouse and his tax deposit were made to suit him.
cite: SITA, 15 October 2025

n: Operation Sysel: bribes intermediated for judges in Kosice and Presov
org_label: A businessman, a former judge and a former MP as intermediaries
rank: Judges of the courts in Kosice and Presov
d: Slovakia's National Criminal Agency charged three men in October 2021 in the anti-corruption operation Sysel, alleging they intermediated bribes worth thousands of euros for judges in Kosice and Presov in eastern Slovakia. The three counts were two cases of softening a sentence and one of removing real estate from bankruptcy proceedings. The accused are the businessman Marian S., whom reporting links to Marian Kocner, a former judge, Miroslav N., and Alexej I., a lawyer and former member of parliament. In December 2023 the Specialized Criminal Court found all three guilty, giving Marian S. two years suspended and a 15,000 euro fine and the others one year suspended each. The Supreme Court annulled that verdict in August 2025, and the retrial opened in March 2026. All pleaded not guilty.
inside: Prosecutors say litigants reached judges in two eastern Slovak courts through paid intermediaries, so sentences were softened and property was lifted out of a bankruptcy.
cite: SITA, 8 March 2026

n: Truck supplier rigged refuse vehicle tenders at three Polish municipal firms
org_label: A Wroclaw supplier of specialised trucks
rank: Presidents and staff of municipal utility companies
d: Poland's Central Anti-Corruption Bureau says the president and a salesperson of a Wroclaw firm that sells specialised trucks agreed with local officials and staff of municipal utility companies to rig tenders for refuse collection vehicles in favour of that firm. The tenders were announced in 2016 and were worth over 2.5 million zloty in total. Eight people were detained: the two from the Wroclaw supplier, the president and a former president of Miejski Zaklad Uslug Komunalnych in Kolo together with the mayor of Kolo, an employee of Miejski Zaklad Oczyszczania in Pruszkow, and, in February 2018, the deputy head and another employee of the municipal utility company PGK in Koszalin. All were to be charged by prosecutors in Lodz.
inside: A truck seller worked through the managers of three municipal waste companies, and a mayor, so their vehicle tenders were set up for it to win.
cite: CBA press release, 13 February 2018

n: Energon's Hidroelectrica power contract pushed with a bribe offer for a vote
rank: Hidroelectrica supervisory board and directorate
d: Hidroelectrica is Romania's state hydropower producer. Prosecutors said that in October 2013 Ioan Mihaila, a member of its supervisory board and an adviser to the energy minister, with trading director Eugen Bradean, promised 1.4 million euro to another board member, Remus Vulpescu, for a favourable vote on a four-year contract selling 7,012,800 MWh to Energon Power & Gas of Cluj for 1,157,112,000 lei, a possible loss of 175 million lei. The money was to be disguised as commission under a contract between an offshore company and the buyer. Vulpescu reported the approach. The Bucharest Court of Appeal jailed Mihaila for three years in February 2015; Bradean also received three years. The report does not say Energon itself paid.
inside: A private electricity buyer's contract was to be carried through Hidroelectrica's own board by paying for the votes that had to approve it.
cite: Adevarul, 26 February 2015, on the Bucharest Court of Appeal ruling; Gandul, 13 November 2013, on the DNA indictment

n: Contractors paid ELCEN's chief and commercial director to release invoices
rank: general director, Electrocentrale Bucuresti
d: ELCEN, Electrocentrale Bucuresti, is the state company that produces the heat and hot water for Bucharest. In December 2025 Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent its former general director, Claudiu-Ionut Cretu-Sarbu, and former commercial director, Cristian-Andrei-Cornel Zamfiroi, for trial for taking bribes, along with two company administrators charged with giving them. Prosecutors allege that on 1 July 2025 a representative of a firm with ELCEN contracts paid 40,000 lei, passed through Zamfiroi the same day, to speed up approval of payments on invoices issued to ELCEN, and that on 30 July 2025 Zamfiroi asked another administrator for 50,000 lei. The 40,000 lei was placed in a state-held account for confiscation. Both have been under judicial control since September; the case went to the Bucharest Tribunal.
inside: Firms selling to Bucharest's state heat producer paid its two most senior commercial officers so their own invoices were approved and paid first.
cite: Spotmedia, 29 December 2025, on the DNA indictment

n: Techno Montaj's owner paid directors at two Romanian state power plants
rank: Rovinari plant director, Complexul Energetic Oltenia
d: Complexul Energetic Oltenia is Romania's largest state coal-fired power group; CET Bucuresti Sud is a plant of the state heat producer ELCEN. In April 2024 anticorruption prosecutors sent Ion Eugen Petru, linked to SC Techno Montaj SRL, for trial in custody for bribe-giving, influence-buying and rigging a tender, with Iosif Circa, former director of Oltenia's Rovinari branch, charged with taking a bribe. Prosecutors allege 5,000 euro reached Circa on 20 December in Gorj county and 10,000 euro reached Adrian Dorin Ecobescu, former director of CET Sud, who admitted bribe-taking in a plea deal and received two years and eight months suspended. A state-majority company's open tender of 7 July 2023 was allegedly fixed in advance, and Petru's firm won on 25 August 2023 without real competition.
inside: A works contractor paid the plant directors who bought from it at two state power companies, and agreed a tender price in advance so its own bid won.
cite: G4Media and Adevarul, 17 April 2024, on the DNA indictment and plea agreements

n: A supplier paid 13,000 euro to CE Oltenia's energy director to be paid first
rank: director of the energy directorate, Complexul Energetic Oltenia
d: Complexul Energetic Oltenia is the state-owned lignite mining and power group in south-western Romania. Anticorruption prosecutors sent Liviu Catalin Stanculescu, director of its energy directorate, for trial for influence peddling in continued form, alleging that between 25 July 2022 and 23 March 2023 he received 13,000 euro directly from the administrator of a company holding contracts with the group, implying he could influence the directorate that approves payments and would push for the firm's invoices to be paid faster. The 13,000 euro was placed under seizure. Three other defendants settled during the investigation, one receiving two years and six months suspended for bribe-giving; their case involved backdating an invoice and an order sent to a state company to avoid late-payment penalties.
inside: A contractor paid a senior officer of the state coal and power group so that the body deciding payments moved its invoices ahead of others.
cite: Puterea.ro, on the DNA indictment of Liviu Catalin Stanculescu

n: Austrian contractor's commission on Romania's Bucharest-Constanta railway
rank: finance minister; transport ministry state secretary; Eximbank president
d: Prosecutors said that in 2005 representatives of the Austrian construction company Swietelsky agreed with Romanian officials to pay a commission on sums it received from the state for rehabilitating the Bucharest-Constanta railway, run by the state rail infrastructure company CNCFR. The commission is given as 3.5 per cent in the indictment and 3 per cent elsewhere, on payments of about 20 million euro; 11,781,842 euro moved through two offshore companies. In March 2022 the High Court convicted five defendants to 30 years, among them former finance minister Sebastian Vladescu, former Eximbank president Mircea Ionut Costea and former transport state secretary Constantin Dascalu; Swietelsky's director Josef Hornegger took a plea deal. On 5 November 2025 the High Court annulled the convictions of Costea and Vladescu on an extraordinary prescription appeal.
inside: A foreign railway contractor bought a standing share of the state's payments by paying the ministers and officials who signed and financed the work.
cite: Radio Free Europe Romania, 25 March 2022, on the High Court verdict; Romania Insider, 5 November 2025, on the annulment

n: Remarul's railcar repair contracts at CFR bought with cash and fake invoices
rank: traction directorate, CFR Calatori; deputy general director, CFR SA
d: CFR Calatori is Romania's state passenger rail operator and CFR SA runs the track. In 2015 prosecutors sent the rail repair works Remarul 16 Februarie SA, its former general director Dumitru Barbacuti and officers of the state railways for trial. Cluj businessman Calin Mitica allegedly paid Teodor Alexandru Gavris, head of CFR Calatori's automotive service and later its traction director, 414,392 lei in twelve tranches between January 2013 and June 2014, through fake invoices, to support bids for Desiro railcar revision contracts worth up to about 220.99 million lei. Adriian Stefan of Transferoviar Grup allegedly paid the CFR Galati branch director, Laurentiu Seceleanu, 105,665 lei. On 19 July 2023 the Cluj Tribunal ended proceedings against all twelve defendants as time-barred, but confiscated 388,933.54 lei from Gavris.
inside: A rail repair works paid the state railway officers who judged its bids, in cash, fake invoices, a job for a wife and flights, to win repair contracts.
cite: Economica.net, 2015, on the DNA indictment; G4Media and Radio Free Europe Romania, 19 July 2023, on the Cluj Tribunal ending the case as time-barred

n: Romania's rail safety authority certified Remarul so it could bid for repairs
rank: director general and inspectors, Romanian Railway Authority (AFER)
d: AFER, the Romanian Railway Authority, certifies who may repair rolling stock. Prosecutors allege that in September 2014 Mircea Cristian Arnautu, director of the Romanian Railway Notified Body within AFER, and inspector Marian Panaite certified the repair works Remarul 16 Februarie SA although it did not meet the legal requirements. That let it bid for repair services on 5100 kW electric locomotives worth up to about 55.28 million lei, and it won the tender. In December 2014 a revised commission report, allegedly produced under pressure from AFER's then director general Gelu Dan, kept the certificate. All were sent for trial in 2015 in the case built around Cluj businessman Calin Mitica, which the Cluj Tribunal ended on 19 July 2023 for all twelve defendants as time-barred.
inside: A repair company had the state rail safety authority certify it against the rules, which is what allowed it to bid for and win locomotive repair work.
cite: Economica.net, 2015, on the DNA indictment; G4Media, 19 July 2023, on the Cluj Tribunal ending the case as time-barred

n: Posta Romana's director took benefits through firms placed in its contracts
rank: director general, Posta Romana
d: Posta Romana is the state postal operator. In June 2020 the Bucharest Tribunal sentenced its former director general, Dumitru Daniel Neagoe, to six years in prison for three counts of bribe-taking, acquitted him of abuse of office and dropped a conflict of interest charge as time-barred, ordering confiscation of about 575,000 lei. Prosecutors alleged he required a cleaning contractor holding a Posta Romana contract to subcontract work to Dig Prodcom SRL, a firm he controlled through an intermediary, and had Dig Prodcom written into a bill-payment partnership and a prepaid recharge arrangement, where it received 1,595,739.28 lei between November 2010 and August 2012 and gained 1,267,741 lei. The verdict was not final and could be appealed to the Bucharest Court of Appeal.
inside: Outside firms were pressed into the post office's contracts and subcontracts, and the benefit ran back to the director general who awarded them.
cite: Newsweek Romania, 16 June 2020, on the Bucharest Tribunal sentence

n: Recruitment firm's rigged selection put a chosen man atop Apa Brasov
rank: general director and board, Compania Apa Brasov
d: Compania Apa Brasov is the county water and sewerage company in central Romania. In 2025 anticorruption prosecutors sent six people and the recruitment firm SC EWORA Resurse Umane SRL for trial over the selection of the company's general and economic directors. On 26 March 2025 Apa Brasov signed a direct-purchase contract with EWORA for recruitment services; prosecutors allege the selection was then rigged so that Liviu Cocos, the acting director, was appointed, that board members were brought in with jobs at the company for themselves or a relative, and that the alleged loss to Apa Brasov was 189,296 lei. Those charged include Brasov county council vice-president Serban Todorica Constantin and the board president. The indictment went to the Brasov Tribunal; all are presumed innocent.
inside: A recruitment company took a direct contract from the county water utility and ran the selection that decided who would run it, in the buyer's favour.
cite: Puterea.ro, 2025, on the DNA indictment sent to the Brasov Tribunal

n: Brasov heating service directors sold procurement secrets to three firms
rank: director and deputy director, Serviciul Public Local de Termoficare Brasov
d: SPLT Brasov is the city's public heating service, which runs the boiler houses and heat substations. In August 2023 anticorruption prosecutors sent its director, Ionut Mircea Marin, and deputy director, Gheorghe Corbos, for trial in pre-trial detention, with the head of the administrative service charged as an accomplice. Prosecutors allege that between June and November 2022 the two arranged direct purchase procedures favouring three companies, causing a loss of 1,912,025 lei, and that the businessman who ran those firms paid them benefits worth 69,785 euro for confidential information about the procedures. Marin is also alleged to have taken benefits worth 39,492 euro and 93,862 lei from another company linked to a contract worth 7,899,160 lei. Four companies and their administrators had already settled by plea agreement.
inside: A contractor bought the inside knowledge of the city heating service's own directors, and the direct purchases they then arranged went to his three firms.
cite: Evenimentul Zilei, on the DNA indictment sent to the Brasov Tribunal on 7 August 2023

n: Velmed sold Ploiesti county hospital inflated equipment after paying its head
rank: manager, Ploiesti County Emergency Hospital
d: The Dr Constantin Andreoiu County Emergency Hospital in Ploiesti is a public hospital in Prahova county. In December 2025 anticorruption prosecutors sent its manager, Bogdan-Cristian Nica, for trial for bribe-taking and abuse of office with particularly serious consequences, together with the supplier Velmed International SRL and its administrator for bribe-giving. Prosecutors allege that between 2021 and 2024 the hospital awarded procurements for radiology, neurosurgery, orthopaedic and cardiology equipment at substantially inflated prices, an estimated loss of 28,700,705 lei, and that Nica received 50,000 lei from Velmed's administrator in two payments into a personal bank account on 18 May and 13 August 2022, linked to the award of later contracts. The financial-accounting director was charged with complicity. The case went to the Prahova Tribunal.
inside: A medical equipment supplier paid the hospital manager who signed its purchases, and the hospital went on buying its equipment at inflated prices.
cite: Stiripesurse, 22 December 2025, on the DNA indictment sent to the Prahova Tribunal

n: Caught paying cash for Romgaz to settle a notarised land purchase
rank: executive empowered to approve payment, Romgaz
d: Romgaz is Romania's state natural gas producer, with its head office at Medias. In June 2020 anticorruption prosecutors sent a businessman for trial under judicial control for bribe-giving, alleging that between 28 April and 11 May 2020 he promised 200,000 euro to a Romgaz executive, treated in the case as a witness, to get that executive to approve payment on a land purchase contract already signed and notarised. He allegedly handed over 50,000 euro in cash as an advance on 11 May 2020 and was caught in the act; the money was seized for possible confiscation. A local report cited in the article says Romgaz paid eight million lei for 1.7 hectares, justified as a future compressed natural gas station, without documents supporting the need for the purchase.
inside: A seller to the state gas company tried to buy the signature that would release its payment, offering cash to the executive who had to approve it.
cite: Bursa, 18 June 2020, on the DNA indictment sent to the Bucharest Tribunal

n: A contractor paid seven Romsilva forest district heads to sign off its work
rank: heads of forest districts, Ocolul Silvic Comanesti, Romsilva
d: Romsilva is Romania's state forestry company. In October 2020 anticorruption prosecutors in Bacau sent seven staff of its Comanesti forest district for trial for taking bribes, with an accountant of a commercial company charged with complicity in giving them. Prosecutors allege that between 2015 and 2020 they demanded and received money from representatives of that company, which the report does not name, for confirming forestry work such as reforestation and clearing and for paying the firm's invoices. The former head of the district, Aurel Paslaru, allegedly asked for 3 per cent of invoice values and received 210,000 lei; the other six allegedly took sums totalling 4,316,850 lei, the largest 1,595,300 lei. Six were sent for trial under house arrest and their property was placed under seizure.
inside: A forestry contractor paid the district heads who certified its work and released its invoices, so the state forest company signed off and paid.
cite: Spotmedia, 22 October 2020, on the DNA Bacau indictment sent to the Bacau Tribunal

n: Car dealer's 182-vehicle Loteria Romana fleet deal bought with cash and cars
rank: director general and procurement service, Loteria Romana
d: Loteria Romana is the state lottery company. On 17 May 2010 it awarded a car dealership run by Nicolae Virgil Sorescu a buy-back contract for 182 vehicles to replace its fleet; prosecutors said the specifications came from the dealer and carried restrictive conditions although only five vans and one car had been requested for 2010, and the dealer was paid 9,902,498 lei by the year's end. Prosecutors alleged the lottery's officers demanded 1.5 million lei, four new cars and the 182 traded-in vehicles. On 23 January 2024 the Bucharest Court of Appeal closed the case definitively because the 2010 offences were time-barred, but confiscated over 2.6 million lei from former procurement head Ovidiu Ripanu and former executive director Remus Leonard Lazareanu.
inside: A car dealership wrote the state lottery's tender conditions and paid its procurement officers in cash and cars, and the lottery bought 182 vehicles it had not requested.
cite: Evenimentul Zilei, 27 September 2017, on the DNA indictment; Spotmedia, 23 January 2024, citing Agerpres on the Bucharest Court of Appeal closing the case

n: Constanta port officials offered 250,000 euro for a berth infill contract
rank: officials of the Constanta Maritime Ports Administration
d: The Constanta Maritime Ports Administration runs Romania's main Black Sea port. In July 2025 two men were convicted on plea agreements after admitting they tried to obtain a contract worth more than 124 million lei. Prosecutors said T.L., an employee of firms operating in the port, promised 250,000 euro to officials of the administration and paid 25,000 euro in cash through an intermediary as an advance, so that a firm he coordinated would win a contract for infilling and site works at Berth 99 worth over 25 million euro. B.R., an administrator of another firm, offered about 400 euro to an official of the same body to speed up permits for a port project. They received two years and four months and one year and four months, both suspended.
inside: Companies working in the state port paid its own officials so the port's contract and permit decisions would fall to their firms.
cite: Spotmedia, 31 July 2025, on the DNA plea agreements sent to the Constanta Tribunal

n: CAF's bid for 51 Bucharest metro trains fed by a Metrorex commission member
rank: tender evaluation commission, Metrorex
d: Metrorex is the state company that runs the Bucharest metro. On 26 June 2014 it launched a procurement for up to 51 six-car trains for metro line 5, estimated at 1,556,259,680 lei. Prosecutors said that between October 2014 and March 2015 Ovidiu Bancescu, an employee of a bidding company, persuaded Valeriu Picu, a Metrorex director on the tender commission, to pass confidential information including rivals' offers, which went to directors of the Spanish manufacturer CAF SA Bilbao, and that Picu was paid for translations through a relative's business. The Bucharest Court of Appeal convicted Picu and Bancescu of misusing non-public information, each to one year and six months suspended with 60 days of unpaid work; Bancescu denied the charges. A winner was declared but no contract was signed.
inside: A bidder for the state metro company's train order got its own tender commission to hand over rivals' offers, and paid the official who passed them.
cite: Economica.net, 28 April 2015, on the DNA investigation; Observator, on the indictment; Adevarul, 18 November 2017, on the final Bucharest Court of Appeal convictions

n: CNAIR road maintenance director fed tender data to a snow-clearing firm
rank: director, national roads and motorways maintenance directorate, CNAIR
d: CNAIR, the Compania Nationala de Administrare a Infrastructurii Rutiere, is Romania's state roads company. In November 2022 anticorruption prosecutors in Timisoara sent Florea Dascalu, director of its national roads and motorways maintenance directorate, for trial in pre-trial detention for bribery and influence peddling in continued form and for letting unauthorised people see non-public information. Prosecutors allege that a company administrator, treated in the case as a witness, gave him 37,060 lei in money and benefits between 7 May and 22 October 2022, in three instalments, the last of which was a caught-in-the-act payment, so that he would use his influence to help the businessman win road aesthetics and snow clearing work and would pass him non-public data to help win CNAIR tenders.
inside: A roads contractor paid the state road company's maintenance director for the tender information and the influence that would win it the work.
cite: Agerpres, 14 November 2022, on the DNA Timisoara indictment sent to the Arad Tribunal

n: Shipbuilding consortium paid Romania's sea rescue agency chief to keep paying
rank: director, Romanian Agency for Maritime Life Saving (ARSVOM)
d: ARSVOM, the Romanian Agency for Maritime Life Saving, is a body under the transport ministry that bought rescue vessels. In January 2026 anticorruption prosecutors sent a plea agreement to the Constanta Tribunal in which its former director, Manole Daniel, admitted taking a bribe and accepted three years suspended with 90 days of unpaid work. Prosecutors allege that on 21 June 2021 he received 88,162 lei indirectly from M.I., who runs several companies, in return for promising not to obstruct contracts and to ensure payments without delay. ARSVOM had signed four 2020 contracts worth 101,774,750 lei with a consortium for three search-and-rescue vessels and a depollution vessel. M.I. is separately charged with claiming influence over transport ministry decision-makers for a 2 per cent commission.
inside: A vessel-building consortium paid the head of the state agency buying its ships so the contracts ran smoothly and its payments were not delayed.
cite: Antena 3 CNN, 8 January 2026, on the DNA plea agreement sent to the Constanta Tribunal

n: Land handed to the Ilfov forestry director after an unqualified man was hired
rank: director, Ilfov Forestry Directorate, Romsilva
d: Romsilva is Romania's state forestry company and the Ilfov Forestry Directorate is its branch around Bucharest. In November 2021 anticorruption prosecutors sent Cezar Mihail Raduta, the directorate's then director and by then Romsilva's deputy general director, for trial for bribery and abuse of office. Prosecutors allege that in 2016 he and an HR engineer allowed Alexandru Constantin to be hired as a hunting guard although he lacked the required forestry training, which prosecutors say harmed Romsilva's interest, and that Raduta later received from him a plot of about 1,169 square metres in Corbeanca through a swap for a very old car valued at no more than 5,000 euro. Romsilva had not said whether it would join the case as a civil party.
inside: A man wanting a job at the state forestry company got it without the required training, and land later passed to the director who approved his hiring.
cite: Agerpres, 22 November 2021, on the DNA indictment sent to the Bucharest Tribunal

n: Consultancy provider's commission ran back to Electrica's general director
rank: general director, SC Electrica SA
d: Electrica is Romania's state electricity distribution and supply group, privatised only in part. In March 2017 anticorruption prosecutors opened proceedings against Ioan Folescu, former general director of SC Electrica SA, for bribe-taking, and placed him under judicial control for 60 days from 22 March 2017. Prosecutors allege that between 2010 and 2013, while he held a leadership post at Electrica, he demanded and received a commission of 30 to 50 per cent from five consultancy contracts between Electrica and a company controlled by the service provider, totalling 6,811,328 lei. The money was said to have moved through several companies the provider controlled before intermediaries handed cash to Folescu, and was linked to awarding the contracts and performing them on advantageous terms.
inside: A consultancy supplier handed back a third to a half of its Electrica fees in cash to the company's own general director, who awarded the contracts.
cite: Bursa, 23 March 2017, citing a DNA press release

n: Asphalt firm's cash in a fridge at Romania's Barlad state roads company
rank: director, Societatea pentru Lucrari de Drumuri si Poduri Barlad
d: The Societatea pentru Lucrari de Drumuri si Poduri Barlad is a state-owned road and bridge company in eastern Romania. Anticorruption prosecutors sent its director, Daniel Buzamat, for trial for bribery and abuse of office, with the administrator of a private firm charged with bribery and instigating abuse of office and the firm itself charged as a legal person. Prosecutors allege a businessman paid Buzamat 100,000 lei in two instalments of 50,000 lei in 2022, through an intermediary who is a witness, over two contracts to asphalt 1,600 square metres of land owned by the businessman's firm. They say 4,725 square metres were asphalted, using 236 tonnes of asphalt that the accounts did not record, and that the state company lost 280,794 lei.
inside: A private landowner paid the state road company's director, and the company laid far more asphalt on his land than it was paid for.
cite: Puterea.ro, on the DNA indictment sent to the Vaslui Tribunal

n: Hidroelectrica branch service head took 732,564 lei to smooth a contract
rank: head of the development service, Hidroelectrica Bistrita branch
d: Hidroelectrica is Romania's state hydropower producer and its Bistrita hydropower branch runs plants on the Bistrita river. In October 2017 anticorruption prosecutors sent Dumitru Comastoc, head of the branch's development service, for trial, alleging that between 2009 and 2011 he demanded and received about 732,564 lei from two businessmen whose firm had signed a contract with the branch, so that the contract would run smoothly. The money was said to have been paid through 23 payment orders against eight invoices recording services that were never performed, issued by a company Comastoc controlled. Neither the businessmen nor their firm is named in the report. The case went to the Neamt Tribunal; the report carries no response from him.
inside: A contractor to the state hydropower company paid its branch's development chief, through invoices for work never done, to keep its own contract running.
cite: Bursa, 24 October 2017, on the DNA indictment sent to the Neamt Tribunal

n: Apele Romane investment director paid through a front firm for flood works
who: River Shore SRL and two businessmen
rank: director of development, investments and acquisitions, Apele Romane
d: Administratia Nationala Apele Romane manages Romania's rivers, dams and flood works. In December 2017 anticorruption prosecutors sent Vasile Ofimias, former director of its development, investments and acquisitions department, for trial for bribe-taking in continued form and money laundering. Prosecutors allege that between 2009 and 2011 two businessmen, one of them Popa Eugen Laurean, paid him 6,450,888 lei and 2,361,314 lei through SC River Shore SRL, described as a front company that issued twelve invoices to disguise the payments, plus a Volvo worth 43,999 euro and a plot in Bihor. In return he allegedly backed a revised estimate for a reservoir on the Mara river, passed funding information, and supported the firm in obtaining direct-award works contracts after the 2010 floods.
inside: A construction firm paid the official who ranked and funded state water works, and the direct-award contracts that followed the 2010 floods went to it.
cite: Stiripesurse, 28 December 2017, on the DNA Oradea indictment sent to the Satu Mare Tribunal

n: Krisda group won 9.9bn baht of Krung Thai Bank loans through the bank's officers
rank: Krung Thai Bank executives and credit officers
d: Krung Thai Bank is Thailand's state-majority commercial bank. On 26 August 2015 the Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted 26 defendants over more than 9.9 billion baht of loans to companies in the property group Krisda Mahanakhon. The court found that RK Professional and Golden Technology Industrial Park obtained the money under false pretences, and that about 4.45 billion baht went on buying preferred shares rather than the stated purposes. Former executives, among them Viroj Nualkhae, and credit officers were jailed for 18 or 12 years and ordered, jointly with the borrower companies, to repay the bank. Two defendants were acquitted because charges were not notified at the inquiry stage. The case against former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra was severed after he failed to appear.
inside: A property group's borrowing reached inside a state bank's credit decisions: its own officers approved 9.9 billion baht of loans and were ordered to repay the bank.
cite: Thaipublica, 26 August 2015, reporting the Supreme Court Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions verdict

n: US film producers paid Tourism Authority of Thailand's governor $1.8m
org_label: Gerald and Patricia Green (US film producers)
rank: Governor, Tourism Authority of Thailand
d: The Tourism Authority of Thailand is the state body that promotes Thai tourism. Its former governor, Juthamas Siriwan, took about 1.8 million US dollars between 2002 and 2007 from the American film producers Gerald and Patricia Green, who wanted the rights to run the Bangkok International Film Festival and other tourism work; Khaosod English reports the deals earned them more than 13 million dollars. Bangkok's Central Criminal Court for Corruption and Misconduct Cases convicted her on eleven counts in March 2017 and jailed her for 50 years, the maximum under Thai law, with her daughter Jittisopa, into whose accounts the money was moved, jailed for 44 years. The Greens had been sentenced in the United States in 2010 to six months. Later appeal reports say the 50-year term was upheld.
inside: Two American film producers' money bought the state tourism agency's governor, so Thailand's film festival rights and tourism work went to their companies.
cite: Khaosod English, 30 March 2017; Khaosod English, 16 November 2020 and Thaiger headlines on the appeal

n: Felda chairman Isa Samad took RM3m over a RM160m Kuching hotel purchase
org_label: unnamed payers in the Merdeka Palace hotel purchase
who: bribe payers in the hotel deal
rank: Chairman, Federal Land Development Authority (Felda)
d: The Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) is Malaysia's state body for smallholder settlement schemes, and also runs commercial ventures. Mohd Isa Abdul Samad, its chairman from 2011 to 2017, was convicted by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on 3 February 2021 on nine counts of taking 3,090,000 ringgit to help approve Felda Investment Corporation's 160 million ringgit purchase of the Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites in Kuching, Sarawak, without board approval. The money came from Ikhwan Zaidel of Gegasan Abadi Properties Sdn Bhd, through Isa's former political special officer Muhammad Zahid Md Arip. The Court of Appeal acquitted him in March 2024; on 10 February 2026 the Federal Court allowed the prosecution's appeal, restored the six-year sentence and the 15.45 million ringgit fine, and ordered him to begin serving.
inside: Bribes from outside the state agency reached Felda's chairman, and Felda then approved a 160 million ringgit hotel purchase its board had not cleared.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 10 February 2026, on the Federal Court ruling

n: MARA Inc's ex-chairman charged over RM20.45m in Melbourne property bribes
org_label: unnamed payers in MARA Inc's Melbourne property deals
who: payers in the Melbourne property deals
rank: Chairman, MARA Incorporated
d: MARA Incorporated is the commercial arm of Majlis Amanah Rakyat, the Malaysian government body for Bumiputera economic advancement. Its former chairman, Mohammad Lan Allani, pleaded not guilty in two Kuala Lumpur Sessions Courts in February 2021 to 22 charges brought after a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission investigation: 20 of taking bribes and two of money laundering, involving 20.45 million ringgit, over MARA Inc's purchases of Melbourne property. The Edge Malaysia reports the holdings include the Dudley International House student block, an apartment block bought in 2013 that The Age said was overpaid by 4.75 million Australian dollars, and a Swanston Street building; the article does not say who paid him. Bail was set at 400,000 ringgit.
inside: Prosecutors say money from MARA Inc's Melbourne property deals reached its own chairman, so the state investment arm paid above value for the buildings.
cite: The Edge Malaysia, 5 February 2021

n: Alcatel paid Telekom Malaysia staff for rival bid data, winning $85m work
rank: Telekom Malaysia employees handling tenders
d: Telekom Malaysia is the country's main telecommunications company; the US Securities and Exchange Commission's complaint says Malaysia's finance ministry then owned about 43 per cent of it and could veto its major spending. The complaint, filed in Florida in December 2010 as part of Alcatel-Lucent's foreign bribery settlement, says staff of Alcatel's Malaysian arm paid Telekom Malaysia employees between October 2004 and February 2006 for documents and budget information on live tenders and for competitors' prices, with the local management's consent. It states that these bribes assisted Alcatel Malaysia in obtaining a contract with a potential value of 85 million dollars. Two consultants were paid 200,000 and 500,000 dollars through US accounts for reports the SEC says they did not appear to have provided.
inside: A French equipment maker bought Telekom Malaysia employees' confidential tender information, so the state-controlled carrier's 85 million dollar contract went to Alcatel.
cite: SEC v. Alcatel-Lucent, complaint filed 27 December 2010, S.D. Fla., paragraphs 14 and 55-63

n: Traders charged with paying RM95,500 to a Tenaga Nasional enforcement man
org_label: operators of raided premises in Melaka
rank: technician, TNB Special Engagement Against Losses unit
d: Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) is Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility, and it enforces the law against electricity theft. On 26 April 2022 two men, Tey Boon Sin, a director of an advertising company, and Leang Tin Sheng, who is unemployed, pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in Melaka to ten charges of paying a total of 95,500 ringgit to Mohd Amir Mohamad, a technician in the Southern Zone of TNB's Special Engagement Against Losses unit. Utusan Malaysia reports the payments were meant to persuade him to take no legal action over an offence under the Electricity Supply Act 1990, and in one man's case to obtain information about raided premises. Bail was set at 15,000 and 10,000 ringgit.
inside: Prosecutors say outsiders facing electricity-theft action paid 95,500 ringgit to a TNB enforcement technician, so the utility's own enforcement spared their premises.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 26 April 2022

n: Trader fined for paying a Tenaga Nasional officer to drop a power-theft case
rank: Tenaga Nasional Berhad enforcement officer
d: Tenaga Nasional Berhad is Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility. On 20 March 2024 the Ipoh Sessions Court convicted a trader, R. K. Sandra Segar, on his own guilty plea of paying 3,000 ringgit and then 3,500 ringgit, in March and April 2021, to Shamsul Ariffin Rahaman, a TNB officer, through an intermediary, so that the officer would take no enforcement action over electricity Segar had dishonestly used at his premises in Taiping. He was charged under section 214 of the Penal Code, fined 20,000 ringgit with two months' jail if he failed to pay, and 8,000 ringgit of bribe money was forfeited to the government under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
inside: A trader's cash reached a TNB officer, so the state utility's enforcement against the electricity he had dishonestly used was not pursued.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 20 March 2024

n: Railway engineer charged over payments not to halt two KTMB station projects
rank: civil engineer and project manager, KTMB project management department
d: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is Malaysia's state-owned railway operator. On 5 August 2020 Mohd Amin Muhammad N Hushaimi, a former civil engineer in KTMB's project management department, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to two charges brought by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission of taking 1,450 ringgit from Mohd Nizam Hasan, in two payments into his bank account in July and September 2015. The charges allege the money induced him, as project manager, not to recommend a temporary stop-work order over safety concerns on works at the Abdullah Hukum station and the planned Kajang 2 integrated commuter station. Bail was set at 6,000 ringgit a charge; Sinar Harian reports he had been dismissed and was selling laksa.
inside: Prosecutors say a payment from outside reached KTMB's project manager, so the state railway did not stop building work it had safety concerns about.
cite: Sinar Harian, 5 August 2020

n: Boat supplier paid RM260,000 to a Melaka state river corporation manager
rank: manager, business and product development, PPSPM
d: Perbadanan Pembangunan Sungai dan Pantai Melaka (PPSPM) is the Melaka state corporation that develops the state's river and coast and runs the Melaka River Cruise. On 13 December 2024 the Melaka Sessions Court convicted Mohd Fariz Mohd Ali, a manager in its business and product development division, on four amended charges of taking 260,000 ringgit in cash from the chief executive of LEC Impressions Sdn Bhd at four meetings in 2017, so that the company would win the contract to supply ten Melaka River Cruise boats. The court said the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt. He was jailed for two years, the terms running concurrently, and fined 1.3 million ringgit in total. A stay was granted pending his appeal.
inside: A boat supplier's chief executive paid 260,000 ringgit to a Melaka state corporation's manager, and the corporation's ten-boat supply contract went to his company.
cite: Sinar Harian, 13 December 2024

n: TNB tender secretary fined after helping a bidder win RM4.33m contract
org_label: unnamed company awarded TNB's 'Project ABC' tender
rank: assistant engineer and secretary of a TNB tender evaluation
d: Tenaga Nasional Berhad is Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility. On 18 November 2025 the Ipoh Sessions Court fined Zamhuri Ahmad Shatiry, a former TNB assistant engineer, 150,000 ringgit, with six months' jail if he failed to pay, after he pleaded guilty to cheating by concealing his interest in a tender evaluation. While serving as secretary of the evaluation for the 4.33 million ringgit tender known as Project ABC, he helped the bidding company prepare its bill of quantities and detailed pricing without declaring that interest, and the tender was then awarded to that company. RTM reports he received goods worth 140,000 ringgit at the end of 2018. The report does not name the company.
inside: Goods worth 140,000 ringgit from a bidder reached the TNB engineer running its tender evaluation, and the utility awarded that firm the 4.33 million ringgit job.
cite: Berita RTM, 18 November 2025

n: Bitcoin miners' agents jailed for offering RM15,000 to a TNB officer
org_label: bitcoin mining operators in Negeri Sembilan
rank: Tenaga Nasional Berhad Southern Zone enforcement officer
d: Tenaga Nasional Berhad, Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility, enforces the law against electricity theft. On 8 March 2022 the Seremban Sessions Court sentenced two traders, Goh How Keong and Gan Tze Lee, on their guilty pleas, to 14 days' jail and a 75,000 ringgit fine each for offering 15,000 ringgit in cash on 5 November 2021 to an officer of TNB's Southern Zone so that he would take no enforcement action against operators of premises suspected of stealing electricity for bitcoin mining around Negeri Sembilan. Both paid the fine. The court ordered 83,380 ringgit of bitcoin-related proceeds forfeited to the government through the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.
inside: Money from bitcoin-mining operators was offered to a TNB enforcement officer so the state utility would leave premises stealing its electricity alone.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 8 March 2022

n: Crypto miners allegedly paid a Provincial Electricity Authority assistant governor
org_label: cryptocurrency mining network in Samut Sakhon and Uthai Thani
rank: Assistant Governor, Provincial Electricity Authority
d: The Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) is the Thai state enterprise that distributes electricity outside Bangkok. On 8 May 2026 the Department of Special Investigation said it had sent six inquiry files, running to 2,266 pages, to the National Anti-Corruption Commission over a PEA assistant governor and accomplices, ten people in all, alleged to have unlawfully received property or other benefits from a group drawing electricity illegally for digital currency mining in Samut Sakhon and Uthai Thani. Investigators seized 3,642 mining machines, put the damage to PEA at more than 3 billion baht and said more than 5 billion baht moved through the network; 19 million baht in cash and bank funds was seized. The announcement reports no decision by the commission.
inside: Investigators say a crypto-mining network's payments reached a PEA assistant governor, so the state power utility's officers did not act on its illegal electricity use.
cite: Department of Special Investigation (Thailand) announcement, 8 May 2026

n: Czech supplier Skoda JS built an 18% markup into Energoatom tenders
rank: Atomkomplekt procurement division, Energoatom
d: Energoatom is the state company that runs Ukraine's nuclear power stations, and Atomkomplekt is the division that buys its equipment. Investigators say the Czech supplier Skoda JS agreed to raise its bids by about 18% between 2009 and 2012 so that a pre-agreed kickback could be paid out of the higher price, costing Energoatom about EUR 6.4 million; one additional agreement is alleged to have added more than CZK 97 million to a contract. The money is said to have gone through Bradcrest Investment S.A., a Panamanian company, to the former MP Mykola Martynenko. NABU served suspicion in October 2017 and the indictment reached the High Anti-Corruption Court in October 2019, where the case is still being heard.
inside: A foreign equipment supplier agreed with insiders at the state nuclear company's buying division to inflate its own bids, so Energoatom paid a markup that funded kickbacks.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2018; Transparency International Ukraine HACC case file 52018000000000153 (case 761/8826/19)

n: Austrian firm Steuermann overcharged Ukraine's SchidGZK by $17.28m
rank: general director and deputy general director, SchidGZK
d: SchidGZK, the Eastern Mining and Processing Plant, is the state enterprise that mines and processes Ukraine's uranium. NABU says a 2013 tender worth over USD 414 million went to the Austrian-registered firm Steuermann, which investigators allege was controlled by the former MP Mykola Martynenko, and that 600 tonnes of uranium concentrate delivered between 2014 and 2016 were priced about 30% above the market, overcharging the plant by USD 17.28 million. The plant's general director is treated as an accessory and its deputy general director for economics as an executor. Martynenko was detained in April 2017; the episode was split off in June 2022 and remains before the High Anti-Corruption Court.
inside: An outside trading firm the investigation links to a sitting-era MP sold the state uranium plant its own output supply at inflated prices through the plant's own senior managers.
cite: NABU half-year reports, first half 2017 and first half 2018; Transparency International Ukraine HACC case file 52018000000000153

n: Bullet Line's used T-72 engines sold to Ukraine's Lviv armour plant
rank: director and deputy director for commercial matters, Lviv Armour Plant
d: The Lviv Armoured Plant is a state enterprise that overhauls tanks for Ukraine's army. NABU says that in 2015 it bought 40 engines for T-72 tanks from the private firm TOV Bullet Line, paying 28.56 million hryvnia, and that the engines were used units that had earlier been sold off as surplus and only overhauled. The reported damage is 14.15 million hryvnia. Those served with suspicion include the plant's director, its deputy director for commercial matters, the founder of Bullet Line, and the chief and a department head of the armed forces' central armour directorate. The indictment was sent to court in July 2018.
inside: A private supplier, with the plant's director and commercial deputy, sold the state tank-repair works second-hand engines at new prices, so its purchasing decision served the firm.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2018

n: Diesel supplier's price rises cost Ukraine's railways 115m hryvnia
rank: officials of the Centre for Procurement, Ukrzaliznytsia
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company. NABU says that after TOV VOG Aero Jet won a tender for diesel fuel in March 2016, the contract price was raised through additional agreements signed on 23, 25 and 29 March, overcharging the railway's procurement centre by 92 million hryvnia on the civil claim and by 115 million hryvnia on the criminal one. A court of first instance voided the additional agreement on 27 July 2017. NABU later sued the firm's successor, TOV Volens Trade, for 92 million hryvnia, and the cases of three railway officials charged with abuse of office were sent to court in March 2018.
inside: A fuel supplier had the state railway's buying officials sign price rises days after winning the tender, so the railway paid more than its own competition had set.
cite: NABU half-year reports, first half 2017 and first half 2018

n: Onyshchenko's firms took Ukrgazvydobuvannya gas below market price
rank: two former deputy chairmen of the board, Ukrgazvydobuvannya
d: Ukrgazvydobuvannya is the state gas producer, wholly owned by Naftogaz. NABU says that between January 2013 and January 2016 companies controlled by the MP Oleksandr Onyshchenko took part in joint-activity agreements with it, and that gas from those projects was sold through exchanges at low prices to buyers linked to him. The reported loss is about 1.6 billion hryvnia, of which 740 million hryvnia was confirmed by expert review; an earlier estimate was about 3 billion hryvnia. Two former deputy chairmen of the board and a department head are among the accused. Indictments against 15 people were sent to court and 10 plea agreements were reached.
inside: An MP's private gas firms worked through the state producer's own board deputies, so joint-venture gas was sold cheaply to buyers connected to him rather than at market price.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2017

n: Grain traders left Ukraine's state grain corporation $60.56m unpaid
rank: former head of the State Food and Grain Corporation
d: The State Food and Grain Corporation of Ukraine is a state joint-stock company that trades grain. NABU says that grain shipped between July and October 2014 through non-resident intermediary companies was never paid for, leaving more than USD 60.56 million outstanding on about 300 thousand tonnes, and puts the corporation's total losses at 1.6 billion hryvnia. A representative of an international grain trader was detained on 24 January 2017. Seven people were served with suspicion, including the corporation's former head and a deputy of its financial and economic department; two cases were sent to court and about 70 million hryvnia was returned voluntarily.
inside: Outside grain intermediaries bought through the state corporation's own head and finance staff, so the corporation shipped grain on terms that left it unpaid.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2017

n: Radio altimeters sold to Ukrspetsexport at nearly seven times the price
org_label: supplier linked to a former NSDC deputy secretary's son
rank: former chief executive, Ukrspetsexport
d: Ukrspetsexport is the state concern that handles Ukraine's arms exports and imports. NABU says that between August 2016 and February 2017 it bought radio altimeters at prices inflated almost sevenfold from a company the investigation links to the son of a former first deputy secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, overpaying about USD 450 thousand. The former chief executive of the state concern was served with suspicion. The report says the suspects are wanted internationally and that the High Anti-Corruption Court authorised a special pre-trial investigation in their absence, so the case has not reached trial on the merits.
inside: A supplier connected to a senior official's family reached the state arms-trading concern through its own chief executive, which bought aircraft parts at nearly seven times their price.
cite: NABU report 2023

n: Estonian shell firm's blanks cost Ukraine's state printer 450m hryvnia
rank: former director, Polygraph Combine Ukraina
d: The Polygraph Combine Ukraina is the state printing works that produces passports and other secure documents. NABU says that between 2013 and 2016 the materials for document blanks were bought through an Estonian shell company and resold to the works at markups of four to six times, causing losses of more than 450 million hryvnia. Suspicion was served on 21 July 2023 on the works' former director and a former head of one of its departments, and documents were sent to Estonia so that suspicion notices could be served on two Estonian nationals, the shell company's owner and its manager. The investigation was still running.
inside: An offshore shell firm sold the state document printer its raw materials at several times the price, with the works' own director and department head arranging the purchases.
cite: NABU report 2023

n: Power plants run by an MP took Naftogaz gas at the heating price
org_label: Novoyavorivska and Novorozdilska heat and power plants
rank: Naftogaz gas supply contracts
d: Naftogaz is Ukraine's state oil and gas company. NABU says that between 2013 and 2017 the Novoyavorivska and Novorozdilska combined heat and power plants, controlled by a sitting member of parliament, bought gas from Naftogaz under contracts at the preferential price meant for heating households, then used it to generate electricity sold at the market price, causing losses of more than 2.1 billion hryvnia. The MP was named as the sixth suspect in October 2023 and the report says he was wanted; the cases of the other participants had already been sent to court. The investigation was continuing.
inside: Privately run power plants obtained Naftogaz supply contracts at the subsidised heating price and resold the output as electricity, so the state company's pricing decision served them.
cite: NABU report 2023

n: Supplier group's kit sold to Ukraine's state communications service
rank: head and deputy head, State Service of Special Communications
d: The State Service of Special Communications and Information Protection runs Ukraine's secure government communications. NABU says that between 2020 and 2022 classified purchases of equipment and software were arranged so that two companies belonging to one owner's group would win, and that a state enterprise within the service paid more than 285 million hryvnia for goods worth about 223 million hryvnia, with more than 62 million hryvnia alleged to have been stolen. Suspicion was served on 20 November 2023 on the head and deputy head of the service, the chief executive and an employee of the state enterprise, the owner described as organiser, and a subordinate. Crypto assets worth USD 1.5 million were seized.
inside: An outside owner's companies reached the secure communications service through its head and deputy head, so secret procurement decisions sent it contracts above the equipment's value.
cite: NABU report 2023

n: Electricity trader took 716m hryvnia of Ukrenergo power unpaid
rank: Ukrenergo electricity sales
d: Ukrenergo is the state company that runs Ukraine's high-voltage grid and sells electricity on it. NABU says that a trading company which already owed the state company money bought electricity worth 716 million hryvnia under bank guarantees issued in breach of procedure, resold it, and moved the proceeds to a controlled foreign company, leaving Ukrenergo unpaid. Four participants were served with suspicion and more than 700 million hryvnia was seized in accounts. The report does not name the trader or the officials involved, and the investigation was still running at the end of the reporting period, so the allegations remain unproven.
inside: An outside electricity trader obtained supply from the state grid company on guarantees issued against procedure, so Ukrenergo delivered power it was never paid for.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Contractor's $424,000 bribe sought at Ukraine's Chornomorsk port
rank: head of legal support service, Chornomorsk sea port
d: The Chornomorsk Sea Trade Port is a state enterprise on Ukraine's Black Sea coast. NABU says the head of the port's legal support service, a former part-time adviser to the port's director and the director of a contractor company together demanded a bribe of USD 424,000, described in the report as almost half a million dollars, to secure a contract assigning a debt claim of the port to another company. All the participants were served with suspicion. The report does not name the firms or the individuals, and the case had not reached court in the reporting period, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: A contractor's director worked with the port's legal chief and a former adviser to the director, so a state port's debt claim would be assigned on the payers' terms.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Transformers reached Ukraine's railways through a Bulgarian shell firm
rank: Ukrzaliznytsia procurement officials
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company. NABU says a chosen company was selected as the supplier of power transformers and sold them to the railway through a Bulgarian shell firm at nearly double the price, with 94.8 million hryvnia taken. Seven people were served with suspicion. NABU's report for the first half of 2025 records that a man described as a member of the organised group in the same 94.8 million hryvnia transformer procurement was extradited to Ukraine. The report names neither the supplier nor the railway officials, and the case had not come to trial, so the figures are the investigators' own.
inside: A transformer supplier used a foreign shell company and the railway's own buyers to double the price the state railway paid for its substation equipment.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024; NABU report, first half 2025

n: Pneumatic tool supplier overcharged Ukraine's railways by 36m hryvnia
rank: Ukrzaliznytsia tender committee
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company, and one of the largest buyers in the country. NABU says that in a separate episode from its cable and transformer cases, a group of companies won a tender for pneumatic tools and then supplied them at inflated value, with an overpayment of 36 million hryvnia. Nine people were served with suspicion. The report does not name the supplier or the railway officials who handled the tender, and the case had not reached court during the reporting period, so the amounts and the mechanism are as the investigators describe them.
inside: An outside supplier group won the state railway's tool tender and billed above value, which the investigation says the railway's own tender staff allowed.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Firms billed Ukraine's railways 17m hryvnia for track repairs undone
rank: Ukrzaliznytsia management
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company. NABU says that predetermined companies were given contracts to repair track machines, did not carry out the work, and forged completion documents, and that this was done with the help of the railway's management, costing 17 million hryvnia. All the participants in the scheme were served with suspicion. The report does not name the contractors or the managers, and the case had not reached trial during the reporting period, so the sum and the account of how the contracts were awarded are the investigators' own.
inside: Outside repair firms were handed the state railway's track machine contracts and paid for work the investigation says was never done, with the railway's own managers helping.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Bankrupt contractor's control kit inflated 170m at Energoatom design arm
rank: former head of a department, Atomproektinzhynirynh branch of Energoatom
d: Atomproektinzhynirynh is the design branch of Energoatom, the state company that runs Ukraine's nuclear plants. NABU says that a company controlled by an entrepreneur who organised the scheme was chosen to supply automated control equipment for the Tashlyk pumped-storage hydroelectric plant, although it had already missed work deadlines and was in bankruptcy proceedings, and that the cost of the equipment was inflated by 170 million hryvnia. Two people were served with suspicion: the entrepreneur and a former head of a department of the branch. The investigation was still running at the end of the reporting period, so the figure is the investigators' own.
inside: An outside contractor already in bankruptcy was picked to supply a nuclear plant's control equipment through a departmental head inside Energoatom's design branch.
cite: NABU report, first half 2025

n: Foreign buyer took 106,000 tonnes of Ukrainian state corn unpaid
rank: officials of the State Food and Grain Corporation
d: The State Food and Grain Corporation of Ukraine is a state grain trading company. NABU and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office say that under export contracts entered into in 2021 about 106,000 tonnes of feed corn worth more than 776 million hryvnia were shipped to a foreign buyer without full payment, with the buyer receiving the original shipping documents and forged bills of lading allegedly used to conceal what had happened. Five people were served with suspicion. The report does not name the buyer or the corporation's officials, and gives no later stage, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: A foreign buyer obtained export contracts from the state grain company's own contracting officials and took delivery of the grain and its documents without paying in full.
cite: NABU report, first half 2025

n: Sleeper suppliers overcharged Ukraine's railways by 13m hryvnia
rank: Industrial Enterprises Directorate, Ukrzaliznytsia
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company. NABU says that between 2014 and 2016 its Industrial Enterprises Directorate, later the Industry Management Centre branch, bought sleepers and beams from commercial companies at prices about 80% above the market, overpaying more than 13 million hryvnia. The case was sent to court on 29 January 2021. The report also records a 2017 plea-agreement verdict against one manager and says a 20 million hryvnia confiscation was later reported to be unenforceable. The supplying companies are not named in the report, and the main case had no verdict at the time it was written.
inside: Outside suppliers sold the state railway's industrial arm sleepers at about 80% above market, which the investigation says the directorate's own managers arranged.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2021

n: Boryspil airport's premises leased below price without competition
rank: head of the enterprise and head of the lease services department, Boryspil airport
d: Boryspil International Airport is a state enterprise and Ukraine's main airport. NABU says that preliminary lease contracts for airport premises were concluded with business entities at understated prices and outside any competitive procedure, causing damage of more than 16.5 million hryvnia on two contracts. Those charged are the enterprise's head and the head of its lease services department. The case was sent to court on 15 June 2021. The report does not name the firms that took the leases and records no verdict, so the figures and the account of how the contracts were made are the investigators' own.
inside: Outside firms obtained leases of a state airport's premises at understated prices without competition, arranged by the airport's head and its lease services chief.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2021

n: Ukrprofmed billed Ukraine's state hospital builder for kit never sent
rank: director, Ukrmedproektbud
d: Ukrmedproektbud is the state enterprise that acted as client for building work at the Okhmatdyt children's hospital in Kyiv. NABU says that more than 30 million hryvnia of budget money was paid for equipment that was never delivered, with TOV Ukrprofmed acting as general contractor. Those under investigation include the state enterprise's director and the heads of the contractor and of the firms meant to store the equipment. The investigation of two suspects was completed on 9 April 2021 and a third person was reported to be wanted. Court rulings on returning the money are mentioned in the report, but their enforcement was blocked.
inside: A general contractor was paid by the state hospital-building enterprise for equipment that never arrived, with the enterprise's own director among those investigated.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2021

n: VAB Bank's inflated valuations won a 1.2bn hryvnia loan from the NBU
rank: National Bank of Ukraine refinancing decision
d: The National Bank of Ukraine is the country's central bank and can lend to commercial banks in difficulty. NABU says that in October 2014 VAB Bank asked for a stabilisation loan of 1.2 billion hryvnia for two years and obtained it although it had submitted incomplete documents and had inflated the value of the property offered as security almost 25 times through forged valuation reports. Seven more suspects were added on 24 May 2021, bringing the total to 17, and the bank's owner was reported to be wanted. The report records no verdict, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: A failing commercial bank got the central bank's own officials to approve 1.2 billion hryvnia of refinancing against security the investigation says was valued almost 25 times too high.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2021

n: Supplier's 980 thousand hryvnia benefit inside Ukraine's bomb squad
rank: former head of the Explosives Service Department, National Police
d: The Explosives Service Department of Ukraine's National Police buys the equipment and protective suits used by police bomb disposal teams. NABU says that a negotiated procurement was used and the absence of competition disguised, so that a private entrepreneur supplied the equipment; the police paid 3 million hryvnia and the unlawful benefit involved was 980 thousand hryvnia. The former head of the department was served with suspicion on 15 April 2021 and placed under night house arrest, and the entrepreneur's bail was set at 158.9 thousand hryvnia. The report records no verdict, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: An outside supplier reached the police bomb squad's buying department through its own head, who the investigation says staged a procurement without real competition.
cite: NABU half-year report, first half 2021

n: Reverse vending machines bought by Ukrekoresursy via a Panama firm
org_label: unnamed seller with a Panamanian intermediary
rank: former director, Ukrekoresursy
d: Ukrekoresursy is a state enterprise working on waste and recycling. NABU says that instead of negotiating with the manufacturer RecycleTech its officials bought 100 reverse vending machines for USD 100 thousand from another company, using a Panama-registered company as intermediary, and that almost 14 million hryvnia of budget money was spent on equipment described as largely unusable. The former director was among those served with suspicion and was sent to a pre-trial detention centre by the High Anti-Corruption Court with bail set at 3.7 million hryvnia as an alternative. The report records no verdict.
inside: An outside seller and an offshore intermediary were chosen over the manufacturer by the state waste enterprise's own director, so it paid for machines said to be largely unusable.
cite: NABU report, first half 2022

n: Two linked firms won a Southwestern Railway tender, costing 9.6m
rank: acting head of the Southwestern Railway branch, Ukrzaliznytsia
d: The Southwestern Railway is a branch of Ukrzaliznytsia, Ukraine's state railway company. NABU says that in a tender announced in 2017 for power devices for passenger carriages, two linked companies received the railway's approval and won, causing losses of 9.6 million hryvnia. The acting head of the branch, who chaired the tender committee, was charged under part 2 of article 364 of the criminal code, which covers abuse of office. The investigation was opened on 19 July 2017, suspicion was served on 23 September 2021 and the case materials were opened to the defence on 31 March 2022. The report records no verdict.
inside: Two connected outside suppliers were approved and awarded a state railway branch's carriage equipment tender by the official who chaired its tender committee.
cite: NABU report, first half 2022

n: Railway PCR test tender priced at 1,280 hryvnia against 837 on market
rank: Ukrzaliznytsia procurement officials
d: Ukrzaliznytsia is Ukraine's state railway company, which bought PCR tests for coronavirus for its staff. NABU says a predetermined company was to win the tender at 1,280 hryvnia a test against a market price of 837 hryvnia, and estimates the overpayment on more than 11 thousand tests at almost 5 million hryvnia. The railway's own audit and security units had flagged the price. Participants in the scheme were served with suspicion and the scheme was stopped before any payment was made, so no money was lost. The report names neither the company nor the officials and records no verdict.
inside: An outside supplier was lined up to win the state railway's test tender at well above the market price, with railway officials arranging the award before it was stopped.
cite: NABU report, first half 2022

n: Suppliers billed Ukraine's state justice IT firm 7.7m for services undone
org_label: companies linked to the defendants' associates
rank: general director and two deputies, Derzhinformyust
d: Derzhinformyust is the state enterprise that ran information technology for Ukraine's justice ministry. NABU says that between January 2014 and February 2015 companies controlled by associates of the defendants were paid for supplying the TrueConf video conferencing software and related services that were allegedly never provided, with losses of more than 7.7 million hryvnia; one supplier's registered field of business was lifting equipment rather than information technology. Those charged are the general director, two deputies and the heads of two private companies. Six requests for international legal assistance were sent. The report records no verdict, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: Outside companies were paid by the justice ministry's IT enterprise for software services the investigation says were never delivered, arranged through its general director and deputies.
cite: NABU report, first half 2022

n: Private firm got 62 Ukrtelefilm properties for a fifth of their value
rank: former general director, Ukrtelefilm
d: Ukrtelefilm is a state television production enterprise. NABU says a private company acquired the property rights to 62 real estate objects for 14.5 million hryvnia when their estimated market value was 82.23 million hryvnia, a loss of 67.73 million hryvnia. Those served with suspicion in December 2021 include the enterprise's former general director for 2016 and 2017, a former deputy head of the state committee for television and radio broadcasting for 2016 to 2020, a former head of its legal service, and a deputy director of the private company. Materials were opened to them on 30 May 2022 and the case is before the High Anti-Corruption Court.
inside: An outside company bought a state film enterprise's buildings far below their valuation, in a sale the investigation says its own director and legal chief arranged.
cite: NABU report, first half 2022

n: Tractor supplier won Forests of Ukraine lots after cheaper bid rejected
rank: executive director and head of the procurement division, Forests of Ukraine
d: Forests of Ukraine is the state enterprise that manages the country's forests. Prosecutors say that between November 2023 and February 2024 its executive director and the head of the procurement division in its procurement department acted in prior conspiracy to reject a cheaper bid in open tenders for 25 tractors, citing an alleged failure to meet technical requirements, and awarded three lots to a company whose bids were higher, causing damage of more than 8.1 million hryvnia. The rejected bids differed in listing an oil pressure gauge rather than an indicator. The Economic Security Bureau investigated and the indictment was sent to Kyiv's Pechersk district court; no verdict has been reported.
inside: An outside supplier won the state forestry company's tractor lots at a higher price after its buying chiefs disqualified a cheaper rival on a technical wording difference.
cite: Economic Security Bureau and Prosecutor General's Office, via Ekonomichna Pravda

n: Chernivtsi businessmen's grey imports cleared at Vadul-Siret customs
org_label: Chernivtsi businessmen including a former regional council deputy
rank: former head and officers, Chernivtsi customs office
d: The Chernivtsi customs office controls Ukraine's border crossing at Vadul-Siret with Romania. NABU says businessmen from Chernivtsi, among them a former regional council deputy, moved goods through the crossing under cover of low-value cargo, and that customs officers recorded loaded vehicles as empty or as carrying personal effects, with damage to the state of nearly 290 million hryvnia. Three customs officers, including a former head of the office, and eight other individuals were served with suspicion. The report does not give the period and records no verdict, so the figures and the description of the scheme are the investigators' own.
inside: Importers paid their way inside a named customs office, including through a former head of it, so officers recorded their loaded lorries as empty and let the goods through.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Firm billed Kherson military administration 15 times inspection cost
rank: head of a department, Kherson regional military administration
d: The Kherson regional military administration governs the Kherson region under martial law. NABU says the head of one of its departments, a private enterprise, its owner and its director arranged a contract for the technical inspection of 107 facilities worth more than 9.9 million hryvnia when the services were actually worth 534 thousand hryvnia, more than 15 times less, and that the scheme aimed to obtain more than 7.7 million hryvnia. Suspicion was served on all the parties in April 2024. The report does not name the firm or the official and records no verdict, so the account is the investigators' own.
inside: A private contractor reached a regional administration through the head of the department that bought its services, which signed for inspections at over fifteen times their cost.
cite: NABU report, first half 2024

n: Paper suppliers' 25bn dong bought Vietnam's state education publisher's chief
org_label: Phung Vinh Hung and Minh Cuong Phat, paper suppliers
who: Phung Vinh Hung and Minh Cuong Phat
rank: chairman of the members' council, Vietnam Education Publishing House
d: The Vietnam Education Publishing House (Nha xuat ban Giao duc Viet Nam) is the state company that prints the country's school textbooks. On 16 January 2025 the Hanoi People's Court sentenced eight people. Nguyen Duc Thai, chairman of its members' council from 2017, was given 12 years for taking bribes of nearly 25 billion dong from two paper bidders, Phung Vinh Hung and Minh Cuong Phat. At their request he had paper bought through a shortened quotation process that the court said breached the bidding law and limited capable bidders. The court put the loss to the publisher at more than 10 billion dong, since repaid by the defendants' families. The two company bosses got 5 years 6 months and 36 months.
inside: Two paper suppliers paid the state textbook publisher's chairman, who then had its paper bought through a shortened process that kept better-placed bidders out.
cite: Luat su Viet Nam (lsvn.vn), 17 January 2025

n: JTC's off-contract money reached Vietnam Railways' project unit directors
rank: directors and deputy directors, Railway Project Management Unit
d: The Railway Project Management Unit (RPMU) ran railway projects for Vietnam Railways Corporation, the state rail company, using Japanese development loans. On 27 October 2015 the Hanoi People's Court convicted six of its former officers of abusing their positions after they agreed with Japan Transport Consultants, a Japanese transport consultancy, that it would pay money outside the contract. Pham Hai Bang, a former deputy director, got 12 years; Nguyen Nam Thai 11 years; Pham Quang Duy 8 years 6 months; Nguyen Van Hieu and Tran Quoc Dong, also a former deputy general director of Vietnam Railways, 7 years 6 months each; and Tran Van Luc 5 years 6 months. All six were ordered to repay 11 billion dong, and their homes were seized.
inside: A Japanese consultancy paid the state rail company's project unit outside its contract, and the unit's own directors agreed to the arrangement and loosened control of payments.
cite: VnBusiness and VTC News, 27 October 2015

n: A coal supplier paid 2.54bn dong to Viglacera Ha Long II's director
org_label: Nguyen Tien Toan's coal supply business
rank: director, Viglacera Ha Long II Joint Stock Company
d: Viglacera Ha Long II is a building-materials company in Quang Ninh province, part of the state Viglacera group. Bao Van Hoa reported on 31 May 2026 that the Quang Ninh Provincial People's Court had sentenced its former director, Nguyen Dan Que, to 15 years for taking bribes. From early 2020 the supplier Nguyen Tien Toan agreed to pay him 50,000 dong a tonne outside the contract. Between July 2020 and 30 November 2024 Toan sold the company 58,233 tonnes of coal and other goods worth over 33.2 billion dong before tax, and made 45 bank transfers to Que totalling over 2.54 billion dong, with a further 40 million dong in 2024 for use of the coal yard. Toan got 10 years.
inside: A coal supplier paid the state group's factory director by the tonne outside the contract, and in return got priority in the company's buying for over four years.
cite: Bao Van Hoa, 31 May 2026

n: A contractor's tips reached Ninh Thuan's water company deputy director
rank: deputy director, Ninh Thuan Water Supply Joint Stock Company
d: Ninh Thuan Water Supply Joint Stock Company runs the water network in Ninh Thuan province.
