On 30 August 2022 the Ninh Thuan Provincial People's Court convicted Le Xuan Phuong, director of Viet Le Company, of giving bribes and of fraud, giving him one year for the bribery and seven for the fraud. The indictment said he tipped the water company's deputy director, Nguyen Duc Cam, five times, about 200 million dong in all, to help win three packages in a water supply expansion project, and that Cam had said Viet Le was capable of the work. Phuong denied bribery, saying the money was for coffee and fuel in hard times, and said he would appeal. Cam died of illness before the trial.
inside: A contractor's payments to the state water company's deputy director preceded its three winning packages, though the payer denies bribery and the official died before trial.
cite: Bao Van Hoa, on the 30 August 2022 verdict

n: Police say buyers' bribes reached the Lao Cai steel venture's director
org_label: buyers of the plant's iron ore and coke
rank: general director, Viet Trung Mineral and Metallurgy (VTM)
d: Viet Trung Mineral and Metallurgy (VTM) owns the Lao Cai iron and steel plant and was formed by Vietnam Steel Corporation, Lao Cai Mineral Corporation and China's KISC. Sai Gon Giai Phong reported on 9 October 2026 that investigation police had proposed prosecuting 31 people. They say VTM's former general director, Bui Thanh Binh, took bribes of 62.2 billion dong, 43.8 billion from iron ore sales and 18.4 billion from coke sales, and that Lao Cai's former vice chairman Le Ngoc Hung benefited by 355 million dong and its former industry and trade director Do Truong Giang by 500 million dong. The report does not say who paid the money. No one has yet been tried.
inside: Police say buyers of the state steel venture's iron ore and coke paid its general director, with smaller sums reaching two Lao Cai province officials.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 9 October 2026

n: 686 Hanoi clinics and pharmacies paid the city health department for licences
org_label: Hanoi clinics, pharmacies and drug businesses
rank: private practice licensing division, Hanoi Department of Health
d: The Hanoi Department of Health licenses private clinics and pharmacies in the city. On the afternoon of 11 November 2026 the Hanoi People's Court sentenced 16 people from its division for managing private medical and pharmacy practice and from its inspectorate, for taking and for brokering bribes. The indictment covers 2019 to 2024, when 686 clinics, pharmacies and drug businesses paid over 8 billion dong through brokers to obtain pharmacy eligibility certificates and treatment licences; the brokers kept 850 million dong and the officials took over 3.5 billion. Nguyen Thi Huy, a division officer, got 8 years 6 months, and the deputy head To Tu Anh, whose share is put at 1.3 billion dong, got 8 years.
inside: Hundreds of clinics and pharmacies paid, through brokers, the Hanoi health department staff who appraised their licences, and the licences were duly issued.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 11 November 2026

n: A food supplier paid 13.2bn dong to Bac Ninh's school food gatekeepers
org_label: Bao An Huy Trading and Services
who: Bao An Huy Trading and Services
rank: education and training department officials and preschool principals
d: Bao An Huy Trading and Services supplied food to state preschools in Bac Ninh and Hanoi. Vietnam News reported on 11 April 2026 that the Bac Ninh Provincial People's Court had convicted 35 people: its director Nguyen Van Huy of offering bribes, and 34 officials of accepting them, among them district vice chairpersons, education and training department officials and preschool principals. Between 2013 and 2024 he paid more than 13.2 billion dong, over 500,000 US dollars, offering officials 1 to 3 per cent of monthly revenue and principals 5 to 15 per cent of contract values, and inflating food prices to 1 to 1.5 times market rates to fund it. Officials signed his contracts and pressed schools that tried to cancel. Huy got 8 years.
inside: A school food supplier paid education officials and principals a cut of its revenue, and they signed its contracts at above-market prices and blocked cancellations.
cite: Vietnam News, 11 April 2026

n: Food firms' bribes ran the Food Safety Department's permits for seven years
rank: director and deputy directors, Food Safety Department
d: The Food Safety Department (Cuc An toan thuc pham) in Vietnam's health ministry registers food product declarations, clears advertising and issues good-manufacturing-practice certificates. On the afternoon of 14 January 2026 the Hanoi People's Court sentenced 55 people. The indictment covers 2018 to 2025, with over 93.7 billion dong paid for declaration receipts, over 12.7 billion for advertising confirmations and over 1 billion for GMP certificates. Former director Nguyen Thanh Phong was held liable for over 94.8 billion dong of bribes and found to have gained over 43.9 billion himself; he got 20 years. Tran Viet Nga, also a former director, got 15 years. The court said the leaders organised the scheme and divided the money by rank. The report names no paying company.
inside: Businesses paid the national food regulator's own leaders and staff for the declarations, advertising clearances and factory certificates they needed, with the money split by rank.
cite: VnEconomy, on the 14 January 2026 verdict

n: Labour-export firms paid over 30bn dong inside Vietnam's overseas labour body
rank: Deputy Minister of Labour and Overseas Labour Management Department officials
d: The Overseas Labour Management Department licenses the Vietnamese companies that send workers abroad. The Hanoi People's Court sentenced 28 people at first instance: Nguyen Ba Hoan, former deputy minister of labour, invalids and social affairs, got 12 years for taking bribes and the department's former director Tong Hai Nam 14 years. Sai Gon Giai Phong reported on 6 November 2026 that Hoan, Nam and other department officials received more than 30 billion dong from people linked to 31 companies, reportedly 100 to 400 million dong for a dispatch licence and about 500 US dollars a worker for the slips approving labour contracts, and that officials created an unlawful review step that stopped firms filing their own papers. The appeal was postponed when a defence lawyer failed to appear.
inside: Companies sending Vietnamese workers abroad paid the ministry department that licensed them, and its officials made the licences and contract approvals turn on those payments.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 6 November 2026

n: Design firms and a kit supplier bought Vietnam Register's two directors
org_label: vehicle design companies and the supplier Net Viet
rank: successive directors, Vietnam Register
d: The Vietnam Register (Cuc Dang kiem Viet Nam) is the state body that inspects vehicles and inland waterway craft. On 23 August 2024 the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced 254 people in a case covering the Register, eleven inspection centres in the city and three in Long An, Ben Tre and Soc Trang. Those convicted included staff of design companies who gave bribes, a group around the equipment supplier Net Viet, and people producing and selling inspection software for unlawful use. Two successive directors of the Register were sentenced, Tran Ky Hinh to 25 years and Dang Viet Ha to 19. The report gives no bribe amounts. The court said the conduct affected the safety of vehicle inspection.
inside: Design companies and an equipment supplier paid their way through the national vehicle inspection body, up to its two successive directors, so its inspections and purchases served them.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, on the 23 August 2024 verdict

n: Son Lam paid over 70bn dong to get its medicines into 13 state hospitals
rank: director, Ho Chi Minh City Institute of Traditional Medicine
d: Pham Van Cach, chairman of Son Lam Pharmaceutical, paid over 70 billion dong to the leaders of 13 state hospitals and medical centres across Vietnam to smooth the supply of his medicines and avoid obstruction, by bank transfer or in cash, to the leaders themselves or to acquaintances' accounts. Huynh Nguyen Loc, former director of the Ho Chi Minh City Institute of Traditional Medicine, took 47 billion dong of it and was given 14 years by the Hanoi People's Court. On 15 June 2026 the Supreme People's Court's appeal court in Hanoi cut his term to 11 years 6 months after his family repaid the money, and cut Cach's 15 years to 11 years 6 months.
inside: A drug company paid the heads of state hospitals and a city medicine institute, and its medicines then flowed into their wards; the largest recipient took 47 billion dong.
cite: Nhan Dan, 15 June 2026

n: Litigants and lawyers paid judges inside the High Court in Da Nang
rank: deputy chief justices, High People's Court in Da Nang
d: The High People's Court in Da Nang heard appeals for central and southern Vietnam; it is now the Supreme People's Court's appeal court in Da Nang. On the afternoon of 24 December 2025 the Hanoi People's Court sentenced 28 people over bribery there. Two of its former deputy chief justices were convicted of taking bribes, Pham Viet Cuong getting 7 years and Pham Tan Hoang 3 years, alongside a former head of the criminal division and a judge of the Dak Lak provincial court. Those convicted of paying included Duong Anh Son, chairman of K-Homes, and two lawyers, and court and procuracy staff were convicted of brokering. The report gives no amounts. The court asked that affected judgments be reviewed.
inside: A property company chairman, lawyers and brokers paid judges and staff of a regional appeal court, which then asked that the judgments it had given be reviewed.
cite: Bao Thanh Tra, on the 24 December 2025 verdict

n: A waterways firm's cut reached Ha Long Bay's board and the city chairman
org_label: River Management Joint Stock Company No. 3
who: River Management Joint Stock Company No. 3
rank: chairman of Ha Long city and head of the Ha Long Bay Management Board
d: River Management Joint Stock Company No. 3 held 18 contracts worth nearly 70 billion dong with the Ha Long Bay Management Board between 2017 and 2021. On 25 April 2023 the Quang Ninh Provincial People's Court sentenced 28 people. Pham Hong Ha, former chairman of Ha Long city's people's committee and former head of the bay management board, got 15 years for embezzlement and taking bribes. The court said the company's board chairman Pham Van Pha gave him 725 million dong in six payments, following a percentage split agreed at the outset, while a board department head took 723 million dong and a staff member 168.5 million. Pha was given 30 years.
inside: A waterways maintenance company paid an agreed percentage back to the Ha Long Bay board officials and the city chairman who oversaw and accepted its contracts.
cite: VietnamPlus, on the 25 April 2023 verdict

n: Buyers' bribes to the Vietnam Rubber Group's acting chairman moved public land
rank: acting chairman, Vietnam Rubber Group
d: On 10 April 2026 the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced 22 people over the transfer of the public plots at 39-39B Ben Van Don in the city, which it said cost the state about 542 billion dong. Le Quang Thung, former acting chairman of the Vietnam Rubber Group, the state rubber company, was described as the main instigator and given 14 years for taking bribes and for asset-loss offences. The court said he agreed to accept a bribe of 3 million US dollars and received 200,000 Singapore dollars and 300,000 US dollars from Dang Phuoc Dua and Le Y Linh, who were tied to the Viet Tin companies. Dua got 7 years and Linh 7 years 6 months.
inside: Private buyers paid the state rubber group's acting chairman, and public land in Ho Chi Minh City passed into their hands at a cost the court put at 542 billion dong.
cite: Tap chi Toa an nhan dan, 11 April 2026

n: Firms' bribes alleged over Vietnam's durian export codes and certificates
rank: Deputy Minister and deputy director, Plant Cultivation and Protection Department
d: Vietnam's Department of Plant Cultivation and Protection issues the growing-area and packing-facility codes and the inspection certificates that durian exports to China need. Sai Gon Giai Phong reported on 1 October 2026 that the Ministry of Public Security had charged 39 people, 18 more than before, under six groups of offences including giving and taking bribes. Hoang Trung, former deputy minister of agriculture and environment, and Nguyen Quang Hieu, the department's former deputy director, were charged with taking bribes and detained on 28 July 2026. Investigators say they issued sub-licences to serve group interests and for personal profit and had subordinates issue fake certificates and codes. Companies named include NhoNho, Retaq and Scitech; the report does not say which paid, or any amounts.
inside: Investigators allege that companies in the durian export trade paid the ministry department that issues its codes and certificates, which then had fake ones issued.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 1 October 2026

n: Truck owners paid through Tuan Vinh for Hanoi's transport inspectors
org_label: Tuan Vinh Trading and Transport Investment
who: Tuan Vinh Trading and Transport Investment
rank: transport inspection teams, Hanoi Department of Transport
d: Tuan Vinh Trading and Transport Investment, run by Pham Van Vinh, used its name and logo to recruit truck owners who paid to be left alone by enforcement or fined less. Between June 2016 and October 2018 the group collected over 6.262 billion dong and paid individual officers from 1.5 million to 60 million dong, among them transport inspection teams in three Hanoi districts, a mobile inspection unit of the city transport department's inspectorate, traffic police, and a road management sub-department. At a trial reopened on 20 July 2021 the Hanoi People's Court gave three inspectors 3 to 5 years for taking bribes, and Vinh 8 years, Nguyen Anh Hao 11 years and Le Van Cuong 10 years for giving them.
inside: A transport company collected monthly payments from truck owners and passed them to Hanoi's transport inspectors, who then left the paying lorries alone or fined them lightly.
cite: Tap chi Toa an nhan dan, 20 July 2021

n: An invoice-trading ring's bribes bought Ho Chi Minh City tax officers
rank: officers of district tax sub-departments, Ho Chi Minh City
d: On 20 December 2024, after a trial that began on 10 December, the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced 55 people over a ring that set up ghost companies to trade fake invoices and evade tax. Two former tax officers were given 15 years each for taking bribes: Le Thanh Nhan of the District 12 and Hoc Mon tax sub-department and Tran Quoc Duy of the District 7 and Nha Be sub-department. A deputy head of an internal inspection team at the Thu Dau Mot tax sub-department in Binh Duong got 7 years. The court found they took bribes and protected the network. Tran Van Thinh, who paid, got 30 years. No bribe amounts are reported.
inside: A fake-invoice ring paid officers inside Ho Chi Minh City's district tax offices, who protected the ghost companies it used instead of acting against them.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 20 December 2024

n: A dredging contractor paid Cam Le district's leaders 33% of its contract
rank: chairman and vice chairman, Cam Le District People's Committee
d: Cam Le District People's Committee in Da Nang put out contracts for maintaining and dredging drainage ditches and culverts. On the afternoon of 31 July 2024, after two days of trial, the Da Nang City People's Court sentenced seven people. The officials had asked for 33 per cent of the contract value back from Thy Nghia Hung Company after a joint venture including it won the bid, in 2021 and 2022, and received over 3.1 billion dong from its deputy director Nguyen Dang Nhat Duy; they prepared the paperwork approving that joint venture as the winner. Ho Van Khoa, the former district chairman, and the vice chairman Vo Thien Sinh got 9 years each, and Duy 8 years.
inside: District leaders in Da Nang demanded a third of the contract value back from a dredging contractor, and then wrote the paperwork that made it the winner.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 31 July 2024

n: Contractor's 20,000-dirham bribe reached the head of Fez's water and power agency
rank: Director general, Autonomous Water and Electricity Distribution Agency of Fez
d: Al-Hanafi Abouker, director general of the Autonomous Water and Electricity Distribution Agency (RADEEF) in Fez, the public body that distributes water and electricity in the city, was convicted of taking a bribe. A contractor, named in the reporting only as M.Q., told prosecutors through a bribery hotline that Abouker had extorted him; police set a trap and arrested him in a cafe as he took the agreed money, and found more cash in his car and home. The criminal chamber for financial crimes at the Fez Court of Appeal, sitting at first instance, gave him one year in prison and a 20,000-dirham fine, and ordered 20,000 dirhams returned to the contractor. He was acquitted of influence peddling.
inside: A contractor's money reached the director general of the utility he dealt with, who took it for handling the contractor's business with the agency.
cite: Hespress (Arabic), 18 May 2022

n: Supplier's owner convicted with officials over Marrakech school purchase orders
rank: Regional Academy of Education and Training, Marrakech region
d: The criminal chamber for financial crimes at the Marrakech Court of Appeal convicted eight of nine defendants over public contracts and purchase orders for schools run by the Regional Academy of Education and Training in the Marrakech region, the state body that manages schooling there. Those convicted included a former regional education deputy and a woman who owned a supplier company; a former academy director was acquitted. Three defendants, among them the deputy and the company owner, were given two years in prison and a 50,000-dirham fine, others part-suspended or suspended terms, and the convicted were ordered to pay the academy 150,000 dirhams jointly. The charges were embezzlement of public funds and forgery of an official document.
inside: A supplier's owner was convicted alongside the officials who issued the academy's purchase orders, so the state schools' buying ran to her company's benefit.
cite: Akhbarona (Arabic), 11 November 2025

n: Beni Mellal drug trafficker paid gendarmes; 31 of them convicted
org_label: A drug trafficking network in Beni Mellal
who: A drug trafficker and four intermediaries
rank: Royal Gendarmerie officers serving in Beni Mellal
d: The criminal chamber at the Casablanca Court of Appeal, sitting at first instance, convicted a drug trafficker named in the reporting as Mohamed S., four intermediaries and 31 gendarmes of bribery, concealment and collusion on 11 March 2025. The trafficker told investigators that he had given money to gendarmes, directly or through intermediaries, as bribes so that his trafficking around Beni Mellal could continue; the report gives no amounts. He received six years; one gendarme got three years, five got two years, twenty got up to twenty months and five were sentenced to the time already served. The gendarmes denied the charges in their final statements. He was arrested only after the prosecutor general ordered action, despite dozens of national arrest warrants.
inside: A trafficker's payments reached the gendarmerie units policing his area, so the force being paid let his trafficking carry on.
cite: Hespress (Arabic), 11 March 2025

n: Judges, lawyers and a businessman convicted of selling Tetouan court rulings
org_label: Lawyers, a notary and a businessman
who: Lawyers, a notary and a businessman
rank: Judges of the Tetouan Court of Appeal
d: The Rabat Court of Appeal convicted sixteen defendants in the case known as the sale of judgments at the Tetouan Court of Appeal. The main accused, a judge identified as R. H., was given three years in prison; a second judge two years with one suspended; three lawyers from the Tetouan, El Jadida and Casablanca bars and a notary from El Jadida between six months and two years; and a businessman known as the Lamborghini owner one year. A lawyer and an official were acquitted. The charges were corruption, abuse of power and forming a criminal organisation to influence judicial decisions. The investigation was run by the national judicial police brigade under the prosecutor general at Rabat's financial crimes court. The report gives no sums.
inside: Lawyers, a notary and a businessman were convicted of working with two appeal judges so that the court's rulings came out as they wanted.
cite: Bladi.net, 4 August 2025

n: Sidi Taibi commune chiefs jailed over a 20,000-dirham land commission
who: A man buying a plot of land
rank: President and vice-president of the commune of Sidi Taibi
d: The president and the vice-president of the commune of Sidi Taibi, near Kenitra in Morocco, were prosecuted at the Kenitra court of first instance after demanding a 20,000-dirham commission from a man who wanted to buy a plot of land for his wife. The two were filmed taking what the report calls a bribe; the report does not say whether the full sum was paid. Each was sentenced to three and a half years in prison without parole, fined 50,000 dirhams, ordered to pay one symbolic dirham in damages to the civil party, and stripped of civic rights with ten years' ineligibility for office. The report, published on 9 February 2023, gives no date for the offence or the verdict.
inside: A land buyer's money reached the two elected heads of the commune that had to approve his purchase, who were filmed taking it.
cite: Bladi.net, 9 February 2023

n: Contractors paid Tunisia's equipment ministry for category 4 licences
rank: Officials of the Ministry of Equipment
d: The criminal chamber of the Tunis court of first instance convicted eleven people of obtaining category 4 contractor licences from Tunisia's Ministry of Equipment, the rating a firm needs to bid for larger public works, using forged documents and bribes. During the investigation contractors admitted paying officials between 6,000 and 12,000 dinars each for the licences. The head of a services company was given 13 years, a former ministry official 11 years, an official of the civil protection service six years, and eight others between two and eleven years. The charges included forming a criminal conspiracy, membership of a criminal association, fraud, document forgery and bribery of a public official. The verdict was reported on 25 February 2026; the report names no defendant or company.
inside: Contractors paid between 6,000 and 12,000 dinars each to ministry officials, who then issued the licences their firms needed to bid for public works.
cite: La Presse via AllAfrica, 25 February 2026

n: Tunisian PM and ministers convicted over lifting Mabrouk's asset freeze
rank: Prime minister and five former members of the government
d: The specialised financial corruption chamber of the Tunis court of first instance convicted the businessman Marouane Mabrouk, a son-in-law of former president Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, together with Youssef Chahed, prime minister from 2016 to 2020, and five other former members of the government. The case concerns the lifting of the European Union asset freeze on Mabrouk, a decision taken by a restricted ministerial council in January 2018. The court found that the accused had deliberately abused their public functions to obtain benefits. On 2 March 2026 each was given six years in prison and they were fined 800 million dinars jointly, about 237 million euros. The report does not say whether they will appeal.
inside: A businessman's interest reached the ministerial council deciding his case, and the government's own decision lifted the EU asset freeze on him.
cite: AFP via AllAfrica, 4 March 2026

n: Tunisia's top judge made the cassation chambers that ruled for two businessmen
org_label: Businessmen Fethi Jenayah and Nejib Ismail
who: Businessmen Fethi Jenayah and Nejib Ismail
rank: First President of the Court of Cassation
d: Taieb Rached, former First President of Tunisia's Court of Cassation, was convicted over cassation rulings without referral that benefited the businessmen Fethi Jenayah and Nejib Ismail. La Presse reports that Rached, as Tunis appeals prosecutor in 2018, helped Ismail's detention lapse, and that in 2019 as First President he created two cassation chambers and appointed the judges Abderrazek Bahouri and Marouane Tlili to them. The rulings are estimated to have cost the state nearly one billion dinars. At first instance in October 2025 Rached was given 30 years and Jenayah 30, with large fines and confiscations; on appeal on 23 May 2026 the sentences of Rached and Bahouri were cut to ten years each for complicity in forgery.
inside: Two businessmen's cases were decided by chambers the court's own president had created and staffed, so Tunisia's highest court ruled in their favour.
cite: La Presse (Tunisia), 23 May 2026

n: Market tenant's 200,000 shillings convicted a Kinondoni council trade officer
rank: Trade officer, Kinondoni Municipal Council
d: Obote Joash Etta, a trade officer at Kinondoni Municipal Council in Dar es Salaam, locked the business frames of Gladen Kafanabo, who sub-let two stalls at Mikocheni B market, and demanded 200,000 Tanzanian shillings to unlock them. The Prevention and Combating of Corruption Bureau marked the money and Kafanabo handed it over at Tegeta in June 2020; Etta was arrested on the spot and then produced the keys. Kinondoni District Court convicted him of a corrupt transaction, and on 28 September 2022 the High Court at Dar es Salaam dismissed his appeal and upheld the conviction and sentence. The judgment also records a further 400,000 shillings promised and rent arrears of 240,000 shillings.
inside: A market tenant's 200,000 shillings reached the council officer who controlled his stalls, and the stalls were unlocked once the money changed hands.
cite: High Court of Tanzania, Obote Joash Etta v Republic, 28 September 2022

n: MP's firms drew UGX 495,444,716 from Namisindwa district via its officers
org_label: Samix Uganda Ltd and Zedkol Financial Services
who: Samix Uganda Ltd and Zedkol Financial Services
rank: Chief administrative officer and acting chief financial officer, Namisindwa District Local Government
d: Uganda's Anti-Corruption Court convicted Pallisa County MP Samuel Otukol, Namisindwa district's former chief administrative officer Francis Odap, its acting chief financial officer Willy Wamburu, and Osire Ezekiel, a director of Zedkol Financial Services. Between June and November 2019 Odap and Wamburu processed payments totalling UGX 495,444,716 of district money as staff loan deductions to three firms that had lent the staff nothing: Samix Uganda Ltd, of which Otukol was a director, took UGX 202,483,413, Zedkol UGX 210,430,890 and United for Development SACCO UGX 82,530,413. On 1 April 2026 Otukol was given two years and ordered to repay 202.5m and 105.2m shillings, Odap 14 months, Wamburu 15 months, and Ezekiel a 6.5m shilling fine and 105.2m in repayment.
inside: Three outside firms were paid district money through its own administrative and finance officers, and the MP who directed two of them drew the cash out.
cite: New Vision (Uganda), April 2026; Nexus Media Uganda, 28 March 2026

n: Engineer's 1,000-rupee note to a Mauritius traffic officer ended in conviction
rank: Officer of the Divisional Traffic Police
d: Yan Shi, a Chinese national working as an engineer in Mauritius since 2019, was booked on 9 May 2021 by PC Mootoo of the Divisional Traffic Police for an expired vehicle licence and insurance vignette and for failing to stop at a red light. At Line Barracks police station in Port Louis he placed a 1,000-rupee banknote in the officer's open satchel. The Intermediate Court's Financial Crimes Division rejected his claim that this was a fine paid on the spot, finding instead a gratification meant to make the offences disappear, and on 28 June 2023 found him guilty of bribery of a public official. The judgment as published does not state his sentence.
inside: A motorist's 1,000 rupees reached the traffic officer who had just booked him, offered so that the traffic charges would be dropped.
cite: Intermediate Court of Mauritius (Financial Crimes Division), ICAC v Yan Shi, 28 June 2023

n: Mauritius transport authority examiner passed a vehicle he never examined
who: A vehicle owner who installed blinds
rank: Vehicle examiner, National Land Transport Authority
d: Girdharry Khurun, a vehicle examiner at the National Land Transport Authority, the Mauritian body that inspects and licenses vehicles, was found guilty on 8 April 2026 of taking a gratification. A witness who had fitted blinds at Khurun's home was given a discount that cut the price from 6,000 to 5,000 rupees, and the Intermediate Court's Financial Crimes Division treated that 1,000-rupee reduction as the payment. In return Khurun issued a favourable examination report and fitness certificate dated 21 December 2015 for vehicle 4023 SP 06 without the vehicle being examined. A second count, over 200 rupees said to have been paid to speed up another examination, was dismissed for want of evidence. No sentence is stated in the judgment.
inside: A vehicle owner's 1,000-rupee discount reached the state examiner, who then certified the man's vehicle as fit without ever looking at it.
cite: Intermediate Court of Mauritius (Financial Crimes Division), ICAC v Girdharry Khurun, 8 April 2026

n: Botswana courts' supplies chief bought from her family's companies
org_label: Crawley Holdings, STD Investments, Radiant Hygiene and Wilkingson
who: Crawley Holdings, STD Investments, Radiant Hygiene and Wilkingson
rank: Chief Supplies Officer, Administration of Justice
d: Kegaisamang Solomon, chief supplies officer at Botswana's Administration of Justice, which runs the courts, was convicted on ten counts of corruption for procuring supplies from companies in which she had an interest she did not declare. Her husband, daughter and sons were directors, shareholders or employees of Crawley Holdings, STD Investments, Radiant Hygiene and Wilkingson (Pty) Ltd. Crawley Holdings supplied two shredding machines on a purchase order she prepared alone and its account received credits of P29,120 and P19,040; STD Investments' transactions between August 2012 and December 2014 came to over P87,000; Radiant Hygiene won High Court tenders for a rat infestation and for toners, and her son Phenyo took a 10 per cent commission on tenders he procured for it. Sentencing was reserved.
inside: Family companies won the courts' supply orders through the officer who placed them, and the money and a 10 per cent commission came back to her household.
cite: The Voice (Botswana), 21 April 2023

n: Chinese contractor's bribes alleged to two Botswana water utility engineers
org_label: Beijing Enterprises Water Group Corporation Limited
who: Beijing Enterprises Water Group Corporation Limited
rank: Engineers, Water Utilities Corporation
d: Two engineers at Botswana's Water Utilities Corporation, the state company that supplies the country's water, face five counts of corruption over bribes the prosecution says they took from Beijing Enterprises Water Group Corporation Limited, a Chinese contractor engaged for waste water treatment and sewer works at the corporation's Glen Valley station outside Gaborone. The engineers are named in the reporting as Timothy Mudongo and Rebaone Letsatle. According to the suit they received bribes to finance lavish lifestyles and lived off the company between 2019 and 2022. Mmegi, reporting the case on 28 August 2023, gives no sums, does not name the posts the two held and does not report the outcome, and the allegations have not been tested in court.
inside: Prosecutors say a Chinese contractor's bribes reached the state water utility's own engineers while it held the works contract at its Glen Valley station.
cite: Mmegi (Botswana), 28 August 2023

n: ETPH's manager and Algeria's water minister convicted over dam contracts
rank: Minister of Water Resources and two directors general of the National Dams and Transfers Agency
d: The economic and financial criminal court at Sidi M'hamed in Algiers convicted five men in a case concerning the National Dams and Transfers Agency, the state body that builds and runs the dams. Arezki Berraki, former minister of water resources, and a former head of the agency each received eight years, and a second former director general seven. The manager of the construction company ETPH, named only as H.R. and absent under an international arrest warrant, got 15 years; a fifth defendant, a fugitive, got ten. Each was fined one million dinars. The charges were influence peddling, abuse of office, embezzlement of public funds and granting unjustified privileges in public contracts with the state. The ruling, reported on 10 November 2026, is first instance and may be appealed.
inside: A construction company's manager was convicted with the minister and the dam agency's directors over public contracts the court found gave unjustified privileges.
cite: Algerie360, 10 November 2026

n: Primex Steel took undue advantages in Alfapipe's state contracts
rank: Procurement commission and senior executives of Alfapipe
d: The economic and financial criminal court at Sidi M'hamed ruled on 15 July 2025 in the case of Alfapipe, Algeria's public pipe-making company. Twenty-two people were prosecuted, among them former senior executives and public procurement officials, with sentences running from acquittal to six years. Those convicted included the deputy director of the Annaba unit, the chairman of the procurement commission and the finance director of the time. The court found that Primex Steel Trading GmbH, a foreign firm, had received unjustified advantages, and fined it 32 million dinars. The public contracts were said to have been awarded illegally, with losses to the treasury put at several billion dinars; damages of one million dinars to the treasury and 500,000 to Alfapipe were ordered.
inside: A foreign steel trader took unjustified advantages in the state pipe company's contracts, which its own procurement commission and executives awarded.
cite: Algerie360, 16 July 2025

n: Owner of the firm 'House' convicted over Imetal group's state contracts
who: B. Chouaib, owner of the company 'House'
rank: Chief executives of the Imetal group companies Sider and the Entreprise nationale de recuperation
d: The economic and financial criminal court at Sidi M'hamed sentenced defendants in the case of Imetal, Algeria's public metallurgy, steel and iron group, on 15 December 2025. Lakhdar A., former chief executive of the Sider group, received six years; Belarbi Anis, former chief executive of the Entreprise nationale de recuperation and a fugitive, 15 years; and B. Chouaib, owner of the company House, five years, with the company fined two million dinars. An operations director of the recovery company and three other defendants received one to three years, and two defendants were acquitted. The charges were granting undue advantages to third parties in contracts with the state, money laundering within a criminal group, embezzlement of public funds and abuse of function.
inside: An outside firm's owner was convicted with the state steel group's chief executives over the undue advantages its contracts with the group gave third parties.
cite: Algerie360, 15 December 2025

n: Malawi arrests Greenbelt Authority staff and three irrigation contractors
org_label: Einstein Construction, PLMB Engineering Investment and EMD Consulting Engineers
who: Einstein Construction, PLMB Engineering Investment and EMD Consulting Engineers
rank: Director of finance and investments and two managers, Greenbelt Authority
d: Malawi's Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested three senior officials of the Greenbelt Authority, the state body that runs the Greenbelt Initiative's irrigation schemes: finance and investments director Linda Phiri, procurement and assets disposal manager Masautso Kamowa and infrastructure development manager Synoden Kautsi. Three private contractors were arrested with them, Kenneth Khonje of Einstein Construction Limited, Victor Chabwera of PLMB Engineering Investment and Ephrone Mwenitete of EMD Consulting Engineers. The bureau says MK36,782,078,832.91 was paid to the contractors for four irrigation schemes without performance bonds and on fake work certificates, then withdrawn from banks, with some of it going to political campaigns and some directly to authority employees. The arrests were confirmed on 18 January 2026 and no court has ruled.
inside: The bureau alleges contractors were paid tens of billions of kwacha through the authority's own finance and procurement managers, with some money going back to its employees.
cite: Nyasa Times via AllAfrica, 19 January 2026

n: Senelec works chief referred over 49m CFA taken from two suppliers
rank: Head of the Civil Engineering Works Unit, Senelec
d: Cheikh Mbacke Seck, a civil engineer who headed the civil engineering works unit of Senelec, Senegal's national electricity company, was dismissed and referred to the public prosecutor for fraud. Two suppliers, who are not named, told investigators that he had taken 49 million CFA francs from them in exchange for contracts with Senelec that turned out to be fictitious; they waited several months before complaining. Seneweb reported on 14 October 2025 that he was arrested by the criminal investigation division after allegedly trying to leave the country. No court has ruled and the allegations remain unproven; the report gives no dates for the scheme itself.
inside: Two suppliers' money, 49 million CFA francs, reached the Senelec manager who promised them the state utility's works contracts.
cite: Seneweb (Senegal), 14 October 2025

n: Security men paid a Mauritian police inspector Rs 25,000 not to arrest them
org_label: Two men in the security services business
rank: Police inspector, Mauritius Police Force
d: Rajendra Raggoo and Yogeshwarsing Pryam, who worked in the security services business, were found guilty of bribery of a public official by the Intermediate Court's Financial Crimes Division on 4 March 2025. They paid Rs 25,000 to Derochoonee, then a police inspector, to stop him arresting them and others over a premeditated assault case. The court held that the bribery was complete once the gratification was given to a public official so that he would abstain from an act within his duties, and that the payment interfered with the normal investigation. It rejected their defence that they had acted under duress, finding no imminent threat. The judgment as published states no sentence.
inside: Two men's Rs 25,000 reached the police inspector investigating them, paid so that the force would not arrest them over the assault case.
cite: Intermediate Court of Mauritius (Financial Crimes Division), ICAC v Ragoo and Pryam, 4 March 2025

n: Ozone's ex-president convicted with Bouznika's council chief over tenders
who: Aziz El Badraoui, former president of the company Ozone
rank: President of the Bouznika commune council
d: The financial crimes chamber of the Casablanca Court of Appeal handed down seventeen years between three men over the running of the Bouznika commune council, on Morocco's Atlantic coast. Mohamed Karimine, the council's former president, was given seven years for misuse of public funds and abuse of power; Aziz El Badraoui, former president of the company Ozone and of the Raja Casablanca football club, six years for mismanaging public tenders and breaching the law on territorial collectivities; and a former commune engineer four years. Forgery charges against the first two were dropped. The case followed an audit of the commune by the regional audit court. The report, published on 29 July 2025, gives no figure for any sum embezzled or benefit obtained.
inside: The head of a waste services company was convicted with the commune council's own president over the public tenders the council awarded.
cite: Hespress (French), 29 July 2025

n: A builder's R$1m payment moved the Rodoanel route away from its quarry
org_label: Rodoanel Norte contractor and engineering firm
rank: Director, Dersa (Sao Paulo state road company)
d: Dersa, the Sao Paulo state road company that built the Rodoanel ring motorway, had a director who took R$1 million, according to the prosecution, so that the Rodoanel Norte route was altered to avoid a quarry owned by one of the contractors. The director suggested a simulated consultancy contract with an engineering firm, backed by a technical report justifying the change, to give the payment the look of a legal fee. The case came out of a plea bargain by the construction company doing the work. In January 2023 the Sao Paulo state appeal court convicted the former director of passive corruption and money laundering, giving him nine years and three months, and convicted the engineering firm's representative of money laundering.
inside: A contractor paid a state road company's own director to redraw a motorway route around its quarry, so the company's engineering decision served the payer.
cite: Tribunal de Justica de Sao Paulo, press release on Apelacao 0087648-38.2018.8.26.0050 (ruling of 10 January 2023)

n: A cable supplier reached Cemig through its supply and logistics chief
rank: Superintendent of Supply and Logistics, Cemig
d: Cemig is the Minas Gerais state electricity company. Prosecutors in Minas Gerais say Paulo Vanelli, its superintendent of supply and logistics, steered tenders and material contracts towards Brascopper, a Sao Paulo supplier, with one rigged notice for a materials purchase dated to 2018. Cemig removed Vanelli and other purchasing officials in 2021 after investigations began, and in August 2022 the state prosecutors ran Operation Mau Contato against Cemig staff and businesspeople who make and resell conductor cable, alleging collusion from the bidding stage through contract delivery. On 29 August 2024 the prosecutors asked the courts to make Brascopper, the supplier Nova Energia, Vanelli and other former purchasing staff return more than R$45 million to Cemig. No court has ruled.
inside: A cable supplier reached the state power company through the officer who ran its purchasing, so Cemig's tenders and material contracts were written to suit the supplier.
cite: O Fator, 2 September 2024; InvestNews/Reuters on Operation Mau Contato, 30 August 2022

n: A R$280m warehouse deal at Petrobras's pension fund paid an 8% commission
org_label: private property operators and an intermediary lawyer
rank: Fund manager, Petros
d: Petros is the pension fund of Petrobras employees. Federal prosecutors in Rio de Janeiro charged 19 people over the fund's 2010 purchase of industrial warehouses in the interior of Sao Paulo state, a deal they call reckless and describe as a facade worth R$280 million. The then manager of the fund is accused of conducting the deal with private operators, with a politically influential lawyer acting as intermediary; the prosecutors allege a bribe disguised as a commission equal to 8% of the deal value, and say more than R$23 million of illicit funds was hidden, mainly in Swiss accounts. The charges are money laundering and criminal organisation, and the prosecutors asked for R$30 million in collective damages for Petros. Their release names none of those charged.
inside: Outside property operators, through an intermediary lawyer and the fund's own manager, got a state oil company's pension fund to buy warehouses at a price that paid them a commission.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal, Procuradoria da Republica no Rio de Janeiro, press release on the Petros warehouse charges

n: Builders paid the Sao Paulo Metro's purchasing manager over Line 5 tenders
rank: Manager of contracting and purchasing, Metro de Sao Paulo
d: Metro de Sao Paulo is the state-owned company that builds and runs the city's underground. In May 2018 state prosecutors charged Sergio Correa Brasil, its manager of contracting and purchasing, with taking R$2.5 million from the builder Camargo Correa and steering the tender for Line 5 construction to a cartel that won Lot 3; the tender opened in October 2008 and the works cost about R$6.6 billion in adjusted terms. A second charge that December, over the same competition, alleged he asked Odebrecht's representatives for R$392,870 to adjust the tender notice to the firms' demands. Camargo Correa had acknowledged overpricing and a cartel in two Line 5 lots in 2017. Odebrecht executives' testimony also named him over R$17.9 million tied to Line 2.
inside: Two of Brazil's largest builders paid the state metro company's purchasing manager to write its tender notice their way, so the contracts went to their cartel.
cite: Diario do Transporte, 11 May 2018; Legismap on the Gedec charge of 17 December 2018

n: Wind firms' money reached the secretary who pushed Copel to buy their assets
org_label: Sao Bento Energia and Dreen Brasil
who: Sao Bento Energia and Dreen Brasil
rank: Parana Secretary of Industry, Commerce and Mercosur Affairs
d: Copel is the Parana state electricity company. In November 2021 Parana state prosecutors charged Ricardo Barros, then the federal government's leader in the Chamber of Deputies, over a scheme they say began in 2011 when he was the state's secretary of industry, commerce and Mercosur affairs. They allege he used that post to push Copel into buying half the assets of two Parana wind companies, Sao Bento Energia and Dreen Brasil, and that part of the purchase price came back to him: more than R$5 million over two years, routed as donations to his party's national office, which he then moved to his own and allied 2014 campaigns as party treasurer. The charges are money laundering, influence peddling and electoral falsity. Barros denies them and calls the complaint political.
inside: Two wind-power firms allegedly paid the state secretary who leaned on the state electricity company to buy their assets, so Copel's purchase served the sellers.
cite: Congresso em Foco, 23 November 2021, on the Ministerio Publico do Parana charge

n: A hospital meals supplier paid two leaders of Brasilia's health institute
rank: Vice-president and chief of staff, Iges-DF
d: Iges-DF is the institute that runs public hospitals and emergency units for Brazil's Federal District. On 21 October 2026 a Brasilia criminal court convicted Caio Falcao, its former vice-president, of passive corruption for taking R$1 million from Waldenes Barbosa, owner of Salutar Alimentacao Servicos, which supplied hospital meals under a contract running in 2021. Alessandra Lobato, former chief of staff to the institute's president, was convicted of taking R$309,000 for pushing the institute's requirements with the company. Both got two years, and Barbosa four years plus a fine, for active corruption; all three had prison replaced by restrictions and may appeal free. A fourth defendant accused of taking R$73,000 was acquitted for lack of evidence. The case came from Operation Escudero.
inside: A catering firm paid the institute's vice-president and the president's chief of staff, so the body buying hospital meals handled its contract on the supplier's terms.
cite: Brasil de Fato, 23 October 2026, on the 8th Criminal Court of the Federal District ruling of 21 October 2026

n: Biotronik's transfers reached a federal university hospital's director
rank: Director-general, Hospital Universitario Maria Aparecida Pedrossian
d: Operation Sangue Frio, opened in 2013, alleged that Jose Carlos Dorsa, director-general of the federal teaching hospital Maria Aparecida Pedrossian in Campo Grande, used a company called Cardiocec as a disguised way of taking bribes from Biotronik Comercial Medica in return for the hospital favouring Biotronik's hospital materials. Prosecutors said Dorsa and his partner Alcides Manuel do Nascimento took R$695,776.02 in 44 transfers between 15 July 2009 and 28 August 2012, R$595,776.02 of it concealed in 43 transfers from Biotronik to Cardiocec, alongside a 2009 tender for perfusionist services they call fraudulent and four Biotronik contracts with the hospital. A federal judge convicted Nascimento of passive corruption 44 times over, with property forfeiture up to R$1,330,170.97. Dorsa died in 2018 and was not a defendant.
inside: A medical devices supplier paid the hospital's own director through a front company, so a public teaching hospital bought its materials.
cite: Campo Grande News on the 3rd Federal Court of Campo Grande ruling; MPF complaint of 17 August 2022

n: Suppliers paid a navy sergeant through his wife over naval air base tenders
rank: Ammunition supply sergeant and auction officer, Sao Pedro da Aldeia naval air base
d: At the Base Aerea Naval de Sao Pedro da Aldeia in Rio de Janeiro state, a navy chief petty officer acting as the base's auction officer ran an electronic tender in a way that favoured two companies, using a sample requirement with no objective criteria so that better bids were disqualified. A first sergeant who handled ammunition supply was accused of ordering goods from one company above the price registry; that company made 15 bank deposits totalling R$59,975.97 into an account in his wife's name, which prosecutors say he controlled. In a decision reported on 29 August 2026 the Superior Military Court reset the sentences, giving the sergeant six years and one month, a businesswoman four years and five months, and the chief petty officer three years and six months.
inside: Two suppliers paid a navy base's own supply sergeant, through his wife's account, so its tenders and orders were decided in their favour.
cite: JuriNews, 29 August 2026, on the Superior Tribunal Militar decision (relator Pericles Aurelio Lima de Queiroz)

n: A consultancy inside Saneago's tenders steered contracts and funded campaigns
rank: President and expansion director, Saneago
d: Saneago is the Goias state water and sewage company. In Operation Decantacao the Federal Police arrested its president, Jose Taveira, and its expansion director, Afreni Goncalves, who also chaired the state PSDB. Federal prosecutors in Goias charged 35 people on 12 September 2016, alleging that Saneago's leadership rigged the hiring of the consultancy Naeng Engenharia for project design, budgeting and bid review, and that Naeng then favoured companies in the arrangement, which made election donations in return. About R$5.2 million of federal money from the PAC programme, BNDES and Caixa Economica Federal was allegedly diverted to pay bribes and campaign debts. Works affected included the R$117.3 million Corumba IV water system and the R$67.4 million Meia Ponte sewage expansion in Goiania.
inside: An outside consultancy was put inside the state water company's own bid evaluation, so its contracts went to firms that paid bribes and funded campaigns.
cite: Rota Juridica, 13 September 2016, on the MPF/GO charge; O Popular on the Federal Police operation

n: Three firms got Cayman loans from Banestado after donating to a campaign
org_label: Tucumann Engenharia, Redram Construtora and Jabur Toyopar
rank: Director, Banestado
d: Banestado was the Parana state bank. In September 2009 a federal court in Curitiba convicted three businesspeople of fraudulent management and corruption over about US$3.5 million in irregular loans made through the bank's Grand Cayman branch to Tucumann Engenharia, Redram Construtora and Jabur Toyopar. The court found the loans were given in return for donations to the 1998 re-election campaign of the then governor, Jaime Lerner: US$200,000 each from Tucumann and Redram and US$131,000 from Jabur. A former Banestado director, Gabriel Nunes, approved them alone, skipping checks on the firms' finances, collateral and board approval, and confessed under a plea deal. Sentences ran to eight years and eight months. Banestado's former board chairman was acquitted for lack of evidence.
inside: Three borrowers got loans from the state bank through a director who approved them alone, after paying donations to the governor whose government owned the bank.
cite: Tribuna do Parana, 12 September 2009, on the 2nd Federal Criminal Court ruling

n: CTIS kept a no-bid Brasilia schools IT contract through Codeplan's president
rank: President of Codeplan
d: Codeplan is the Federal District's planning company. In April 2021 an appeal panel of the Federal District court upheld a finding of administrative misconduct against CTIS Tecnologia over contract 003/2003, awarded without a tender, for maintaining the schools management system of the district's education secretariat. Prosecutors said an emergency was claimed that did not exist, the contract was worth more than R$2 million and it was then extended on the same justification, with Codeplan acting as the intermediary for the work. Durval Barbosa, Codeplan's former president, was responsible for the contract and was also found liable, though his penalties were waived under a plea deal in which he said an earlier tender had been directed to CTIS. The firm was barred from public contracts for five years.
inside: An IT supplier reached the territory's planning company through its president, who had the work routed through Codeplan and awarded without a tender.
cite: Tribunal de Justica do Distrito Federal e dos Territorios, 19 April 2021, case 0012288-98.2006.8.07.0001

n: A health charity running Manaus clinics paid Amazonas health officials monthly
rank: Officials of the Amazonas health secretariat and its state health fund
d: Operation Maus Caminhos, begun in September 2016, concerns the Instituto Novos Caminhos, a nominally social organisation that managed three health units in Amazonas and, federal prosecutors say, was run in practice by the doctor and businessman Mouhamad Moustafa. Of about R$900 million passed from the national health fund to the Amazonas state health fund in 2014 and 2015, more than R$250 million went to the institute, whose largest suppliers were found to belong to the same economic group. Prosecutors allege monthly bribes of up to R$133,000 to officials of the state health secretariat and the state health fund, plus trips, hotels and vehicles, and that a hospital management system worth about R$318,000 was bought from a group company for over R$1 million. Total diversion is put at over R$100 million.
inside: A private institute, placed in charge of public clinics, paid monthly sums to the health officials who approved and renewed its contracts.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal, Operacao Maus Caminhos case page

n: A builder paid the engineer who approved its hospital contract top-up in Parana
rank: Works inspector and technical director for the Hospital Regional de Toledo project
d: The Hospital Regional de Toledo in western Parana was built mostly with federal money. In a ruling reported on 28 August 2026 a federal court convicted the engineer who was the works inspector, technical director and chair of the committee that reviewed the contractor's request to rebalance the contract, together with the construction company's sole managing partner, who was held responsible for offering and paying the bribes. Price adjustments of up to 55% were applied to items whose official index moved about 11%, producing a 72.9% overpayment and damage of about R$1.16 million. Bribes of at least R$66,000, including a R$15,000 cheque, were paid between June 2012 and February 2014, with about R$51,000 laundered in deposits kept under R$10,000. Both got 11 years. A third defendant was acquitted.
inside: The contractor paid the public engineer who inspected its hospital works and chaired the committee that granted its price increase, so the top-up served the payer.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal, Procuradoria da Republica no Parana, 28 August 2026, Acao Penal 5000356-79.2025.4.04.7017

n: A farm company's warehouses were leased by Brasilia's health secretariat
rank: Office aide, Federal District health secretariat
d: In December 2021 a Brasilia criminal court convicted Cicero Candido Sobrinho, a former office aide in the Federal District health secretariat, and the businessman Ailton Pereira de Almeida of corruption over the secretariat's direct hiring, without a tender, of warehouses owned by Almeida's company Agropecuaria Sao Gabriel. Prosecutors said the warehouses were overpriced and of no use to the secretariat. Both were sentenced to two years and a fine, starting in open regime, with appeal possible. The former health secretary, Rafael de Aguiar Barbosa, was acquitted. The court found no proof of intent on the separate charge of unlawfully waiving the tender, noting that this might still be an administrative breach being examined in a parallel misconduct case. The ruling gave no figures for the contract or the payments.
inside: A landowner's company got a no-bid lease from the health secretariat through an aide inside it, who was convicted of corruption over the hiring.
cite: Tribunal de Justica do Distrito Federal e dos Territorios, 3 December 2021, case 0006211-53.2018.8.07.0001

n: An audit court member in Espirito Santo sold approvals of a town's accounts
org_label: businesspeople and municipal agents of Presidente Kennedy
rank: Member of the Espirito Santo audit court
d: Brazil's audit courts approve or reject public bodies' accounts and review their tenders. On 19 November 2025 the Special Court of the Superior Court of Justice convicted Jose Antonio Almeida Pimentel, a former member of the Espirito Santo audit court, of aggravated passive corruption for soliciting and taking bribes in cases he handled as rapporteur, covering the accounts and tenders of the town of Presidente Kennedy. Prosecutors said he steered tenders, favoured particular companies and made approval of the accounts conditional on payment, and that he received more than R$1.5 million in 16 deposits flagged by Brazil's financial intelligence unit. A covert recording was made in his office in 2011. He was given eight years, one month and 23 days, lost his post and his pension, and must forfeit R$1,525,423.88.
inside: Companies and town officials paid a member of the court that audits them, so its rulings on their tenders and accounts went their way.
cite: Migalhas on Superior Tribunal de Justica, APn 869, judgment of 19 November 2025

n: A businessman and an agent paid federal staff to regularise Ceara coastal land
org_label: a businessman and a document agent in Fortaleza
who: a Fortaleza businessman and a despachante
rank: Staff of the federal property secretariat and a federal audit office auditor
d: The Secretaria de Patrimonio da Uniao (SPU) decides who may regularise title to federally owned land, including the shoreline strips known as terrenos de marinha. Federal prosecutors in Ceara charged four people over a scheme they say ran from 2016 to 2021 in Fortaleza and several coastal towns: a businessman they call the leader, a document agent, a former auditor of the federal audit office and an SPU administrative employee. The charges are criminal association, passive corruption and money laundering, with transactions kept mostly under the R$10,000 reporting threshold; the prosecutors asked for at least R$65,700 in collective damages. A first-instance judge rejected the complaint, but in a decision reported on 16 September 2025 the regional federal appeal court reinstated it and the case went to evidence.
inside: Outside landholders paid staff inside the federal property secretariat and a federal auditor, so decisions on who could title coastal land served the payers.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal, Procuradoria da Republica no Ceara, 16 September 2025, Acao Penal 0816619-03.2024.4.05.8100

n: Odebrecht's plea deal named three Sao Paulo Metro officers over Line 2 works
rank: President, operations director and a manager of Metro de Sao Paulo
d: In a plea-bargain hearing reported on 13 April 2017, the Odebrecht executive Fabio Gandolfo told prosecutors that payments the firm booked as commitments were, in his words, bribes, approved by email by Marcelo Odebrecht. He said that over 2004 to 2006, in connection with Lots 2 and 3 of Line 2-Verde of the Sao Paulo Metro, worth about R$125 million and R$150 million, about R$10 million went to the Metro's then president Luiz Carlos Frayse David, about R$1.5 million to the manager Sergio Brasil and about R$1.5 million to the operations director Decio Tambelli, with R$2.754 million to an intermediary of the Sao Paulo audit court. The aim, he said, was approval of amendments extending the contracts; 20 amendments were signed before work began.
inside: A builder's payments went to the state metro company's president, a director and a manager, so the amendments extending its contracts were approved.
cite: Tribuna do Parana, 13 April 2017, on Fabio Gandolfo's plea-bargain testimony to the Procuradoria-Geral da Republica

n: Managers of Santa Catarina's state health plan are charged over R$66.5m in bribes
org_label: ALFA Gestao de Negocios and the SC Saude management company
rank: Public agents of the Santa Catarina health secretariat
d: SC Saude is the health plan for Santa Catarina state employees. State prosecutors say the contracts for managing it, traced by the defence to contract 465/2009 of the state health secretariat, paid out more than R$400 million between July 2011 and June 2019, and that at least R$66.5 million of that was diverted or paid as bribes to public agents. In September 2021 the federal court in Santa Catarina accepted complaints against six groups of defendants, among them Alissa Maria Guerreiro Martini, a partner in ALFA Gestao de Negocios, charged with tender and contract fraud, embezzlement, corruption and money laundering. In at least three plea deals R$7 million is to be returned, with sentences of up to seven years.
inside: The firms paid to run the state employees' health plan are accused of passing part of the money back to the health secretariat's own officials as bribes.
cite: Brasil de Fato Parana, 23 October 2024, on Operation Hemorragia and the Santa Catarina federal court

n: Port suppliers' payments are traced to Codesp's president and legal chief
org_label: Catamaran do Brasil, DOMAIN Consultores and other port contractors
rank: President and legal superintendent, Codesp
d: Codesp, now the Santos Port Authority, ran Brazil's largest port. In a request for further investigation filed in the Operation Tritao inquiry, a federal prosecutor set out messages indicating R$200,000 described as consultancy or commission tied to Codesp's contract with Catamaran do Brasil and reaching its then president, Jose Alex Botelho de Oliva, and signs of improper benefit to the former legal superintendent, Gabriel Nogueira Eufrasio, over approval of a R$1,629,657.24 rebalancing payment to DOMAIN Consultores that had been refused three times. The prosecutor also noted that the port channel dredging contracts of roughly 2013 to 2016, flagged as irregular by federal auditors, had not been investigated at all, and said most of the alleged payments still needed bank records to confirm.
inside: Port contractors' money is traced to the state port company's president and legal chief, over payments and contract approvals those officers controlled.
cite: Ministerio Publico Federal request for further investigation in Operacao Tritao, published by Consultor Juridico, September 2023

n: CBI: a Chennai ground handler paid an Airports Authority executive director
rank: executive director, Airports Authority of India
d: The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is the state company that runs most of the country's airports and awards the contracts to handle aircraft and baggage on the ground. On 20 March 2019 the CBI arrested an AAI executive director named in the report only as Ravichandran, who it said had demanded 4 lakh rupees to award a ground handling contract at smaller 'Group D' airports. The complaint was made on 16 March 2019 by V. Venkatesh, chief executive of Bright Shine Services, a Chennai partnership firm, who said the official had contacted him in Chennai on 13 March and told him to come to Delhi in person. He was booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act; the report carries the allegations only.
inside: A ground handling firm's 4 lakh rupees allegedly reached the AAI director who awarded its contract, so a state airport operator's purchasing decision turned on the payment.
cite: IANS via Business Standard, 20 March 2019

n: CBI: Aurangabad airport director held over a ground handling bribe
rank: airport director, Airports Authority of India, Aurangabad
d: Chikalthana airport at Aurangabad in Maharashtra is run by the Airports Authority of India, the state airport company, and its director signs off the ground clearance work that lets handling firms service flights. The Millennium Post reported on 2 August 2016 that the CBI had arrested the airport's director, Alok Varshney, the previous day after he allegedly accepted 10,000 rupees for ground clearance work. The complaint came from a private company based at Malad West in Mumbai, which alleged he had been demanding payments from ground handling companies for every flight. The firm was not named. Searches of his office and home followed and he was questioned for three hours before being taken to Pune; no court outcome was reported.
inside: A handling company complained it was paying the state airport company's own director per flight, so clearance to work at Aurangabad turned on cash rather than the rules.
cite: Millennium Post, 2 August 2016

n: Delhi ACB: a tanker owner's 50,000 rupees taken for Delhi Jal Board bills
rank: junior engineer and driver, Delhi Jal Board
d: The Delhi Jal Board is the city government's water utility and hires private tankers to deliver water. On 11 July 2024 Delhi's Anti-Corruption Branch said it had arrested a board driver, Niranjan, as he took 50,000 rupees from a tanker owner from Mandawali in east Delhi, and had booked a board junior engineer, Sandeep Shekhar, who it said had told the driver to make the demand. The owner had about 30 lakh rupees of bills outstanding for tankers hired since 2022; the demand was a tenth of the total, and about 14 lakh had already been released as a show of good faith before 1.4 lakh was asked for the rest. The branch said it was raiding to arrest Shekhar.
inside: A tanker contractor's cash allegedly reached the Jal Board staff who release his bills, so the utility's payments moved only for the ones who paid a tenth.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 11 July 2024

n: CBI: a Bhopal service agent paid Karnataka Antibiotics' managing director
rank: managing director, Karnataka Antibiotics and Pharmaceuticals Limited
d: Karnataka Antibiotics and Pharmaceuticals Limited (KAPL) is a central government drug company based at Bengaluru that sells medicines to public buyers through authorised service agents. The CBI laid a trap on 15 July 2026 and arrested its managing director, not named in the report, in Noida. It alleges he demanded 15 lakh rupees from a Bhopal firm that is KAPL's authorised service agent for Madhya Pradesh and accepted 5 lakh as part payment, in return for approving the firm's service agent agreement, renewing its pending applications for the year, allotting it more government agencies to supply, and a share of commission on medicine sales. Searches followed at homes and offices in Bengaluru, Noida and Jabalpur. The investigation continues.
inside: A distributor's 5 lakh rupees allegedly reached the head of the state drug company, so which firm held its sales agency and which agencies it supplied followed the payment.
cite: IndianPSU, 17 July 2026

n: CBI: a Bhubaneswar firm paid Bridge and Roof's group general manager
rank: group general manager, Bridge and Roof Co (India) Limited
d: Bridge and Roof Co (India) Limited is a central public sector construction company under the Ministry of Heavy Industries. The CBI registered a case on 7 December 2024 and the same day caught a group general manager of the company taking 10 lakh rupees from the director of a Bhubaneswar private company, who was arrested with him along with one other man described as a co-conspirator. The CBI alleges the manager sought payments to influence the award of work orders and the clearing of bills; the firm and the men were not named in the report. The pair had met in Bhubaneswar on 6 December. Searches covered eight premises in Bhubaneswar and Kolkata, where documents, a vehicle and devices were seized. No court finding has been reported.
inside: A contractor's 10 lakh rupees allegedly reached the state construction company manager over its work orders and bills, so who got the work followed the payment.
cite: PTI via Devdiscourse, 8 December 2024

n: Andhra ACB: a borrower's 50,000 rupees sought by a state co-op bank manager
rank: branch manager, Andhra Pradesh State Cooperative Bank, Gollapudi
d: The Andhra Pradesh State Cooperative Bank is the apex co-operative bank in the state. Indian Cooperative reported on 11 July 2018 that the state Anti-Corruption Bureau had arrested the manager of its Gollapudi branch at Vijayawada, Thumati Chaitanya, while he was taking 50,000 rupees from a loan applicant, Thota Srinivas Kumar, in return for sanctioning a personal loan of 5 lakh rupees. A retired bank manager, not named, was arrested with him for colluding. Both were produced before the Anti-Corruption Bureau's special court and remanded to judicial custody. The report records the arrest and the allegation; it gives no later court finding.
inside: A loan applicant's 50,000 rupees allegedly reached the co-operative bank manager who decides his loan, so the bank's credit decision turned on the payment.
cite: Indian Cooperative, 11 July 2018

n: CBI: a medicine supplier's 1 lakh rupees taken by AIIMS Bhopal's deputy director
org_label: an AIIMS Bhopal medicine and equipment supplier
rank: deputy director (administration), AIIMS Bhopal
d: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences at Bhopal is a central public hospital and medical school, and its administration wing passes suppliers' bills. Medical Dialogues reported on 25 September 2021 that the CBI's anti-corruption branch had arrested the institute's deputy director after a trap with marked currency outside a restaurant near Shahpura police station in Bhopal. The complainant, a pharmacist who supplied medicines and equipment to the hospital, said he had been asked for a tenth of his bills, that 2 lakh rupees was first demanded and the figure settled at 1 lakh, to get a pending bill of about 40 lakh approved. The official was not named. A search of his home was reported to have turned up deposit, insurance and property papers. No verdict was reported.
inside: A hospital supplier's 1 lakh rupees allegedly reached the AIIMS administrator who clears his bills, so a public hospital's payments moved for the suppliers who paid a tenth.
cite: Medical Dialogues, 25 September 2021

n: CBI: a hospital group paid CGHS officers at Meerut to stay on the panel
org_label: a private hospital group in Meerut
rank: additional director and office superintendent, Central Government Health Scheme, Meerut
d: The Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) pays for the treatment of central government employees at private hospitals it puts on its panel; losing that place stops a hospital treating those patients. Medical Dialogues reported that on 12 August 2025 the CBI caught an additional director and an office superintendent of the CGHS office at Swasthya Bhavan, Meerut, with a middleman, Raees Ahmad, as they took money. A director of a hospital group had complained that after a surprise inspection of two of its hospitals on 8 July, notices citing what the complaint called frivolous deficiencies threatened removal from the panel, and that 50 lakh rupees was demanded, with 5 lakh agreed as a first instalment. The officials were not named in the report's text.
inside: A hospital group says it paid the CGHS officers who could strike it off the panel, so a state health scheme's decision on who treats its patients turned on the money.
cite: Medical Dialogues, 13 August 2025

n: Karnataka Lokayukta: a contractor's 50,000 rupees taken by a KPTCL chief engineer
rank: chief engineer, Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited
d: The Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL) is the state-owned company that carries electricity across Karnataka and decides whether a site can be connected. The Deccan Herald reported on 9 August 2023 that Lokayukta police, the state's anti-corruption body, had arrested a KPTCL chief engineer named Nagarajan the previous evening at a KPTCL office, after an electrical contractor, Mohan Kumar, complained that 1 lakh rupees had been demanded for a feasibility study and report on a power connection for a factory. Nagarajan was caught taking 50,000 rupees as a first instalment and was remanded to judicial custody. The report does not say whether the connection was later approved; the case is placed at the company's Bengaluru seat, the city not being named in the report.
inside: A contractor's 50,000 rupees allegedly reached the state grid company engineer deciding his factory's connection, so the study that decides it followed the payment.
cite: Deccan Herald, 9 August 2023

n: Maharashtra ACB: two MSEDCL engineers took 1.84 lakh of a contractor's payment
rank: deputy executive engineer and junior engineer, MSEDCL Panvel
d: The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) is the state-owned power distributor. The Anti-Corruption Bureau at Navi Mumbai laid a trap on Friday 25 April 2025 and arrested Sandeep Daware, 45, a deputy executive engineer in the company's Binghari division at Panvel, and Pratamesh Chowgle, 35, a junior engineer. A contractor who had finished maintenance work for the company and been paid complained that the two had each sought 92,000 rupees, 1.84 lakh in all, as a commission for processing that payment and for a site visit. Both were booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the bureau said it was checking whether other officials were involved. No court ruling was reported.
inside: A contractor's 1.84 lakh rupees allegedly reached the state power company engineers who process his payment, so the utility's money moved on a commission.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 27 April 2025

n: Karnataka Lokayukta: a contractor carried 50,000 rupees for a BESCOM engineer
who: an applicant for a temporary power connection
rank: assistant executive engineer (electrical), BESCOM S-12 subdivision
d: The Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (BESCOM) is the state-owned power distributor for Bengaluru and sanctions how much electricity a connection may draw. On Tuesday 19 May 2026 Lokayukta police, Karnataka's anti-corruption body, arrested Manojkumar B, 53, assistant executive engineer (electrical) at the company's S-12 subdivision office at JP Nagar 7th Phase, and caught Kantharaju, a private electrical contractor, taking 50,000 rupees. The complainant, N Raghuraj, 30, of Hegganahalli, said the engineer had demanded the money to sanction an additional 25 kilowatts for a temporary meter connection and had told him to hand it to the contractor. The reports do not say whether the extra load was sanctioned, and record the allegations only.
inside: An applicant's 50,000 rupees allegedly reached the state power company engineer through a contractor, so how much electricity his meter could draw turned on the payment.
cite: Deccan Herald, Bengaluru; PTI via Devdiscourse, 19 May 2026

n: Odisha Vigilance: a coal trader's 30,000 rupees taken by a deputy director of mines
rank: deputy director, Mines Department, Cuttack Circle
d: Odisha's Mines Department licenses and polices mineral trading through circle offices. OdishaTV reported on 25 February 2026 that the state Vigilance directorate had caught Debabrata Mohanty, deputy director of mines for the Cuttack Circle, taking 30,000 rupees the previous day from a coal trader for official work relating to the complainant; the report gives no further detail of the decision and names no firm. Searches of his office and of his home in the Sree Vihar area of Bhubaneswar followed, and other reports put the cash found at about 4.27 crore rupees. The report describes the allegations as unproven and says an inquiry into his assets continues.
inside: A coal trader's 30,000 rupees allegedly reached the mines officer handling his paperwork, so a state licensing office's work on his file moved on the payment.
cite: OdishaTV, 25 February 2026; Deccan Herald, 25 February 2026

n: MP Lokayukta: Mandla council's chief officer took 2 lakh of a supplier's bill
org_label: M/S Palak Ben, Jabalpur district supplier
rank: chief municipal officer, Mandla Municipal Council
d: Mandla Municipal Council is the local authority for the town of Mandla in Madhya Pradesh and pays the suppliers it buys from. On 25 September 2026 Lokayukta police from Jabalpur trapped its chief municipal officer, Gajanan Nafde, at the council office. The complainant, contractor Gyanchand Ben, 57, of Pindrai village in Jabalpur district, said Nafde had demanded 4 lakh rupees, described as 12 per cent of a payment of 39.23 lakh already processed, to release a further 15 lakh outstanding for supplies; his wife Manju Ben runs the supplying firm, M/S Palak Ben. Officials say Nafde agreed to take 2 lakh and was caught receiving it. He was booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act; the allegations are unproven.
inside: A council supplier's 2 lakh rupees allegedly reached the officer who releases his money, so a municipality's payments moved for the firms that paid a percentage.
cite: Free Press Journal, 25 September 2026

n: MP Lokayukta: Raisen municipality men took 1 lakh over a contractor's deposit
rank: chief municipal officer and staff, Raisen Municipality
d: Raisen Municipality is the local authority for Raisen town in Madhya Pradesh and holds cash security deposits from the contractors it hires. On Friday 13 December 2024 Lokayukta police from Bhopal arrested its chief municipal officer, Badri Prasad Sharma, with two municipality staff, Shubham Jain and Jai Kumar, as they accepted two cheques of 40,000 and 60,000 rupees, 1 lakh in all. The complainant, contractor Rajesh Mishra, had built a cremation ghat in Raisen in 2021 and been paid in 2023 but had not recovered his 3.50 lakh rupee deposit, and said the three demanded 1 lakh to release it. All three were caught while accepting; an FIR was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
inside: A contractor's 1 lakh rupees allegedly reached the municipal officers holding his deposit, so a council's return of his own money turned on a payment to them.
cite: Free Press Journal, 14 December 2024

n: Telangana ACB: Huzurabad municipality engineer took 50,000 of a drain bill
org_label: a Huzurabad storm water drain contractor
rank: assistant engineer, Huzurabad Municipality, Karimnagar
d: Huzurabad Municipality in Karimnagar district is the local authority for the town, and its engineers enter completed work in the measurement book before a contractor's final bill is paid. On Wednesday 15 April 2026 Telangana's Anti-Corruption Bureau trapped and arrested its assistant engineer, Nusum Sudhakar Reddy, as he took 50,000 rupees from a contractor who had built a storm water drain. The bureau says he demanded the money to record the work in the measurement book and process the final bill. He was produced before the bureau's special police establishment at Karimnagar.
