The report carries the bureau's allegations; no court finding is recorded.
inside: A drain contractor's 50,000 rupees allegedly reached the municipal engineer who must certify his work, so the council's record of what was built and paid for followed the money.
cite: The Siasat Daily, 15 April 2026

n: Telangana ACB: an electric contractor paid two TSPDCL staff for a connection
rank: assistant engineer and line inspector, TSPDCL Banjara Hills circle
d: The Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TSPDCL) is the state-owned electricity distributor for southern Telangana and decides when a meter is released and a service connection given. Telangana Today reported on 31 May 2022 that the state Anti-Corruption Bureau had arrested two of its staff in the Banjara Hills circle: I. Avinash, assistant engineer (operations) for the Sanathnagar section, caught demanding and accepting 10,000 rupees from a private electrical contractor to release a meter and give a service connection, and C. Krupananda Reddy, a line inspector, who demanded 7,500 rupees and took 3,500 as a first payment from the same contractor. Officials said the two had performed their duties dishonestly to obtain undue advantage.
inside: A contractor's cash allegedly reached the two power company staff who release meters, so a state utility gave his customers connections on the strength of the payments.
cite: Telangana Today, 31 May 2022

n: Maharashtra ACB: MSEDCL engineer at Dahanu took 2 lakh over a power theft case
who: an electricity consumer facing a theft penalty
rank: junior engineer, MSEDCL Dahanu, Palghar district
d: The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) is the state-owned power distributor, and its engineers decide whether to pursue a case of electricity theft and whether to restore supply. The Free Press Journal reported on 21 March 2025 that the Anti-Corruption Bureau in Palghar district had caught Atul Ashok Avhad, a junior engineer posted at Dahanu, taking the first instalment of a 2 lakh rupee bribe; the report says he demanded 3 lakh in all. The complainant, who was not named, ran a buffalo stable where electricity was said to have been stolen by tapping the main line, and faced a penalty of 7 lakh rupees. The money was allegedly sought to drop the theft action and reconnect the supply. The complaint was filed on 20 March.
inside: A consumer facing a power theft penalty allegedly paid the utility engineer handling his case, so the state company's enforcement and his supply both turned on the money.
cite: Free Press Journal, 21 March 2025

n: CBI: a Kolkata rice transporter paid Food Corporation's Odisha general manager
org_label: SP Traders and Suppliers Pvt Ltd, Kolkata
rank: general manager, Food Corporation of India, Odisha region
d: The Food Corporation of India is the state company that buys, stores and moves the grain behind India's public food system, and hires private firms to carry it. The CBI registered a case on 28 June 2024 and in a trap arrested Prem Singh Bhanot, general manager of the corporation's Odisha region at Bhubaneswar, with a middleman, Syed Hasnain Ahmed, and Malina Dey, proprietor of M/s SP Traders and Suppliers Pvt Ltd; a manager (accounts), Sanjoy Dey, was arrested later. The CBI says Bhanot favoured the firm, declared lowest bidder in a tender for transportation of rice grain, to help it secure the work order, and asked 5 lakh rupees for the favour; 1 lakh was received in the trap. All four were remanded to police custody.
inside: A transport firm's money allegedly reached the Food Corporation's regional head, so the state grain buyer's rice haulage contract went to the bidder that paid.
cite: PTI via Business Standard, 2 July 2024; Free Press Journal, 2 July 2024

n: Maharashtra ACB: MIDC engineer took 1 crore rupees over a pipeline bill
rank: assistant engineer, Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation, Ahmednagar
d: The Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) is the state company that builds and services industrial estates. On 3 November 2023 the state Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested Amit Kishore Gaikwad, 32, an assistant engineer with the corporation at Ahmednagar, near the Ahmednagar-Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar bypass road, over a bribe of 1 crore rupees demanded and accepted from a contractor doing pipeline work in the Ahmednagar estate. The report says the money was sought to sanction the contractor's pending final bill of 2,66,99,244 rupees, to clear a back-dated bill and to obtain the signature of the then sub-divisional engineer, and that Gaikwad sought it for himself and for that engineer, who was then being sought by the bureau.
inside: A contractor's 1 crore rupees allegedly reached the state industrial corporation's engineer, so the final bill of 2,66,99,244 rupees it owed him moved only once he paid.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 4 November 2023

n: Karnataka Lokayukta: KIADB land officer took 15 lakh over a revenue order
who: a landholder with a case before the board
rank: special assistant commissioner (north) and special land acquisition officer, KIADB
d: The Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (KIADB) acquires land for industrial estates in the state, and its special land acquisition officers decide revenue matters over that land. ThePrint reported on 29 April 2026 that Lokayukta police had arrested Nagaprashanth, special assistant commissioner (north) and special land acquisition officer-1 with the board, and his outsourced driver, after a trap in which 15 lakh rupees was accepted. The complainant, Ravi Kumar, 41, of Attur in Yelahanka, said 30 lakh had been demanded for a favourable order in a pending Rapid Revenue Team matter before the assistant commissioner (north) office, and that the driver had earlier taken 15 lakh on the officer's instructions. The allegations are unproven and the investigation continues.
inside: A landholder's 15 lakh rupees allegedly reached the board officer deciding his own revenue case, so the decision on his land turned on the payment.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 29 April 2026

n: CBI: a Delhi shed holder paid a DSIIDC manager 1.7 lakh to avoid sealing
who: a small manufacturer holding a DSIIDC shed
rank: senior manager, Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation
d: The Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC) is the city government's industrial company and allots and polices the sheds in its estates. On 13 January 2022 the CBI arrested S.K. Singh, a senior manager with the corporation, and a man named Subhash, after they were caught taking 1.7 lakh rupees. The complainant made cream separator machines in a shed at Mangolpuri allotted to him by the corporation, and said Singh demanded the money so that the shed would not be sealed over an alleged encroachment, telling him to hand it over to Subhash at Karol Bagh. Both were produced in court and sent to 14 days' judicial custody; the CBI reported recovering documents in searches.
inside: A shed holder's 1.7 lakh rupees allegedly reached the corporation manager who could seal his workshop, so the state estate company's enforcement followed the payment.
cite: IANS via Lokmat Times, 13 January 2022

n: Maharashtra ACB: CIDCO engineer at Belapur caught over six pending bills
who: a contractor with bills before CIDCO
rank: engineer, City and Industrial Development Corporation, Belapur
d: The City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) is the Maharashtra state company that built Navi Mumbai and pays the contractors who work for it. The Free Press Journal reported on Wednesday 19 January 2022 that the Anti-Corruption Bureau had caught Kalyan Patil, 57, an engineer with the corporation posted at Belapur, taking 30,000 rupees as an instalment. The complainant said Patil had demanded 3 lakh rupees to clear six pending bills and had earlier taken 1.20 lakh. A case was booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act; the report does not say he was arrested and records no court outcome.
inside: A contractor's instalment allegedly reached the state corporation engineer sitting on six of his bills, so the money Navi Mumbai's builder owed him moved on a cut.
cite: Free Press Journal, 19 January 2022

n: Telangana ACB: a rice miller's 75,000 rupees skipped a PDS quality check
rank: district manager, Civil Supplies office, Asifabad
d: The district civil supplies offices of Telangana take in the rice that mills deliver for the public distribution system and check its quality before it enters the state godowns. On Thursday 6 November 2025 the state Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested the district manager at the civil supplies office in Asifabad district, not named in the report, after 75,000 rupees was recovered from him. The bureau says the money was demanded from the complainant, who owns a rice mill, to let three lorries of public distribution rice from his mill go to the godown without the rice being checked for quality, and that a technical assistant on an outsourced contract made the demand on the manager's instructions. The case is under investigation.
inside: A miller's 75,000 rupees allegedly reached the district civil supplies manager, so the state took in three lorries of ration rice without checking its quality.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 6 November 2025

n: Telangana ACB: 1.40 lakh rupees to police to stop an arrest in a PDS rice case
org_label: a complainant facing arrest in a ration rice case
who: a man facing arrest over ration rice
rank: sub-inspector and constable, Thirumalagiri police station, Suryapet
d: Thirumalagiri police station in Suryapet district, Telangana, was handling a case over the distribution of subsidised public distribution system rice. The state Anti-Corruption Bureau said that a sub-inspector and a constable there, Vukkurthy Suresh and Nagaraju, demanded 3 lakh rupees from the man under investigation and were paid 1.40 lakh in all, 1 lakh for the sub-inspector and 40,000 for the constable, in return for issuing him a notice under section 35 of the new criminal procedure code that would keep him from being arrested. The constable took 30,000 rupees by PhonePe on 25 January 2025 and a further 70,000 passed through him on 28 January; the tainted 70,000 was recovered from him.
inside: A man under investigation over ration rice allegedly paid the two officers handling his case, so the police decision not to arrest him was bought.
cite: The Siasat Daily, 28 January 2025

n: Telangana ACB: Keesara police took 5 lakh rupees over a ration rice case
org_label: a complainant in a ration rice case
who: a man held in a public distribution rice case
rank: inspector and sub-inspector, Keesara police station
d: Keesara police station, on the edge of Hyderabad in Telangana, was handling a case under the public distribution system, which supplies subsidised rice. Telangana Today reported on 17 September 2026 that the state Anti-Corruption Bureau had arrested the station's inspector, Arkapally Anjaneyulu, and its sub-inspector, Dyapa Gnanender Reddy, over a bribe of 5 lakh rupees. The bureau says the money was demanded from a complainant, who was not named, in return for granting him station bail and showing him favour in the rice case, and that it was collected on the inspector's instructions, with Reddy caught accepting it on the Wednesday night. The report carries the bureau's allegations only.
inside: A man in a ration rice case allegedly paid 5 lakh rupees to the two officers running it, so his bail and the course of the case followed his money.
cite: Telangana Today, 17 September 2026

n: Delhi ACB: a sewage plant bidder's money and a Jal Board tender rewritten
rank: chief executive and consultant, Delhi Jal Board; former Delhi minister
d: The Delhi Jal Board is the city government's water and sewage utility. On 18 August 2026 Delhi's Anti-Corruption Branch arrested six people over the tender to upgrade the board's sewage treatment plants: Satyendar Jain, a former Delhi minister; Udit Prakash Rai, a former chief executive of the board; Ankit Srivastava, a former contractual consultant to it; and three private individuals, Nagendra Yadav, Raja Kumar Kurra and Pankaj Verma. The branch, which registered the case on 11 May 2024, alleges restrictive technical specifications favoured Euroteck Environment Pvt Ltd and that conditions drafted among private persons, officials and intermediaries were put into the board's tender notice. It alleges commission money moved through intermediaries Srijanhar and AN Enterprises and that Rai received 1.52 crore rupees in his and relatives' accounts.
inside: A supplier's conditions were allegedly written into the Jal Board's own tender and 1.52 crore rupees reached its chief executive, so the utility bought what that firm sold.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 18 August 2026

n: CBI: a Mumbai developer's 50 lakh rupees for a CPWD no-objection letter
rank: executive engineer, Central Public Works Department, Mumbai
d: The Central Public Works Department builds and holds land for the central government, and a developer needs its no-objection certificate to show the department has no claim on a plot. The CBI laid a trap on 1 October 2026 and caught Vikrant Verma, an executive engineer of the department at Mumbai, at Vashi in Navi Mumbai, with his relative Saurav Gupta, who allegedly collected 50 lakh rupees. Also named were Arvind Semwal, a vice president of the Baya Group of Companies, which was building apartments and sought the certificate, its manager Chetan Mahajan, and Anil Deshmukh, a partner in Baya's firm Renaissance. The CBI says Verma demanded 1 crore, settled at 70 lakh, and issued the letter without a dispatch number.
inside: A developer's 50 lakh rupees allegedly reached the works department engineer, so the certificate clearing its Mumbai site of any state claim was issued for payment.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 2 October 2026

n: CBI: Delhi courts works engineer took three per cent of contractors' bills
rank: executive engineer, judiciary civil division-2, Public Works Department, Delhi
d: The judiciary civil division of Delhi's Public Works Department maintains the city's court buildings and pays the contractors who do the work. On Monday 28 July 2025 the CBI arrested Kalu Ram Meena, executive engineer of its division-2 at the Rouse Avenue district court complex, in a trap in which a contractor paid him 30,000 rupees. The CBI alleges he demanded three per cent of the contractors' bills he was responsible for clearing. Searches at Delhi and Jaipur recovered cash, which the CBI's statement put at 1.60 crore rupees, along with property documents and a bank account. No court decision has been reported.
inside: A contractor's cash allegedly reached the works engineer who clears his bills, so payment by a government department ran on a standing three per cent cut.
cite: PTI via ThePrint, 29 July 2025

n: Maharashtra ACB: Jalgaon works engineer took 5 lakh over a road bill
rank: branch engineer, Public Works Department, Jalgaon
d: The Public Works Department in Maharashtra sanctions and pays for local road building. The Free Press Journal reported on 11 May 2026 that the Anti-Corruption Bureau at Jalgaon had caught Yogesh Abhimanyu Ahire, a branch engineer with the department, taking 5 lakh rupees as a first instalment, the cash left under the front seat of his car. The complainant had built a cement-concrete road in Vinoba Nagar, ward 14, sanctioned in 2024 at 80.39 lakh rupees, had been paid about 42 lakh in October 2025 and had 38.49 lakh outstanding. He said 17 lakh was first demanded and 15 lakh settled, half of it for Ahire and the rest for senior officials. A court remanded Ahire for two days.
inside: A road contractor's 5 lakh rupees allegedly reached the works engineer holding his bill, so the balance a government department owed him moved only on a share.
cite: Free Press Journal, 11 May 2026

n: Telangana ACB: Moinabad municipality officers took 75,000 over a building
who: an owner of a building facing demolition action
rank: town planning officer and senior assistant, Moinabad Municipality
d: Moinabad Municipality, on the western edge of Hyderabad, decides whether a building is unauthorised and whether to act against it. Telangana's Anti-Corruption Bureau said it trapped two of its officers on 30 September 2026: Gundu Vani, the town planning officer, who it alleges demanded 75,000 rupees from the complainant so that his construction would not be treated as illegal and faced with coercive action, and Yelamoni Sudarshan, a former Moinabad gram panchayat secretary on deputation as a senior assistant, from whom the 75,000 rupees was recovered. Both were taken into custody and were to be produced before the special judge for anti-corruption cases at Nampally. The case remains under investigation.
inside: A builder's 75,000 rupees allegedly reached the municipal planning officer judging his building, so a council's decision on whether to demolish it turned on the money.
cite: Deccan Chronicle, 1 October 2026

n: MP Lokayukta: a road contractor's 10 lakh rupees for a works superintendent
rank: superintendent engineer, Public Works Department, Narmadapuram
d: Madhya Pradesh's Public Works Department pays the contractors who build its roads, and the bill passes through the superintendent engineer of the circle. The Free Press Journal reported that on Sunday 28 July 2024 a Lokayukta special police establishment team from Bhopal caught RC Tirole, superintendent engineer at Narmadapuram, taking 10 lakh rupees at his government residence. The complainant, a contractor who had built eight roads at Multai and Bhaidehi in Betul district, said he had been asked for 20 lakh rupees to clear his bill and that the 10 lakh was a first instalment. The report records the trap and the allegation; it does not say he was charged or tried.
inside: A road contractor's 10 lakh rupees allegedly reached the engineer who signs off his bill, so a state department's payment for eight finished roads waited on the money.
cite: Free Press Journal, 29 July 2024

n: Odisha Vigilance: a contractor's 2 lakh rupees taken by a rural works engineer
rank: executive engineer, rural development, Rayagada
d: Odisha's rural development department builds village roads and works and pays its contractors through the executive engineer of each division. The Deccan Chronicle reported on 24 June 2026 that the state Vigilance directorate had arrested Prasanna Pattnaik, executive engineer for rural development at Rayagada, in a trap as he accepted 2 lakh rupees. The complainant, contractor Sanyasi Subuddhi, said Pattnaik had first demanded 3 lakh to clear a pending bill, that he could not pay the whole sum, and that 50,000 rupees was also sought for issuing experience certificates. Pattnaik, who was due to retire on 30 June, was booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and four premises linked to him were searched over his assets.
inside: A contractor's 2 lakh rupees allegedly reached the engineer holding his bill, so a state department's payment and even his work certificates turned on the money.
cite: Deccan Chronicle, 24 June 2026

n: CBI: a Mumbai firm's 3 crore rupees to BECIL's chairman for a 50 crore loan
rank: chairman and managing director, Broadcast Engineering Consultants India Limited
d: Broadcast Engineering Consultants India Limited (BECIL) is a central government company that advises on and funds broadcasting projects. The CBI registered a case on 3 September 2024 and alleges that its then chairman and managing director, George Kuruvilla, took 3 crore rupees from Prateek Kanakia, chief executive and founder of the Mumbai firm M/s TGBL, and sanctioned a 50 crore rupee venture loan to it; that the firm put in a fake 25 crore rupee performance bank guarantee; and that the money was neither used as intended nor repaid, leaving BECIL a wrongful loss of 58 crore. Kanakia was arrested on 24 March 2025; Kuruvilla and a former general manager, W.B. Prasad, were produced before the special CBI court at Mumbai on 19 April 2025.
inside: A borrower's 3 crore rupees allegedly reached the state company's chairman, so its 50 crore rupee loan went to the firm that paid him and was never repaid.
cite: Free Press Journal, 19 April 2025

n: Delhi ACB: Jal Board junior assistant took 20,000 to clear a pension file
org_label: the son of a former Delhi Jal Board employee
who: the heir of a deceased utility employee
rank: junior assistant, Delhi Jal Board, Dilshad Garden
d: The Delhi Jal Board is the city government's water utility and settles the dues owed to the families of its dead employees. The Millennium Post reported on 24 November 2023 that Delhi's Anti-Corruption Branch had arrested Meetu Goswami, 35, a junior assistant at the board since 2016, at its office in GTB Enclave, Dilshad Garden, at about 3.30pm. The complainant, whose late father had worked for the board and who was given the pseudonym Rajesh in the report, said she first demanded 60,000 rupees and settled at 40,000, and that during the raid she asked for 20,000 as a token with the rest to follow once his father's file was cleared. He handed over 20,000 before a witness. A case was registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
inside: A dead employee's son allegedly had to pay 20,000 rupees to the clerk holding his father's file, so the utility settled what it owed him only for money.
cite: Millennium Post, 24 November 2023

n: Entrepreneur paid KMG EP-Catering's director for food supply decisions
org_label: An individual entrepreneur supplying food products
rank: General director, KMG EP-Catering
d: KMG EP-Catering is a company wholly owned by Kazakhstan's state oil firm JSC NC KazMunayGas, and it feeds the oil company's subsidiaries in the Mangystau region. Its general director, B. Kiyalbaev, took a bribe of 3 million tenge from an individual entrepreneur in exchange for a favourable decision on buying and supplying food products, and for continuing protection. Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Service in Mangystau investigated, and on 28 January Aktau City Court found Kiyalbaev guilty of accepting a bribe, fining him 56 million tenge and barring him for life from certain state posts. The case was announced by the national Anti-Corruption Agency.
inside: A private food supplier paid the head of the state oil company's catering arm 3 million tenge, and the arm's purchasing decisions then went the supplier's way.
cite: Azattyq Ruhy, citing the press service of Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Agency, 29 January 2020

n: Power grid director paid Jetisu monopolies regulator for a higher electricity tariff
org_label: Taldykorgan Transport and Power Grid Company
who: Taldykorgan Transport and Power Grid Company
rank: Head of the Department for the Regulation of Natural Monopolies
d: In Kazakhstan electricity tariffs are set by a state regulator, the Department for the Regulation of Natural Monopolies. Aibek Kuzembayev, director of the Taldykorgan Transport and Power Grid Company, paid 500,000 tenge to Arman Sagymbekov, who headed that department, for approval of an increased electricity transportation rate for households in 2025. The anti-corruption agency Antikor described the approved rates as inflated. A court in the Jetisu region convicted both men: Sagymbekov was fined 15 million tenge and Kuzembayev 10 million tenge, and both were barred from public service and quasi-state posts. The report is inconsistent about which man handed the money over.
inside: An electricity company paid the official who sets its tariffs 500,000 tenge, and the regulator then approved the higher rate the company wanted charged to households.
cite: Orda (English), 21 May 2025, citing Antikor

n: SpetsKommunStroy paid Almaty's heating network chiefs to sign off work
rank: General director and chief engineer, Almaty Heating Networks
d: Almaty Heating Networks (AlTS) runs the heat supply system of Kazakhstan's largest city, and was rebuilding it under contract. Three of its managers took a bribe of 16 million tenge for signing work-completion certificates and releasing payments under those contracts: general director K. Beisenbinov, chief engineer D. Kazymbetov and capital construction head S. Dzhingilbayev. Medeu District Court in Almaty, giving a second verdict in the case, fined each of them 560 million tenge and barred them permanently from state service. The director of the contractor SpetsKommunStroy, whose name was not given, was fined 400 million tenge for paying the bribe.
inside: A contractor paid three managers of the city's state heating company 16 million tenge, and they then certified its work and released its payments.
cite: Bizmedia.kz, 13 March 2023

n: Contractor paid Elorda Qurylys Kompaniyasy's director 170m tenge to raise an estimate
rank: General director, Yelorda Kurylys Kompaniyasy
d: Elorda Qurylys Kompaniyasy, also written Elorda Qurylys Kompaniyasy, is a state-owned developer in Kazakhstan's capital that takes over and finishes stalled building projects. A contractor, which the report does not name, paid its general director Ruslan Kadesov a bribe of 170 million tenge to increase the cost estimate for a building. Kadesov was sentenced to 10 years in prison and an intermediary who passed the money to six months; both had property confiscated and were banned from civil service work. They appealed, asking the court to reclassify the offence, but the sentence was left unchanged and the decision has entered into legal force.
inside: A building contractor paid the state developer's own chief executive 170 million tenge, and the company then raised the price it would pay for the contractor's work.
cite: Orda (English), 20 November 2024

n: Clinic director paid North Kazakhstan's health chief to overturn a council decision
rank: Head of the North Kazakhstan regional health department
d: Ainagul Karabayeva, director of the private non-profit clinic Densaulyk in Petropavlovsk, put 200,000 tenge in an envelope in the work folder of Kabdrakhman Saktaganov, head of the North Kazakhstan regional health department, on 23 September 2021. She wanted him to help overturn a May 2021 decision of the regional maslikhat, the elected regional council, which had barred graduates posted to her clinic from social support including a 1.5 million tenge settling-in payment, because the clinic is not state-run. He said he would personally back the request. Both admitted guilt and signed plea agreements; Petropavlovsk City Court fined him about 5.8 million tenge and her 4 million tenge, with lifetime bans from office.
inside: A private clinic paid the regional health chief 200,000 tenge to get a council decision that excluded its staff from state support reopened in its favour.
cite: Forbes Kazakhstan, 27 October 2021

n: Construction firm paid Astana emergency, building and audit officials for approvals
rank: Heads of Astana's emergency situations and construction departments
d: Representatives of a private construction company, which the report does not name, bribed officials across three Astana bodies. B. Beisenkanov, head of the city's Emergency Situations Department, took 5 million tenge for approving documents declaring the Kazhymukan Mungaitpasuly Central Stadium to be in an emergency state, and was jailed for five years. A. Zhangaskanov, head of the city construction department, took 400,000 tenge for patronage and for signing completed-work certificates under state procurement contracts, and got four and a half years. Two internal state audit officials were fined for a positive audit conclusion. The company's representatives were fined about 500 million tenge in total. The verdict had not entered into force.
inside: A builder's money reached three city bodies at once, which then declared a stadium unsafe, signed off its work and gave it a clean audit.
cite: Forbes Kazakhstan, 10 October 2023, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency

n: Entrepreneur paid Shymkent's building department head to accept a sports complex
rank: Head of the construction department, Shymkent
d: An entrepreneur paid 400,000 tenge to the head of the construction department in Shymkent, Kazakhstan's third city, so that the certificate accepting a finished building into operation would be signed without obstruction. The official was also accused of general patronage over a sports complex being built in the village of Agybet, in the Baydibek district of the Turkestan region. He was fined 12 million tenge, which the report describes as thirty times the bribe, and the verdict had not yet taken effect at the time of publication. The case was reported in May 2023.
inside: A builder paid the city official who signs buildings into use 400,000 tenge, and his department then cleared the work without obstruction.
cite: Bizmedia.kz, 18 May 2023

n: Shanyrak Stroy Invest won no-tender contracts from Shymkent's state housing firm
rank: Deputy director, Turgyn Uy Shymkent
d: Turgyn Uy Shymkent is the city's state housing company. In 2023 and 2024 its deputy director, Serik Kusherbekov, terminated an existing contract with the firm PMK-7 LTD and awarded the work without a tender to Shanyrak Stroy Invest, run by his accomplice Baglan Pernebek; the price rose to 172 million tenge and the scope to 78 houses, and the contract was described as fictitious. Work on 43 apartment blocks already paid for at 6.45 million tenge was paid again to the same firm at 88.7 million tenge. Shymkent's interdistrict criminal court jailed Kusherbekov for seven and a half years and Pernebek for seven, with restitution of 88.74 million tenge.
inside: A contractor took the state housing company's work without a tender through its deputy director, who shared in the proceeds and was ordered to repay them.
cite: Kazinform, 13 June 2025

n: Street contractor paid the head of Almaty Tazalyk to sign and extend its contract
rank: Head of Almaty Tazalyk
d: Almaty Tazalyk is the state enterprise that cleans Kazakhstan's largest city. Its head, Adlet Toktasynov, held back the signature on a work-completion certificate and the extension of a street and pavement maintenance contract worth up to 222 million tenge, signed in May 2023 with the firm Qala Korkeitu. On 15 December 2023 the firm's director Samat Baizhanov handed him 2.7 million tenge in a car. Toktasynov entered a plea agreement, admitted guilt, was fined about 78.4 million tenge without confiscation and was released in the courtroom. Baizhanov was sentenced to three years and six months in a medium-security facility.
inside: A maintenance contractor paid the city cleaning enterprise's director 2.7 million tenge, and he then signed off its work and extended its contract.
cite: Bes.media, 3 July 2024

n: Businesswoman paid Aktobe medical university's rector to win equipment tenders
rank: Rector, West Kazakhstan Medical University
d: Aset Kaliev became rector of the West Kazakhstan Marat Ospanov Medical University in Aktobe in autumn 2022. According to the case materials he promised the businesswoman Inessa Muturganova help with state contracts, and her companies then repeatedly won the university's equipment tenders, worth nearly 196 million tenge, with over 182 million tenge paid out between December 2023 and May 2024. A charity agreement for 249 million tenge had been signed in September 2023. On 28 May 2024 she handed him 11.64 million tenge near a hotel in Aktobe; investigators found the cash in his freezer. Both pleaded not guilty and both were jailed for eight years.
inside: A supplier paid the rector 11.64 million tenge and her firms then kept winning the university's equipment tenders, which is how its purchasing served her.
cite: Informburo.kz, report on the verdict against the former rector of the Aktobe medical university

n: Sixteen shippers paid Kaztemirtrans staff for scarce railway wagons
rank: Officials of a branch of JSC Kaztemirtrans
d: JSC Kaztemirtrans owns and allocates the freight wagons of Kazakhstan's state railway. Businessmen shipping freight paid officials of one of its branches, systematically between 2019 and 2022, for unhindered provision of wagons at a time when wagons were scarce; the scheme was uncovered in 2022. The case was heard on 18 March 2024. Four Kaztemirtrans employees were convicted of taking bribes, three receiving prison terms and one released from punishment because he had died. Sixteen businessmen who paid were found guilty; fifteen were released from criminal liability for admitting guilt and helping solve the crime, and one who did not admit guilt was fined 49 million tenge. The verdict had not entered into legal force.
inside: Freight firms paid the state wagon company's own staff, and the queue for scarce wagons was then ordered to suit the payers rather than other shippers.
cite: Newtimes.kz, 19 March 2024, citing the prosecutor's office

n: Diesel trader's $100,000 for fuel contracts at KTZ's locomotive subsidiary
org_label: Nur Tabys Munay NTM LLP (per earlier reporting)
rank: Executive director, JSC Lokomotiv
d: JSC Lokomotiv is the locomotive arm of Kazakhstan's state railway KTZ and buys large volumes of diesel. Its executive director Yergali Kalaubaev agreed on 29 May 2013 that a businessman would pay him 15 dollars for every tonne of diesel delivered, in return for supply contracts, prompt payment and help with paperwork; Kalaubaev knew an open tender was not practicable because few suppliers could handle the volumes. On 16 May 2014 the businessman handed 100,000 dollars to a trusted intermediary for onward delivery, and the intermediary was detained during the handover. Earlier reporting cited in the account linked the money to a representative of the firm Nur Tabys Munay NTM. Astana's specialised interdistrict criminal court jailed Kalaubaev for seven years with confiscation.
inside: A fuel trader bought the state railway's locomotive company's diesel contracts at a dollar-a-tonne rate agreed with its executive director.
cite: Tengrinews.kz, 9 February 2015

n: Entrepreneurs paid 25.4m tenge to the head of Kazakhstan's suburban rail branch
rank: Director, Suburban Transportation branch, JSC Passazhirskie Perevozki
d: JSC Passazhirskie Perevozki runs Kazakhstan's state passenger rail services, and its Suburban Transportation branch handles commuter trains. The branch director, Sultan Tabynbayev, repeatedly took bribes from entrepreneurs totalling 25.4 million tenge for the unimpeded signing of work-completion certificates and for patronage. Astana's interdistrict criminal court jailed him for seven and a half years with a lifetime ban from state posts; two of the entrepreneurs who paid, D.R. Sabitov and A.Zh. Dusikenov, were sentenced to seven and four years with lifetime bans of their own. The verdict had not entered into force. The facts come from an Anti-Corruption Service official, Arman Tleukenov.
inside: Contractors paid the state commuter rail branch's director 25.4 million tenge, and he then certified their work without obstruction.
cite: BES.media, 15 November 2023, citing Antikor; Kazpravda.kz, citing the Astana department of the Anti-Corruption Agency

n: Contractor's men paid Pavlodar's deputy mayor to sign off completed work
rank: Deputy akim (deputy mayor) of Pavlodar
d: Arslan Kaliyakbarov, deputy akim or deputy mayor of the northern Kazakh city of Pavlodar, took 1.8 million tenge from representatives of a private contracting organisation for the unimpeded signing of work-completion certificates and for general patronage. He was arrested in June 2023 and sentenced to three and a half years in prison, with a bar on returning to the civil service. The case was announced by an official of Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Service, Arman Tleukenov, and the report does not give the court's city or the date of his sentence.
inside: A contracting firm paid the deputy mayor 1.8 million tenge, and the city then signed off its work without obstruction.
cite: BES.media, 15 November 2023, citing Antikor

n: Road contractor paid for signatures at KazAvtoZhol's Pavlodar branch
rank: Deputy director, Pavlodar branch of JSC NC KazAvtoZhol
d: JSC NC KazAvtoZhol is Kazakhstan's national roads company. A businessman who had been given five road sections for capital and medium repairs in the Pavlodar region completed the work, but said he had to pay to get the completion certificates signed. He paid 90,000 tenge to the deputy director of KazAvtoZhol's Pavlodar branch for one signature, and 300,000 tenge to the head of the state road laboratory Pavlodarzhollaboratoriya. The branch director, his deputy and the laboratory head all asked for money, and he did not refuse. The deputy director and the contractor both took procedural agreements; he was fined 1.8 million tenge and the contractor ordered to pay the state 6 million tenge. Cases against the other two continued.
inside: A road contractor paid the state roads company's branch deputy and the state road laboratory's head to get his completion certificates signed.
cite: NUR.KZ, 1 July 2019

n: Businessman paid Yekibastuz emergency chiefs to win fire service contracts
rank: Head and deputy head, Yekibastuz city emergency department
d: The emergency department of Yekibastuz, a coal and power town in northern Kazakhstan, is part of the civil defence service. Its head Kukonev and his deputy Maimanov repeatedly took bribes from a local businessman, Zhumashev, totalling 7.4 million tenge, and in return helped his company win contracts with a non-governmental fire service. Yekibastuz city court jailed Kukonev for seven years and six months, Maimanov for seven years and Zhumashev for seven years, barred all three permanently from the civil service and the quasi-public sector, and stripped the two officers of their civil defence ranks. The verdict had not entered into legal force. The case came from Antikor.
inside: A businessman paid the town's emergency chiefs 7.4 million tenge, and they then helped his company win fire service contracts.
cite: Orda (English), 7 April 2025, citing Antikor

n: Contractor billed Aqkol's housing department for boilers it never installed
rank: Head of the Aqkol District Housing Department
d: In 2022 the housing department of Aqkol district, in Kazakhstan's Aqmola region, contracted a private company to repair heating boilers. The company's paperwork said three boilers had been installed; they never were. The department head knowingly signed the documents and approved payment, and over 8 million tenge was taken. The district court gave the department head and the company's director three and a half years of restricted freedom each, with a lifetime bar from the civil service for the official and bans on management and financial roles for the director. The court counted his breach of his official oath as an aggravating factor, and remorse, young children and repayment of the damage as mitigating. Neither the people nor the company were named, and the verdict had not taken legal effect.
inside: A repair company was paid for boilers it never installed because the district housing department's own head signed its paperwork and released the money.
cite: Orda (English), 10 February 2025

n: Lorry drivers paid Qostanay phytosanitary inspectors to move quarantined cargo
rank: Phytosanitary control inspectors, Qostanay region
d: Phytosanitary control inspectors in Kazakhstan's Qostanay region check whether plant products under quarantine may be moved. Thirteen lorry drivers paid two of the inspectors sums between 2,000 and 20,000 tenge so that quarantined agricultural goods could pass without obstruction. The transport prosecutor's office brought the case and the Qarabal district court convicted the inspectors and the drivers, barring the two inspectors from government agencies for life and ordering all the defendants to repay what they had taken. At the prosecutor's request the court also sent a private ruling to the State Inspection Committee under the Ministry of Agriculture. The report does not give the dates of the offences.
inside: Hauliers paid the inspectors who police plant quarantine, and the quarantine checks then let their cargo through.
cite: Orda (English), 12 May 2025

n: Businessman paid Jambyl's land management chief to get a plot returned
org_label: An entrepreneur seeking a land plot
rank: Head of the land management department, Jambyl region
d: D.M. headed the land management department of Kazakhstan's Jambyl region, having earlier been a chief specialist at the region's own civil service and anti-corruption office. The court found he conspired to extort money from a businessman, offering to resolve a land issue and help return a plot to him in exchange for payment, although he had no legal authority to do so. One million tenge changed hands in January 2025 at a street corner in Taraz, where Anti-Corruption Agency officers detained him on the spot. He fully admitted guilt to fraud and incitement to bribery and was sentenced to three and a half years in a medium-security facility with a permanent ban from state posts.
inside: An entrepreneur's million tenge reached the official who runs the region's land records, bought with a promise that his plot would be returned.
cite: Orda (English), 2 May 2025

n: Company directors paid Ulytau's ecology chiefs over emission approvals
org_label: Directors of several limited liability companies
rank: Head and deputy head, Ulytau regional ecology department
d: The ecology department of Kazakhstan's Ulytau region approves environmental projects and emission standards, including for the mining town of Satpayev. General directors of several unnamed limited liability companies allegedly paid its head Dastan Tleubekov and his deputy, who took a combined 5,250,000 tenge in autumn 2024, with a further 2,500,000 tenge to Tleubekov in January, in exchange for assisting businesses. A separate allegation that a businessman paid him for an environmental permit was dismissed for unstated reasons. A court in Jezkazgan jailed Tleubekov and his deputy for six years and fined the two business executives 35 million and 70 million tenge.
inside: Industrial companies' directors paid the officials who approve emission limits, and the region's environmental approvals then assisted the payers.
cite: Orda (English), 20 February 2025

n: Chinese road firm's Kazakh arm paid East Kazakhstan's ecology chief
rank: Head of the East Kazakhstan regional ecology department
d: Xinxin LLP is the Kazakh arm of a Chinese company repairing the Kalbatau-Maikapshagay highway in eastern Kazakhstan. Kanat Dyrynbaev, a road construction company deputy director and Xinxin's head of government relations, allegedly paid Mamay Butabayev, head of the East Kazakhstan regional ecology department, who received 8.5 million tenge on 13 July 2024 as what investigators called an advance against an expected 130 million tenge. In exchange Butabayev allegedly promised Xinxin general protection and to ignore environmental violations. He was arrested the same day, did not admit guilt, and was jailed for ten years and one month, as was Dyrynbaev. His lawyer Erik Khalelov said there is not a single fact confirming the alleged patronage, and the defence may appeal.
inside: A foreign road contractor's local arm paid the regional environment chief, who allegedly promised to overlook the firm's environmental violations.
cite: Orda (English), 17 October 2025

n: Customs brokers paid Almaty's central customs laboratory for fast expert reports
rank: Head of the Central Customs Laboratory, Almaty
d: The Central Customs Laboratory, which answers to the State Revenue Committee of Kazakhstan's finance ministry, tests goods crossing the customs border for composition, quality and legal compliance, and importers cannot clear them without its expert reports. Its head Satybaldiev and chief specialist Alibekov took bribes from business owners for the accelerated issuance of those reports. The Almaly District Court in Almaty sentenced both men to seven years and fined customs brokers who had paid them, though the report names neither the brokers nor the amounts. The case was reported by the anti-corruption service in November 2024.
inside: Brokers and importers paid the customs laboratory's head, and the reports their cargo needed were then issued faster than the queue allowed.
cite: Orda (English), 21 November 2024, citing the anti-corruption service

n: Medical equipment supplier convicted with Shymkent health department's building chief
rank: Head of the Capital Construction and Equipment Department, Shymkent Health Department
d: A two-year case in Shymkent, Kazakhstan's third city, ended with convictions across the regional security service, the city health department and a medical equipment supplier. Yerlan Tyshkanbayev, of a medical equipment supply company, was convicted of complicity in embezzling budget funds and given a suspended seven-year sentence with a ban on company leadership. Chingis Dzhanabayev, head of the Capital Construction and Equipment Department of the Shymkent Health Department, got seven years for embezzling state property on an especially large scale. Manat Sarbasov, former first deputy head of the National Security Committee department for Shymkent, was jailed for 12 years for taking a bribe, ordered to repay 70 million tenge, and acquitted of fraud. The jury voted six to five.
inside: A medical equipment supplier was convicted alongside the city health department's own building and equipment chief for taking the budget money meant for that equipment.
cite: Orda (English), 8 October 2025

n: Developers won Almaty permits to build flats on land zoned for houses
rank: Chief architect and land relations heads, Almaty
d: Almaty's chief architect and the heads of its land relations and land management offices approved the construction of multi-apartment complexes on land designated for private houses, which let developers avoid paying the proper cadastral values. A specialised criminal court examined 25 cases of illegal permit approvals. Former chief architect Almaskhan Akhmedzhanov was jailed for 11 years, former land relations head Ardak Samambetov for 10 and former land management head Yerlan Zharmukhanbetov for 14. Two entrepreneurs received five years' probation each and the director of an appraisal company eight years. Akhmedzhanov said the charges were fabricated and denied wrongdoing, and the defendants had 15 working days to appeal.
inside: Developers and a valuer obtained Almaty's building permits through its architect and land chiefs, and so built flats on cheap house plots.
cite: Orda (English), 17 February 2025

n: Bus carrier and road firm paid North Kazakhstan's transport deputy chief
org_label: Alekseev & K LLP and NBS Construction LLP
who: A bus carrier and a road contractor
rank: Acting deputy head, Passenger Transport and Highways Department, North Kazakhstan region
d: Kanat Barkitov was acting deputy head of the Passenger Transport and Highways Department in Kazakhstan's North Kazakhstan region. From 2024 the bus carrier Alekseev & K paid him 500,000 tenge a month, 5.5 million tenge over ten months, to his card or his wife's, for help with subsidised bus routes that he did not in fact control. Separately, Didar Makhashov of the road company NBS Construction left an envelope in a wall cabinet to buy his signature on a February 2025 road repair certificate in the Shal Aqyn district, at a price Barkitov set. He was caught on 6 April 2025 and jailed for five years; the carrier's director got three years, and two road company men were fined. All have appealed.
inside: A bus operator and a road contractor paid the regional transport department's deputy head for route support and for his signature on repair certificates.
cite: Orda (English), 12 December 2025

n: Businesspeople paid Karaganda revenue chiefs to drop customs penalties
rank: Department heads, Karaganda regional State Revenue Department
d: The State Revenue Department collects tax and enforces customs rules in each Kazakh region. Two department heads in the Karaganda regional office, M. Akbiev and B. Mukashev, repeatedly took bribes from businessmen in exchange for not holding them administratively liable for customs control violations. Karaganda's Kazybek District Court fined Akbiev 21.7 million tenge and Mukashev 2.5 million tenge, and fined four business owners who paid, A. Balatskaya, Kh. Bekishev, N. Bekshin and I. Andrienko, between 540,000 and 3 million tenge each. All were barred for life from public office and the quasi-public sector. The verdict has entered into legal force. The report gives no bribe amounts or dates.
inside: Importers paid two heads inside the regional revenue office, and the customs penalties they had incurred were then not applied to them.
cite: Tengrinews.kz, 3 March 2025, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency

n: Russian haulier paid 100m tenge to wave 1,003 lorries past West Kazakhstan checks
org_label: A Russian citizen moving lorries into Kazakhstan
rank: Acting head of a regional office of the State Revenue Department, West Kazakhstan
d: A citizen of Russia agreed to pay the acting head of a regional office of the State Revenue Department in West Kazakhstan, who agreed to take the money: 100 million tenge was handed over for the unimpeded passage of lorries through checkpoints, with general patronage and connivance, covering 1,003 lorries moved from Russia into Kazakhstan between September and October 2025. An intermediary took 24.8 million tenge. On 5 November 2026 Astana's specialised interdistrict criminal court jailed the official for ten years with confiscation and a lifetime ban, and the intermediary for one year and six months. The verdict had not yet taken effect, and the report does not say whether the Russian citizen was charged.
inside: A haulage operator's 100 million tenge reached the revenue official who controls the border checkpoints, and a thousand lorries then crossed unchecked.
cite: Zakon.kz, 5 November 2026

n: Trader charged with paying RM53,000 to a Tenaga Nasional man over power cases
rank: Tenaga Nasional Berhad employee
d: Tiang Soon Ying, 40, pleaded not guilty at the Butterworth Sessions Court in March 2026 to two charges of giving RM53,000 in cash to Mohd Ashraf Mohd Yunus, 42, an employee acting for Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility. Prosecutors allege RM10,000 was handed over on 5 January 2021 and RM43,000 on 15 September 2021, both at a hotel room in George Town, to induce TNB not to act against several premises around Manjung and Sitiawan, Perak, suspected of tampering with or stealing electricity and damaging TNB installations. The case was moved to the Ipoh Sessions Court to be heard with related charges.
inside: Prosecutors say a trader paid an officer of the state electricity company so it would not pursue premises suspected of stealing its power.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 9 March 2026

n: Scrap dealer gave a TNB subsidiary manager RM940,000 and a BMW for copper discounts
rank: general manager of a Tenaga Nasional subsidiary
d: Shahanom Uthman, 55, a former general manager of a subsidiary of Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Malaysia's state-controlled electricity utility, was convicted of eight counts of taking bribes from Ahsan Sabri Pang Abdullah, a director of Bina Mekar Sdn Bhd, and Te Boon Chun, an employee of that company. He took RM940,000 in cash and a BMW valued at RM140,000 between December 2013 and December 2014, to secure a discount on the weighing of unprocessed copper. The Sessions Court jailed him six years and fined him RM5.4 million in 2017; the High Court dismissed his appeal in March 2019. The report does not name the subsidiary.
inside: A metals company paid the manager who weighed its copper at a state electricity subsidiary, so the company was charged for less than it took away.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 4 March 2019

n: Cleaning firm owner paid a Shah Alam council assistant to stop a payment notice
who: owner of a cleaning services company
rank: operations administrative assistant, Shah Alam City Council
d: Mohammad Zaki Jamian, 44, who owns a cleaning services company, pleaded guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in August 2024 to paying RM3,500 to an operations administrative assistant at Majlis Bandaraya Shah Alam (MBSA), the city council. The money went through an account belonging to Syarikat Gabungan Selatan Resources between October 2020 and December 2021, so that no Notice To Correct would be issued over his payment claims for cleaning council stalls in Zone SA G12, Section 24, covering September 2020 to December 2021. He was jailed for one day and fined RM30,000, with six months' jail if the fine is unpaid.
inside: A council contractor paid a council officer to drop the notice that would have questioned his cleaning bills, so his claims were paid as submitted.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 30 August 2024

n: Air Kelantan's general manager charged over a RM27m water scheme subcontract
who: Ng Te Wei, for Zog Technology Sdn Bhd
rank: general manager, Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd
d: Wan Mohd Zamri W. Ismail, 61, former general manager of Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB), the Kelantan state water company, pleaded not guilty at the Kota Bharu Sessions Court in August 2022. Prosecutors allege he took RM10,000 by cheque from Ng Te Wei, 44, credited to his bank account in January 2015, so that AKSB would appoint Zog Technology Sdn Bhd as a subcontractor for design, construction, testing and mechanical and electrical work on the Merbau Chondong water supply scheme, Phase II Package I, at Machang, a project worth over RM27 million. Three people, including a former general manager and an AKSB officer, had been remanded in July 2022.
inside: Prosecutors say a subcontractor paid the state water company's general manager to have his firm appointed to a water supply scheme worth over RM27 million.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 14 August 2022

n: Singapore fertiliser supplier paid US$300,000 to a NAFAS officer, charges say
who: Kim Jong Kwa, director of Sung Chang Asia Pte Ltd
rank: officer, Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (NAFAS)
d: Nordin Ibrohim, 77, a former officer of Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (NAFAS), Malaysia's National Farmers' Organisation, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in January 2025 to two charges of taking bribes. Prosecutors allege Kim Jong Kwa, a director of the Singapore fertiliser supplier Sung Chang Asia Pte Ltd, transferred US$300,000 from the company's account to his own between 16 November and 21 December 2022, through a bank at Plaza Mont Kiara, as a reward for helping the company be appointed a fertiliser supplier to paddy farmers through NAFAS. Bail was set at RM100,000. The report names no contract number.
inside: Prosecutors say a foreign fertiliser supplier paid an officer of the national farmers' body to be made its supplier to paddy farmers.
cite: Portal Berita RTM, 28 January 2025

n: Contractor paid a farmers' authority manager RM20,000 over a galangal project
rank: officer, Lembaga Pertubuhan Peladang
d: Mohd Zairey Yahya, 42, an economic affairs officer at Lembaga Pertubuhan Peladang (LPP), Malaysia's Farmers' Organisation Authority, pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in Melaka in May 2024. Prosecutors allege that on 5 March 2021, at a food court car park in Pekan Selandar, Jasin, he took RM20,000 in cash from a cleaning contractor aged 42 for clearing, land preparation and infrastructure work on a galangal planting project. When the first of the two charges was committed he was general manager of a district farmers' organisation in Johor. A second charge alleges he submitted a false certificate of completion for the same project.
inside: Prosecutors say a contractor paid the farmers' authority officer who ran a planting project to get and be signed off for its ground works.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 14 May 2024

n: ProLintas highway chief took RM90,000 from a firm bidding for SUKE work
rank: chief operating officer, ProLintas
d: Rostam Shahrif Tam, 59, chief operating officer (operations and projects) at ProLintas, the toll-road group that Malay Mail reports is wholly owned by the state-owned asset manager Permodalan Nasional Berhad, was fined RM100,000 by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in June 2025. He pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of failing to report to the anti-corruption commission a RM90,000 bribe he took from Satunas Technologies Sdn Bhd, through Mohd Rosman Alias, in February 2023 at a restaurant in Puchong. The money was an inducement, while he was deputy supervising officer, to award the company a work package on the SUKE elevated highway. Over RM1 million in cash and seven watches were forfeited.
inside: A supplier paid the state-owned toll group's operations chief for a work package on a highway he supervised, and he kept the payment to himself.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 25 June 2025; Malay Mail, 15 July 2025

n: Carpet supplier's agent paid a MARA college clerk RM500 for a RM7,840 job
rank: senior administrative clerk, Kolej Poly-Tech MARA Ipoh
d: Mohamad Al Amzar Dualali, 32, a senior clerk in the administration section of Kolej Poly-Tech MARA (KPTM) Ipoh, a MARA college, pleaded guilty at the Ipoh Sessions Court in May 2026 and was fined RM5,000. In February 2025, in the Kinta district, he took RM500 in cash from a man aged 29 who had helped the firm Carpetssouq Global win the supply and installation of carpets in Meeting Rooms 1 and 2 at the college, work valued at RM7,840. He was charged under section 165 of the Penal Code, which carries up to two years' jail. He had no lawyer and paid the fine.
inside: A carpet supplier's go-between paid the college clerk who handled the order, so a small public contract went the supplier's way.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 20 May 2026

n: E-waste firm's representative fined RM75,000 for paying an environment officer
who: Chan Suit Seong, for Sumber Bumi Sdn Bhd
rank: officer, Department of Environment
d: Chan Suit Seong, 61, a representative of Sumber Bumi Sdn Bhd, pleaded guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in August 2026 and was fined RM75,000, with two years' jail if the fine is unpaid. In February 2025 she gave RM15,000 in cash to an officer of the Department of Environment (JAS) in Putrajaya, Malaysia's environmental regulator, to stop legal action against the company's premises, which were alleged to be processing electronic waste illegally under the Environmental Quality Act 1974. She was convicted on an alternative charge under section 214 of the Penal Code, and the RM15,000 seized was forfeited to the government.
inside: A waste company paid the environment regulator's own officer to drop enforcement against its illegal e-waste plant.
cite: Portal Berita RTM, 6 August 2026

n: Stadium corporation CEO charged over RM1.45m for a squash centre tender
who: Yap Yeow Kuen, for Aerolux Power Constructions Sdn Bhd
rank: chief executive, Perbadanan Stadium Malaysia
d: Iliyas Jamil, 42, chief executive of Perbadanan Stadium Malaysia (PSM), the state corporation that runs the national stadium complex, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in June 2026 to seven charges of soliciting and taking RM1.45 million from Yap Yeow Kuen, 60. Prosecutors allege the money was to make him pick Aerolux Power Constructions Sdn Bhd as the winning bidder for a tender to upgrade the National Squash Centre at Kuala Lumpur Sports City, Bukit Jalil, valued at RM8,733,197. The payments are alleged to have been made at the PSM office and at a restaurant in Sri Petaling. Bail was set at RM100,000.
inside: Prosecutors say a builder paid the state stadium corporation's chief executive RM1.45 million to be chosen for its squash centre upgrade.
cite: Portal Berita RTM, 18 June 2026

n: Suppliers paid an IIUM communications officer RM32,000 for university work
rank: assistant director, corporate communications, IIUM
d: Mohd Hakimi Mohd Badrol Afandi, 44, an assistant director in the corporate communications division of the International Islamic University Malaysia (Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia), pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in June 2021 to four charges of taking RM32,000 in cash, deposited into his bank account between November 2014 and March 2015. Prosecutors allege the money was for helping three companies obtain voucher work at the university, including modification works for the IIUM Gallery and the printing of the university's 2015 corporate collateral. He had earlier been charged at Shah Alam over a RM5,000 payment from the same individual, and the cases were joined.
inside: Prosecutors say suppliers paid a public university officer to get its printing and fit-out work, so the university's small purchases went to them.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 3 June 2021

n: Defence intelligence chief charged over US$20,000 and flights on a cyber contract
org_label: Sheikh Ahmad Nafiq Sheikh A. Rahman
who: Sheikh Ahmad Nafiq Sheikh A. Rahman
rank: Director-General of Defence Intelligence
d: Mohd Razali Alias, former Director-General of Defence Intelligence in Malaysia's armed forces, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in January 2026 to three charges. Prosecutors allege he took US$20,000 in cash from Sheikh Ahmad Nafiq Sheikh A. Rahman at Kem Kementah, Kuala Lumpur, between August and November 2024, as a reward for approving a verification certificate and acceptance of services for payments under a maintenance contract for the Cyber Defence Operations Centre system. Two further charges concern air tickets worth RM26,800 and RM37,800 for flights to Spain and Estonia; the report does not say who paid for them. Bail was set at RM50,000.
inside: Prosecutors say a contractor paid the head of military intelligence to sign off the work and release payments on a cyber defence contract.
cite: Portal Berita RTM, 29 January 2026

n: Businessman charged with paying two Sabah assemblymen for mining licences
rank: Sabah assemblymen, one an assistant minister
d: Three men pleaded not guilty at a corruption court in Kota Kinabalu in June 2025 over mineral prospecting licences in Sabah. Prosecutors allege the Selangor businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, known as Albert Tei, paid RM150,000 in cash to Andi Muhammad Suryady Bandy, the Tanjung Batu assemblyman and assistant minister for industrial development, in May 2024 to facilitate a licence application for Sinaran Hayat Sdn Bhd, and RM200,000 to Yusof Yacob, the Sindumin assemblyman and chairman of Qhazanah Sabah, in March 2023 over a prospecting licence application for Nusa Kini Sdn Bhd. Tei faces two counts of bribery. All three deny the charges.
inside: Prosecutors say a businessman paid two serving Sabah legislators, one of them a minister, to push through mining licences for his companies.
cite: The Vibes, 30 June 2025

n: Tabung Haji manager charged over RM170,477 for steering office renovations
who: Yusaidi Mohd, through Amaneez Creative Solution
rank: senior technical manager, Lembaga Tabung Haji
d: Zaharuddin Hamid, 47, a senior technical manager in the property development section of Lembaga Tabung Haji, Malaysia's state pilgrims' savings fund, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to three charges of taking bribes totalling RM170,477. Prosecutors allege Yusaidi Mohd paid him through the company Amaneez Creative Solution, by a cheque deposited into his sister's bank account, between 5 October 2015 and 24 May 2018, as commission for recommending Consoline Sdn Bhd and MNB Engineering Sdn Bhd for renovation work at four Tabung Haji offices: Ipoh in Perak and Muar, Batu Pahat and Kluang in Johor. Bail was set at RM50,000.
inside: Prosecutors say a middleman paid the fund's technical manager a commission so named firms were recommended for its office renovation work.
cite: Siakap Keli

n: Supplier's claims certified by a Melaka health officer who took RM27,901
rank: assistant medical officer, Jasin Health Office
d: Mohd Zamry Yazid, 46, an assistant medical officer at the Jasin Health Office in Melaka, pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in March 2021 to 14 charges of using his position to obtain bribes. Prosecutors allege he received RM27,901 in total from Pella Maju Enterprise, a company owned by his relative Norfazilah Yazid, through 14 payment vouchers for medical supplies between 9 October and 12 November 2018. The charges say he prepared the quotations and certified the payment claims for the same supplier. Bail was set at RM7,000 with one surety.
inside: Prosecutors say a supplier paid the health office officer who wrote its quotations and signed off its invoices, so its medical supply claims were approved.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 24 March 2021

n: Agriculture ministry officer charged over RM100,000 on a RM37.47m fertiliser tender
rank: chief assistant senior secretary, Ministry of Agriculture
d: Shahrulzaman Jaafar, 43, a chief assistant senior secretary at Malaysia's Ministry of Agriculture and Agro-based Industry, pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in January 2021 to two charges of taking RM100,000 in total as a reward for helping KIIK Resources Sdn Bhd win a tender. A 46-year-old man is alleged to have paid on the company's behalf in May and September 2020, at a roadside near Serdang Hospital and at Taman D'Alpinia, Puchong. The tender, for supplying bio-fertiliser containing beneficial local microbes under the Production Incentive Scheme, was worth RM37.47 million. Eight days earlier he denied three related charges in Kuala Lumpur.
inside: Prosecutors say a fertiliser supplier paid the ministry officer handling its tender, so a RM37.47 million supply contract went to the company.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 21 January 2021

n: Minister's political secretary charged over RM350,000 on a RM381m police IT tender
who: Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, of Nexuscorp Group Sdn Bhd
rank: political secretary to the Home Minister
d: Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad, 42, former political secretary to Malaysia's then Home Minister Hamzah Zainudin, pleaded not guilty in May 2024 to charges of demanding RM350,000 in cash from Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, managing director of Nexuscorp Group Sdn Bhd. Prosecutors allege the money was a reward for helping the company win a tender to maintain and supply spare parts for infrastructure equipment, servers, software and user radios for the RMPNet system of the Royal Malaysia Police, valued at RM381,112,042.44. The alleged payments date to December 2020. Bail was set at RM60,000 and the Shah Alam charges were moved to Kuala Lumpur.
inside: Prosecutors say a contractor paid the home minister's own political secretary to win a RM381 million police communications contract.
cite: Portal Berita RTM, 24 May 2024

n: Funeral agent paid Hospital Kajang forensic staff to handle bodies
who: Nur Azlan Azmi, a funeral agent
rank: forensic unit staff, Hospital Kajang
d: Three staff of the forensic unit at Hospital Kajang in Selangor, a government hospital, pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in December 2021. Prosecutors allege Mohd Nizam Noordin, 41, Mohd Redzuan Che Husain, 34, and Muhd Azhar Nahar, 44, took RM4,950 between them, in payments of RM300 to RM650, from an agent named Nur Azlan Azmi, 33, between 2019 and 2021, so that he was given the handling of fourteen Muslim bodies. Two more staff from the same unit were to be charged in Ipoh and Alor Setar. Five forensic unit staff had been remanded in October 2021 over suspected payments from agents.
inside: Prosecutors say an outside funeral agent paid hospital mortuary staff so the bodies in their care were released to him for burial work.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 8 December 2021

n: Logistics firm's owner paid KLIA customs officers not to inspect lorries
who: the owner of a logistics company
rank: customs enforcement assistants, KLIA cargo
d: Three officers of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court on 30 May 2024 to 24 charges of taking bribes totalling RM8,600 between January 2017 and April 2023. Prosecutors allege the money came from the owner of a logistics company, who is not named, so that they would not inspect lorries carrying goods out of the KLIA cargo complex. Four other enforcement assistants had already denied 49 charges totalling RM39,800 over the same cargo inspections. The commission said 23 customs officers and staff would be charged in six Sessions Courts following Ops Samba 2.0, which it said found tax leakage of about RM2 billion.
inside: Prosecutors say a freight company paid customs enforcement officers at the airport cargo complex so its lorries left uninspected.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 30 May 2024

n: Supplier paid a KEMAS Melaka clerk RM9,500 for a contract and staff charts
who: Mohd Hyzery Elec, for Bati Enterprise
rank: senior administrative assistant, KEMAS Melaka
d: Norshahril Ramlee, 39, a former senior administrative assistant at the Melaka branch of Jabatan Kemajuan Masyarakat (KEMAS), the Department of Community Development, pleaded not guilty at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court in October 2020 to two charges. Prosecutors allege Mohd Hyzery Elec paid him RM9,500 on behalf of Bati Enterprise in 2016: RM7,000 for giving the company a contract to supply spare parts for office equipment, electrical items and other goods, and RM2,500 for supplying the department's organisational chart and its chart of officer and staff movements. Bail was set at RM2,500 with one surety.
inside: Prosecutors say a supplier paid the department clerk who handled its contract, and also bought the department's internal staff charts from him.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 26 October 2020

n: Cleaning contractors paid a DBKL housing manager over public housing work
who: owners of two cleaning contractor companies
rank: Zone 2 housing manager, Kuala Lumpur City Hall
d: Mohamed Helfien Nordin, 45, an assistant administrative officer serving as Zone 2 housing manager in the housing management and community development department of Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL), the city hall, pleaded guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in January 2022 to six of 34 charges. The payments, RM2,700 of an alleged RM82,700 across all his cases, came from the owners of two cleaning contractor companies for cleaning work at public housing (PPR) blocks and rubbish houses between February 2014 and December 2016. He was fined RM18,000, with 15 months' jail in default, and 28 charges were taken into consideration. A separate case involving 86 charges remained.
inside: Cleaning contractors paid the city hall manager who handled public housing cleaning, and he admitted taking the money for that work.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 10 January 2022

n: Shah Alam council officer admitted RM36,000 tied to a cleaning tender
who: an unnamed man paying by cheque
rank: administrative officer, Shah Alam City Council
d: Azlan Dollah, 47, an administrative officer at the Kota Kemuning branch of Majlis Bandaraya Shah Alam (MBSA), the city council, admitted guilt at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in July 2023 to the first of four charges and had the other three taken into consideration. He received four cheques totalling RM36,000, of RM2,000, RM10,000, RM17,000 and RM7,000, in June and July 2014 at a bank in Section 15, Shah Alam, without any return service and in connection with his official duties on a tender for public cleaning services in Section 32, Shah Alam. He was fined RM7,000. The report does not name who paid.
inside: A council officer handling a public cleaning tender admitted taking RM36,000 in cheques from outside the council in connection with that tender.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 28 July 2023

n: Subcontractor paid RM200,000 for a DBKL road permit; official convicted on appeal
who: Wong May Kuan, subcontractor to Dusari Niaga
rank: senior deputy director, DBKL civil engineering department
d: Sabudin Mohd Salleh, 61, former senior deputy director in the civil engineering and urban transport department of Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL), was convicted in 2023 of two counts of taking RM200,000 from Wong May Kuan, a subcontractor to Dusari Niaga, to issue a work permit to that company for milling and resurfacing former utility trench sites in Kuala Lumpur. The payments were made in June 2018 and January 2019. The Sessions Court had acquitted him twice; the High Court allowed the prosecution's appeals and in August 2023 jailed him four years and fined him RM1 million. The judge stayed both pending his appeal to the Court of Appeal.
inside: A road contractor paid the city hall director who issued work permits, and the High Court found the permit for its resurfacing job was bought.
cite: Utusan Malaysia, 15 August 2023

n: MRT-3 chief hid his tie to PH Trams, which won the maintenance deal
rank: General Manager, MRT-3
d: Al Vitangcol III, general manager of MRT-3, the state-run light rail line through Metro Manila, was convicted of graft and of breaking the Government Procurement Reform Act over the 2012 interim maintenance contract awarded to the joint venture of PH Trams and CB&T. The Sandiganbayan, the Philippine anti-graft court, said in a 45-page decision promulgated on 31 January 2020 that Vitangcol "purposely concealed" his relationship with his wife's uncle Arturo Soriano so that PH Trams would not be disqualified from bidding. Under the contract MRT-3 was to pay PH Trams $1.15 million a month. Both men got 12 to 16 years and a lifetime bar from office. Four PH Trams incorporators were acquitted.
inside: A bidder's hidden link to the rail line's own general manager kept it in the running, and it won the maintenance contract worth $1.15 million a month.
cite: Philippine Star, 7 February 2020

n: Aurora province rigged two road repairs for RMCR Construction
rank: provincial governor and bids committee
d: The provincial government of Aurora, on the east coast of Luzon, awarded two 2014 repair contracts on the Casiguran-Dilasag provincial road to the private contractor RMCR Construction in a bidding that prosecutors said was rigged in its favour. Former governor Gerardo Noveras, provincial administrator Simeon de Castro, budget officer Paz Torregosa, the bids and awards committee chairman Ricardo Bautista, three committee members and RMCR's Manding Claro Ramos were convicted of graft and sentenced on 4 September 2024 to up to ten years. An accomplishment report dated 18 August 2014 declared both projects complete three days after the notice to proceed. The Sandiganbayan's Sixth Division affirmed the convictions on 27 February 2025.
inside: The contractor's own man was convicted with the provincial officials who ran the bidding, which the court found was arranged so his firm would win the road repairs.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 16 September 2025

n: Four suppliers convicted with public works officials over ghost vehicle repairs
rank: Department of Public Works and Highways bureaus
d: The Sandiganbayan's Fourth Division convicted eleven people on 21 November 2016 over a scheme to take about P13 million from the Department of Public Works and Highways through claims for repairing its service vehicles in the early years of the Arroyo administration. Seven were departmental officers, among them Burt Favorito of the administrative service and Florendo Arias of the Bureau of Equipment. Four were private suppliers: Conchita dela Cruz, Janette Bugayong, Vicente Santos Jr. and Augusto Capuz. The court said the reimbursements "were actually false claims", with contracts split to avoid procurement rules and job orders, inspection reports and acceptance reports falsified. The suppliers each got up to 20 years for estafa and ten for graft.
inside: Outside repair suppliers worked with the department's own officers to file false claims, so the public works budget paid for repairs that were never done.
cite: Philippine Daily Inquirer, 2 December 2016

n: Publisher convicted with Muslim Mindanao officials over P77m undelivered packages
rank: ARMM regional governor and education officers
d: The Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao paid about P77 million for information technology packages that were never delivered. MBJ Learning Tools received P31 million on 21 December 2000 and CPR Publishing received P46,261,250 on 24 July 2001. On 24 May 2024 the Sandiganbayan convicted the former regional governor Nur Misuari, the regional education director Leovegilda Cinches, a chief accountant, a supply officer, an accountant and the resident state auditor of graft, along with CPR Publishing's owner Criseta Ramirez, a private party. Misuari was given six to eight years for each case and barred from office for life. All seven were acquitted of malversation through falsification for want of proof.
inside: A publisher's owner was convicted alongside the regional government's own officers and auditor after her firm was paid P46,261,250 for packages it never delivered.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 24 May 2024

n: Housing authority officers paid Triad Construction P1,280,964.20 for cheaper work
rank: National Housing Authority Visayas office
d: Five officers of the National Housing Authority, the Philippine state corporation that builds public housing, were convicted of graft over an overpriced 1992 contract on the Pahanocoy Sites and Services Project in Bacolod City. The private contractor Triad Construction and Development Corp received about P1,280,964.20 from them for work the court put at P330,075.76. Those convicted were the Visayas management office division manager Josephine Angsico, the manager Virgilio Dacalos, the regional project director Felicisimo Lazarte Jr., the project management officer Josephine Espinosa and the supervising engineer Noel Lobrido. Each was given six years and one month to ten years and barred from office for life. The Sandiganbayan's Second Division refused their motions for reconsideration.
inside: A construction firm was paid nearly four times the court's figure for the work by the housing authority's own regional officers, who were convicted of graft for it.
cite: Philippine Daily Inquirer, conviction upheld report

n: Businessmen and city engineer convicted over a warehouse that did not exist
rank: Quezon City engineer and MMDA assessment director
d: Quezon City's government paid P3,291,840 in November 1993 to Servy Realty Corp for a 457-square-metre warehouse said to have been demolished to clear the route of the public works department's C-3 Road. The Sandiganbayan found the warehouse never existed. It convicted the former city engineer Alfredo Macapugay, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority's real property assessment director Ramon Mateo and the businessmen Margarito Chan and Dickson Lim of graft on 12 April 2019, and denied their motions for reconsideration in a resolution dated 27 August 2019 that was released in September 2025. The court said a 240-square-metre warehouse on the remaining lot did not exonerate them.
inside: Businessmen got the city engineer and the metropolitan assessment director to certify a warehouse that was never there, and their firm was paid P3,291,840 for it.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 17 September 2025

n: Iloilo road contract worth P54.31m handed to IBC Builders without bidding
rank: DPWH Regional Office VI bids committee
d: The Department of Public Works and Highways regional office in Iloilo City awarded the P54.31 million asphalt overlay of the Iloilo-Jaro Diversion Road to IBC International Builders Corp on 10 January 2008 without the public bidding required by the Government Procurement Reform Act, and with no appropriation for it.
