The Sandiganbayan's Sixth Division convicted five bids and awards committee members on 31 July 2019 and later denied their motions for reconsideration, saying "The BAC, as a collective unit, served as the enabler and the abettor of an illegality." Berna Coca, Luvisminda Narciso, Danilo Peroy, Marilyn Celiz and Fernando Tuares got six to eight years. The contractor is not reported as convicted.
inside: A builder took a P54.31 million road contract that the regional bids committee handed it without bidding, which the court called the committee abetting an illegality.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 16 September 2025

n: Fertilizer trader convicted with Lazi town officials over a P4.99m rigged supply
rank: municipal mayor and bids committee, Lazi
d: The municipal government of Lazi, on the island of Siquijor, hired Mangopina Trading Company Inc in May 2004 to supply about P4.99 million of liquid and foliar fertilisers under the agriculture department's farm inputs programme. The Sandiganbayan's Third Division found the procurement rigged in Mangopina's favour, citing "blatant violations of the applicable procurement laws, rules and regulations", and noting that the purchase request was dated 12 March 2004, almost a month before the municipality's agreement with the department's regional unit. The former mayor Orville Fua, three bids and awards committee members and the private defendant Merlyn Lu were convicted of graft on 7 December 2023 and given six to ten years. The court affirmed the convictions in 2025.
inside: A fertiliser trader's representative was convicted with the town's mayor and bids committee after the court found the P4.99 million supply deal rigged for her firm.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 23 September 2025

n: Viga town council bought a P13.95m backhoe from CAMEC without bidding
rank: municipal mayor and council, Viga
d: The municipal government of Viga, in Catanduanes province, bought a backhoe loader for P13.95 million in 2005 from Compressed Air Machineries Equipment Corp without public bidding and without the review by the bids and awards committee that the Government Procurement Reform Act requires. The Sandiganbayan's Third Division, in a 48-page decision by Associate Justice Ronald Moreno, convicted the former mayor Jose Torres, the former vice mayor Yolando Tuquero and eight former council members of graft, naming CAMEC as the supplier that received an unwarranted advantage. Each was given six to ten years and barred from office for life. The case was filed in 2017. The article does not say whether CAMEC or its officers were charged.
inside: A machinery firm took a P13.95 million municipal purchase that the mayor and council pushed through without bidding, giving it what the court called an unwarranted advantage.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 22 September 2025

n: Romblon mayor agreed with CAMEC before the loan, then bought its backhoe unbid
org_label: Compressed Air Machineries and Equipment Corporation
rank: municipal mayor and council, Romblon
d: The municipality of Romblon, the capital town of Romblon province, bought a new JCB backhoe loader from Compressed Air Machineries and Equipment Corporation for P13,950,000 with a loan from the state-owned Philippine National Bank. The Ombudsman said the council awarded it by negotiated purchase instead of the public bidding required by the Government Procurement Reform Act, and never referred it to the bids and awards committee. The Sandiganbayan's Fourth Division found that the former mayor Leo Merida had already agreed with the firm before he obtained authority to apply for the loan in November 2005. He and nine former councillors were convicted of graft, given up to ten years, and barred from office; reconsideration was denied on 26 March 2018.
inside: The same machinery firm had an agreement with the mayor before the town even had the money, and the council then bought its P13,950,000 backhoe without bidding.
cite: GMA News, 4 April 2018

n: Shopping plaza owner convicted with Samar governor over unbid supplies
rank: provincial governor of Samar
d: The provincial government of Samar bought equipment, medicine and supplies worth P16.2 million without bidding during the first term of governor Milagrosa Tan, from 2001 to 2004. The Sandiganbayan's Fourth Division convicted Tan and the provincial administrative officer Rolando Montejo of eight counts of graft each and barred both from office for life. Raynaldo Yabut, owner of the private firm Raechel Shopper's Plaza, was convicted of two counts and given 14 to 25 years. The court found his firm had been picked in advance as winner of a simulated bidding for 1,176 electric fans worth P1.635 million, of which "none was in fact legitimately carried out", and that typhoon relief goods were bought two months before the storm.
inside: A trading firm's owner was convicted with the governor after a bidding for 1,176 electric fans was staged so that his shop would win it.
cite: Rappler, Sandiganbayan Fourth Division

n: Kitchenware supplier convicted with Lopez town mayor over an unfinished delivery
rank: municipal mayor of Lopez, Quezon
d: The municipality of Lopez in Quezon province paid P1,055,432 to Revuelta Enterprises on 8 December 2008 for plasticware and glassware for barangay assemblies, after an inspection and acceptance report of 24 November 2008 recorded P1,122,800 of goods as fully delivered. The Sandiganbayan's Sixth Division found delivery was not complete when the slip was signed; the owner Leonardo Revuelta had told the state auditor he made staggered deliveries, the last on 10 March 2009, because the town had no warehouse. The former mayor Isaias Ubana II, a senior administrative assistant and Revuelta were convicted of graft in 2021 and given six to eight years. The court held Revuelta equally guilty for taking payment early.
inside: The supplier was convicted with the mayor for taking P1,055,432 from the town on paperwork saying his goods were delivered when they were not.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 22 July 2021

n: Napoles foundation drew Biazon's P2.7m fund through state training centre
rank: Technology Resource Center managers
d: The Technology Resource Center, a Philippine state corporation for livelihood training, released P2.7 million of the 2007 development fund of the congressman Rozzano Rufino Biazon to the Philippine Social Development Foundation, an organisation the Sandiganbayan's Special Seventh Division described as bogus and owned by Janet Lim Napoles. In a 191-page decision dated 30 May 2025 the court convicted Biazon, by then the re-elected mayor of Muntinlupa, Napoles, the centre's deputy director general Dennis Cunanan, its group manager Maria Rosalinda Lacsamana and the private defendant Evelyn De Leon of graft, with six to eight years each. It called Biazon's endorsement letter naming the foundation "an indispensable instruction" to the centre. Napoles and De Leon must return the P2,700,000.
inside: An outside foundation named in a lawmaker's letter was handed P2.7 million by the state corporation's own managers, who were convicted with its owner.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 30 May 2025

n: FFJJ Construction paid in full before finishing a P5m water project
rank: municipal mayor of Northern Kabuntalan
d: The municipality of Northern Kabuntalan, in what is now Maguindanao del Norte, awarded a small water impounding project worth P5 million to FFJJ Construction in 2011 in a procurement the court found irregular. The Sandiganbayan's Fifth Division convicted the former mayor Datu Umbra Bayam Dilangalen, the municipal accountant Rahima Ali and the then municipal treasurer Kabiba Mael of graft, giving each six to seven years and barring them from office for life, and denied their motions for reconsideration. It held that the contractor received an unwarranted benefit because it was paid in full before the project was finished, and that damage to the government is not needed for a graft conviction, so completing the work did not change the result.
inside: The builder was paid the whole P5 million before it had finished, which the court called an unwarranted benefit given by the town's mayor, accountant and treasurer.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 5 December 2022

n: Aloguinsan town bought P1.12m of panels from one firm with no real bidding
rank: municipal mayor and bids committee, Aloguinsan
d: The municipality of Aloguinsan in Cebu province bought 311 sheets of aluminium composite panels from Diamond Interior Industries Corporation for P1.12 million in 2007 using a price canvass instead of competitive bidding. The Sandiganbayan's First Division convicted the former mayor Cynthia Moreno and seven members of the municipal bids and awards committee of graft, giving each six years and barring them from public office for life. It found no emergency that would justify negotiated procurement, and said the accused gave the firm an unwarranted benefit through partiality, bad faith and gross negligence. The purchase was already complete before the date of the bidding the defendants said had taken place.
inside: A panel supplier got a P1.12 million municipal order through what the court found was partiality and bad faith by the mayor and her bids committee.
cite: Rappler, Sandiganbayan First Division

n: Binidayan mayor gave E.B. Ople Trading an unbid P20m equipment order
rank: municipal mayor of Binidayan
d: The Sandiganbayan's Special Seventh Division ruled on 5 October 2018 that the former mayor of Binidayan, in Lanao del Sur, Aman Misbac Datumulok, was guilty of graft for buying a dump truck and a wheel loader worth P20 million from E.B. Ople Trading without public bidding, giving the firm what the court called unwarranted preference. The dump truck cost P11 million and the wheel loader about P9 million; investigators found the loader was a second-hand machine worth P1.7 million, an overpricing of P7.3 million. He was given six to ten years and barred from office for life. The complaint was brought by his brother, the incumbent mayor.
inside: A trading firm sold the town P20 million of heavy equipment with no bidding, including a second-hand loader worth P1.7 million billed at about P9 million.
cite: Philippine Daily Inquirer, Sandiganbayan Special Seventh Division

n: Philflex Trading's president convicted over P18.93m of radios never delivered
rank: municipal mayor and bids committee, Lingig
d: The municipality of Lingig, in Surigao del Sur, spent P18.93 million in 2007 on 71 long-range and super long-range cordless radio handsets that a technical audit found never arrived. The Sandiganbayan's Seventh Division, in a 98-page decision, convicted the former mayor Roberto Luna Jr, the bids and awards committee vice chairman Jethro Lindo, the municipal treasurer Ebrencio Indoyon Jr and Ma. Luzviminda Lopez, president of the supplier Philflex Trading and General Merchandise, of graft, finding a conspiracy among the four. Each was given six to eight years, and all four must pay the municipality P18,928,571.43 with interest. The money came from the development fund of the late congressman Peter Paul Jed Falcon.
inside: The supplier's president was convicted with the mayor, treasurer and bids committee over P18.93 million paid for radio handsets that were never delivered.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 18 September 2025

n: Baganga paid Villtrade Marketing for tires the court found were never delivered
rank: municipal mayor of Baganga, Davao Oriental
d: The municipality of Baganga, in Davao Oriental, bought tires costing P101,086.37 in 2002 and released payment to Villtrade Marketing, a firm dealing in farm animals and general merchandise, although the Sandiganbayan found none were delivered. Its owner Donald Villademosa was convicted of graft and given ten years. The court convicted the former mayor Gerry Jovilla Morales, the municipal engineer Roseller Macayra, the municipal accountant Emeritos Jovilla and the municipal treasurer Francisco Jimenez Jr in 2014, and acquitted the general services officer Reymundo Escamillan in 2020. On 20 April 2021 it denied Villademosa's motion for reconsideration, saying "no tires were actually delivered".
inside: The firm's owner was convicted with the mayor and three town officers after it was paid P101,086.37 for tires the court found were never delivered.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 20 April 2021

n: Northgate Technologies won a P75m school package on a fake release order
rank: Department of Education Region IX director
d: The Department of Education's Region IX office in Pagadian City contracted multimedia packages worth P75 million in 2007 without public bidding, in a procurement the Sandiganbayan's First Division said was "precipitously done", finishing in twelve days and resting on a fake special allotment release order. The court found manifest partiality and evident bad faith, convicted the former regional director Jesus Nieves and the administrative officer Crisologo Singson of graft, and gave them six to ten years with perpetual disqualification from office. Vina Tuparan, linked to the supplier Northgate Technologies Inc, was charged but not convicted: the court ordered her case archived pending her arrest.
inside: A supplier took a P75 million regional schools contract that officials awarded with no bidding, which the court found was manifest partiality and evident bad faith.
cite: Manila Bulletin, 26 April 2022

n: Unaccredited NGO given P3m of fertiliser money by agriculture officials
rank: Department of Agriculture Region 10 technical director
d: The Department of Agriculture's Region 10 office gave the Philippine Social Development Foundation Inc the job of buying and distributing fertiliser with P3 million meant for farmers in the Cagayan de Oro district of the congressman Constantino Jaraula. The Sandiganbayan's Second Division found the organisation dubious: it was not accredited by the department, was based outside the region and lived on donations, grants and membership fees. On 8 July 2024 it convicted Jaraula, the regional technical director Joel Rudinas, the budget officer Ma. Reina Lumantas, the accountant Claudia Artazo and the private defendant Evelyn de Leon of giving it unwarranted benefits. All got six to ten years. The order to repay the P3 million was later set aside.
inside: An unaccredited outside foundation was handed P3 million of fertiliser funds by the regional agriculture office, and its private agent was convicted with the officials.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, 15 September 2025

n: Unlicensed insurer's owner convicted with Pagsanjan mayor over tourist cover
rank: municipal mayor of Pagsanjan
d: The municipality of Pagsanjan in Laguna awarded a contract for accident insurance covering tourists and boatmen at the Pagsanjan Gorge Tourist Zone to First Rapids Care Ventures through negotiated procurement, without public bidding, although the firm held no licence from the Insurance Commission. In a decision dated 5 February 2025 the Supreme Court's First Division upheld the graft convictions of Emilio Ramon Ejercito, then the town's mayor and later governor of Laguna, and of the firm's owner Marilyn Bruel, who it found had misrepresented the firm's qualifications and conspired with him. Each was given eight years and permanently barred from public office. Local council members convicted at trial were acquitted for lack of evidence.
inside: An unlicensed insurer's owner conspired with the mayor to take the town's tourist insurance contract without bidding, and both convictions were upheld.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, Supreme Court First Division, 5 February 2025

n: Drug firm owner convicted of conniving in Janiuay's medicine bidding
rank: municipal officials of Janiuay, Iloilo
d: Rodrigo Villanueva, president and general manager of AM-Europharma Corporation and sole proprietor of Mallix Drug Center, was convicted of graft for conniving with officials of the municipality of Janiuay, in Iloilo, in a flawed bidding that sold the town P13,191,223 of medicines from Europharma, with a further P1,744,926 awarded to Mallix. The health department had suspended the accreditation of Europharma and another bidder at the time of the bidding on 15 January 2001, which disqualified it. Cotrimoxazole worth P240,000 delivered by the two firms failed analysis by the Bureau of Food and Drugs. The Supreme Court affirmed the Sandiganbayan in G.R. No. 218652, holding the two firms were alter egos.
inside: A drug company owner was convicted of conniving with town officials in a bidding that gave his two firms the municipality's medicine supply worth P13,191,223.
cite: Supreme Court of the Philippines, G.R. No. 218652

n: FABMIK's president convicted over Lapu-Lapu's P83.94m lamppost contract
rank: city mayor and DPWH Region 7 bids committee
d: A lamppost contract worth P83.94 million dated 2006, for the approach to the 2007 ASEAN summit in Lapu-Lapu City, went to FABMIK Construction and Equipment Supply Co Inc without public bidding. The Sandiganbayan's Seventh Division, in a 174-page decision, convicted the former city mayor Arturo Radaza, the city engineer, the Department of Public Works and Highways Region 7 regional director Robert Lala, its bids committee chair and eight other engineers and committee members, together with FABMIK's president Isabelo Braza, and gave each six to ten years. It found no proof of an emergency, no posting of the invitation to bid, and a close match between the firm's estimates and the department's own.
inside: The contractor's president was convicted with the city mayor and the regional bids committee over a P83.94 million lamppost contract awarded without bidding.
cite: Malaya Business Insight, Sandiganbayan Seventh Division

n: Hardware suppliers billed Ukraine's railway supply arm 20m hryvnia above market
org_label: Druzhkovsky Hardware Plants PJSC and Inkomm LLC
rank: Ukrzaliznychpostach, supply branch of Ukrzaliznytsia
d: Ukrzaliznychpostach, the supply arm of Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia, bought metal fasteners in 2015 through a rigged state procurement that a predetermined company won, then signed a supply contract at prices almost twice the market average. The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU), Ukraine's anti-corruption police, names Druzhkovsky Hardware Plants PJSC and Inkomm LLC in the scheme and puts the damage at 20 million hryvnia. Ten people were implicated, among them a former member of parliament described as the organiser, his financial adviser, a freelance adviser to the head of the Presidential Administration and a private entrepreneur. Three were served with suspicions on 2 October 2019 and the investigation was completed on 20 November 2019.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2019
inside: Two hardware firms and a former MP's circle rigged the state railway's fastener tender, so the supply arm paid almost twice the market price, a loss of 20 million hryvnia.

n: Kreatyv group's $20m Oschadbank loan secured on a nonexistent contract
rank: Head of corporate business and head of project finance, Oschadbank
d: The State Savings Bank of Ukraine (Oschadbank), wholly state-owned, lent Kreatyv PJSC 20 million US dollars for three years at 11% a year in 2013-2014, nominally to buy sunflower seed. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the loan was secured on an elevator valued at over 123.3 million hryvnia and on receivables from a contract that did not exist, and that the bank's asset value fell by 133 million hryvnia. Thirteen people were served with suspicions, including a former member of parliament who had been a beneficiary of the Kreatyv group, the bank's former head of corporate business, since promoted to deputy chairman of the board, and its former head of project finance. The investigation was completed on 13 December 2019.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2019
inside: A borrower's group obtained a $20m loan from the wholly state-owned savings bank with the help of its own corporate business and project finance chiefs, on security that did not exist.

n: Energomerezha's claim deals diverted 346m hryvnia from Zaporizhzhiaoblenerho
rank: Acting director general, Zaporizhzhiaoblenerho
d: Zaporizhzhiaoblenerho, the Zaporizhzhia regional electricity company in which the state held 60.2%, signed assignment-of-claims agreements that diverted payments owed by its consumers, among them the state titanium works ZTMK and Dniprospetsstal. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the loss at 346.22 million hryvnia over 2014-2015 and says the scheme was run by the then chairman of the board of the private holding company Energomerezha together with the acting director general of Zaporizhzhiaoblenerho. Five of the agreements were invalidated by the courts and 74 million hryvnia was refunded during the investigation. The chairman was detained on 15 April 2019 after extradition from Germany; the former acting director general remained on the wanted list.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2019
inside: A private power-trading holding reached the state-controlled regional electricity company through its acting director general, so claims on consumers' payments were signed over to it, costing 346.22 million hryvnia.

n: UAE firm paid $2.225m by Ukraine's arms exporter for support services
org_label: Non-resident company in the United Arab Emirates
rank: Directors and deputy directors, Spetstechnoexport
d: Spetstechnoexport, a state arms trading enterprise in the Ukroboronprom group, signed an additional agreement to a foreign economic contract for support services with a non-resident limited company in the United Arab Emirates in 2014 and paid 2.225 million US dollars, equal to 55.5 million hryvnia, for services NABU says were never provided. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, served suspicions on five people on 4 March 2019: a former director who had been deputy director when the agreement was made, another former director, a former deputy director, the former deputy head of contract department No. 1 and a former unit head. The state enterprise Plant 410 CA also features. The indictment was sent to court on 24 January 2020.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2019
inside: A United Arab Emirates company was paid $2.225m by Ukraine's state arms exporter for support services never provided, under an agreement signed by the exporter's own directors.

n: Ticket software bought for Ukraine's railways without an open tender
rank: Director, Ukrzaliznytsia Main Information and Computing Centre
d: The Main Information and Computing Centre, a branch of Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia, bought ticketing software for the Boryspil Express airport service through a negotiated procedure that avoided an open tender. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, served suspicions on five people: the branch's director, its former deputy director, and the beneficial owner, director and deputy director of the commercial company that was to be paid, which the report does not name. Payment was halted, so the 10.4 million hryvnia the railway would have lost was prevented rather than lost. The report gives no date for the purchase; the suspicions fall in the second half of 2020.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2020
inside: A supplier reached the state railway's computing branch through its director, which bought its ticket software without an open tender; the 10.4 million hryvnia payment was stopped.

n: Donenergoexport's goods cost three Ukrainian state coal mines 51m extra
rank: Tender committee heads, secretaries and members at three state coal enterprises
d: Three state coal enterprises in Donetsk region - Selydivvuhillia, Myrnohradvuhillia and the Pivdennodonbaske No. 1 mine administration - bought about 174.5 million hryvnia of goods through 69 tenders between 2016 and 2018 and overpaid about 51.17 million hryvnia. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, served suspicions on ten people: the heads, secretaries and members of the tender committees at the three mines, an individual it describes as the organiser, and the director of the private company Donenergoexport, which supplied through an intermediary the report does not name. The case was at the suspicion stage in the second half of 2020. The record is placed at Selydove, the seat of Selydivvuhillia.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2020
inside: A private supplier reached three state coal mines through their tender committees, winning 69 tenders at prices about 51.17 million hryvnia above value.

n: Centrgaz director's gas contract let a counterparty take 8.6m hryvnia
org_label: Private gas counterparty; seized funds held by Naftogazgroup Demetra
rank: Director, Centrgaz, subsidiary of Kirovohradhaz
d: Kostiantyn Starovoit, director of Centrgaz, a subsidiary of the state regional gas company Kirovohradhaz, signed a gas sale-and-purchase contract in 2017 shortly before leaving the post, on terms that let the enterprise's money be taken. The High Anti-Corruption Court found he created an artificial debt to the counterparty, so 8.6 million hryvnia was recovered from the enterprise as a prepayment and a penalty for non-performance, by a group acting in prior conspiracy. On 6 August 2020 he was sentenced to eight years in prison and partial confiscation of property including a Kia Optima. The Supreme Court left the verdict unchanged. The seized money stood in the account of the private firm Naftogazgroup Demetra; Starovoit did not appear to serve the sentence and was put on a wanted list.
cite: Slovo i Dilo, 6 August 2020 and 28 October 2021; NABU report for the second half of 2020
inside: An outside gas counterparty reached the state gas subsidiary through its own director, whose contract and invented debt moved 8.6 million hryvnia out of the enterprise.

n: Supplier's kit cost Ukraine's courts administration 51m hryvnia extra
rank: Head of a department, State Judicial Administration
d: The State Judicial Administration, the body that runs Ukraine's courts, bought audio and video recording equipment for courtrooms under a tender and supply contract that NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says cost it 51 million hryvnia more than the goods were worth. Two people were served with suspicions in November 2021: the head of one of the administration's departments at the time and the head of the supplying company, which the report does not name. NABU filed a civil claim in December 2018 to void the contract, and the case was pending at the Kyiv Economic Court. The competition authority later fined the suppliers more than 8 million hryvnia over the procurement.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: A supplier reached the body that runs Ukraine's courts through a department head, selling courtroom recording equipment at 51 million hryvnia above its worth.

n: Arkona Gaz-Enerhiia's gas permit granted without auction on false figures
rank: Deputy director, Ukrainian State Geological Research Institute; experts, State Commission on Mineral Reserves
d: A gas-condensate subsoil use permit was granted without an auction to the private company Arkona Gaz-Enerhiia after, NABU says, invented production figures were used to lower the fee the state should have received. Six people were served with suspicion on 31 July 2020: the deputy director and a sector head of the Ukrainian State Geological Research Institute, two experts of the State Commission on Mineral Reserves, one of whom also directed the private firm Proekt-Naftogaz, that firm's senior and chief engineers, and Arkona's director. The Poltava regional council approved the allocation in April 2017. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the damage at 196.8 million hryvnia. The file was opened to the defence on 9 September 2021.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: Two private gas firms reached the state geological institute and the mineral reserves commission through their own experts, so a drilling permit was issued without auction, costing 196.8 million hryvnia.

n: Licence applicants' 90 thousand dollars reached Ukraine's gambling regulator
rank: Member of the Commission for the Regulation of Gambling and Lotteries
d: A sitting member of Ukraine's Commission for the Regulation of Gambling and Lotteries (KRAIL), the state body that licenses casinos and betting, was caught taking a bribe of 90 thousand US dollars from entrepreneurs seeking gambling licences. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the money was for approving hotel premises in Chernihiv and Zaporizhzhia regions as suitable for gambling and for issuing the licences, and that the arrangement ran from the start of 2021. The commissioner was detained while receiving the money. The report names neither the commissioner nor the entrepreneurs, and the investigation was continuing at the end of 2021.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: Licence applicants' bribe of 90 thousand US dollars reached a serving member of Ukraine's gambling regulator, who approved their premises and issued the licences they wanted.

n: Road firms' 575 thousand dollars reached Ukraine's acting roads agency chief
rank: Acting head, Ukravtodor state road agency
d: The former acting head of Ukravtodor, Ukraine's state agency for motor roads, is accused of taking 575 thousand US dollars and 70 thousand euros between 2017 and 2019 from the beneficiary of a group of road-building companies. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the payments secured approval of payments for road works, extensions of work deadlines and a decision not to terminate the contracts. Suspicion was served on 13 April 2021, the beneficiary's episode was split into a separate case on 15 September 2021 and the file was opened to the defence on 22 September 2021. The report names neither the former official nor the companies.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: A road-building group's beneficiary paid the acting head of Ukraine's roads agency 575 thousand US dollars and 70 thousand euros, so its payments were approved and its contracts left in place.

n: Contractor's 24m hryvnia offer aimed at Ukraine's defence audit chief
rank: Director, Internal Audit Department, Ministry of Defence
d: A commercial company carrying out works under Ukraine's state defence order offered 24 million hryvnia so that an internal audit of its contract, worth 422 million hryvnia, would come out in its favour. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the head of a control division in the Defence Ministry's Military Representatives Department made the offer, that almost 17 million hryvnia of it was intended for the director of the ministry's Internal Audit Department and that 7 million hryvnia was a fee for the intermediary. The events fall in spring 2021. The report names neither the company nor the officials and does not say whether suspicion was served; the investigation was continuing.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: A defence contractor's 24 million hryvnia was aimed at the Defence Ministry's internal audit director, to buy a favourable audit of its 422 million hryvnia contract.

n: Agency fees of $1.93m left Kharkiv's state aircraft plant
rank: Head of the Kharkiv State Aviation Plant
d: The Kharkiv State Aviation Plant, an aircraft maker in the Ukroboronprom group, paid a commercial company 553.24 thousand euros and more than 1.93 million US dollars between 2013 and 2015 under contracts for agency services in foreign sales, services NABU says were never performed. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the damage at about 30 million hryvnia at the National Bank exchange rate and served suspicion in late July 2021 on the person who headed the enterprise when the payments were made. Because his whereabouts were unknown the notice was served under the procedure for absent suspects, and the investigation continued. The report names neither the company nor the official.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2021
inside: A commercial company took 553.24 thousand euros and more than 1.93 million US dollars from the state aircraft plant for sales agency services never performed, paid by the plant's own head.

n: Odesa Port Plant's fertilizer sold below market to a chosen buyer
rank: Deputy director and a department head, Odesa Port Plant
d: Odesa Port Plant, a chemical works 99.57% owned by the Ukrainian state, sold mineral fertilizers between March and December 2015 at prices below market value to a company chosen in advance, which resold them abroad. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the damage at 93.3 million hryvnia. It names as organiser a former member of parliament of the eighth convocation, and among the suspects the buyer's owner, the plant's deputy director and a department head. Four accomplices were served with suspicions in March 2020 and the organiser in October 2022; a court ordered his arrest in absentia on 7 December 2022, and his defence appeal was pending at the end of the year.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022
inside: A chosen private buyer reached the state fertilizer works through its deputy director and a department head, taking fertilizer below market price at a cost of 93.3 million hryvnia.

n: Seized property sold cheap through Ukraine's asset recovery agency
rank: Head of ARMA; an employee of the state enterprise SETAM
d: Property seized in criminal cases and handed to Ukraine's National Agency for Asset Recovery and Management (ARMA) was sold to buyers below market value through SETAM, the state enterprise that runs ARMA's auctions. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the damage at almost half a billion hryvnia in 2019, and says the lots included three land plots in Odesa that had belonged to the Auchan retail chain, 2,600 tonnes of sand, 4,500 tonnes of carbamide, grain, cereals and oilseeds. It says the then head of ARMA lobbied the government for the resolution that allowed the sales and that a SETAM employee published the lots. Five people were charged in early July 2022 and the group had grown to eleven by the end of the year.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022
inside: Buyers of seized assets reached the state asset recovery agency and its auction enterprise through their own officials, taking land and goods at below-market prices.

n: Developer's flat swap cost Ukraine's border guard service 10.68m
rank: Head of the State Border Guard Service and its capital construction department
d: A development company contracted to provide 66 flats in Lviv for Ukraine's State Border Guard Service instead delivered 53 flats in the suburbs, and the flats in the centre were sold to third parties. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the loss to the state at 10.68 million hryvnia and says the service's then head obtained a parking space at nearly half price. Suspicions were served on 28 October 2022 on the former head of the service, the head of its first separate capital construction department and the developer's director; the investigation was completed about two months later. The project dates from 2019 and the report names neither the company nor the officials.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022
inside: A developer reached the border guard service through its head and construction department, swapping 66 central Lviv flats for 53 suburban ones, a loss of 10.68 million hryvnia.

n: Agrarian holdings' payments reached Ukraine's fiscal service head
rank: Head of the State Fiscal Service
d: The former head of Ukraine's State Fiscal Service and an accomplice are accused of taking 5.5 million US dollars and more than 21 million euros, together more than 722 million hryvnia, as bribes for granting value added tax refunds to agrarian holding companies. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the refunds exceeded half a billion hryvnia and that the money moved through non-resident companies. Suspicion was served in October 2022 and the pre-trial investigation was continuing. The report names neither the former official nor the companies. The State Fiscal Service collected taxes and customs duties and was split into separate tax and customs services in 2019.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022
inside: Agrarian holdings' payments of 5.5 million US dollars and more than 21 million euros reached the head of Ukraine's fiscal service, who granted them VAT refunds.

n: Developer's land swap with Ukraine's National Guard cost 81m hryvnia
org_label: Development company linked to a former MP
rank: National Guard of Ukraine property decisions
d: About a hectare of land in central Kyiv belonging to Ukraine's National Guard was exchanged with a development company for flats and parking spaces, and a supplementary agreement then moved 70 of the flats to the city outskirts. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the damage at more than 81 million hryvnia and says the company was linked to a former member of parliament of the eighth convocation, who was served with suspicion on 18 October 2022 and repaid 50 million hryvnia voluntarily. The arrangement dates from the early 2000s; the criminal case was opened on 5 September 2022 and the case was sent to court on 18 January 2023.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022
inside: A former MP's development company reached the National Guard's property decisions, swapping a hectare of central Kyiv for flats and then moving 70 of them to the outskirts.

n: DTEK staff helped write the tariff formula Ukraine's regulator adopted
rank: Heads, members and staff of the NEURC energy regulator
d: In March 2016 Ukraine's energy and utilities regulator, the NEURC, approved a method of setting the wholesale electricity price that costed coal for thermal power stations at the Rotterdam port price plus delivery to Ukraine, transport that NABU says never took place. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says regulator officials adopted the resolution with help from staff of the private energy group DTEK, whose stations then sold power at higher prices, and that consumers overpaid more than 39 billion hryvnia in 2016-2019, of which 22.4 billion went to the initiators. Fifteen people were charged in a second episode in October 2022. The High Anti-Corruption Court has since released several defendants, among them former NEURC head Oksana Kryvenko, reported in August 2025, because the limitation period had expired; eleven remain.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022; Mind.ua, 21 August 2025; Ekonomichna Pravda
inside: A private power group's staff helped Ukraine's energy regulator adopt a coal price formula that included transport never performed, so its stations sold electricity at higher prices.

n: Skoda JS's 311.6 thousand euro fee reached a Ukrainian energy ex-chair
rank: Former chairman of the Verkhovna Rada fuel and energy committee
d: NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, served a new suspicion on 28 July 2022 on Mykola Martynenko, former chairman of the Ukrainian parliament's committee on fuel and energy issues, alleging he took 311.6 thousand euros paid as agency fees to promote in Ukraine the interests of the Czech nuclear engineering firm Skoda JS. Transparency International Ukraine records that the money came from Skoda JS management between July and December 2014, and that on 28 May the High Anti-Corruption Court granted the defence's motion and released him from criminal liability for this episode because the limitation period had run out in December 2024. The prosecutor agreed and guilt was not determined. He remains on trial over embezzlement at the state enterprises SkhidGZK and Energoatom.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2022; Transparency International Ukraine, HACC case monitoring
inside: A Czech nuclear supplier's agency fee of 311.6 thousand euros reached the former chair of parliament's energy committee, to advance its interests inside Ukraine's state nuclear enterprises.

n: Shell intermediaries' pasta cost Ukraine's railways 62.5m hryvnia extra
org_label: Intermediary shell companies and foreign pasta suppliers
rank: First deputy minister of agrarian policy and food; former deputy minister of economy
d: In the first months of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, Ukrzaliznytsia, Ukraine's state railway company, bought food for humanitarian needs through intermediary shell companies supplied by foreign producers of pasta products, at prices raised by up to 150%. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the overpayment at more than 62.5 million hryvnia. Suspicion was served on 24 August 2023 on the first deputy minister of agrarian policy and food and on a former deputy minister of economy, who held office when the second scheme ran. The investigation was continuing at the end of 2023. The report names neither the officials nor the companies.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2023
inside: Intermediary shell companies reached the state railway's food buying with two deputy ministers' help, raising prices by up to 150% and overcharging more than 62.5 million hryvnia.

n: Contractor's spent-fuel store contract at Energoatom rose to 1.497bn
rank: Director general of an Energoatom separate unit
d: A separate unit of Energoatom, Ukraine's state nuclear power company, awarded the construction of a central store for spent nuclear fuel outside an open tender to a contractor chosen in advance, and supplementary agreements for radiation control equipment raised the contract price from 421 million to 1.497 billion hryvnia. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, puts the overpayment at almost 100 million hryvnia. Suspicions name the unit's director general and the head of its estimate and contract department, together with the contractor company, its head and an employee of its legal department. The contract was signed in 2020 and construction had begun in 2017. The investigation was continuing at the end of 2023; the report names neither the company nor the officials.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2023
inside: A pre-selected contractor reached Energoatom's spent-fuel store project through the unit's director general, lifting its contract from 421 million to 1.497 billion hryvnia.

n: MP's firm took 312m hryvnia for an unfinished Ukrainian army arsenal
org_label: Construction company controlled by a member of parliament
rank: Ministry of Defence construction contract; senior officers
d: A construction company controlled by a Ukrainian member of parliament was paid 312 million hryvnia for building an arsenal for the Defence Ministry, a project estimated at about 3 billion hryvnia, after Cabinet of Ministers decrees were amended to allow an 80% advance payment. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says senior officers lobbied for the changes to the decrees. The work began in 2018 and the 2021 completion deadline was missed. Suspicions were served on 25 October 2023 on the former member of parliament, who held the seat when the scheme ran, his assistant, three serving and former military personnel and the company's director. The investigation was completed on 24 January 2024 after a court refused to extend the deadline.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2023
inside: An MP's construction company reached the Defence Ministry's arsenal project, taking a 312 million hryvnia advance after Cabinet decrees were changed to allow 80% prepayment.

n: Two state farms' land near Kyiv reallocated through the land cadastre
org_label: Private organisers of the land scheme
rank: Officials of the Kyiv regional main department of Derzhheokadastr
d: Land belonging to two state enterprises in Kyiv region - about 920 hectares of the Dmytrivka research farm at Fastiv and about 284 hectares of Pushcha-Vodytsia - was handed out free of charge, had its permitted use changed and in some cases was resold at up to a tenth of market value. NABU, Ukraine's anti-corruption police, says the organisers influenced officials of the regional main department of Derzhheokadastr, the state land cadastre service, and used the names of veterans of the anti-terrorist operation in the east without their knowledge. It puts the combined market value at more than 1.8 billion hryvnia. Five people were served with suspicion on 15 August 2023 and seven by 7 September; the land was arrested and building banned.
cite: NABU report for the second half of 2023
inside: Private organisers reached the state land cadastre's Kyiv regional department, so two state farms' land was issued free in veterans' names and resold far below value.

n: BMS's robots and its cash reached Bach Mai Hospital's director
rank: director, Bach Mai Hospital
d: Bach Mai Hospital in Hanoi is one of Vietnam's largest state hospitals. BMS Medical Technology, a private supplier, offered it two surgical robots at prices its chairman Pham Duc Tuan set. The Rosa robot had been imported from France for just over 7.4 billion dong and went into a joint venture with the hospital at 39 billion. Director Nguyen Quoc Anh signed the contract without the hospital's agreement. Prosecutors said Tuan gave him 400 million dong and 10,000 US dollars; Anh told the court he took it as traditional holiday gifts. The robot was used on 637 patients, overcharged by more than 10 billion dong. On 24 January 2022 the Hanoi People's Court jailed Anh for five years and gave Tuan 36 months suspended.
inside: A private medical supplier set the price of robots a state hospital bought and paid its director 400 million dong and 10,000 US dollars, and 637 patients were overcharged.
cite: Lien doan Luat su VN (lsvn.vn), 24 January 2022; Sai Gon Giai Phong, 20 January 2022

n: A case-fixing ring bought psychiatric findings at Vietnam's forensic institute
org_label: Nguyen Thi Mai Anh's case-fixing ring
rank: director and assessment council, Central Institute of Forensic Psychiatry
d: The Central Institute of Forensic Psychiatry in Hanoi decides whether criminal suspects are mentally fit to be tried. In June 2025 Hanoi police opened a case alleging that its director Tran Van Truong took money sent by Nguyen Thi Mai Anh, herself a patient under compulsory treatment there, and passed part of it to members of the assessment council, so that psychiatric symptoms were added to case files or patients' conditions misstated to give the conclusion wanted. Police said Mai Anh brokered case-fixing for nearly 200 defendants, took billions of dong in some matters and passed several hundred million to Truong. By 6 October 2025, 49 people had been charged, 34 of them from the institute. The investigation continues.
inside: A case-fixing ring's money reached the state institute that rules on criminal suspects' sanity, so its assessors allegedly wrote into files the psychiatric findings the payers wanted.
cite: Tien Phong, 23 June 2025; Bao Phap luat Viet Nam, 7 October 2025

n: Vehicle owners' 2.7bn dong bought Da Nang's vehicle inspection centre
rank: director and inspector, Da Nang Motor Vehicle Inspection Centre
d: Vietnam's motor vehicle inspection centres issue the certificates a vehicle needs to stay on the road. At the Da Nang Motor Vehicle Inspection Centre, inspector Luong Ngoc Vu took money from vehicle owners, directly and through Luong Kim Quang, director of LKQ Co., to issue modification certificates for vehicles altered without authorisation or lacking design documents, fabricating the design files and acceptance records. Between February 2020 and 23 November 2022 they handled 655 files and more than 2.7 billion dong, of which Vu kept over 1.1 billion, centre director Bui Van Tan 382 million and Quang over 178 million. On 18 June 2024 the Da Nang People's Court convicted all three of taking bribes, jailing Vu for 13 years, Tan for eight and Quang for seven.
inside: Vehicle owners and a go-between firm paid more than 2.7 billion dong to the state inspection centre's own director and inspector, who certified vehicles that should not have passed.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 18 June 2024

n: Hue's inspection centre and a design firm sold files for altered vehicles
org_label: vehicle owners and Thong Nhat Hue Auto Design
who: vehicle owners and Thong Nhat Hue Auto Design
rank: director and three deputy directors, Thua Thien Hue vehicle inspection centre
d: The Thua Thien Hue provincial motor vehicle inspection centre, now the Hue City centre, certifies that vehicles are roadworthy. From 2018 to February 2023 four of its officers took money from vehicle owners inside and outside the province to put through illegal vehicle modifications, with design firms preparing and certifying the files so that non-compliant vehicles passed. Director Dao Huu Long took about 2.3 billion dong from 258 owners and kept over 1 billion; deputy director Tran Hung Huy took over 2.074 billion from 255 owners. Nguyen Phan Phu Nguyen, director of Thong Nhat Hue Auto Design, profited over 934 million. On 5 June 2025 the Hue People's Court jailed Long for 15 years and three months, Huy and Nguyen for 15 years each, and ordered all profits repaid.
inside: Vehicle owners and a design company paid the state inspection centre's director and deputies about 2.3 billion dong and more, and modified vehicles were certified as compliant.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 5 June 2025

n: Drivers paid Hoa Binh's state inspection centre 28-01S to pass failed vehicles
rank: director and staff, Vehicle Inspection Centre 28-01S
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 28-01S sits under the Department of Transport of Hoa Binh province and issues the certificates a vehicle needs to stay on the road. Prosecutors said that between March and September 2022 its director, department heads and inspectors took more than 107 million dong from drivers so that vehicles failing safety and emissions checks were passed. On 11 March 2024 the Hoa Binh provincial court convicted ten of them of taking bribes: former director Trinh Thanh Cong, described by prosecutors as a key figure, was jailed for four years, inspection department head Kim Ngoc Hieu for 36 months, deputy director Tran Thu Huong and deputy department head Bui Trung Linh for 30 months each, and six inspectors given 24 months suspended.
inside: Drivers paid more than 107 million dong to the provincial transport department's own inspection centre, which then certified vehicles that had failed its safety and emissions checks.
cite: RFA Vietnamese, 11 March 2024

n: Drivers' 5.3bn dong ran inspection centre 78-02D in Phu Yen
rank: chairwoman, general director and inspectors, Inspection Centre 78-02D
d: Inspection Centre 78-02D in Phu Yen province, run by the Bach Viet Inspection Company and certified to operate by the Vietnam Road Administration from 12 October 2020, issues state roadworthiness certificates. Prosecutors alleged that vehicle owners and drivers paid its staff between 100,000 and 3 million dong a vehicle, depending on how bad the fault was, to have violations overlooked at inspection, and that the centre's leaders let the director, inspectors, cashier, accountant and staff take the money, over 5.3 billion dong in all. On 4 September 2024 the Phu Yen provincial court convicted ten of taking bribes, 79 years in total: chairwoman Ngo Thi Thu Hang 17 years, general director Phan Dinh Tham 15 and deputy director Phan Trung Hieu 10.
inside: Vehicle owners paid over 5.3 billion dong to the authorised inspection centre's own chiefs and inspectors, who then overlooked the faults and issued roadworthiness certificates.
cite: RFA Vietnamese, 4 September 2024

n: Customers' payments passed failed vehicles at Bac Kan's centre 97-01D
rank: chairman and director, Vehicle Inspection Centre 97-01D
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 97-01D in Bac Kan province, run by the Bac Kan Vehicle Inspection Joint Stock Company, issues the state certificates a vehicle needs to stay on the road. According to the indictment, from 2020 to 2022 customers paid between 150,000 and 1.5 million dong a visit so that vehicles failing the requirements would pass and be certified, with nearly 334 million dong taken in all, and chairman and director Tran Duc Duong directed the scheme with deputy director Hoang Huy Truong, inspectors and other staff. On 26 April 2024 the Bac Kan provincial court convicted ten of bribery, jailing Duong for four years with a 50 million dong fine and Truong for three years and six months with a 40 million dong fine.
inside: Vehicle owners paid nearly 334 million dong to the inspection centre's own chairman and staff, who certified vehicles that had failed the roadworthiness requirements.
cite: RFA Vietnamese, 26 April 2024

n: Vehicle owners and two firms paid Dong Nai's inspection centre 60-04D
org_label: vehicle owners, Vu Khang Co. and a driving school
who: vehicle owners and Vu Khang Co.
rank: director and inspectors, Vehicle Inspection Centre 60-04D
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 60-04D in Tan Bien ward, Bien Hoa, issues roadworthiness certificates. Police said vehicle owners paid its staff directly or through intermediaries so that failed inspection items were overlooked, with officers typically taking 200,000 to 800,000 dong a day and former director Luong Minh Tu 2 to 6 million, and that from early 2020 to December 2022 the group took over 2.2 billion dong. The centre was raided on 10 January 2023. On 7 October 2024 the Dong Nai provincial court sentenced 15 people: Tu seven years and two deputy directors three years six months and 22 months for taking bribes, and for giving bribes Le Tien Trung of Vu Khang Co. six months and a Saigon driving school employee eight months suspended.
inside: Vehicle owners, a company and a driving school paid over 2.2 billion dong to the inspection centre's own director and inspectors, who passed vehicles that had failed.
cite: RFA Vietnamese, 7 October 2024

n: Can Tho's inspection centre director took 918m dong on 778 vehicle files
rank: director, Can Tho Motor Vehicle Inspection Centre 65-02D
d: Can Tho Motor Vehicle Inspection Centre 65-02D certifies that vehicles are fit for the road. Chau Ngoc Y, its director from September 2019, was accused of taking money from vehicle owners or their representatives to overlook violations, and of conspiring with others to forge thousands of agency documents to validate files for modified vehicles. Prosecutors said he took bribes on 778 vehicle acceptance files, more than 918 million dong in all. On 21 May 2025 the Can Tho People's Court jailed him for 11 years for taking bribes, forging agency documents and using forged documents; Nguyen Si Hung, who altered an image of a truck-crane inspection certificate, got five years, and two acceptance inspectors were given suspended terms.
inside: Vehicle owners paid the state inspection centre's own director more than 918 million dong across 778 files, and forged documents were used to certify modified vehicles.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 19 May 2025

n: Cuong Phat's money passed 379 false modification files in Binh Dinh
rank: director and inspectors, Vehicle Inspection Centre 77-04D
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 77-04D, in the Nhon Hoi Economic Zone at Quy Nhon, belongs to the Binh Dinh Engineering Joint Stock Company and certifies that modified vehicles are fit for the road. Tran Huy Cuong, who ran Cuong Phat Company offering turnkey vehicle modifications, was accused of paying the centre's inspection team 189.5 million dong to pass 379 modification files that were falsified because the work had not been done to regulations. He had taken over 1.6 billion dong from the 379 vehicle owners, of which 478.7 million was found to be illicit profit. On 13 May 2025 the Binh Dinh provincial court tried five people, jailing former centre director Nguyen Vu Ka for three years and former deputy director Nguyen Duc Thach for two years and six months.
inside: A vehicle modification firm paid the state inspection centre's team 189.5 million dong, and 379 files were certified for work that had not been done to regulations.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 13 May 2025

n: Money for insanity findings reached the Bien Hoa forensic psychiatry institute
rank: director, deputy director and forensic assessors, Bien Hoa institute
d: The Central Institute of Forensic Psychiatry at Bien Hoa, in Dong Nai province, decides whether criminal suspects can be held responsible for what they did. On 16 June 2024 the Ministry of Public Security's criminal police arrested its director and deputy director, and on 23 June opened a case for taking, giving and brokering bribes. Police said outsiders exploited the policy of reduced liability for people with psychiatric records, working with some of the institute's leaders, doctors and assessors to create files and diagnoses showing lost or limited capacity so that penalties were cut or avoided, and that some doctors and assessors took money to record diagnoses as they chose. Sixteen people have been charged, twelve of them institute officers. No sums were given.
inside: Criminal suspects' money allegedly reached the state institute that assesses their sanity, so its doctors wrote the diagnoses that cut or avoided their penalties.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 26 December 2024

n: A driving school paid Lang Son's transport department over the theory test
rank: vehicle and driver management office, Lang Son Department of Transport
d: The Lang Son provincial Department of Transport runs the driving tests that decide who gets a licence. At a trial from 20 to 23 December 2022, the Lang Son provincial court found that Dang Hoang Tam, director of the Truong An driving school, and Luong Thi Thu had paid Chu Thi Xuan and Bui Duy Hai, civil servants in the department's vehicle and driver management office, for support in the theory part of students' driving tests in 2020. The case also covered forged health certificates issued through the Lang Son General Clinic. 24 people were convicted: Xuan got two years and three months, Hai two years, Tam a year and six months and Thu a year. The court ordered the illicit gains recovered but no figure was reported.
inside: A private driving school paid two officials of the provincial transport department for help with the theory test its students had to pass, and 24 people were convicted.
cite: Nhan Dan, 23 December 2022

n: Vehicle owners' go-betweens paid Dong Nai's inspection centre 60-05D
rank: director and inspectors, Vehicle Inspection Centre 60-05D
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 60-05D in Dong Nai province issues the certificates a vehicle needs to stay on the road. The indictment said that between 2018 and October 2020 its director Nguyen Ngoc Minh had the deputy directors and seven inspectors take money from vehicle owners to overlook minor faults and pass vehicles, nearly 127 million dong in all. The court treated nearly 80 million of that as bribes, the rest having been given voluntarily by owners of sound vehicles. Two intermediaries, Bui Quang Thong and Nguyen Tien Lan, passed over 30 million and over 27 million dong. On 14 June 2024 the Dong Nai court jailed Minh for three years and 11 others for 18 months to two years and six months.
inside: Vehicle owners and two go-betweens paid nearly 80 million dong in bribes to the inspection centre's own director and inspectors, who passed vehicles with faults.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 14 June 2024

n: No cash, no pass: 750m dong at Hanoi's inspection centre 29-18D
rank: chairman and staff, Vehicle Inspection Centre 29-18D
d: Vehicle Inspection Centre 29-18D in Son Tay town, Hanoi, is run by Minh Hung Vehicle Inspection Company and issues roadworthiness certificates. Investigators found that vehicle owners left money among the documents on the passenger seat, collected by the staff who moved cars into the inspection bays, so that defects in cargo-body dimensions, tyres, lights, brakes, emissions and wipers were overlooked; cars whose owners did not pay were not passed. The centre's leaders, inspectors and staff took 750 million dong, of which Pham Van Khang, chairman of the company's members' council, and his wife Nguyen Thi Trang, the centre's accountant, took 450 million. On 6 August 2024 the Hanoi People's Court jailed Khang for five years and six months and Trang for four years and six months.
inside: Vehicle owners paid 750 million dong to the inspection centre's own chairman, inspectors and staff, and vehicles with defects were certified while those that did not pay were failed.
cite: VOH (Voice of Ho Chi Minh City), 6 August 2024

n: A trucking firm paid 224m dong for badges from Soc Trang's transport department
rank: vehicle, transport and driver management division head, Soc Trang Department of Transport
d: A vehicle badge, or phu hieu, is the permit a lorry needs to work commercially, and in Soc Trang province it was issued by the provincial Department of Transport. Thai Thanh Son, chairman and director of the trucking company Son Phung, made twelve transfers totalling 236.2 million dong to Cao Thanh Sang, head of the department's vehicle, transport and driver management division, to smooth the firm's licensing and badge approvals, which had run into repeated problems: 224 million was for badges for 448 vehicles at 500,000 dong each, and 12.2 million was tied to a training course. On 26 December 2025 the People's Court of Regional Area 5 in Can Tho jailed Sang for five years and Son for a year and six months.
inside: A trucking company paid the provincial transport department's division head 224 million dong for badges for 448 of its vehicles, and he was jailed for five years.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 26 December 2025

n: Transport firms' monthly payments ran Can Tho's traffic inspectorate
rank: traffic inspectors, Can Tho transport inspectorate
d: Can Tho's traffic inspectorate, the thanh tra giao thong, checks lorries for overloading and other breaches. From 2013 to 2016 its inspectors took monthly payments of 1 million to 28 million dong, or payments per violation, from transport firms through two brokers, Tran Truong An and Nguyen Van Can, so that breaches were overlooked or lightly punished; the officers took nearly 4 billion dong. In 2017 the Can Tho People's Court convicted seven former inspectors of taking bribes and the two brokers of brokering, and on 19 October 2017 the high-level court in Ho Chi Minh City upheld the sentences, including life imprisonment for Doan Vu Duy. Police later recommended prosecuting seven company directors who had paid, more than 2 billion dong between them.
inside: Transport companies paid Can Tho's traffic inspectors nearly 4 billion dong through two brokers, and the inspectorate overlooked or lightly punished breaches by their lorries.
cite: Lien doan Luat su VN (lsvn.vn), 5 January 2021

n: LanQ's 700m dong bought Bac Giang's social insurance director
rank: director, Bac Giang Provincial Social Security
d: Bac Giang Provincial Social Security pays hospitals and clinics out of the state health insurance fund. Investigators found that from the first quarter of 2017 to the last of 2021, Nguyen Manh Quyen, chairman and chief executive of the pharmaceutical company LanQ, had its chief accountant hand the agency's director Than Duc Lai 7 to 60 million dong a quarter, 700 million in all, usually on the days claim forms went in. After each payment Lai told staff to favour LanQ when processing advances for insured treatment, which he then approved early and above the permitted amounts; LanQ was paid over 40 billion dong. On 15 June 2026 the appeal court in Hanoi ruled on the appeals: Lai's sentence is four years and Quyen's was cut to 17.
inside: A pharmaceutical company paid the provincial social insurance director 700 million dong, and he released health insurance advances to it early and above the permitted amounts.
cite: Vietnam Finance, 17 May 2025; Tien Phong, 16 June 2026

n: Agents' money bought judicial record certificates in Ho Chi Minh City
rank: Judicial Record Division, Ho Chi Minh City Department of Justice
d: The Judicial Record Division of the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Justice keeps the criminal record database and issues the certificates people need for work and visas. In an indictment reported on 22 July 2026 the city procuracy charged 16 people: four with taking bribes and twelve with giving or brokering them. Prosecutors say agents collected 2.5 to 4.5 million dong a case from clients, including foreign nationals, and paid officials to process certificates on fake temporary-residence confirmations, without the applicant appearing or authorising anyone. Hoang Thi Huong Lan is alleged to have handled 951 improper files and received over 2.5 billion dong, and Tran Vo Tan Khoa 2,465 files for over 481 million dong.
inside: Document agents paid officials of the city's judicial records division, which then issued criminal record certificates on fake residence confirmations, 951 files through one official alone.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 22 July 2026

n: Shopkeepers paid a Ho Chi Minh City ward's urban order team 518m dong
org_label: business households of Pham Ngu Lao ward
rank: urban order team, Pham Ngu Lao ward
d: An urban order team, or doi trat tu do thi, enforces the rules against blocking pavements and roads in a Vietnamese ward. Prosecutors allege that from November 2021 to December 2023 business households in Pham Ngu Lao ward, in the former District 1 of Ho Chi Minh City and now part of Ben Thanh ward, paid the team's collaborators 518 million dong so that their encroachment offences were not acted on, with deputy team leader Nguyen Tien Mai directing members who worked three-person shifts rotated weekly. Nguyen Thanh Tung was caught taking 750,000 dong from a complainant on 15 December 2023, and 32 further complainants came forward. Five are charged with taking bribes; their trial was postponed on 1 June 2026.
inside: Shopkeepers paid a city ward's urban order team 518 million dong, and prosecutors say their pavement encroachment offences were then left unpunished.
cite: Sai Gon Giai Phong, 1 June 2026

n: Tai Loc's 8.1bn dong cleared 1,814bn of timber through Hai Phong customs
rank: leaders and staff, Port 2 Customs Sub-department, Hai Phong
d: The Port 2 Customs Sub-department in Hai Phong clears goods through the port. In an indictment completed on 18 May 2025 the Supreme People's Procuracy alleged that the Hanoi company Tai Loc, whose director was Nguyen Tai Loc and chief accountant Ngo Quang Tuyen, smuggled veneer wood worth over 1,814 billion dong past it between January 2021 and January 2024, gaining over 210 billion dong, and paid more than 8.1 billion dong through Nguyen Quang Long to the sub-department's leaders and staff so goods were cleared quickly and violations skipped. Former team head Dang Hoang Lan is said to have taken over 860 million dong, other staff between 14 million and over 800 million each. The former sub-department head and her deputy are charged with abuse of office.
inside: A smuggling company paid over 8.1 billion dong to a Hai Phong customs sub-department's own officers, and 1,814 billion dong of timber went through quickly with violations skipped.
cite: Tien Phong, 18 May 2025

n: Hoang Sa's bribes let banned meat past Vietnam's regional veterinary office
rank: head and officers, Veterinary Sub-Department Region VI
d: Veterinary Sub-Department Region VI, under Vietnam's Department of Animal Health, inspects imported animal products. On 6 February 2026 the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court convicted 25 people over a scheme led by Tran Nguyen Binh, founder and director of the Hoang Sa company, in which firms paid officials to skip sampling, avoid full document checks and bypass procedures so that ruminant products from European countries with mad cow disease or its risk, which Vietnam had not permitted, could enter. Former sub-department head Bach Duc Luu took 1.2 billion dong and Ly Hoai Vu 800 million from Tran Trung Nhan, who had taken over 2.9 billion from businesses between 2018 and 2023. Luu and Vu got seven years each, Nhan nine and Binh 30.
inside: An importer paid the regional veterinary office's own head 1.2 billion dong and other officers more, and banned ruminant products from mad-cow countries were let into Vietnam.
cite: Tuoi Tre, 6 February 2026

n: Go-betweens' 1.3bn dong sped land certificates at Sam Son's registry branch
rank: director and staff, Sam Son Land Registration Office branch
d: The Land Registration Office branch in Sam Son city, Thanh Hoa province, handles changes to land records and the certificates that prove who holds land. The Thanh Hoa provincial court found that from 2021 to 2023 its staff took money outside the rules to speed up certificates and other paperwork, with 28 intermediaries paying over 1.3 billion dong in all, and that four defendants also abused their power by deliberately delaying files so that citizens paid more than they should. On 13 May 2025 the court sentenced 44 people: branch director Nguyen The Hung to 48 months, deputy director Le Huy Hoang to 30 months and three intermediaries to 42 months each. A tax official from the Sam Son-Quang Xuong regional office was among those charged.
inside: Paperwork go-betweens paid over 1.3 billion dong to the land registry branch's director and staff, who put their clients' land certificates through ahead of the rules.
cite: Bao Thanh tra, 13 May 2025

n: Vessel owners' 2.09bn dong bought Ca Mau's fishing boat papers
rank: officers of Ca Mau's fisheries sub-departments and vessel inspection centre
d: Ca Mau's fisheries bodies register fishing vessels, licence them and certify them for safety and food hygiene. The Ca Mau provincial court found that from 2018 to 2023 Pham Dang Chien, a specialist in the provincial Fisheries Sub-department, Nguyen Viet Trieu, deputy head of the Sea, Island and Fisheries Surveillance Sub-department, and Huynh Van Dang, deputy director of the Fishing Vessel Inspection Centre, signed large numbers of vessel documents in return for bribes totalling over 2.09 billion dong from the vessel owners Do Huu Nhan and Nguyen Minh Duong. On 20 July 2026 it jailed Chien for 15 years, Dang for 14, Trieu for seven and Duong for three years and six months. Nhan was not prosecuted, having confessed before the case came to light.
inside: Fishing vessel owners paid over 2.09 billion dong to Ca Mau's fisheries officers, who signed the registrations, licences and inspection certificates their boats needed.
cite: VOV, 20 July 2026

n: A counterfeit supplement maker's 1.5bn dong freed a shipment at customs
rank: two former leaders, Customs Supervision and Management Department
d: Vietnam's Customs Supervision and Management Department oversees how goods are cleared. On 31 July 2026 the Hanoi People's Court convicted 14 people in a case over counterfeit food supplements, finding that Nguyen Nang Manh, chairman of MediUSA and director of MegaPharco, paid 1.5 billion dong to two of the department's former leaders, Nguyen The Viet and Nguyen Huu Tuan, when a shipment of raw material from China was held at a border gate, so that it would be cleared irregularly. Manh was jailed for 16 years and six months for counterfeiting, accounting violations and bribe-giving, Tuan for seven years and Viet for six. Phan Cong Chien, former head of drug business management at the health ministry's Drug Administration, got 30 months suspended for taking bribes.
inside: A counterfeit supplement maker paid 1.5 billion dong to two former leaders of the customs supervision department, and a held shipment of raw material was cleared irregularly.
cite: Tien Phong, 31 July 2026

n: Zakarpattia customs officer moved a jewellery group's smuggled diamonds
rank: customs officer
d: Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office says a group ran a channel bringing diamonds, precious stones and finished jewellery into Ukraine from abroad, mainly the United Arab Emirates, through the checkpoints of the Zakarpattia customs house between 2022 and 2026. A serving Zakarpattia customs officer was drawn into the scheme and, with his wife, carried the goods across the border concealed from customs control, so the group avoided duty and other compulsory payments. The organisers own the Kyiv jewellery boutique where the stones were worked into pieces under their own brand and sold. Searches of a car, a workshop and the boutique recovered stones and jewellery valued at more than $1 million.
inside: A serving Zakarpattia customs officer and his wife carried a group's undeclared diamonds past the checkpoints he worked on, so a Kyiv jewellery boutique paid no duty.
undone: Detectives of the Bureau of Economic Security are running the pre-trial investigation with operational support from the Security Service of Ukraine, under article 364(2), abuse of office, and article 201-3(2), smuggling of goods. As of 10 November 2026 nobody had been served with a formal notice of suspicion: the investigators said they would fix the final loss to the state after expert examinations and then decide whom to notify. No defendant has been named publicly, so the officer and the boutique's owners are unnamed here, and none of them is before a court.
cite: Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine statement, reported by LB.ua, 10 November 2026; Ukraina Kryminalna (cripo.com.ua) and Mukachevo.net, 10 November 2026, on the criminal code articles and the Bureau of Economic Security's role; Zaxid.net, 10 November 2026

n: Taliban infiltrators in uniform overran the 209th Corps base
rank: army corps soldiers
d: Camp Shaheen outside Mazar-i-Sharif was the headquarters of the Afghan National Army's 209th Corps, with as many as three thousand personnel. On 21 April 2017 about ten Taliban fighters wearing army uniforms drove two military Ford Rangers through several rings of security, saying they carried wounded soldiers needing urgent care, then opened fire on men at Friday prayers in the base mosque and in a dining hall. Responding troops could not tell the attackers from their own because of the uniforms, and the battle ran more than six hours. The Taliban said four of the attackers had served in the corps until recent years and had changed sides. The provincial governor opened an inquiry into inside help.
inside: Attackers in Afghan army uniforms drove military vehicles through several security rings of the corps headquarters, and the Taliban said four of them had served in that corps.
undone: No prosecution followed: all the attackers were killed or, in one account, one was captured. Afghan officials put the dead at about 135 to 140 with 60 or more wounded on the first day; the 209th Corps was later described as having lost more than 160, and TOLOnews reported on 25 April 2017 that 256 soldiers had died and that the government was withholding the higher figure. The Taliban claimed at least 500 killed or injured. Minister of Defence Abdullah Habibi and Army Chief of Staff General Qadam Shah Shahim both resigned on 24 April 2017. The claim that four attackers were former soldiers of the corps is the Taliban's own and was not confirmed by the Afghan army, which is why this record is coded probable.
cite: Washington Post, 22 April 2017; TOLOnews, 22 and 25 April 2017; Associated Press via Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, 22 April 2017; New York Times, 24 April 2017, on the resignations

n: A quarter of Afghan insider attacks came from Taliban placement
rank: army and police recruits
d: The Afghan National Defense and Security Forces were built fast, and vetting did not keep pace with recruitment. A 2017 study by West Point's Modern War Institute counted 102 insider attacks from 2007 to 2016, in which a member of the Afghan forces turned on coalition or Afghan colleagues, and attributed 25 per cent of them to Taliban infiltration and 40 per cent to personal grievance. The coalition's own estimate was similar: about a quarter of insider attacks came from Taliban placement or suspected Taliban links. Attacks of this kind killed 157 NATO personnel and 557 members of the Afghan forces from May 2007 onward, and the Taliban named them as a tactic of its spring offensives.
inside: The Afghan army and police were recruited faster than they could be vetted, and about a quarter of insider attacks on them were traced to men the Taliban had placed inside.
undone: This record is a pattern drawn from a counted series rather than one proceeding: it names no single defendant or court, so no outcome round can resolve it, and it is coded reported for that reason. The map holds separate records for the Camp Shaheen attack of April 2017 and for the first quarter of 2021, when insider attacks rose 82 per cent. The share attributed to infiltration is an estimate by the coalition and by the study's authors, not a court finding, and the alternative explanation they weigh more heavily is personal grievance rather than placement.
cite: Modern War Institute at West Point, 'Dress Like Allies, Kill Like Enemies', 2017, reported by Associated Press via Navy Times, 18 June 2017; Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction quarterly reports to Congress

n: Hezbollah's man ran Beirut airport security and was put back by the army
rank: head of airport security, General Directorate of General Security
d: In May 2008 the Druze leader Walid Jumblatt, then in government, accused Hezbollah of running a hidden remote-controlled camera overlooking a runway at Beirut's Rafik Hariri International Airport. On 6 May the Lebanese cabinet took two decisions: it declared Hezbollah's private fibre-optic telephone network illegal and referred it to the judiciary, and it removed Brigadier General Wafiq Shoucair, the airport's head of security, for failing to stop that surveillance and for his reported closeness to the opposition. Shoucair was a political ally of the parliament speaker Nabih Berri, leader of Hezbollah's coalition partner Amal. Hassan Nasrallah called the telecoms decision a declaration of war, and fighting began the next day.
inside: A government that tried to remove the airport's security chief over a movement's surveillance of the runways lost a week of street fighting and had him reinstated by its own army.
undone: The clashes of 7 to 14 May 2008 killed between 60 and 110 people and were the first use of Hezbollah's weapons on an internal front since the civil war. The government then suspended both decisions and handed them to the army command, which reinstated Shoucair and said it would handle the telephone network in a way that did not harm Hezbollah's security. The Doha Agreement of 21 May 2008 settled the wider crisis. No prosecution followed and no court established who placed the camera, which is why this record is coded probable: the cabinet's decision, the fighting and the reinstatement are established, while the claim that Shoucair acted on Hezbollah's instructions is the government's.
cite: Al Jazeera, 9 May 2008; Committee to Protect Journalists, 'Attacks on the Press in 2008: Lebanon', February 2009, on the dismissal and the army's reinstatement; The Times via GlobalSecurity, 8 May 2008

n: Six Haitian police officers worked inside the Tokyo gang
rank: serving officers of the Haitian National Police
d: Police investigations opened in February 2026 found links between at least six serving Haitian National Police officers and Ralph Woodmyr Louissant, alias Chale, who leads the Tokyo gang inside the Viv Ansanm coalition. Officer Charlemagne Volmar identified police checkpoints so the gang could carry out kidnappings without being intercepted, checked how much money intended victims had before they were seized, and moved large sums meant for buying ammunition; Chale called him after each kidnapping to report any deaths. Volmar named a further officer who sold Chale an AR-15 rifle.
