n: Modugno's ex-mayor on trial over Parisi clan votes traded for jobs
who: the Parisi clan and the Diomede clan of Bari
rank: former mayor and former productive-activities assessore of Modugno
d: On 13 October 2026 the Bari preliminary-hearing judge sent six defendants to trial over alleged mafia-political vote exchange at the 2020 municipal elections in Modugno. They include the former mayor Nicola Bonasia, who the prosecution says accepted, through the then productive-activities assessore Antonio Lopez, a promise by people considered close to Bari's Parisi clan to procure votes for the October 2020 run-off in exchange for jobs. Lopez is said to have handed money to clan members for votes himself. Prosecutors say Bonasia made the same pact with Adriana Diomede, considered a referent of the Diomede clan, in exchange for her daughter's candidacy for the Modugno council. The ordinary trial starts on 14 January 2027; the comune, the interior ministry and the anti-racket commissioner are civil parties.
inside: Prosecutors say Bari clans delivered run-off votes to Modugno's mayor and were promised jobs and a council candidacy in exchange.
cite: Antenna Sud, 22 Jun 2026; TRM, 13 Oct 2026

n: Statte's mayor convicted of giving a clan permits for its own businesses
rank: Mayor of Statte and two members of his electoral list
d: Reasons published for a September 2025 judgment explain why the former mayor of Statte, Francesco Andrioli, was sentenced to four years and five months for mafia-political vote exchange in the Domino inquiry. The judge found the Sudoso clan in control of the comune from 2021, through violence and threats against opponents but also with the contribution of "men of the police forces" and "members of the local institutions". Andrioli's rise to mayor was helped by Davide Sudoso, who had two trusted candidates put on the Uniti per Statte list. In exchange, the judgment says, the mayor made himself available to the clan's interests, issuing public-land occupation permits to businesses traceable to Sudoso, promising public works to an associate, and dealing with the comune's contractors over street-lighting near one of them.
inside: A court found a Taranto clan controlling Statte's comune, with the mayor it helped elect granting permits and works to the clan's own businesses.
cite: Antenna Sud, 6 Jan 2026

n: Neviano ex-mayor jailed for buying fifty votes from a Coluccia clan
who: the Coluccia clan of the Sacra Corona Unita
rank: Mayor and later assessore of the comune of Neviano
d: Carabinieri arrested Antonio Megha, 64, former mayor of the comune of Neviano in Salento, on a committal order issued on 31 March 2026 by the prosecutor general at the Lecce appeal court, to serve a final sentence of nine years, eight months and 18 days for mafia-political electoral vote exchange, made definitive by the Court of Cassation on 11 March 2026. Prosecutors said he bought, at the September 2020 municipal elections, a package of at least fifty votes from the Coluccia clan of the Sacra Corona Unita, and that the votes the clan supplied proved decisive for his election and for his later post as assessore. In exchange he is said to have promised money and benefits, including sums of about 3,000 euros and personal favours, and his readiness to put the public function and the administrative apparatus at the organisation's service.
inside: A Salento clan sold a mayor the votes that elected him, and he undertook to put the comune's administration at the organisation's disposal.
cite: TRM, 10 Apr 2026

n: Trinitapoli comune dissolved over crime's hold on waste and housing
who: local organised crime in the Barletta-Andria-Trani area
rank: mayor, council and the waste, public housing and civil protection services of Trinitapoli
d: The comune of Trinitapoli was dissolved on 31 March 2022 for mafia infiltration, the first such case in the Barletta-Andria-Trani province. The decision rested on the findings of an access commission's inquiries between 2016 and 2021, which set out conditioning by local organised crime over waste, public housing and civil protection, and which led the then mayor, Emanuele Losapio, to resign. Antenna Sud reports that it was later shown that the claims about the mayor associating with a clan boss were false. Losapio, who was neither investigated nor accused but was made ineligible to stand by operation of law, says the mayor's sash was taken from him not for a judgment but for a prejudice. In March 2026 the file reached the Italian parliament's anti-mafia committee.
inside: An official inquiry found local crime groups shaping how Trinitapoli ran its waste, housing and civil protection, and the state dissolved the council.
cite: Antenna Sud, 12 Mar 2026

n: Casabona council dissolved over cosca favours; defendants then acquitted
who: the cosca dominant in the Casabona area
rank: mayor and members of the municipal administration of Casabona
d: The council of Casabona was dissolved in April 2025 after checks following the Catanzaro anti-mafia prosecutors' Nemesis operation, which in October 2024 led to ten precautionary measures involving the then mayor and other members of the municipal administration. The report attached to the decree set out alleged relations between figures on the mayor's list and the local criminal milieu, and a supposed agreement to obtain electoral support in exchange for favours. The checks also covered hirings, contract awards and alleged favours in water distribution to people close to the dominant cosca. In June 2026 the Catanzaro judge acquitted the defendants tried in the abbreviated procedure of mafia association and mafia-political vote exchange, because the fact did not exist. In August 2026 the government extended the dissolution by six months.
inside: A ministerial report said Casabona's administration gave hirings, contracts and water to a cosca's associates, but the criminal charges were then acquitted.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 5 Aug 2026

n: Badolato report found a cosca inside the council's lists and giunta
who: the local cosca, through a businessman said to belong to it
rank: mayor, deputy mayor, council president and two assessori of Badolato
d: The council of Badolato was dissolved after an inquiry by the Catanzaro anti-mafia prosecutors which in January 2025 led to 44 precautionary measures; those involved included the mayor, the deputy mayor, the president of the city council and two assessori. The ministerial report says a businessman described as belonging to the local cosca influenced the 2021 election campaign, the drawing-up of the lists and of the giunta, and some administrative decisions. The allegations concerned appointments, public works, property sales and the making permanent of a municipal police officer. The report spoke of "direct infiltration of the cosca into the political and managerial body" of the comune and of an administrative apparatus bent to interests traceable to organised crime. In August 2026 the government extended the dissolution by six months.
inside: A ministerial report found a cosca's businessman shaping Badolato's candidate lists, its council executive and decisions on jobs, works and property.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 5 Aug 2026

n: Marano di Napoli council dissolved over proven crime interference
org_label: organised crime groups, named in the decision only as "criminalità organizzata"
who: organised crime at Marano di Napoli
rank: mayor, giunta and council of Marano di Napoli
d: In September 2025 Italy's Council of Ministers, on the interior minister's proposal, dissolved the council of Marano di Napoli and handed the running of the comune to a special commission for 18 months. The government's statement said the step was taken in view of "proven interference by organised crime, which compromises the free determination and the impartiality of the local administration". At the same meeting the government extended by six months the existing dissolution of the council of Cerva, in Catanzaro province, so that the work of putting that authority right could be completed. The statement from the prime minister's office named no clan and set out no individual decision of the council. Marano di Napoli lies immediately north of Naples.
inside: Italy's government found organised crime interfering with Marano di Napoli's council so far that it removed the elected administration altogether.
cite: Anteprima24, 4 Sep 2025

n: Nuoro prison officer convicted of carrying phones for a Naples clan
rank: Assistente capo, prison police, Badu 'e Carros prison, Nuoro
d: Salvatore Deledda, a prison officer at the Badu 'e Carros high-security prison in Nuoro, took money to carry mobile telephones to inmates. Carmela Mele, sister of the jailed Vincenzo Mele and of Giuseppe Mele, head of the clan of the same name in the Pianura district of Naples, sent the parcels containing the phones, which reached Deledda, who investigators say took 200 euros for each telephone. The Nuoro prosecutors' inquiry had begun in the summer of 2022, on a tip-off, before the escape of the Gargano mafia boss Marco Raduano from the same prison on 24 February 2023. Both were arrested in April 2023. In December 2023 the Nuoro judge, in an abbreviated trial over 21 phones, gave Deledda and Carmela Mele six years and two months each, and Vincenzo Mele ten years and four months.
inside: A Naples clan family paid a prison officer, so phones reached its jailed relatives and the prison's own security controls were set aside.
cite: l'Immediato, 7 April 2023; Sardiniapost, 6 April 2023; Cagliaripad, 6 December 2023

n: Crotone police superintendent sold case secrets to 'ndrangheta clans
who: Megna clan of Papanice and other Crotone clans
rank: Sovrintendente, state police, Questura of Crotone (cabinet office)
d: Massimiliano Allevato, a superintendent of the state police who at the time worked in the cabinet office of the Crotone police headquarters, the section that coordinates the work of the other sections, passed information on coming operations to Rocco De Vona, held by prosecutors to be a senior figure in the Megna clan of Papanice. The Catanzaro anti-mafia prosecutors said he asked for money in exchange and, charging him with external participation in a mafia association, that he told clan members of matters covered by official secrecy learnt through his duties. He admitted a near-daily friendship with De Vona and two loans of 500 and 400 euros. In June 2021 the Crotone court sentenced him to eight years and two months; his lawyer announced an appeal.
inside: A Calabrian clan paid a police superintendent in the headquarters' coordinating office, so its members learnt of raids and investigations before they happened.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 16 and 20 October 2019 and 30 June 2021

n: Policeman Seby Vecchio convicted as the Serraino clan's man inside
rank: Assistente capo coordinatore, state police (railway police, Venice); former councillor and assessore, Reggio Calabria
d: Sebastiano 'Seby' Vecchio, a senior officer of the state police serving with the railway police in Venice and earlier a councillor and assessore of Reggio Calabria, was held by the Reggio anti-mafia prosecutors to be the Serraino cosca's point of reference inside the institutions. The charge in operation Pedigree said he used his police position to protect clan members and obtain confidential information about investigations under way, and his elected offices to do favours for them, with the clan supplying blocks of votes at elections. Eight collaborators spoke about him. In December 2021 the judge convicted all fifteen defendants; Vecchio received four years, ten months and twenty days. The report says he had by then become a collaborator with prosecutors.
inside: A Calabrian clan supplied votes and got a serving policeman who, prosecutors said, fed it investigation secrets and protected its members.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 15 October 2020 and 13 December 2021

n: Clan held seizure papers from an unidentified Genoa finance officer
who: Guardavalle clan and the Pesce-Bellocco-Mole clans
rank: Unidentified member of the Guardia di Finanza, Genoa
d: The Guardia di Finanza is Italy's financial and customs police. South American suppliers demanded payment for cocaine even when it was seized, but accepted an official seizure report instead, so the Calabrian groups collected police paperwork. In the flat of Emanuele Fonti, whom the Florence anti-mafia prosecutors treat as the link between the Guardavalle clan and the Pesce-Bellocco-Mole clans of the Gioia Tauro plain, investigators found at least five pages of police documents: three on the letterhead of the Livorno police mobile squad and the Customs Agency, and two seizure reports of the Guardia di Finanza of Genoa. Investigators say one was drawn up to order by an unfaithful member of that Genoa force, not yet identified, and that the group demanded 7,000 euros back from him.
inside: Investigators say a clan paid someone inside the Genoa finance police to produce official seizure papers it needed to settle debts with cocaine suppliers.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 19 November 2021 (DDA Firenze investigation)

n: Finance officer accused of warning a Piromalli clan man of an inquiry
rank: Finanziere, Guardia di Finanza (unit not named in the source)
d: In March 2023 the Carabinieri of Gioia Tauro arrested 49 people in an inquiry by the Reggio Calabria anti-mafia prosecutors into the Piromalli cosca and the Mole clan, which had come back together. Among those placed under house arrest were a finance police officer, Salvatore Tosto, and a parish priest. Tosto, together with his wife, who is among the suspects, is accused of revealing to Cosimo Romagnosi, a man of the clan and one of those arrested, that he was under investigation. The report does not say in which unit Tosto served, and does not date the alleged tip-off. The sources read do not report a trial outcome.
inside: Prosecutors say a clan had a finance police officer who told one of its men that investigators were building a case against him.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 9 March 2023

n: Orta di Atella municipal police paid to manufacture Italian passports
rank: Two municipal police officers and registry officials, comune of Orta di Atella
d: In May 2025 the Naples metropolitan police arrested eight people in an inquiry by the prosecutors at Naples North into an organisation that sold Italian passports to foreign buyers, among them Belarusian businessmen and Egyptian and Albanian traffickers wanting entry to the Schengen area. Registry officials entered invented Italian ancestors in the municipal records and municipal police officers certified checks on residences that did not exist. Those arrested include Giulio Mozzillo and Salvatore Aletto, municipal police officers of Orta di Atella, and Carmelina Del Prete, a registry official of the same comune; another registry official of Frattaminore was also arrested. Buyers paid up to 110,000 euros, and payments were traced in Bitcoin. The charges are criminal association, forgery of public documents and corruption.
inside: A document-selling organisation paid municipal police officers and registry staff, so a comune's own records and checks produced passports for its paying clients.
cite: Cronache della Campania, 14 May 2025

n: Four prison officers accused in the Camorra's drone delivery service
who: Camorra clans of Naples and its province
rank: Four officers of the prison police corps (prison not named in the source)
d: An inquiry by the Naples anti-mafia prosecutors, which led to 21 custody measures on 19 March 2023, described an organisation that used drones to drop drugs and mobile telephones into 19 prisons from Sicily and Calabria to Puglia, Campania and Piedmont, so that clan leaders could keep giving orders from high-security wings, in particular from Secondigliano prison in Naples. The price list ran from 250 euros for a basic micro-telephone to 7,000 euros for half a kilogram of drugs. Listening to the telephone calls of a prisoner's wife, investigators found four officers of the prison police who, for large payments, allegedly turned a blind eye or actively covered the deliveries. The appeal opened on 15 April 2026; at first instance 29 defendants were given close to 290 years in total.
inside: Camorra clans paid prison officers to let a drone delivery service through, so bosses in high-security wings kept phones and kept running their clans.
cite: Cronache della Campania, 8 April 2026

n: Crotone prison officer arrested over phones paid for by inmates
org_label: Inmates of Crotone prison and their relatives
who: Inmates of Crotone prison and their relatives
rank: Officer of the prison police corps, Crotone prison
d: On 18 December 2025 the state police in Crotone arrested an officer of the prison police serving at Crotone prison, on a custody order of the judge for preliminary investigations at the request of the Crotone prosecutors. After an inquiry lasting more than two years by the police mobile squad and the central operations service, he is held to be gravely suspected of corruption, revealing official secrets, forgery by a public officer and allowing detainees improper access to communication devices. Investigators say he obtained or was promised money from detainees or their relatives, helped mobile telephones into the prison, passed on information covered by official secrecy and made himself available for any service in breach of his duties. The report says he also promised families help with their court cases.
inside: Detainees and their families paid an officer inside a prison, so phones, official secrets and promised court favours flowed to them past the rules.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 18 December 2025

n: Open Gates: Catanzaro prison's governor and police commander charged
org_label: Two criminal groups formed inside Catanzaro prison
who: Two criminal groups formed inside Catanzaro prison
rank: Governor of the Ugo Caridi prison and commander of its prison police, Catanzaro
d: A note of 29 September 2021 from the Ugo Caridi prison in Catanzaro reported drug dealing inside the prison headed by a member of the prison police, named by investigators as Maurizio Corasaniti, who allegedly brought drugs in against payments to a prepaid card. The resulting inquiry by the Catanzaro anti-mafia prosecutors, operation Open Gates, described two almost overlapping associations of detainees and outsiders trading drugs, telephones and sim cards, with 48,000 euros passing through two prepaid cards between April 2021 and October 2022. In February 2024 the prison's governor, Angela Paravati, and Simona Poli, commander of its prison police from 2018 to 2022, were taken into custody; both are investigated for external participation in the association. Seventy-seven people face trial, the first hearing set for 25 November 2024. In the abbreviated procedure the Catanzaro judge convicted ten defendants on 25 June 2025, giving Corasaniti eight years and two months, and acquitted nine; an appeal followed in 2026.
inside: Criminal groups inside a prison allegedly had its governor, its police commander and officers, so drugs and phones moved as the inmates wanted.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 15 February 2024 and 31 October 2024; Corriere della Calabria, 25 June 2025 (www.corrieredellacalabria.it/2025/06/25/open-gates-droga-e-cellulari-nel-carcere-di-catanzaro-10-condanne-in-abbreviato-nomi/)

n: Dozza prison employee handed out phones for clan-linked inmates
who: Mazzarella clan and other Camorra and 'ndrangheta groups
rank: Employee of the Dozza prison in charge of inmates' extra provisions, Bologna
d: In October 2022 the Bologna police mobile squad carried out two custody orders in an inquiry into mobile telephones and drugs taken into the Dozza prison in Bologna. One was against Simone Iacomino, held to be linked to the Mazzarella clan and already a prisoner, who investigators say coordinated the deliveries, destined also for inmates linked to the Camorra and the 'ndrangheta; the other against a courier. During a search of the prison in May, when fifteen telephones were found, officers arrested a 40-year-old employee of the Dozza in charge of inmates' extra provisions, with no previous convictions, who investigators say spoke to the courier and distributed the telephones, hiding them in sacks of sugar. The closed inquiry counts more than a hundred telephones and sim cards and fifty suspects.
inside: Clan-linked inmates reached a prison employee who handed out the phones they needed, so orders kept moving out of the Bologna prison.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 14 October 2022

n: Foggia prison officer paid 500 euros to take hashish in for an inmate
org_label: Inmate of Foggia prison from Cerignola and his suppliers
who: Inmate from Cerignola and his suppliers
rank: Officer of the prison police corps, Foggia prison
d: Domenico De Bellis, an officer of the prison police at Foggia prison, was arrested after an inquiry by the Foggia prosecutors into micro-telephones and hashish taken into the prison. A confidential source warned an inspector on 14 October 2024 that drugs and telephones were about to be brought in on the officer's night shift. The custody order describes him buying 'small telephones' and unregistered sim cards in a Bari shop on 9 December 2024, two micro-telephones found under a lavatory on 14 January 2025, and 93 grams of hashish hidden in a refrigerator for an inmate from Cerignola, Pasquale Diliso, for which the officer allegedly received 500 euros. A second officer was suspended for a year. The charges are corruption and taking drugs and banned devices into prison.
inside: An inmate's network paid an officer, so untraceable phones and drugs passed the prison's own searches and reached the wings he guarded.
cite: l'Immediato, 9 October 2025

n: Carabiniere accused of taking a monthly wage from Metapontino clans
rank: Carabiniere, Bernalda station area, province of Matera
d: Michele Fico, a 49-year-old carabiniere, was arrested at Castellaneta in the province of Taranto in November 2021. During the period under investigation he served at Bernalda, in the province of Matera in Basilicata, and he was by then stationed in the province of Bari. Investigators allege that from at least September 2015 to November 2019 he received what the report calls a fixed wage from the clans of the Metapontino, about 75,000 euros over four years, and in exchange passed the group any useful information. The report says he used the money on betting and online gaming in an attempt to conceal its origin. He is under investigation for complicity with Vincenzo Porcelli, convicted and detained for drug trafficking. The report gives no outcome and records no response from him.
inside: Prosecutors say clans in Basilicata paid a serving carabiniere a regular wage, so police information they wanted flowed out to them for years.
cite: Open, 19 November 2021

n: Finance officer at the port of Bari waved cigarette loads through
org_label: Cigarette-smuggling organisation operating between eastern Europe, Greece and Italy
rank: Finanziere, Guardia di Finanza at the port of Bari
d: In January 2022 the Bari anti-mafia prosecutors obtained arrests in a case about a suspected organisation smuggling cigarettes between eastern Europe, Greece and Italy. Prosecutors say Vincenzo Azzarello, a finance police officer at the port of Bari, guaranteed the untroubled passage of vehicles carrying cigarettes: he gave the names of officers on duty, sent shift rosters by WhatsApp and let vehicles and luggage through without customs checks, telling the group 'I have to oil my friends'. Another officer pretended to accept a bribe and reported the scheme to his superiors, which led to the arrests. A transit planned for 20 September 2020, a polling day, ended with the lorries and 50,000 euros in cash seized. The charges are forgery, corruption and incitement to corrupt public officials.
inside: Smugglers paid an officer inside the port's finance police, so customs checks and patrol rosters were arranged around their cigarette lorries.
cite: il Fatto Quotidiano, 15 January 2022

n: Valle-Lampada clan kept Milan finance police officers on a payroll
rank: Three officers of the Guardia di Finanza, Milan group, operational unit for state monopolies
d: In January 2012 the Milan judge, at the anti-mafia prosecutors' request, ordered the arrest of three officers of the Guardia di Finanza's Milan group, all in the operational unit covering state monopolies: Michele Di Dio, Michele Noto and Luciano Russo. The order says they were promised and then took 40,000 to 60,000 euros a month, no less than 720,000 euros over eighteen months between 2008 and December 2009, in a case about the Valle-Lampada 'ndrangheta clan in Lombardy, whose leaders ran Milan bars and venues and were in the gambling business. At the 2014 appeal the prosecutor general sought four years for a former finance officer, Luigi Mongelli, given five years and three months at first instance, and asked that three other finanzieri acquitted of clan links be convicted.
inside: A Calabrian clan put finance police officers in Milan on a monthly payroll, so the force policing its gaming business worked for it instead.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 27 January 2012 and 30 April 2014

n: Leak on the Alvaro clan in Rome traced to a finance police unit
rank: Unidentified member of the GICO organised-crime unit of the Guardia di Finanza
d: Two conversations recorded in February 2018 between Antonio Carzo and Giulio Versace, both later arrested in operation Propaggine against the 'ndrangheta locale of the Alvaro clan in Rome, record a leak about the Carabinieri investigation into the clan. On 10 February 2018 Carzo says he has been warned that 'there is something big here with the Calabrians'. In a memorandum filed by the prosecutor general in the appeal, prosecutors say the boss Pasquale Vitalone passed the warning on and that the source was a member of the GICO, the organised-crime unit of the Guardia di Finanza, who had precise information about the Rome anti-mafia prosecutors' inquiry. Fearing arrest, Carzo moved to Calabria. The officer is not identified in the account read.
inside: Prosecutors say a clan in Rome was tipped off from inside a finance police organised-crime unit about the investigation that was closing on it.
cite: Corriere della Calabria, 5 November 2024 (Procura Generale memorandum, Propaggine appeal)

n: Xydi: police inspector convicted of serving Canicatti's mafia
who: Canicatti mafia district and the Stidda
rank: Inspector and an assistente capo of the state police; station not named in the sources read
d: On 2 February 2021 the Carabinieri ROS detained 23 people in operation Xydi, opened in 2018 by the Palermo anti-mafia prosecutors into the mafia district of Canicatti. Among them were an inspector and an assistente capo of the state police, charged with external participation in a mafia association, unlawful access to the police computer system and revealing official secrets. Bosses met in the office of the lawyer Angela Porcello, who prosecutors say carried orders out of the 41-bis high-security regime for the jailed boss Giuseppe Falsone, with the complicity of some prison officers in visiting rooms. On 11 January 2025 the Agrigento court convicted seven and acquitted two. Filippo Pitruzzella, described as a retired police inspector, got twelve years and one month for giving Porcello and her partner information.
inside: Prosecutors said Sicilian clans reached police officers and prison staff, so police records and prison visiting rooms served the bosses' own communications.
cite: LiveSicilia, 2 February 2021; Quotidiano di Ragusa, 2 February 2021; Quotidiano di Sicilia, 11 January 2025

n: Palermo policeman accused of warning a convicted mafioso of raids
who: Calogero Di Stefano, convicted of mafia association
rank: Officer of the state police, administrative section, Palermo
d: A Palermo policeman, named in the report only by his initials, is accused of passing information about arrests and checks to Calogero Di Stefano, a man convicted of mafia association. In April 2015 the prosecutor asked the court for a four-year sentence for aggravated assistance to an offender. The officer has always rejected the accusation, saying Di Stefano was his informant. What made investigators suspicious, according to the report, is that he worked in the administrative section, which does not formally deal with mafia offences, together with intercepted telephone calls, in one of which Di Stefano says 'I have one at San Lorenzo'. The sources read do not report a verdict.
inside: Prosecutors say a convicted mafioso had a policeman who told him about raids and checks, while the officer says the man was merely his informant.
cite: LiveSicilia, 14 April 2015

n: A supplier's cash reached the heads of two Romanian mechanical plants
org_label: Companies run in fact by the businessman identified as V.M.
who: Supplier companies run by a businessman
rank: Directors general of Uzina Mecanica Bucuresti SA and Uzina Mecanica Plopeni SA, and Plopeni's commercial director
d: Romania's anti-corruption prosecutors say a businessman who was the de facto administrator of several supply firms paid the heads of two mechanical plants, Uzina Mecanica Bucuresti and Uzina Mecanica Plopeni, to keep their orders coming. Between 18 December 2025 and 16 July 2026 Rafiu Mihai, director general of Uzina Mecanica Bucuresti SA, allegedly took 48,000 lei in twelve instalments over starting purchases, running the contracts and approving the firms' invoices; Pirvu Tiberiu Alexandru at Uzina Mecanica Plopeni SA allegedly took 25,900 lei and commercial director Sorescu Liliana 24,250 lei plus 3,800 US dollars from another supplier. The contracts covered maintenance, materials and services. A search of Pirvu's home found about 500,000 euros in cash, which was seized. The four were detained on 23 and 24 July 2026 and the charges are not a finding of guilt.
inside: A supplier paid the managing directors of two state arms factories, and the factories' purchasing and payment decisions then favoured his firms.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 508/I-36, 24 July 2026

n: Plopeni plant managers demanded half of a supplier's contract value
org_label: A businessman supplying cleaning products to Uzina Mecanica Plopeni
rank: Management adviser to the director general, and legal adviser, Uzina Mecanica Plopeni SA
d: Uzina Mecanica Plopeni SA is a Romanian mechanical plant whose purchases the prosecutors examined. Prosecutors say that in April 2022 Bratu Marian, then adviser in management to the factory's director general and later its commercial director, helped by legal adviser Oprisenescu Claudia, demanded from a businessman half the value of a cleaning-products contract of about 60,000 lei and half the value of future contracts, in return for using his influence with the director general to approve a payment, issue promissory notes and keep the factory's business with the businessman's firm. He allegedly received 8,500 euros, 7,000 lei and thirteen lamb carcasses worth about 6,000 lei. Both were sent for trial in December 2022; the businessman is a witness.
inside: A supplier's money and goods went to senior staff inside a state arms factory so that its payments and future orders stayed with his firm.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 1156/VIII/3, 27 December 2022

n: Caransebes hospital manager promised 250,000 lei by a repairs contractor
org_label: A construction company whose administrator is identified as D.I.
rank: Manager, Caransebes Municipal Emergency Hospital
d: Prosecutors say that on 4 May 2025 Singh Bhupinder, manager of the Caransebes Municipal Emergency Hospital in western Romania, accepted a promise of 250,000 lei, directly and for himself, from the administrator of a company, in return for an act within his duties: awarding that company a public contract by direct purchase, for repair works on the hospital's sixth floor worth 900,400 lei before VAT. Both men were investigated from 19 September 2025, the manager was detained for 24 hours and a court in Timis ordered him held for 30 days. Romania's anti-corruption directorate notes that starting a prosecution does not displace the presumption of innocence.
inside: A building firm's promised payment reached the manager who awards hospital contracts, and the repair job was handed to that firm directly.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 536/VIII/3, 19 September 2025

n: Cernavoda hospital's administrative chief took 366,870 lei from a contractor
org_label: Three companies run by the businessman identified as M.E.
rank: Head of the administrative service, Cernavoda Town Hospital
d: Cocor Laura Iuliana, head of the administrative service at the town hospital in Cernavoda in south-eastern Romania, was sent for trial in July 2025 for taking bribes in 42 separate acts. Prosecutors say that between October 2021 and January 2025 she demanded and received 366,870 lei, for herself and others, from M.E., who administers three companies, in connection with signing public procurement contracts and paying them. In January 2025 she allegedly asked for 30,000 euros over a contract to refurbish the operating block and intensive-care unit, and on 10 February 2025 received 15,000 euros, which reached the hospital's manager, Sponoche Marius Ion. The businessman admitted the facts and agreed a two-year suspended sentence.
inside: A contractor's payments went to the hospital officer who signed and paid its contracts, and the hospital's purchases then went his way.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press bulletin no. 480/VIII/3, 7 August 2025

n: Botezatu Construct convicted of paying Bacau hospital's supply chief
rank: Head of the technical, administrative and supply service, and an economist, Bacau Pneumophthisiology Hospital
d: The Bacau Court of Appeal, in criminal decision 745 of 9 October 2025, convicted Alexa Dragos-Constantin, head of the technical, administrative and supply service at the Bacau Pneumophthisiology Hospital, and Pralea Doru-Ion, an economist there, of taking a bribe, giving each two years' imprisonment suspended for four years. The company SC Botezatu Construct SRL was fined 60,000 lei and ordered to display the judgment for three months for giving bribes, and its administrator received one year and four months, suspended. The indictment said that in November 2023, during a contract for maintenance and cleaning work in the hospital's basement and kitchen block, the two officials asked the administrator for 20,000 lei to sign off the works, pay the invoices quickly and buy further work from him.
inside: A building firm paid the hospital staff who accept its work and release its invoices, and the hospital kept signing and paying.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), conviction notice on Bacau Court of Appeal decision 745/09.10.2025; DNA press release no. 328/VIII/3, 29 March 2024

n: Railway hospital manager took a tenth of suppliers' invoices in Bucharest
org_label: Companies supplying the Bucharest railway clinical hospital
rank: Manager, Clinical Hospital CF no. 2, Bucharest
d: Bucur Serban, manager of Clinical Hospital CF no. 2 in Bucharest, a hospital in Romania's railway health network, was convicted on 12 November 2024 by the Bucharest Tribunal on a guilty-plea agreement and given three years' imprisonment suspended for four, final on 31 December 2024. Prosecutors said that between December 2019 and June 2024 he demanded and received about 764,370 lei from representatives of companies under contract to the hospital, amounting to between 5 and 10 per cent of the invoices the hospital paid, in 146 separate acts, usually cash in an envelope handed over in his office. The contracts covered patients' meals, repairs to electrical, plumbing and heating systems, ward refurbishment, online appointment software, sterile sets, gowns and cleaning products. Four company representatives also admitted giving bribes.
inside: Suppliers paid the hospital manager a share of every invoice, and the hospital's contracts and payments kept flowing to them.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 784/VIII/3, 24 October 2024, and conviction notice on Bucharest Tribunal sentence 1385/12.11.2024

n: Amrita Com kept Brasov hospital's catering after a tender was cancelled
rank: Financial director and head of the public procurement service, Brasov County Emergency Clinical Hospital
d: Prosecutors sent for trial in July 2025 the former financial director of the Brasov County Emergency Clinical Hospital, Barra Floare, its procurement chief Stoica Ovidiu Mihnea, the catering company SC Amrita Com SRL and the company's general director. The indictment says that between November 2020 and June 2021 Barra Floare performed her duties improperly and pushed her subordinate to breach his, supporting an unlawful tender for catering for the hospital's inpatients so as to favour Amrita Com, which won it. In 2020, after the earlier framework agreement with the company expired, the two allegedly delayed a new tender while the company carried on supplying under short contracts, then cancelled the competitive procedure by agreement with its representative. Charges are not a finding of guilt.
inside: A catering firm's representative worked with the hospital's finance and buying chiefs, and the hospital's tender was shaped and cancelled to keep his contract.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 394/VIII/3, 1 July 2025

n: Hidraconstruct Geovig paid the land-improvement branch director in Galati
rank: Service head, then director, Galati territorial branch of the National Land Improvement Agency
d: The National Land Improvement Agency is the Romanian state body that runs irrigation and drainage works. Prosecutors sent for trial in April 2024 Danaila Sorin, head of service and then director of its Galati territorial branch, for taking a bribe, together with the de facto administrator of SC Hidraconstruct Geovig SRL and the company itself for giving one. The indictment says that between 19 May and 30 September 2021 Danaila accepted and received 134,821 lei, disguised as payments between two companies the men controlled, after making sure the branch awarded Hidraconstruct Geovig several maintenance and repair contracts by negotiation without publishing a tender notice, approved its invoices, and passed the businessman planning documents that were not public. Charges are not a finding of guilt.
inside: A works firm paid the state agency's branch director, who then awarded it contracts without a tender and approved its bills.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 424/VIII/3, 29 April 2024

n: Otopeni airport's shop concessions and a facilities director's 15,000 euros
org_label: A company operating retail space at Otopeni airport
rank: Director of airport facilities management, and former director general, Bucharest Airports National Company
d: The Bucharest Airports National Company runs Romania's main airport at Otopeni. Prosecutors say that between 29 December 2021 and 1 February 2023 Litoi Bogdan-Serban, director of its airport facilities management directorate, received 15,000 euros through an intermediary from an associate of a company with retail space at the airport, in return for delaying by four months the approval of tender papers for a consultancy contract. In the same case a man with no official post allegedly demanded 10,000,000 euros twice and 1,200,000 euros twice from the retail operator and another company, claiming he could get the transport minister and the company's director general to extend their shop contracts, and a former director general allegedly handed a rival the tender papers before publication. Charges are not a finding of guilt.
inside: Airport shop operators paid men inside the state airport company, whose approvals and tender papers were then timed to suit them.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 360/VIII/3, 29 March 2023

n: Holidays for the head of Romania's boiler inspection company
org_label: Two companies represented by the same person
rank: Director general, National Company for the Control of Boilers, Lifting Equipment and Pressure Vessels (CNCIR SA)
d: CNCIR SA is the Romanian state company that inspects boilers, lifting equipment and pressure vessels. Prosecutors sent its former director general Timofte Ioana for trial in October 2025 for taking bribes in ten separate acts, with six other defendants from the company and her circle charged with instigating or assisting. The indictment says she signed professional training contracts unlawfully with two companies and, for signing them and promising more, demanded and received between 2021 and 2023 ten holidays worth 586,492 lei and 39,707 euros in Greece, Spain, Italy and Turkey, for herself and others. The trips were dressed up as training courses abroad for CNCIR staff and paid out of the company's own budget. Charges are not a finding of guilt.
inside: A training supplier gave the state inspection company's director general holidays, and she signed its contracts and promised it more work.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 710/VIII/3, 20 October 2025

n: Quarry firm paid the Arad water management director to call off checks
rank: Director, Arad Water Management System, Mures River Basin Administration
d: The Arad water management system, part of the Mures River Basin Administration in Romania's state water authority, can order inspections of extraction companies and can have their extraction contracts terminated. Prosecutors say that on 24 August and 3 October 2022 its director, Parpala Caius Mihai, received 8,000 lei in total, through an intermediary and directly, from the administrator of a company working in mineral aggregate extraction, so that he would support the company by not ordering inspections able to find, stop and penalise its allegedly illegal activities, and by preventing its extraction contracts from being terminated. In March 2023 the case went to court on a guilty-plea agreement in which he admitted the facts and accepted three years' imprisonment, suspended.
inside: A quarrying company paid the state water body's local director, who then kept inspectors away and its extraction contracts alive.
cite: Direcția Națională Anticorupție (Romania), press release no. 300/VIII/3, 14 March 2023, and no. 912/VIII/3, 25 October 2022

n: Intratrek's $10,000 reached the Zimbabwe Power Company board chairman
rank: Board chairman, Zimbabwe Power Company
d: Zimbabwe Power Company generates electricity for the state utility ZESA. On 21 January 2016 its board chairman, Stanley Kazhanje, received US$10,000 into his personal bank account from the account of Intratrek Zimbabwe, the company of businessman Wicknell Chivayo that held the 100-megawatt Gwanda solar contract. A Harare magistrate convicted Kazhanje in September 2019 of concealing the transaction from his principals and jailed him for three years, two of them suspended; the court heard he failed to declare his interest and then chaired a meeting at which the company resolved to pay Intratrek's subcontractors rather than terminate the contract, and the utility paid further advances. In 2021 a second prosecution of him on the same facts was stopped as double jeopardy. Chivayo denied bribery, saying the transfer predated the appointment and paid for professional services. On 29 September 2021 a Harare magistrate, Ngoni Nduna, acquitted Chivayo and his company, ruling that the state had failed to establish a prima facie case and that Kazhanje had done consultancy work for them before becoming board chairman.
inside: A contractor's money reached the chairman of the state power company's board, which then kept paying the contractor instead of cancelling.
cite: NewZimbabwe.com, 2 September 2019 and 8 May 2021; NewZimbabwe.com, 'Chivayo off the hook in bribery saga', 30 September 2021 (www.newzimbabwe.com/chivayo-off-the-hook-in-bribery-saga/)

n: Cigarette smuggling group paid Ukraine's border guard chief for 68 crossings
rank: Former Head of the State Border Guard Service (a general)
d: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau said on 22 January 2026 that it had charged three people over cigarette smuggling into the European Union: the former head of the State Border Guard Service, a general, a checkpoint unit head, and a former official. A group organised the smuggling in 2023 and senior officials of the service allegedly facilitated it for regular benefits. Between July and November 2023 border guards allegedly received at least 204,000 euros for 68 vehicles. Those cars carried plates resembling diplomatic ones and their passengers held diplomatic passports, so they crossed uninspected. The Kyiv Independent reported that sources identified the former head as Serhiy Deineko, who led the service from 2019 until January 2026, and that he did not respond to a request for comment.
inside: Prosecutors say a smuggling group paid the head of Ukraine's border guard service, whose officers then waved its cigarette convoys through unchecked.
cite: NABU and SAPO release, 22 January 2026; Kyiv Independent, 22 January 2026; NABU report for the first half of 2026

n: Forged UN letters moved 76 conscripts out through the border service
org_label: Conscript-smuggling ring run by a border service lieutenant colonel and his cousin
rank: Lieutenant colonel, State Border Guard Service of Ukraine
d: Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office says a lieutenant colonel of the State Border Guard Service and his cousin, a Russian citizen, ran a scheme moving men liable for military service out of the country. From May 2024 they produced forged petition letters made to look as if they came from the International Organization for Migration's office in Ukraine, sent them to the border service's administration and used them at crossings, so departures appeared lawful. About 76 conscripted men left by April 2025 at roughly 20,000 US dollars a person, part paid in cryptocurrency. Charges include illegal smuggling of persons across the state border and document forgery. The officer was suspended and the indictment went to court on 15 June 2026; his cousin is being sought separately.
inside: Prosecutors say a smuggling ring worked through a serving border officer, who fed forged United Nations letterheads into his own service's system for paying clients.
cite: Interfax-Ukraine citing the Office of the Prosecutor General, 15 June 2026; UNN citing the Prosecutor General's Office, 4 February 2026

n: Criminal organisation ran clearances at Ukraine's Volyn customs
org_label: Criminal organisation led by Oleksandr Hromyk, a former SBU employee
rank: Ten officials of Volyn Customs, including officers of the Yahodyn checkpoint
d: On 8 November 2023 Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and anti-corruption prosecutors, helped by Poland's Central Anti-Corruption Bureau, exposed a criminal organisation working inside Volyn Customs, the customs office on the Polish border. The group moved phones, computer equipment and branded clothing through the Yahodyn crossing hidden behind cheaper cover items; officials cleared the goods without proper checks, filed false inspection reports and entered false data in the Inspector clearance system. The state lost more than 475 million hryvnia. In March 2025 prosecutors sent 21 people to court, ten of them customs officials. Slovo i Dilo names the organiser as Oleksandr Hromyk, a former Security Service employee. In July 2026 the High Anti-Corruption Court approved a plea deal with one middle-ranking member.
inside: A criminal organisation run from outside customs had ten of its officials clearing its hidden cargo and falsifying the inspection records meant to catch it.
cite: Slovo i Dilo, 20 March 2025 (www.slovoidilo.ua/2025/03/20/novyna/ekonomika/sap-skeruvala-sudu-spravu-pro-zlochynnu-orhanizacziyu-volynskij-mytnyczi); NABU and SAPO release, 9 November 2023 (nabu.gov.ua/en/news/zlochinna-organ-zatc-ia-na-volins-k-i-mitnitc-10-p-dozriuvanikh/); Slovo i Dilo, 31 July 2026

n: Chernivtsi recruitment centre soldier sold blank call-up papers at $150 each
rank: Soldier of a Territorial Centre for Recruitment and Social Support, Chernivtsi, in its military registration and reservation department
d: A soldier of a Territorial Centre for Recruitment and Social Support in Chernivtsi, the offices that run Ukraine's call-up, who had been moved from its guard company to its military registration and reservation department, took unaccounted blank summonses and filled them in with names for money. A man holding such a summons could not be given a new one by recruitment patrols for about a month. The verdict says the criminal intent arose in spring 2023. He asked 150 US dollars a summons and the same for each renewal. A discharged former serviceman who was offered the scheme reported it to police, who detained him as he took the money. The Shevchenkivskyi District Court of Chernivtsi convicted him of receiving an improper benefit after a guilty plea and fined him 8,500 hryvnia. The verdict could be appealed.
inside: Men trying to dodge call-up paid a recruitment centre soldier, who issued them its own paperwork so its patrols would leave them alone.
cite: Zaxid.net, 16 December 2024

n: Dentist and recruitment officer took $10,000 for an unfitness ruling
org_label: Private dentist acting for a man seeking exemption
rank: Specialist, mobilisation department of a Territorial Centre for Recruitment and Social Support
d: A dentist at the CityDent clinic in Khmelnytskyi met a man liable for call-up while treating his teeth. The man asked about getting out of service, so the dentist approached a specialist in the mobilisation department of a Territorial Centre for Recruitment and Social Support, the offices that run Ukraine's call-up. They agreed to obtain a military medical commission finding of unfitness and removal from military registration in return for money. On 2 February 2024 the dentist offered to arrange it for 10,000 US dollars, repeating the offer on 20 February, by which time the man was acting under law enforcement control. No money was paid and the charge was an attempt. On 28 July 2026 the Khmelnytskyi City-District Court fined each 68,000 hryvnia; appeal is still possible.
inside: A private dentist was the way in to a recruitment centre, where an official agreed to produce the unfitness paperwork his paying client wanted.
cite: Zaxid.net, reporting the Khmelnytskyi City-District Court verdict of 28 July 2026

n: Pavlohrad drug gang of 13 included serving and former police officers
rank: Police officers in leadership posts, Pavlohrad; a former first deputy head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional police
d: In November 2021 Ukraine's State Bureau of Investigation said it had dismantled a gang of 13 people in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region, that had operated under police cover, its members including serving and former police officers. The bureau said the gang held a monopoly on making and selling drugs in the city, with officers in leadership posts clearing out competitors, and earned about 100,000 hryvnia a week. The bureau said the business was organised by a man born in Georgia, a Dnipro resident and a former first deputy head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional police; the last allegedly advised on concealment and on police documenting plans and passed part of the profits to serving officers through an intermediary. Investigators said members sold to minors. Nine people were detained. The report named no charges and no court stage.
inside: The State Bureau of Investigation says a drug gang held the local police from inside, with officers in command posts clearing rivals out of its market.
cite: LIGA.net citing the State Bureau of Investigation press service, 23 November 2021

n: Chernivtsi police unit head jailed over a draft-evasion case bribe
rank: Former head of a structural unit, Police Main Directorate in Chernivtsi Oblast
d: Investigators alleged that the head of a structural unit of the police Main Directorate in Chernivtsi Oblast demanded 40,000 euros from a local woman in return for not prosecuting her and closing a case about draft evaders. They recorded the first 10,000 euros changing hands and arrested him as he took the second instalment. The Security Service of Ukraine and the State Bureau of Investigation detained him on 25 July 2023 and the case went to trial in March 2024. Investigators suspected he was only an intermediary and was to pass the money to unidentified officials in the investigative unit. On 19 August 2025 the High Anti-Corruption Court convicted him of abetting bribery and fraud, imposing seven years with confiscation of all his property. The verdict was not yet final.
inside: Money from a suspect in a draft-evasion case reached a senior Chernivtsi police officer, who was to have that case closed for her.
cite: Slovo i Dilo citing the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office, 19 August 2025

n: Two Ukrainian border inspectors ran a $7,000 route for draft-age men
org_label: Illegal border crossing scheme with two local recruiters
rank: Two border service inspectors, Ivano-Frankivsk region
d: The State Border Guard Service's press office said in November 2024 that two of its inspectors in the Ivano-Frankivsk region, in western Ukraine, had been detained for organising an illegal scheme to move men of call-up age out of the country. Two local residents were brought in to find the men and guide them to the border, while the inspectors provided cover. Clients were charged 6,000 to 7,000 US dollars a person. Searches turned up tens of thousands of dollars, about 5,000 euros and 100,000 hryvnia. The suspects face three to nine years under the article of the criminal code on illegal transfer of persons across the state border. The report records the detentions only, with no court hearing or verdict.
inside: A crossing scheme with civilian recruiters worked through two serving border inspectors, whose patrol cover let paying clients leave the country unrecorded.
cite: Ukrinform citing the State Border Guard Service press office, 14 November 2024

n: Six officers at Romania's Sculeni crossing charged over excise smuggling
org_label: Eleven transporters carrying excise goods from Moldova
rank: Two customs inspectors and four border police agents, Sculeni border crossing point
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent to the Iasi Tribunal a case against six officials of the Sculeni border crossing point, in Iasi county on the border with Moldova: two customs inspectors and four border police agents. Between July and November 2023 they allegedly let parcels of excise goods, including cigarettes, alcohol and food, pass from Moldova into the European Union without taking the measures required, causing significant losses to the state budget. Bribes allegedly ran from 70 to 700 euros a transport. On 4 August 2023 one agent allegedly took 200 euros to let a coach through, part of it allegedly passed to the head of the crossing point, who the report does not say is charged. Eleven transporters with no official status are accused of giving bribes.
inside: Prosecutors say hauliers paid customs and border police officers at one crossing, who then let their untaxed cargo into the European Union unchecked.
cite: BZI citing the National Anticorruption Directorate indictment, 23 December 2024

n: Romanian border and customs officers held over three smuggling groups
org_label: Three organised criminal groups smuggling from Ukraine
rank: Two border police officers and three customs agents
d: Prosecutors of Romania's organised crime directorate, DIICOT, detained seven people between 8 and 9 May 2026, among them two border police officers and three customs agents, after 137 searches. They identified three organised criminal groups active in 2024 and 2025 that allegedly smuggled cigarettes and toxic substances from Ukraine into Romania with help from officials at border control; one example cited is 400 litres of pesticides banned in the European Union brought in from Ukraine in October 2025, the officials running that border control carrying out only a formal check. Seizures included 155,920 cigarettes, pesticides, rodenticides, other goods and large sums of money. Five more people were placed under judicial control. The case is run by DIICOT's Suceava territorial service, and the crossing named for the pesticides is Siret, on the Ukrainian border. The release describes detentions and searches and mentions no court proceedings.
inside: Prosecutors say three smuggling groups had border police and customs officers inside the checks, who let their cigarettes and pesticides cross from Ukraine.
cite: DIICOT release of 10 May 2026, as carried by Digi24 (www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/doi-politisti-de-frontiera-si-trei-vamesi-retinuti-intr-un-dosar-care-vizeaza-grupari-ce-aduceau-produse-de-contrabanda-din-ucraina-3763985); also reported by Agerpres, 10 May 2026 (not opened)

n: Giurgiulesti customs officers falsified cargo papers for cash
rank: Two customs officers, Giurgiulesti border checkpoint
d: Radio Moldova reported on 29 January 2026 a criminal investigation into two customs officers at the Giurgiulesti border checkpoint, where Moldova meets Romania and Ukraine. They are suspected of demanding and accepting bribes of 50 to 500 US dollars from international transporters to speed up customs clearance, and in return falsifying cargo manifests by misreporting the type and volume of goods. Investigators had monitored them since October 2024. Leaked transcripts of intercepted calls show negotiations over service fees: in one exchange an officer first asked for 200 euros, about 3,920 lei, and settled for 150 after the transporter objected. The report does not name the officers or give the specific charges, and the case is at the investigation stage.
inside: Hauliers paid two customs officers, who in return wrote false descriptions of their cargo into Moldova's own clearance paperwork.
cite: Radio Moldova, 29 January 2026

n: Cahul border police officers charged in a cigarette smuggling group
rank: Former interim chief of Border Police Sector Cahul; former head of the SOUTH Regional Directorate; a non-commissioned officer
d: Moldova's Security and Intelligence Service said in January 2022 that prosecutors for organised crime had sent to court a case over the smuggling of 179 boxes of Ashima cigarettes through Cahul, in southern Moldova, whose intended destination was the European market. Fourteen people aged 30 to 50, from Cahul and Chisinau, are accused. Three are Border Police officers: a former interim chief of the Border Police Sector Cahul, a former head of the SOUTH Regional Directorate, and a non-commissioned officer. Experts valued the cigarettes at about 1.6 million lei on the Moldovan market and 4.3 million on the European market, with illegal income of about 2.7 million lei. The investigation involved more than 20 searches and more than 20 interceptions. No verdict is reported, and suspects are presumed innocent.
inside: A cigarette smuggling group counted serving and former border police commanders among its members, so the force guarding the border covered its cargo.
cite: Security and Intelligence Service of Moldova release, 31 January 2022

n: Thirteen Lithuanian officers tipped off balloon cigarette smugglers
org_label: Organised groups flying cigarettes in by weather balloon
rank: Three State Border Guard Service officers, including two shift supervisors; ten police officers, eight of them patrolmen of the Salcininkai district commissariat
d: Lithuanian police said on 22 May 2026 that 27 people had been detained in the previous week, 13 of them officials. They are three officers of the State Border Guard Service, including two shift supervisors, eight patrolmen of the Salcininkai district commissariat, an investigator of a Vilnius city commissariat and a senior investigator of the Vilnius County Chief Police Commissariat, plus a municipal utilities specialist. The officials allegedly gave smugglers sensitive operational information. Organised groups used weather balloons to carry cigarettes, tracking landing points by GPS and encrypted communication. Charges include smuggling, criminal association and aiding a foreign state in activities against Lithuania. Police made 74 searches and seized assets worth 4.2 million euros. The pre-trial investigation has 49 suspects; the officers were suspended.
inside: Smuggling groups had police officers and border guards feeding them operational information, so the patrols meant to intercept their cargo knew nothing useful.
cite: LRT English citing Lithuanian police and the chief prosecutor of the Organised Crime and Corruption Investigation Department, 22 May 2026

n: Seven senior customs supervisors at Latvia's Terehova post jailed for bribes
org_label: Drivers crossing the Latvian customs border
rank: Seven senior customs supervisors, Terehova customs control point
d: Seven senior customs supervisors at the Terehova customs control point, on Latvia's border with Russia, were convicted of taking bribes. Between 24 December 2020 and 7 April 2021 the group, acting by prior agreement, systematically accepted cash from drivers crossing Latvia's customs territory, the payments turning on whether they carried out their official duties. They hid the cash in their uniforms and in a locker cache, then split it after shifts. The charged total was 1,615 euros and 500 Russian roubles: the prosecution says the evidence suggested considerably larger sums, but charges used the minimum for each episode, except in individual cases where larger sums were clearly recorded. The Economic Cases Court convicted them on 13 April 2023, giving three years six months to five years in prison. On 16 December 2025 the Supreme Court refused cassation, so the judgment took effect.
inside: Lorry drivers paid senior customs supervisors at one crossing, who then decided whether to carry out the checks their posts required.
cite: LV portals, publishing the Prosecutor's Office statement, 18 December 2025

n: Narva customs inspector let a cigarette smuggler through 14 times
rank: Customs inspector and shift manager, Tax and Customs Board, Narva border crossing point
d: Konstantin Tsernilovski, a customs inspector and shift manager of Estonia's Tax and Customs Board at the Narva crossing point on the Russian border, was convicted of bribery. Maksim Koltsov, who transported the cigarettes, agreed with him that the men would cross without inspection or with only a sham inspection; in return Tsernilovski received cigarettes and narcotic substances. The smuggling ran from spring 2019 to May 2020, and the bribed crossings happened on at least 14 occasions between October 2019 and May 2020. Viru County Court convicted both, as reported on 26 June 2020. Tsernilovski received two and a half years, three months of it served immediately; Koltsov received a combined three years. The article does not say whether the verdicts are final.
inside: A cigarette smuggler paid a customs shift manager in goods, and the inspections at his crossing became sham inspections for that smuggler's runs.
cite: ERR News, 26 June 2020, reporting the Viru County Court verdict

n: Fifty border police at Hungary's Zahony crossing convicted of bribes
org_label: Smugglers of tobacco, fuel and alcohol across the Ukrainian border
rank: Border police and excise guards at the Zahony crossing, all of them subordinates
d: Fifty-one border police at Zahony, Hungary's crossing on the Ukrainian border, were charged with accepting bribes on the job as part of a criminal organisation, and the Military Council of the Capital Court convicted 50 of them, finding that 38 committed corruption offences as part of a criminal organisation. The guards, whom the report also calls excise guards, colluded in smuggling by letting tobacco products, fuel and alcohol cross the border illegally in commercial quantities, and took cash, cigarettes and drinks in return; the report gives no amounts and does not name who paid them. The suspects were arrested on 29 July 2015. Forty received prison terms and ten probation. All but one lieutenant were dismissed.
inside: Smugglers bought the staff of one border crossing in bulk, and a court found the officers there acted as part of a criminal organisation.
cite: XpatLoop, 12 July 2019, reporting the Military Council of the Capital Court

n: Slovak crime agency operative leaked raid plans to businessman Peter Petrov
org_label: Peter Petrov, a businessman with ties to organised crime
rank: Operative, National Crime Agency (NAKA)
d: Jan Kalavsky, an operative of Slovakia's National Crime Agency, NAKA, which has since been dissolved, was convicted of leaking police material. The businessman Peter Petrov, known as Tiger, allegedly paid him for inside information about coming police raids, providing money for a Range Rover, a mobile phone and home renovations; the report gives no amounts. The Slovak Spectator says Petrov was involved in economic crimes and had ties to organised crime, and that Kalavsky also tipped off a former police officer now a convicted criminal. He was first charged in May 2021, charges were dismissed within weeks, and a new prosecutor indicted him in early 2022. On 4 March 2025 an appellate court upheld his conviction and imposed five years and a 5,000 euro fine.
inside: A businessman tied to organised crime paid an officer inside Slovakia's crime agency, who told him which police raids were coming so they could be avoided.
cite: The Slovak Spectator, 4 March 2025

n: Operation Genesis: Ceara military police sold a drug gang rivals' secrets
org_label: an unnamed drug trafficking gang in Ceará
rank: Military police officers, Ceará state
d: On 2 February 2023 seventeen members of Ceará state's military police and fourteen suspected drug traffickers were detained in the latest round of Operation Genesis, a long-running operation in north-east Brazil aimed at dismantling corruption inside the police. The Ceará Attorney General's Office said the detained officers were allegedly bribed by a drug trafficking gang for "privileged information" on its criminal rivals, which allowed the gang to dominate the drug trade in parts of the state capital, Fortaleza, and in the municipalities of Caucaia, Pacatuba and Maranguape. The release also stated that the officers sold weapons and ammunition they had seized from criminals. Since the operation began in 2016, at least 63 military police officers have faced charges of drug trafficking, robbery, weapons trafficking and criminal association.
inside: A drug gang allegedly paid Ceará military police for intelligence on its rivals, so a state police force's own files served one trafficking group.
cite: InSight Crime, 14 February 2023, citing a press release by the Ceará Attorney General's Office

n: Sao Paulo narcotics police asked the PCC for R$1m to close its man's case
rank: Officers of the 4th precinct of the narcotics investigation division (Dise), Denarc, São Paulo civil police
d: Three officers of the 4th precinct of the narcotics investigation division (Dise) of Denarc, São Paulo state's civil police drug department, are accused of demanding a million reais to close a police inquiry and so spare a member of the Primeiro Comando da Capital from investigation. The PCC is Brazil's largest prison-born criminal organisation. A video recovered from a seized phone shows investigator Murilo Muniz, agent Alan Fernandes Dias and Wander Tadeu de Araujo talking to Ademilson Alves de Brito, lawyer to Wagner Nascimento de Souza, alias "Costurado", described as handling the group's financial logistics. The prosecution service says it shelved the inquiry for lack of evidence after the civil police's final report. Two officers and the lawyer were held on 10 December 2025 in Operation Mata-Nota; prosecutors said the arrest of Araujo, the third officer, was not needed for now, and his defence denied any involvement in unlawful practices. The defence of the others could not be reached.
inside: Prosecutors say a faction's lawyer was asked for a million reais by narcotics police, and the inquiry into his client was then shelved.
cite: Metrópoles, 10 December 2025, citing the São Paulo public prosecution service's application (MPSP) and Gaeco

n: Operation Infiltrados: Campinas drug-squad chief held as a PCC insider
rank: Chief of investigators, narcotics investigations unit (Dise), Campinas civil police
d: On 9 June 2026 prosecutors in São Paulo state arrested Maurício Aparecido de Oliveira, then chief of investigators at the Campinas narcotics investigations unit (Dise) of the civil police, with an expelled former civil police officer and a former intern of the prosecution service, as suspected insiders for the Primeiro Comando da Capital. The prosecution service says that a week before the 2025 operation that foiled a plot to kill Gaeco prosecutor Amauri Silveira Filho, one of the main suspects in that plot met Oliveira, and seized videos recorded the meeting; it suspects material from the two investigations he was handling reached the faction. A prison officer is also under investigation.
inside: Prosecutors say the faction had its own people inside a drug squad and a prosecutor's office, giving it the secrets of investigations aimed at it.
cite: Correio da Manhã (Campinas), 9 June 2026, citing Gaeco and the São Paulo public prosecution service

n: Guarulhos prison officers ran a price list for phones, drugs and visits
org_label: detainees of the CDP II Guarulhos and their families
rank: Prison officers (policiais penais), Centro de Detenção Provisória II, Guarulhos
d: An investigation by the São Paulo public prosecution service found what its organised-crime unit, Gaeco, describes as a price list for banned goods at the CDP II provisional detention centre in Guarulhos, outside São Paulo. Prison officers are suspected of charging to let in mobile phones, drugs, alcohol and sex workers, in a scheme estimated to have moved up to 1.6 million reais. Federal police and Gaeco served sixteen arrest warrants on 10 November 2026 and six prison officers were held. Prosecutors have asked for the conviction of officer Vinícius Freitas Silva for passive corruption. Those investigated denied taking part, and the officer said he received no undue advantage and facilitated nothing.
inside: Prisoners' money allegedly bought prison officers' decisions, so a detention centre's own staff carried in the phones and drugs their inmates wanted.
cite: Correio da Manhã, 11 November 2026, citing the São Paulo public prosecution service (MP-SP), Gaeco and the federal police

n: Mato Grosso do Sul prison officer ran system checks for a PCC-linked boss
who: a faction linked to the PCC
rank: Prison officer, Agência Estadual de Administração do Sistema Penitenciário (Agepen), Mato Grosso do Sul
d: Jonathas Wilson Moraes Cândido, a serving officer of Mato Grosso do Sul's prison agency Agepen, was a target of Operation Blindspot, which broke up one of the state's largest interstate trafficking structures. Prosecutors' organised-crime unit Gaeco found that in December 2022 Edimilson Santos Pereira, whom it names as a boss of a faction linked to the Primeiro Comando da Capital, asked the officer for a restricted database check on a prisoner who owed him 300,000 reais; on 13 December the officer sent a photograph of the official screen. He had already been held in March 2022 over a scheme selling favours to PCC detainees; the Superior Court of Justice ruled that detention unlawful and he was released, with no final judgment. He remains in post.
inside: A faction boss used a serving prison officer as his own clerk inside the prison service, getting sealed records, plate checks and warnings about operations.
cite: Campo Grande News, 10 July 2025, citing Gaeco and the Mato Grosso do Sul public prosecution service

n: Ecuador's police chief Varela accused of shielding trafficker Gjika
rank: General, head of Ecuador's National Police
d: Tannya Varela headed Ecuador's National Police between March 2021 and January 2022 and is under investigation by Ecuador's prosecutor in relation to Dritan Gjika, the Albanian businessman accused of leading a network that shipped tons of cocaine from Colombia through Ecuador to Europe. Authorities say Varela was his most important contact. Ecuadorian lawmakers alleged she began working with him when she was posted at an airport in Guayas province, and believe she supposedly helped him by placing trusted officers in key locations. In mid-2021 the anti-narcotics police opened an investigation naming Gjika; Varela appears to have saved them from prosecution, taking the investigators off the case in September 2021 and reassigning them, and the case was closed in January 2022. Varela denied the allegations connecting her to the criminal structure.
inside: Prosecutors say a trafficking network reached the head of Ecuador's police, whose postings and case decisions then protected it from its own anti-drug officers.
cite: InSight Crime, 4 July 2024, citing Ecuadorian and Spanish police, Ecuadorian lawmakers and prosecutor Diana Salazar

n: Ecuador general over prisons and anti-narcotics convicted in Norero case
rank: General; head of the prison authority and of the police anti-narcotics unit
d: General Pablo Ramírez headed both Ecuador's prison authority and the national police's anti-narcotics unit before his conviction on charges of collaborating with organised crime. Evidence of corruption at that level emerged after the death in 2022 of Leandro Norero, one of Ecuador's most prominent drug traffickers; Norero's communications showed that he maintained connections with a number of high-level officials, Ramírez among them. The United States ambassador to Ecuador had spoken out in 2021 against the presence of "narco generals" in the police force, and the US government later revoked the visas of at least three senior police officials it believed were linked to organised crime. Ecuador's government has since expanded police powers without adding measures against criminal infiltration of the security forces.
inside: A trafficker's contacts reached the general running Ecuador's prisons and anti-drug police, and he was convicted of collaborating with organised crime.
cite: InSight Crime, 12 June 2025, citing Ecuavisa, Primicias and the conviction of General Pablo Ramírez

n: Ecuadorian sailors suspected of arming the Choneros and Chone Killers
who: Los Choneros and the Chone Killers
rank: Sailors and officers, Ecuadorian Navy
d: Intelligence reports cited by the Ecuadorian newspaper Primicias showed that at least 43 sailors of Ecuador's navy were under investigation for offences including gang involvement and drug trafficking. Thirteen were suspected of providing arms to some of Ecuador's deadliest gangs, among them Los Choneros and the Chone Killers. A journalist who read the reports, Arturo Torres, said corruption in the armed forces follows the cocaine trade: most of it now leaves by sea, and those spaces are controlled by the navy, whose officers sit in the ports and decide on permits.
inside: Gangs allegedly got weapons from sailors inside Ecuador's navy, so a service guarding the coast armed the groups fighting over its ports.
cite: InSight Crime, 26 January 2023, citing intelligence reports reported by Primicias

n: Ecuadorian navy officers said to have sold data to ex-FARC mafia fronts
org_label: Oliver Sinisterra Front and Urías Rondón Mobile Column (ex-FARC mafia)
rank: Officers, Ecuadorian Navy
d: The same intelligence reports obtained by the Ecuadorian newspaper Primicias stated that several Ecuadorian navy officers had been selling information to Colombian criminal groups, including the Oliver Sinisterra Front and the Urías Rondón Mobile Column. Both belong to what is known as the ex-FARC mafia, a loosely connected network of dissident groups once belonging to the now-demobilised Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia. According to the journalist who read the reports, most weapons reaching criminal hands in Ecuador are now taken from navy arsenals; in the 2000s navy and army weapons were bought or stolen for Colombian groups such as the FARC and the National Liberation Army.
inside: Colombian armed groups allegedly bought information from officers inside Ecuador's navy, the force meant to watch the sea routes they use.
cite: InSight Crime, 26 January 2023, citing intelligence reports reported by Primicias

n: Three serving Ecuadorian soldiers held over arms sent to ex-FARC dissidents
rank: Active members of the Ecuadorian armed forces
d: In November 2021 Ecuadorian police arrested three active members of the military who reportedly belonged to a criminal structure operating in the province of Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, towards the Ecuador–Colombia border. The officers were alleged to have trafficked arms to dissident units of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, the Colombian guerrilla force since demobilised. The case was one of several: in August 2021 a soldier was arrested for allegedly supplying a local criminal group with weapons. A 2015 report by Ecuador's Attorney General's Office found that weapons stolen from official arsenals are one of the main sources of trafficked arms in the country.
inside: Armed groups across the border allegedly had serving soldiers inside Ecuador's army supplying them with weapons from its own stocks.
cite: InSight Crime, 31 May 2022, citing Ecuavisa, Ecuador's National Police and the Attorney General's Office

n: Peru's 'Sinchi' clan allegedly paid 50 police, Cusco's chief among them
rank: Cusco regional chief of police and his predecessor; four regional and provincial police chiefs
d: At least 50 members of Peru's national police force were linked to a criminal organisation called "Mecanismo" and were allegedly bribed by a drug gang known as "Sinchi" to help move cocaine to Bolivia. Prosecutors say Sinchi is led by Julio César Sánchez Tello and works around Ayacucho, Cusco and Madre de Dios. Sixteen officers were arrested on 2 December in Cusco, Puno and Moquegua. Two colonels, Cusco's then regional chief of police and his predecessor, reportedly received bribes and took an active part. Witness statements collected by prosecutors and published anonymously said officers received between 2,000 and 4,000 soles a week, around US$590 to US$1,200, for not patrolling the region and not telling the intelligence agency in Lima what the clans were doing.
inside: A cocaine clan allegedly paid police chiefs in Cusco a weekly sum to keep their patrols away and their reports to Lima silent.
cite: InSight Crime, 18 December 2019, citing La República quoting the Attorney General's Office, and the Andina news agency

n: Lima police officer convicted of pushing victims to pay Tren de Aragua
rank: Sub-officer, Barboncito police station, San Martín de Porres, Lima
d: Peru's Seventh Superior Criminal Prosecutor's Office in Lima upheld a sentence of seven years and six months in prison for Paul Galarza, a sub-officer of the Peruvian National Police, for belonging to a criminal gang that extorted people in the capital.
