Prosecutors say that in 2020 she received benefits of 36,500 euros and 56,530 lei, about 11,000 euros, disguised as the sale of a property at a derisory price, in exchange for signing the planning documents a Navodari property project needed, and later accepted fitting-out works worth 12,853 lei from a second developer for similar permits. The directorate notes the presumption of innocence.
inside: Developers paid the official who signs a town's building permits, prosecutors say, and the permits their projects needed were then signed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 28/VIII/3, 29 January 2025

n: Contractors paid Zanesti's mayor about half their profit on commune works
org_label: S.C. LEI IN INSTALATII S.R.L. and S.C. YOUPLAN DEVELOPMENT S.R.L.
rank: mayor of the commune of Zanesti, Neamt county, and staff of its town hall
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent the mayor of Zanesti, Ioan Filip, to trial on 29 July 2026 on three counts of taking bribes and two of abuse of office. Prosecutors say that in 2022 and 2023 he demanded from a company representative about half the profit expected from a pavement contract worth over three million lei, and received in return a house built on his family's land, works and materials valued at about 430,000 lei. On a park contract worth 476,205.64 lei excluding VAT signed in March 2025 he is said to have taken 50,000 lei and plumbing work at his farm. Two town hall staff and a school head signed guilty-plea agreements.
inside: Firms seeking a commune's works contracts paid its mayor a share of their profit, prosecutors say, and the contracts were awarded, approved and paid.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 524/I-36, 4 August 2026

n: Road contractor's 421,930 lei reached Prahova's county council president
org_label: road maintenance contractors of Prahova county
who: firms holding the county's road framework agreements
rank: president of the Prahova County Council
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent to trial in December 2024 Iulian Dumitrescu, at the time of the facts president of the Prahova County Council, on six counts including influence peddling and two of taking bribes. Prosecutors say that between March and June 2022, as associations of firms carried out two framework agreements with the county council for road and bridge maintenance, he demanded 5 per cent of the VAT-excluded value of the invoices one firm issued to the council and collected from it, and that between July and August 2022 he received 421,930 lei through an intermediary. They also say he demanded 47.5 million lei from another contractor for shares in a company valued at 30,382,818 lei. The directorate notes the presumption of innocence.
inside: Firms paid a county council's president a cut of the invoices the council itself paid them, prosecutors say, so their road contracts kept running.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 850/VIII/3, 9 December 2024

n: Land seller's 1.15 million lei bought Lehliu-Gara's mayor planning acts
org_label: a company de facto run by Iulian Dumitrescu
who: a land-dealing company run in fact by a county council president
rank: mayor of the town of Lehliu-Gara, Calarasi county
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent to trial in December 2024 Iulian Iacomi, mayor of the town of Lehliu-Gara in Calarasi county, on a continuing count of taking bribes made up of 55 separate acts. Prosecutors say that between October 2021 and February 2023 Iulian Dumitrescu, then president of the Prahova County Council, helped by two accomplices, gave him 1,153,350 lei in 48 instalments and 74,000 euros in seven instalments, which were not due to him, in connection with planning acts within his duties concerning a 70,000 square metre plot that a company Dumitrescu ran in fact sold for 1,120,000 euros. The directorate notes the presumption of innocence.
inside: A company's owner paid a mayor in dozens of instalments, prosecutors say, for the planning decisions that let its land be sold at a high price.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 850/VIII/3, 9 December 2024

n: An MNLA commander holds a seat in Mali's parliament and transition council
org_label: Mouvement national de liberation de l'Azawad (MNLA) and the CMA coalition
who: MNLA and the CMA armed coalition
rank: Member of Parliament for Ansongo and member of the National Transition Council
d: The United Nations Panel of Experts on Mali recorded that Akli Iknane Ag Souleymane, the representative of the Imididaghan tribe in the Gourma area, was elected Member of Parliament for Ansongo in April 2020 and is a member of the National Transition Council, one of Mali's transitional institutions. He is at the same time a senior military commander of the MNLA, an armed movement in northern Mali, and was reappointed Gourma zone commander for the CMA armed coalition on 29 January 2021. The Panel also recorded that he joined a delegation received by the then prime minister in July 2020 and has lobbied for a meeting with the president of Niger.
inside: An armed movement's serving zone commander also holds a seat in Mali's legislature, so the movement has its own officer inside the body that makes the country's laws.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Mali, final report S/2021/714, paras. 43 and 46

n: Sanctioned armed-group secretary-general sits on Mali's transition council
rank: member of the National Transition Council
d: The United Nations Panel of Experts on Mali reported that Mohamed Ousmane Ag Mohamedoune, an individual designated under the Mali sanctions regime, continues to accumulate positions: secretary-general of the armed group Coalition du peuple de l'Azawad, member of the Agreement Monitoring Committee, president of a tribal council and member of the National Transition Council, one of Mali's transitional institutions. The Panel had previously set out how he benefited from Malian state support to advance his career as a political entrepreneur, and said it had received information that the government continued to provide him with financial support despite the sanctions measures decided in December 2018.
inside: A sanctioned armed group's secretary-general holds a seat in Mali's transition legislature, and the state has gone on paying him while he keeps that post.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Mali, final report S/2021/714, para. 48; S/2022/595, para. 132

n: Armed coalition packed Birao's branch of the national elections authority
org_label: Kara-Goula armed group coalition (MLCJ, PRNC, RPRC)
rank: local branch of the ANE, the national elections authority, in Birao
d: The United Nations Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic investigated how armed groups claiming to represent the Goula and Kara communities worked to favour their preferred candidates in the 2020 legislative elections in the Birao constituency. Several sources told the Panel that the coalition's leaders, both community and armed group leaders, had made sure that most members of the ANE, the national elections authority, in the area were from their own ethnic group. The Panel recorded that international partners had to press that branch to carry out voter registration in areas populated by Saras, and that this, together with insecurity, left fewer Sara and Rounga voters registered. The coalition also asked the government to stop the sitting member of parliament from travelling to Birao.
inside: An armed coalition filled a town's election office with its own community, and registration then ran against the voters who backed its rivals.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic, S/2021/87, paras. 20-22 and annexes 2.15 and 2.16

n: Armed group leader named mayors himself after rejecting a presidential decree
org_label: Rassemblement patriotique pour le renouveau de la Centrafrique and allied Kara-Goula groups
rank: mayoralties in Vakaga and Haute-Kotto prefectures
d: The United Nations Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic recorded that on 19 February 2020 the armed group leader Zakaria Damane contested presidential decree 20.049, which appointed mayors across the country. In the territory held by combatants under his command the appointed mayors were prevented from taking office and Damane personally named some of the mayors instead, using his combatants to enforce his decisions. In Sam-Ouandja local sources told the Panel that the decree had appointed a Sara as mayor but that armed group members rejected the appointment and he never took office. Meeting the Panel in October 2020, Damane complained that the president had not consulted him and said he should have a say on appointments in areas his fighters control.
inside: An armed group leader blocked the mayors the president had appointed and installed his own, so local government in his area answered to his fighters.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic, S/2021/87, annex 2.16 ('Further information on actions by the leaders of the Kara-Goula coalition to prevent or maintain control over the process of the restoration of State authority')

n: CAR peace deals put armed groups' advisers in Bangui's legislature
org_label: Unite pour la paix en Centrafrique (UPC) and Retour, reclamation et rehabilitation (3R)
rank: key adviser roles in the legislative branch in Bangui
d: The United Nations Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic reported in June 2026 that the armed groups had had several individuals appointed in key adviser roles in the executive and legislative branches in Bangui, and that other senior-level appointments were expected in the forthcoming government. The Panel based this on interviews in Bangui in March and April 2026. It described the 2025 N'Djamena agreements as narrower and more transactional than the earlier peace agreement: they provide for the participation of the armed groups 3R and UPC in senior government positions within national institutions and the administration, and for appointments within the military chain of command, consulting the groups' own leadership. The Panel said this creates ambiguity over the number of posts.
inside: Armed groups negotiated posts for their own people and have had advisers appointed inside Bangui's legislature, where they now sit close to decisions.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic, S/2026/481, paras. 15 and 19

n: Barge owners pay Haitian police to guard a private sea route from APN port
org_label: private barge owners and port-area business operators
rank: police officers escorting the APN barge route and policing the APN zone
d: Gangs have closed Haiti's RN2 road south of Port-au-Prince, and freight now moves by sea from the National Port Authority (APN) terminal to the southern coast. The United Nations Panel of Experts on Haiti reported that barge owners charge between 2,500 and 5,000 US dollars a container, that a number of police officers ensure the security of the about eight barges on the route and reportedly receive substantial financial compensation from barge owners, and that private actors also reportedly pay for police security around the APN zone. Sources told the Panel they were pressured by business figures to slow efforts to unblock the RN2 and to secure the APN port area. The Panel said its investigations would continue.
inside: Barge and port companies pay serving Haitian police, so police effort goes to guarding a private sea route the companies profit from.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Haiti, report S/2026/714 (October 2026), section on air and sea routes, paras. with footnotes 177-181, pp. 49

n: Clearing agents' palm-oil diversion drew in Ghana customs officers
org_label: clearing agents and the importers behind a transit consignment
rank: Customs officers of the Ghana Revenue Authority and National Security operatives
d: Ghana's Office of the Special Prosecutor says it is investigating the diversion of fifty twenty-foot containers of palm oil worth 25.8 million cedis. The consignment was declared as being in transit to Burkina Faso, which would exempt it from Ghanaian duty, but was unlawfully diverted onto the local market without payment of the applicable duties and taxes. The Office says it has identified certain Customs officers of the Ghana Revenue Authority, National Security operatives and clearing agents in an alleged corrupt scheme that resulted in an estimated tax loss of 10 million cedis. The case began with an intelligence-led operation in November 2025. The investigation is recorded as ongoing and no one is named.
inside: Clearing agents allegedly worked with customs and national security officers so a cargo declared as transit was released onto Ghana's market duty-free.
cite: Office of the Special Prosecutor (Ghana), case profile 'Diversion of Palm Oil'

n: Importers' men paid customs inspectors at Romania's Constanta border post
org_label: representatives of importing companies at Constanta
rank: customs inspectors, Constanta Border Customs Office
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent plea agreements for two customs inspectors at the Constanta Border Customs Office to the Constanta Tribunal on 17 July 2026. Prosecutors say Suliman Diner took money from representatives of importing companies seeking clearance between November and December 2025 and again from January to April 2026, and that on 9 April 2026 a company representative identified as G.G. left 6,500 lei in his car over clearances requested in March. In February 2026 the second inspector, Vilsan Bogdan, allegedly asked a company's representative for 200 US dollars a container for quick clearance. All three admitted the facts and agreed suspended sentences of three years, two years and four months, and eighteen months.
inside: Importing companies' representatives paid two customs inspectors, who admitted it, so clearance decisions at a frontier post suited the firms that paid.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release no. 512/I-36, 27 July 2026

n: A company boss paid Slovakia's counter-intelligence chief 200,000 euros
org_label: Dusan Bockay, head of the company Bopal
who: the head of the company Bopal
rank: head of counter-intelligence, Slovak Information Service (SIS)
d: The Specialised Criminal Court in Pezinok found Peter Gasparovic, former head of counter-intelligence at the Slovak Information Service, and a former police officer, Ladislav Vican, guilty of accepting bribes. The judge, Ruzena Sabova, said Gasparovic asked for at least 350,000 euros from the businessman Dusan Bockay and was given 200,000. According to the prosecution the two offered, for a bribe of 400,000 euros from Bockay as head of the company Bopal, to reverse a decision of the Financial Administration's criminal office impounding Bopal's property; because the decision was not reversed, only the advance changed hands. They were arrested in December 2020 in a police operation nicknamed Judas. Gasparovic was jailed for eleven years, Vican for ten.
inside: A company owner paid the head of the state's counter-intelligence branch, who used his position to try to undo a seizure of the company's property.
cite: Radio Slovakia International (STVR) citing TASR, 'Former Counter-intelligence Director found guilty', 22 October 2021

n: Brazilian tax officer removed over millions paid by firms in customs cases
org_label: businessmen with customs proceedings before the Receita Federal
rank: federal official of the Receita Federal handling customs proceedings
d: On 2 June 2026 Brazil's Federal Police and the Receita Federal, the federal tax and customs service, launched Operation Benaia in Florianopolis against a scheme of corruption, criminal association and money laundering said to involve a federal public servant. Search warrants were executed in Santa Catarina and Sao Paulo and the main suspect was removed from his duties. According to the investigation he received at least 2 million reais to favour businessmen in customs proceedings, and also worked on creating logistical mechanisms in the group's interest; the total of benefits received may exceed 5 million reais, paid in cash, deposits and personal expenses. The inquiry began after the tax service's own internal affairs unit found unexplained wealth.
inside: Investigators say businessmen paid a federal customs official, who then favoured them in customs proceedings and built logistics arrangements they wanted.
cite: Correio da Manha, 'PF e Receita Federal deflagram operacao contra esquema milionario em SC', 2 June 2026

n: Drone maker's owner and a Ukrainian border guard official demanded $1m
org_label: the owner of a drone-manufacturing company
who: the owner of a drone-manufacturing company
rank: official of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine
d: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau reported that an official of the State Border Guard Service and the owner of a company that makes unmanned aircraft were caught demanding one million US dollars. For the money they promised to secure the unhindered conclusion and performance of a contract to supply unmanned aviation complexes. After a company offering a lower price won the procurement, the owner of the losing firm, in collusion with the border guard official, began demanding the money from its director. To press him, they arranged a telephone call with a representative of the service who assured him that all the demands had been agreed with the service's own Administration. Two people are suspects and the investigation continues.
inside: A drone firm's owner allegedly worked with an official inside the border guard service, using its power over a supply contract to squeeze a rival.
cite: National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU), report for the first half of 2026, section on corruption in the defence industry

n: Entrepreneur paid $110,000 to SBU investigators in Poltava for a plea deal
org_label: an entrepreneur whose company director faced arrest
who: an entrepreneur facing a case against his company
rank: head of the investigative department, SBU directorate in Poltava region
d: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau reported in April 2026 that the head of the investigative department of the Security Service of Ukraine directorate in Poltava region and a subordinate had demanded 110,000 US dollars from an entrepreneur through a lawyer. In exchange they promised not to apply to a court for the arrest of the director of his company, and to conclude a plea agreement with him. Those involved were caught in the act while receiving the second instalment of 55,000 dollars. The Security Service of Ukraine is the state's main internal security and counter-intelligence body, and its regional investigative departments run criminal cases. Three people are suspects and the investigation continues.
inside: A businessman's money allegedly reached the security service unit investigating his firm, buying a promise its director would not be held.
cite: National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU), report for the first half of 2026, section on corruption in the law enforcement system and prosecution service

n: Company administrator caught paying Bacau's police business-crime chief
org_label: the administrator of a company under a forestry inspection
rank: head of the business crime investigation bureau, Bacau County Police Inspectorate
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged Razvan Rujan, a police chief commissar who headed the business crime investigation bureau in the economic crime service of the Bacau County Police Inspectorate, with taking a bribe. Prosecutors say that on 1 April 2026, while carrying out a check on compliance with forestry law at a company's place of business, he received 1,000 lei from the administrator of the company being inspected, in connection with his duties on that check. Prosecutors recorded it as an offence caught in the act. The Bacau Tribunal placed him under house arrest for thirty days on 2 April 2026. The directorate notes that charging does not displace the presumption of innocence.
inside: Prosecutors say a company's owner paid the police officer inspecting it, so the inspection of his own firm was handled to suit him.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 2 April 2026

n: Hotel firm's man paid a Valcea economic-crime officer 2,000 euros
org_label: the representative of a hotel and catering company
who: the representative of a hotel and catering company
rank: police officer, economic crime investigation service, Valcea County Police Inspectorate
d: Prosecutors of Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged Constantin Casian Anghel, a police officer in the economic crime investigation service of the Valcea County Police Inspectorate, with taking a bribe. They say he asked, directly and through another person, for 2,000 euros from the representative of a company working in the hotel and catering trade, so that he would not carry out his duties by applying the legal measures required after an inspection. He is said to have received the 2,000 euros on 31 August 2024, when the offence was recorded as caught in the act, and he was brought before the Arges Tribunal with a request for pre-trial detention. The directorate notes the presumption of innocence.
inside: Prosecutors say a company's representative paid the police officer who inspected it, so the legal measures the inspection called for were never applied.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 1 September 2024

n: 25,000 lei bought a smaller fine from Tulcea's environment chief
org_label: a businessman whose company had been inspected
who: a businessman whose company had been inspected
rank: chief commissar, Tulcea County Commissariat of the National Environmental Guard
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent Dorin Meran, at the time chief commissar of the Tulcea county commissariat of the National Environmental Guard, for trial in pre-trial detention on a continuing charge of taking bribes. Prosecutors say that between 30 August and 4 September 2023 he asked a businessman, a witness in the case, for 25,000 lei and other undue benefits so as to impose a smaller fine, or only a warning, after an inspection he had carried out at a site of a company the businessman ran. The money is said to have been handed to him in his car on 4 September 2023 and the offence recorded as caught in the act. The file went to the Tulcea Tribunal.
inside: Prosecutors say a company owner's money reached the head of the county environment inspectorate, who was to cut or waive his firm's fine.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 5 September 2023 and committal release

n: Solar park builder paid a Giurgiu police chief over overweight lorries
org_label: the de facto representative of the company building a photovoltaic park at Coteni
rank: head of Rural Police Section no. 6 Mihailesti, Giurgiu county
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged Stefan-Claudiu Barbu, a police commissar heading Rural Police Section no. 6 at Mihailesti in Giurgiu county, with taking a bribe, his brother with complicity, and a man identified as M.E., the de facto representative of a company, with giving one. Prosecutors say that during 2026 Barbu asked for and received money, including 20,000 lei passed through his brother on 2 April 2026, and service contracts for his brother's firm. In exchange he is said to have promised not to perform his duties and to stop officers under his command from checking the company's transports: the firm was building a photovoltaic park at Coteni and needed overweight lorries to cross nearby villages. The Bucharest Tribunal ordered his detention.
inside: Prosecutors say a construction company's representative paid the local police chief, who then kept his officers from checking the firm's overweight lorries.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 22-23 July 2026

n: Importers paid Constanta South port customs $500-700 a container, DNA says
org_label: importers and the customs brokers acting for them at Constanta South
rank: customs officers, Constanta South Border Customs Office, Port of Constanta
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate says it is investigating how customs staff at the Constanta South border customs office took money from importers using the port of Constanta South Agigea, through customs brokers, so as not to carry out physical checks properly and to clear containers whose goods did not match the import papers or were counterfeit. According to prosecutors importers habitually give between 500 and 700 US dollars a container, rising by 30 to 50 dollars a parcel and reaching 10,000 dollars for goods banned from import into the EU. The customs officer Marius Oprea was caught on 12 September 2024 taking 5,000 dollars and 8,100 lei from a broker; two others were charged with complicity.
inside: Prosecutors say importers paid customs staff through brokers, so physical checks were skipped and containers that did not match their papers were released.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 13 September 2024

n: Traders' cash and counterfeit goods reached Romania's customs authority
org_label: traders operating in Bucharest and Ilfov commercial centres
rank: officials and a director of the Bucharest Regional Customs Directorate, Romanian Customs Authority
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged five customs officials of the Romanian Customs Authority and the Bucharest Regional Customs Directorate with continuing bribery. Prosecutors say that during 2023, while carrying out inspections, Alexandru Cernat, Marius Marin, Nicolae-Stefan Teianu, Marian-Vladimir Vulcan and Demetrius Gheorghe asked for and received from several businessmen trading in commercial centres in Bucharest and Ilfov a total of 60,600 lei, 11,500 US dollars, 600 euros, 408 pairs of sports boots and 1,000 counterfeit perfumes, so as to omit filing a criminal report about what they had found and to close the inspections in the traders' favour. The directorate's regional director Paul Petrof and a bureau head were charged over separate dealings with businessmen.
inside: Prosecutors say traders paid customs officials inspecting them, so inspections ended in the traders' favour and no criminal report was filed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 13-14 February 2024

n: Companies paid Bucharest Sector 1 local police to soften confiscations
org_label: representatives of companies trading in Bucharest's Sector 1
rank: officers and the head of the commercial activities control unit, Sector 1 Local Police
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged three officers of the Sector 1 Local Police in Bucharest, including the head of its commercial activities control unit, with continuing bribery and influence peddling. Prosecutors say that in 2023 and 2024, while inspecting companies with premises in Sector 1, they asked their representatives for sums between 2,500 and 14,000 euros, 26,500 euros in all, and received 18,000 euros and 2,500 lei. In return one inspected company had only 214,708 lei confiscated rather than its total takings of about 1,353,000 lei; another was to be fined quickly so that less of its income during suspension could be seized; a third escaped penalty for trading without a licence.
inside: Prosecutors say companies paid the local police unit inspecting them, so far less of their unlawful takings was confiscated than the records showed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 4-5 June 2024

n: Companies' work permit files bought speed at a Romanian immigration bureau
org_label: companies hiring non-European workers, acting through an intermediary
rank: acting head of the Ialomita County Immigration Bureau
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged Rares-Gabriel Bulimej, a police chief commissar and acting head of the Ialomita County Immigration Bureau, with continuing bribery. Prosecutors say that in 2022 and 2023 he accepted, from a police officer at the Bucharest immigration directorate, the promise of money in exchange for speeding up appointments and decisions on work permit applications and for issuing those permits preferentially in the name of several companies. On 3 October 2024 he is said to have accepted 12,000 euros to hurry 25 employment applications for non-European nationals lodged by several companies, and was caught in the act. The day before, the officer had taken 31,400 euros for permits for 38 Asian nationals.
inside: Prosecutors say money from companies hiring foreign workers reached the immigration bureau's chief, who put their permit files ahead of others'.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 4 October 2024

n: Developer's 40,000 euros reached Bucharest Sector 5's local police
org_label: two businessmen and an administrator of several companies, A.R.A.
who: businessmen finishing a Sector 5 housing block
rank: deputy director general, General Directorate of Local Police, Sector 5, Bucharest
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate charged Florin Chioran, deputy director general of the General Directorate of Local Police in Bucharest's Sector 5, with continuing bribery, and the Sector 5 chief architect with influence peddling. Prosecutors say that between December 2025 and February 2026 a man identified as A.R.A., who runs several companies, took 40,000 euros in two instalments from two businessmen to use his influence over officials so that documents needed to finish a housing block would be issued, and passed 15,000 euros to the chief architect. Chioran is said to have signed the completion papers, reassigned the file after irregularities were found at a check on 13 January 2026, and separately taken 70,000 lei and 3,100 euros from a subordinate.
inside: Prosecutors say businessmen's money reached the local police directorate's deputy head, who then pushed through the sign-off their housing block needed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie (Romania), press release of 6-7 February 2026

n: Mining litigant's Rp150m bought rulings from two South Jakarta judges
org_label: PT Citra Lampia Mandiri's director Martin P. Silitonga and advocate Arif Fitrawan
who: PT Citra Lampia Mandiri's director and his advocate
rank: judges of the South Jakarta District Court (PN Jakarta Selatan)
d: Two judges of the South Jakarta District Court, R. Iswahyu Widodo and Irwan, were convicted of taking money to shape a civil case they were hearing. The suit, number 262/Pdt.G/2018, sought to cancel an acquisition agreement between CV Citra Lampia Mandiri and PT Asia Pacific Mining Resources. PT CLM's director Martin P. Silitonga and his advocate Arif Fitrawan routed Rp200 million through M. Ramadhan, a clerk at the East Jakarta court, on 31 July 2018; Rp150 million reached judge Irwan. On 15 August 2018 the judges rejected the defendants' preliminary objections, and about Rp500 million was prepared for the final ruling. On 11 July 2019 the Jakarta corruption court jailed the judges for four years and six months each.
inside: A company director and his lawyer paid two judges and a court clerk so the judges' rulings in his own civil suit went his way.
cite: Hukumonline, 'Dianggap Coreng Lembaga Peradilan, Dua Hakim PN Jaksel Dihukum Penjara', 12 July 2019 (judgment of the Jakarta Corruption Court, 11 July 2019)

n: A company's lawyer paid a Surabaya judge to have the company dissolved
org_label: PT Soyu Giri Primedika and its lawyer Hendro Kasiono
rank: sole judge, Surabaya District Court (PN Surabaya)
d: Itong Isnaeni Hidayat sat as sole judge on a petition to dissolve PT Soyu Giri Primedika at the Surabaya District Court. Indonesia's anti-corruption commission, the KPK, caught a handover on 19 January 2022 and seized Rp140 million, which its deputy chairman Nawawi Pomolango described as a down payment on meeting the wishes of the company's lawyer, Hendro Kasiono. Prosecutors put the sum arranged for the case at around Rp1.3 billion and said the ruling sought was that PT SGP be dissolved with divisible assets of Rp50 billion. Substitute clerk Hamdan was the intermediary, the two using the word 'upeti' for the money. On 25 October 2022 the Surabaya corruption court jailed Itong for five years; appeal and review were rejected.
inside: A company's lawyer paid the judge hearing its dissolution petition, so the ruling on the company's own case was fixed to its liking.
cite: Hukumonline, 'OTT PN Surabaya; KPK Tetapkan Hakim, Panitera dan Pengacara sebagai Tersangka', 21 January 2022; Metrotvnews, 'Eks Hakim Terpidana Korupsi Kembali Jadi ASN di PN Surabaya', 26 August 2025 (sentence and final outcome)

n: Businessman and the Las Palmas judge agreed to annul the case
org_label: Miguel Angel Ramirez, administrator of Seguridad Integral Canaria
who: the administrator of Seguridad Integral Canaria
rank: magistrate running Investigating Court no. 8 of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
d: Salvador Alba asked for and obtained the post of investigating judge at Court no. 8 in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria on 3 November 2015, taking over a tax investigation, case 644/2014, against Miguel Angel Ramirez, then administrator of the firm Seguridad Integral Canaria, and his deputy Hector de Armas. On 16 March 2016 Alba let Ramirez into the court building through the garage for a private meeting. The Canary Islands High Court found that Ramirez handed over information damaging to the judge Alba had replaced, Victoria Rosell, and that in exchange Alba undertook to annul the proceedings so they could not continue. He was jailed for six years and six months in 2019; the Supreme Court confirmed it in 2021.
inside: A businessman being investigated met the judge handling his case privately, and the judge agreed to end the proceedings in exchange for information.
cite: Consejo General del Poder Judicial, 'El TSJ de Canarias impone al juez Alba seis anos de carcel y 18 de inhabilitacion', 10 September 2019; Economist & Jurist, 'Condena de prision para el juez Salvador Alba por prevaricacion, cohecho y falsedad', 25 November 2021 (Supreme Court confirmation)

n: Builders' bribes steered ASL Bari's hospital works to six firms
org_label: Costruzioni Bioedili, Gadaleta Ignazio, Falegnameria Moderna, Costruzioni Murgolo, Perrone Global Service and Ism impianti servizi medicali
rank: Director of the technical management unit and head of health building, ASL Bari
d: The ASL di Bari is the public health authority that runs hospitals and clinics in the Italian province of Bari. On 12 November 2024 ten people were arrested over bribes tied to its contracts, among them Nicola Sansolini, who ran its technical management unit until January 2024, Nicola Iacobellis, head of health building, and an official of the same unit. Prosecutors say the contractors paid in luxury handbags, house renovations and cash, in return for work including the detainee ward at Bari's San Paolo hospital and a health centre at Giovinazzo. Searches seized 250,000 euros in cash from the public officials and 70,000 from the entrepreneurs, with 17 high-value bags. The charges include criminal association, corruption, forgery and rigging the bidding.
inside: Building firms paid the officials who ran the Bari health authority's works contracts, and the authority then awarded and signed off work that suited the payers.
cite: Il Fatto Quotidiano, 12 November 2024 (reporting the Bari prosecutors' arrest measure and the Guardia di Finanza investigation)

n: Medical suppliers' agents and officials rigged 33m euro Calabrian health tenders
org_label: companies supplying medical materials and services in Calabria
rank: Officials of the health authorities of Catanzaro, Crotone and Cosenza, the Reggio Calabria hospital group and Magna Graecia University
d: Italy's provincial health authorities, the aziende sanitarie provinciali, buy supplies and services for public hospitals. On 3 July 2024 the Guardia di Finanza in Catanzaro served fifteen precautionary measures over nine public tenders worth more than 33 million euros, put out by the Calabria region's single contracting station, Magna Graecia University, and the Pugliese-Ciaccio and Mater Domini hospitals, since merged into the Dulbecco hospital trust. Investigators allege illicit links between public officials who ran the tenders and the agents and representatives of firms supplying medical materials or services. Thirteen officials of those bodies were barred from public office; two entrepreneurs and a hospital doctor were placed under house arrest, and a company worth about 530,000 euros was seized.
inside: Sales agents of medical supply firms built ties with the officials running Calabria's health tenders, and prosecutors say nine contracts were then steered their way.
cite: LaPresse, 3 July 2024 (Guardia di Finanza of Catanzaro, under the direction of the public prosecutor's office)

n: Sorella sanita: health suppliers bought Sicily's hospital tender chief
rank: Manager of the Trapani health authority and head of the Sicilian Region's single contracting station; manager of the Palermo health authority
d: In May 2020 Sicilian finance police ran an operation called Sorella sanita, after the nickname for Fabio Damiani, then manager of the Trapani health authority and head of the Sicilian Region's single contracting station, which ran health tenders for the whole island. Prosecutors described a corrupt pact between public administrators and entrepreneurs to divide up health contracts. In December 2023 the appeal court convicted all the defendants, including Damiani, the former Palermo health authority manager Antonio Candela, two executives of Tecnologie Sanitarie and the former chairman of Pfe. On 23 May 2025 the Court of Cassation made some convictions final, annulled other counts and ordered a fresh appeal, and acquitted Candela outright on one charge. Damiani and the entrepreneur Salvatore Manganaro agreed to co-operate with prosecutors.
inside: Health supply companies worked through a fixer to reach the manager who ran Sicily's health tenders, and he passed them tender papers so chosen firms would win.
cite: LiveSicilia, 1 December 2023 (appeal convictions) and 23 May 2025 (Court of Cassation verdict); LiveSicilia, 21 May 2020 (the arrests)

n: Sorella sanita 2: equipment firms reached an Enna health authority official
org_label: Althea, Dedalus Italia, Vivisol, Viviso, Healtech and Generay
who: Althea, Dedalus Italia, Vivisol and other suppliers
rank: Official of the health authority of Enna
d: On 21 October 2022 a Palermo investigation called Sorella sanita 2 put ten people under precautionary measures over a system said to control Sicilian regional tenders worth 700 million euros. Giovanni Luca Vancheri, an official of the Enna health authority, was jailed pending trial on charges of corruption and interfering with the choice of contractor. Among the others were two representatives of Althea, charged with corruption, the chief executive of Dedalus Italia, managers of Vivisol and Viviso, and the heads of Healtech and Generay. A lieutenant of the carabinieri was investigated for attempted bid rigging and a Milan accountant for money laundering and false invoicing. The judge temporarily barred Healtech, Vivisol and Althea from contracting with public bodies.
inside: Medical equipment firms' representatives are accused of paying an official inside a Sicilian health authority so that regional supply contracts were awarded to them.
cite: LiveSicilia, 21 October 2022 (list of those placed under precautionary measures by the Palermo preliminary investigations judge)

n: An auditor's circle took bribes on six Sicilian hospital tenders worth 130m euros
org_label: hospital supply companies and their intermediaries in Sicily
rank: Purchasing head of the Villa Sofia-Cervello hospital trust; former administrative director of the Caltanissetta health authority
d: On 13 June 2025 a Palermo investigation named 22 suspects, among them hospital managers, public officials, entrepreneurs and fixers, over bribes said to have been paid to steer six public health contracts worth almost 130 million euros. Prosecutors describe a business committee of entrepreneurs, lobbyists and public officials. Two people were placed under house arrest, five barred from the area and three firms temporarily barred from trading. The central figure is the accountant Antonio Maria Sciacchitano, who held posts on the audit boards of the Palermo health authority and the Civico hospital and chaired the evaluation body of the Trapani health authority. The tenders named include equipment maintenance put out by the Trapani health authority in 2021 and sterilisation services at Palermo's Civico hospital in 2022.
inside: Suppliers and their intermediaries are accused of paying officials inside Sicilian health authorities so that six large hospital contracts went to the firms that paid.
cite: LiveSicilia, 13 June 2025 (Palermo public prosecutor's office; measures ordered by the preliminary investigations judge)

n: Builder's bribes won split contracts at ASL Caserta's mental health department
rank: Former director of the mental health department and staff handling contracts, ASL Caserta
d: The ASL di Caserta is the public health authority for the Italian province of Caserta. In February 2021 an investigation by the Napoli Nord prosecutors led to twelve arrests of its officials and staff. Prosecutors and the carabinieri of the NAS health unit say the former director of the mental health department, Luigi Carrizzone, with the help of two arrested ASL employees who handled contracts, split a job worth more than 150,000 euros into small works below the 40,000 euro European threshold so they could be handed directly, without a tender, to entrepreneurs who paid bribes, among them the builder Antonio Papa, also arrested. Investigators say the method was used whenever the department had works to award.
inside: Contractors paid officials of the Caserta health authority, which then broke up its works into small direct awards so the firms that paid got them without competing.
cite: Stylo24, 22 February 2021 (Napoli Nord public prosecutor's office and NAS carabinieri investigation)

n: So.Re.Sa's ex-president jailed over bribes from two Campania entrepreneurs
rank: Former president of So.Re.Sa. SpA, Campania's regional health purchasing company
d: So.Re.Sa. SpA is the company through which the Italian region of Campania buys for its health service. In November 2026 its former president, Tommaso Casillo, was jailed pending investigation on two counts of corruption. Prosecutors Henry John Woodcock and Francesca Paola Colonna Romano allege he received 20,000 euros over a waste contract at Somma Vesuviana and 100,000 euros over two lots of a tender to rent out stretchers for health facilities, both from the entrepreneurs Mario and Marco Langella. The judge wrote of a settled readiness to subordinate public office to private interests. Questioned for two hours by the judge on 14 November 2026, Casillo denied the charges and distanced himself from the intercepted conversations; the Langella brothers declined to answer.
inside: Two entrepreneurs are accused of paying the head of Campania's health purchasing company, which then decided contracts and tender lots in their favour.
cite: Stylo24, 14 November 2026 (questioning before the preliminary investigations judge) and 12 November 2026 (the charges and the regional response)

n: Operation Aspide: six convicted over rigged tenders and posts at ASP Trapani
org_label: suppliers to the Trapani health authority
who: suppliers to the Trapani health authority
rank: Manager of the Trapani health authority's health centre; former provveditore and other officials
d: Operation Aspide was a Guardia di Finanza investigation, run by the Trapani prosecutors, into what they call a settled mechanism for taming and manipulating tender procedures, public competitions and management appointments inside the Trapani health authority. It began with a tender the authority put out for intensive care equipment during the Covid-19 emergency, which went to Althea Italia. On 18 December 2024 the preliminary hearing judge convicted six people after a fast-track trial. The heaviest sentence, four years and eight months for corruption, went to a former ASP official, Antonio Sparaco, who was acquitted of other charges including fraud; the president of Trapani city council got two years and eight months. One doctor was acquitted and the former manager Fabio Damiani and two others were sent for an ordinary trial.
inside: Suppliers and politicians reached officials inside the Trapani health authority, which then ran its tenders and filled its posts to suit them.
cite: LiveSicilia, 18 December 2024 (the convictions) and 9 May 2024 (close of the investigation, with the tender that triggered it)

n: Drug and supply firms paid a Messina hospital chief through his congress
rank: Director of the complex plastic surgery unit, Policlinico G. Martino, Messina
d: The Policlinico G. Martino is the university teaching hospital in Messina, Sicily. In December 2025 the preliminary investigations judge placed its former head of plastic surgery, Francesco Stagno d'Alcontres, under house arrest. Prosecutors say he demanded thousands of euros from pharmaceutical companies and supply firms for a medical congress he was organising at Giardini Naxos, and in return helped those firms with supplies to the hospital. Thirty-one people are under investigation, among them doctors, entrepreneurs and sales representatives, on charges ranging from extortion in office and corruption to fraud against the state. Investigators put at about 700,000 euros the total taken for sponsorships, registrations, hotel stays and dinners. His phone was tapped from 10 May 2024.
inside: Drug and supply companies paid into a surgeon's congress, and prosecutors say he then helped them win and keep supply orders at the Messina teaching hospital.
cite: LiveSicilia, 5 December 2025 (custody order of the Messina preliminary investigations judge; Messina public prosecutor's office)

n: Orthopaedic suppliers paid an ASP Palermo doctor in cash and shellfish
org_label: orthopaedic supply companies in Palermo and Mazara del Vallo
rank: Doctor responsible for outpatient specialist services, health authority of Palermo
d: In March 2026 Palermo prosecutors asked for the arrest of Leonardo Gaziano, a doctor of the Palermo health authority responsible for outpatient specialist services, together with doctors and entrepreneurs. Wiretaps by the flying squad record him describing gifts from two administrators of companies selling orthopaedic material, Biagio Mendolia and Massimiliano Contino: lobsters, king prawns, octopus. Police photographed him leaving his office with the polystyrene boxes used for fish. Prosecutors Gianluca De Leo and Andrea Zoppi say supplies and invalidity pension certificates were secured with these payments, with a fixer, Giuseppe Nicoletti, collecting clients' applications and passing them on, and that certificates were issued without the patients being examined.
inside: Orthopaedic supply firms gave a health authority doctor cash and food, and prosecutors say he then prescribed their products and signed certificates they wanted.
cite: LiveSicilia, 3 March 2026 (wiretaps in the Palermo prosecutors' arrest request)

n: Sogi Medical's money reached the Civico hospital's purchasing office in Palermo
rank: Administrative official of the purchasing office, ARNAS Civico hospital, Palermo
d: ARNAS Civico is a public hospital trust in Palermo. In April 2025 the preliminary investigations judge imposed five precautionary measures in a corruption investigation into two supply tenders: one put out by the Civico hospital, the other for supplies to health bodies across western Sicily. Prosecutors say an administrative official of the hospital's purchasing office, Giuseppe Salamone, took money and other benefits from the owner of a Palermo medical supply firm and acted against his duties. He is said to have interfered with a two-year electrophysiology supply procedure launched in 2021 and awarded in 2023, and interceded with unit heads so a contract was not cancelled despite significant failures to deliver. Sogi Medical was barred for a year from contracting with public bodies.
inside: A medical supply firm paid an official in a Palermo hospital's purchasing office, who passed it tender information and protected its contract from being cancelled.
cite: LiveSicilia, 3 April 2025 (precautionary measures) and 8 March 2025 (the two tenders and the prosecutors' case)

n: Romeo Gestioni's gifts to officials over the Cardarelli hospital cleaning contract
rank: Executive director of the Cardarelli hospital cleaning contract; former head of the hospital's purchasing office
d: The Cardarelli is the largest public hospital in Naples. In October 2019 Naples prosecutors asked for 55 committals for trial against 54 people and the company Romeo Gestioni SpA over what they call the Romeo system: watches, jobs, consultancies, dinners and hotel stays with spa access given to public officials so that the entrepreneur Alfredo Romeo's firms won cleaning and property management contracts in public buildings. Among those named are a doctor who was executive director of the Cardarelli cleaning contract, won by a company of the Romeo group, and Ciro Verdoliva, the hospital's former purchasing office head and later head of the ASL Napoli 1, accused among other things of aiding an offender. Verdoliva said his conscience was clear. The preliminary hearing was set for 6 December.
inside: A services group gave public officials gifts and jobs, and prosecutors say cleaning and property contracts at a Naples hospital and other public bodies then went to its firms.
cite: Stylo24, 31 October 2019 (committal requests by Naples prosecutors Carrano, Raffaele and Woodcock) and 22 February 2019 (Verdoliva's response). Later stages of the trial were not established.

n: Equipment suppliers' deal with a Bacau hospital manager cost it 1.09m lei
org_label: Orion Mob, Raldia Distrib and Proton Impex 2000
who: Orion Mob, Raldia Distrib and Proton Impex 2000
rank: Manager of the Bacau Pneumophthisiology Hospital
d: Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate sent the manager of the Bacau Pneumophthisiology Hospital, Madalin-Nicolae Pararianu, for trial over four counts of abuse of office. Prosecutors say that between May 2022 and January 2023, under an earlier fraudulent understanding with the administrator of Orion Mob and Raldia Distrib, he had the hospital buy equipment from favoured firms at inflated prices, causing it a loss of 1,093,730 lei. In one purchase, a mobile X-ray unit costing 593,810 lei, the supplier Proton Impex 2000 is said to have supplied the technical characteristics that were written into the specification, and a rival offer about 200,000 lei cheaper for the hospital was unlawfully declared unacceptable before Proton Impex was named the winner in July 2022.
inside: Suppliers wrote the specification for a state hospital's purchases through its manager and a subordinate, so the hospital bought from them at inflated prices.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, indictment press release, release id 13272 on dna.ro (Territorial Service Bacau)

n: Road firms' payments ran through Anas's roads centre in Catania
rank: Head of the Catania centre and the official in charge of extraordinary works, Anas
d: Anas is the Italian state company that manages the national road network. In late September 2019 the Guardia di Finanza made a first round of arrests at its Catania centre, which handles the biggest road contracts in eastern Sicily. One of its senior managers, Antonio Urso, then went to prosecutors Fabio Regolo and Agata Santonocito and described the system. He said he began the illicit activity in 2015 with the engineer Giuseppe Romano, and gave an early example: on a bridge repair the firm Polistrade of Misilmeri handed Romano 7,000 euros, which the two then split, after the firm declared a greater thickness of demolished concrete than it had removed and was paid for it. Urso said the firms all knew Romano, who from 2017 signed the payment certificates.
inside: Road contractors paid the Anas managers who directed and certified their works, and the state roads company then paid for work that had not been done.
cite: LiveSicilia, 19 October 2019 (Antonio Urso's statements to Catania prosecutors). Later stages of the prosecution were not established.

n: Arete's representative caught paying the Catania Policlinico's tender chairman
rank: Director of the cardiac surgery unit and chair of the tender technical commission, Policlinico of Catania
d: The Policlinico of Catania is a public university hospital trust in Sicily. In 2022 the Guardia di Finanza filmed Valerio Fabiano, a medical products representative for the firm Arete, handing 2,000 euros to Carmelo Mignosa, head of the hospital's cardiac surgery unit and chair of the technical commission for a supply tender of 122 lots with a reserve price of 17,008,200 euros, launched by the trust on 21 January 2022. Both were arrested in the act and both admitted the charges when questioned. Fabiano said the money was meant to ingratiate himself with the doctor in the hope of more orders, and denied supplying draft specifications. A search of Mignosa's home turned up more than 21,000 euros said to have come from a single entrepreneur over the previous eight months.
inside: A medical supply firm's representative paid the doctor who chaired a hospital's tender commission, and passed him lists of the rival companies bidding.
cite: LiveSicilia, 14 August 2022 (custody order of the Catania preliminary investigations judge; statements to prosecutor Fabio Regolo)

n: Arad food-safety chiefs kept paying a vet concession that did no work
org_label: the company holding the Vladimirescu veterinary concession
rank: Executive director and deputy executive director, Arad Sanitary Veterinary and Food Safety Directorate
d: Romania's county sanitary veterinary and food safety directorates inspect animal health and food premises and pay private vets to run local districts under concession. On 18 June 2026 the National Anticorruption Directorate opened criminal proceedings against the executive director of the Arad directorate, Marcel Rosu, his deputy Gheorghe Cioban and a state vet, Marin-Casian Paven. Prosecutors say that between August 2024 and December 2025 Rosu, helped by the other two, ordered 10,000 lei to be paid each month to the company holding the Vladimirescu district concession although he knew the vet it had named was not working there and did not attend the office, causing the directorate a loss of 170,000 lei. The deputy and the vet are also charged with taking bribes, and a company representative with giving one.
inside: A veterinary concession company kept drawing monthly public money because the directorate's own chiefs signed the payments off, two of them allegedly for bribes.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 470/I-36, 19 June 2026 (Territorial Service Timisoara)

n: Botosani environment inspectors shielded polluting firms for cash and goods
org_label: economic operators inspected in Botosani county
rank: Environment commissars, National Environmental Guard, Botosani county commissariat, and staff of the Botosani Environmental Protection Agency
d: Romania's National Environmental Guard inspects and fines polluters; the Environmental Protection Agency issues the permits. In June 2025 the National Anticorruption Directorate sent 26 defendants for trial, among them environment commissars of the Botosani county commissariat and staff of the Botosani agency, over the protection of firms that were not meeting environmental rules. Prosecutors say that between April and October 2022 they left breaches out of inspection papers or recorded untrue findings so no penalties followed, including vegetation fires they knew had been set deliberately and illegal dumping of construction waste. Some tipped off companies about complaints and planned inspections. Two commissars are said to have taken 300 to 1,000 lei and goods, including three tonnes of waste timber and 500kg of wheat.
inside: Firms that were breaking environmental rules paid or supplied the inspectors meant to police them, and the inspection reports were written so no penalty followed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 390/VIII/3, 25 June 2025 (Territorial Service Suceava)

n: Haulage firms paid Timis road transport inspectors to wave overloaded lorries through
org_label: road haulage companies in Timis county
rank: Chief territorial inspector and county coordinator, State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, Territorial Inspectorate no. 5
d: The State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, known as ISCTR, polices lorry weights, licences and drivers' hours on Romania's roads. In June 2025 the National Anticorruption Directorate charged the chief territorial inspector of its Territorial Inspectorate no. 5, Ilie-Lucian Sirbu, his Timis county coordinator and twelve traffic inspectors. Prosecutors say that from December 2024 to May 2025 Sirbu repeatedly took sums of 2,500 euros and goods from representatives of haulage companies and from subordinates, so that inspectors under him would not penalise those firms when their lorries were caught above the legal weight. In April and May 2025 he is said to have taken 5,000 euros through an intermediary for one haulier, and on 10 June 2025 a further 1,500 euros, when prosecutors caught him in the act.
inside: Haulage firms paid the inspectorate's own chief so his inspectors would not fine their overloaded lorries, turning road weight enforcement to the payers' benefit.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 370/VIII/3, 11 June 2025 (Territorial Service Timisoara)

n: Road transport inspectors in three Romanian counties protected haulage firms
org_label: road haulage operators in Cluj, Bihor and Maramures
rank: Traffic inspectors, and the chief territorial inspector, State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, Territorial Inspectorate no. 4
d: Romania's State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, ISCTR, checks lorries on the public road network. Prosecutors of the National Anticorruption Directorate investigated how, between 2021 and 2023, traffic inspectors of its Territorial Inspectorate no. 4, serving in Maramures, Bihor and Cluj, protected several road haulage firms. They gave the firms' managers information not meant to be public about inspections that were coming, prosecutors say, and took no lawful action over breaches they found, including loads above the authorised weight and missing transport licences. Two inspectors, Ioan Orha and Cristin Viorel Tepele, are alleged to have received sums of up to 20,000 lei, directly or through intermediaries. A later release describes the same inspectorate's chief being sent for trial over protecting haulage firms between 2020 and 2023.
inside: Haulage operators got advance word of inspections and escaped penalties because inspectors inside the road transport inspectorate were paid to look after them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, indictment releases, release ids 12507 and 12660 on dna.ro (Territorial Service Cluj; monthly summary for July-August 2024)

n: Twenty transport firms and five Bacau road inspectors admitted bribery
org_label: transport companies, hauliers and driving schools in Bacau county
who: transport companies, hauliers and driving schools
rank: Traffic inspectors, State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, Territorial Inspectorate no. 3, Bacau county centre
d: In October 2025 the National Anticorruption Directorate sent the court guilty-plea agreements reached with 25 defendants. Five of them were traffic inspectors at the Bacau county centre of Territorial Inspectorate no. 3 of the State Inspectorate for Road Transport Control, each admitting bribe-taking, abuse of office and forgery of official documents in continuous form. The other twenty were representatives or employees of transport companies, hauliers or driving schools, each admitting bribery. Prosecutors found that between 6 July and 2 November 2021 the five inspectors failed to take the measures the law required when they found serious or very serious breaches in Bacau county of the rules on road use, on operating as a road transport operator, and on drivers' driving periods, breaks and rest and their recording equipment.
inside: Transport firms and driving schools paid traffic inspectors inside the road transport inspectorate, which then let their serious breaches pass without penalty.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, monthly summary of cases concluded in October 2025, release id 13262 on dna.ro (Territorial Service Bacau)

n: Care providers' gifts to the Maramures health insurance house directors
org_label: medical service and home-care provider companies in Maramures
rank: Director general and executive director for contractual relations, Maramures Health Insurance House
d: Romania's county health insurance houses hold the contracts through which the state pays clinics, home-care providers and hospitals. In December 2024 the National Anticorruption Directorate sent for trial Carmen Eleonora Prodan, director general of the Maramures house, on nine counts of bribe-taking, and brought guilty-plea agreements for her contractual relations director and two people charged with giving bribes. Prosecutors say that between March and December 2023 the two directors took sums of between 300 and 5,000 lei and other benefits from businesspeople and hospital managers, for carrying out their duties on the signing and smooth running of contracts between companies or health units and the institution they ran. Investigators found a real concern among providers in contract with the house to keep the two women's goodwill.
inside: Companies paid the directors of the state body that signs and pays their health contracts, and those contracts were then concluded and run to suit them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release no. 886/VIII/3, 12 December 2024, and no. 8/VIII/3, 12 January 2024 (Territorial Service Cluj, Baia Mare office)

n: Logging firm's cash closed a forestry guard inspection at Ramnicu Valcea
rank: Control adviser, Ramnicu Valcea Forestry Guard
d: Romania's forestry guards are state bodies that police logging. The National Anticorruption Directorate sent for trial Nicu-Gabriel Simionescu, at the time a control adviser at the Ramnicu Valcea Forestry Guard, for bribe-taking, together with the administrator of a timber exploitation company, charged with giving a bribe. Prosecutors say that on 23 August 2022, during inspections of the man's company, Simionescu received a sum of money connected with the exercise of his duties. The money, they say, was handed over so that he would not fine the company for failing to clear the ground from which it had taken timber, and so would close the inspection in a way favourable to it. The file went to the Gorj tribunal, with assets of the defendants provisionally seized.
inside: A logging company paid the state forestry inspector checking it, and the inspection closed in the company's favour with no fine for leaving the ground uncleared.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, monthly summary of cases concluded in February 2024, release id 12474 on dna.ro (Territorial Service Craiova)

n: Recycling firm's 5,000 lei stopped a Prahova environment fine
org_label: a recyclable materials company in Blejoi
rank: Commissar, National Environmental Guard, Prahova county commissariat
d: The National Environmental Guard is the Romanian state body that inspects and fines breaches of environmental law. In September 2024 the National Anticorruption Directorate charged Aristide-Valentin Turcea, a commissar of its Prahova county commissariat, with bribe-taking, and the administrator of a company with giving a bribe. Prosecutors say that during an inspection on 29 and 30 January 2024 at the firm's site in the commune of Blejoi, Turcea found it had stored collected recyclable material improperly, an offence carrying a fine of between 50,000 and 100,000 lei, and asked for 5,000 lei not to impose it. On the evening of 31 January 2024, in Ploiesti, he is said to have taken the 5,000 lei directly, and the penalty was not applied.
inside: A recycling company paid the environment commissar inspecting it, and the fine of up to 100,000 lei that his own finding required was never imposed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticoruptie, press release, release id 12670 on dna.ro (Territorial Service Ploiesti)

n: Kazakh fisheries committee chiefs jailed for systematic bribes from business
org_label: small and medium businesses in the Kazakh fisheries sector
rank: Chairman of the Fisheries Committee of the Ministry of Agriculture, and head of its department for the protection of fish resources and regulation of fishing
d: The Fisheries Committee of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture licenses and polices commercial fishing. The inter-district criminal court of Astana convicted its chairman, Nariman Zhunusov, and his subordinate Yerasyl Suyukbayev, who headed the department for the protection of fish resources and the regulation of fishing. Each was sentenced to six years in prison and barred from holding public office. According to the state news agency, citing the anti-corruption service, the two were accused of taking bribes on a systematic basis from representatives of small and medium business between 2021 and February 2024 in exchange for general patronage. The report of 19 June 2024 does not say which licences or decisions the payments bought, and names none of the businesses.
inside: Fishing businesses paid the chiefs of the state committee that regulates them, and the court found the two had sold their general patronage over the sector.
cite: Kazpravda, 19 June 2024, citing the Anti-Corruption Agency (Antikor), on the sentence of the Astana inter-district criminal court

n: Ghana charges the illegal-mining committee's secretary over a licence bribe
who: ORR Resources Enterprise and Benjamin Adjapong
rank: Secretary of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Illegal Mining
d: Ghana's Inter-Ministerial Committee on Illegal Mining was set up in March 2017 to vet and verify small-scale mining firms and decide which could resume work after a ban. Its secretary, Charles Cromwell Nanabanyin Onuawonto Bissue, a former presidential staffer, was the officer chiefly responsible for that vetting. The Office of the Special Prosecutor has charged him with fifteen counts including using public office for profit, corruption by a public officer and bribery. Its facts sheet says the evidence would establish that Bissue, with the collaboration of Anthony Thomas Owusu, received 35,000 cedis from one Benjamin Adjapong to circumvent the committee's own requirements and unlawfully secure a fast-tracked renewal of an expired mining licence for ORR Resources Enterprise without valid documentation. Bissue pleaded not guilty and is on bail.
inside: A mining firm's money reached the official who vetted mining licences, and prosecutors say the committee then fast-tracked its expired licence without the papers required.
cite: Ghanaian Times, on the OSP facts sheet signed by the Director of Prosecutions; Office of the Special Prosecutor, case profile CR/0559/2025 The Republic v Charles Cromwell Nanabanyin Onuawonto Bissue & 2 Ors (https://osp.gov.gh/case_files/case_profile/7/cases/)

n: Militia commander Bahrun sat inside Libya's Zawiyah security directorate
rank: Commander of the Al Isnad Force, Zawiyah General Security Directorate
d: Mohamed Bahrun, known as Al Far, commands an armed force called the Isnad Force, which the UN Panel of Experts on Libya placed inside the Zawiyah General Security Directorate of Libya's interior ministry. Libya's Office of the Attorney General issued an arrest warrant for him on 17 October 2017 under case No. 131, suspecting him of belonging to Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant-Libya. In July 2017 he wrote to the Prime Minister on interior ministry letterhead, signing as head of the Isnad Force. In March 2018 the head of the Zawiyah Security Directorate wrote to the Minister of the Interior confirming Bahrun's membership, contested the warrant and implicitly refused to execute it. The Panel reported in 2021 that the warrants remained valid and that he had refused subpoenas.
inside: An armed group's commander held a post in the city security directorate, which then declined to arrest him on a prosecutor's warrant.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2021/229 (8 March 2021), para. 15 and annex 8 ('The Case of Mohamed Bahrun'), pp. 77-82

n: Libya's Presidency Council made two militia leaders deputy spy chiefs
org_label: Western Joint Security Room and the Ghenewa militia
who: Western Joint Security Room; Ghenewa militia
rank: Deputy head of the General Intelligence Service; deputy head of the Internal Security Service
d: On 8 September 2020 Libya's Presidency Council appointed two armed group leaders to deputy posts in its intelligence services: Imad Trabelsi, formerly of the Western Joint Security Room, as deputy head of the General Intelligence Service by decree 595, and Lotfi Harari, formerly of the Ghenewa militia, as deputy head of the Internal Security Service by decree 596. Both services report directly to the Council. The UN Panel of Experts on Libya set the appointments out in an annex titled 'Continued encroachment of armed groups on state institutions'. On 17 January 2021 the Council also appointed the Ghenewa militia leader Abdel Ghani Belgassem Khalifa to head a new Stability Support Service. By 2024 the Panel recorded Harari as head of the Internal Security Agency in Tripoli.
inside: Two militia leaders were given the deputy posts in Libya's intelligence and internal security services, which then answered to the council that appointed them.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2021/229 (8 March 2021), annex 6 ('Continued encroachment of armed groups on state institutions'), p. 72; S/2024/914, annex 20, appendix B

n: Libya gave a Haftar-allied brigade chief a new state force in the south
rank: Head of the Counter-Terrorism and Organized Crime Force in the Libyan south
d: On 17 June 2021 Libya's Presidential Council, acting as commander-in-chief of the Libyan army, created a Counter-Terrorism and Organized Crime Force in the Libyan south by decision No. 7. The decision says the force is made up of the first company of the 116th infantry brigade and is subordinate to the commander-in-chief, and gives it powers to apprehend armed gangs and confront terrorism through arrests and investigations. By decision No. 9 the same day the Council appointed Masoud Abdallah Masoud Abdeljallil, known as Masoud Jeddi, as the force's commander. The UN Panel of Experts on Libya records that he was then commander of the 116 brigade and the main military ally of the Haftar Affiliated Forces in Sabha. On 11 September 2021 Khalifa Haftar issued a decree disbanding the brigade.
inside: An armed brigade's commander and one of its companies were turned into a state counter-terrorism force under his own command.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2022/427 (27 May 2022), para. 17 and annex 10 ('Decrees by the Presidential Council'), pp. 72-75

n: Militia deputy Ayub Aburas made head of Libya's Presidential Guard
who: Tripoli Revolutionary Brigade / Stability Support Apparatus
rank: Head of the Presidential Guard
d: The UN Panel of Experts on Libya recorded in May 2022 that Ayub Aburas, from the Tripoli Revolutionary Brigade and one of the deputies of the armed group leader known as Ghenewa, had been appointed head of the Presidential Guard. The Panel gave the appointment as an illustration of the incumbent Prime Minister Abdulhamid Al Dabiba's efforts to win the support of the Stability Support Apparatus, the force the Presidential Council created on 11 January 2021 and which Ghenewa commands. It gave no date for Aburas's appointment. The Panel also reported that the Council had had to postpone replacing the commander of the Tripoli Military Zone, a close ally of Ghenewa.
inside: A Tripoli armed group's deputy was made head of the guard that protects Libya's government, part of a bid to buy the group's support.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2022/427 (27 May 2022), para. 14 and footnote 24

n: Libya's cabinet made revolutionary brigades into a state security body
rank: National Support Forces Authority, subsidiary to the Cabinet
d: On 22 May 2023 the cabinet of Libya's Government of National Unity established a National Support Forces Authority by decision No. 313, a security force based in Tripoli operating directly under Prime Minister Abdulhamid Al Dabiba. The decision says the Authority shall bring together members of support forces and the 17 February Revolutionaries' Brigades in order to restructure them, defines members of the support forces as the 17 February Revolutionaries, civilians who take part in military operations and trainers assigned from the military and security services, and gives it powers to support the army at Libya's borders and the interior ministry at sovereign installations. The UN Panel of Experts on Libya said the new force's composition, mandate and capabilities remained vague.
inside: Revolutionary brigades were written into a new state security authority with its own budget, answering directly to the prime minister who created it.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2023/673 (12 September 2023), para. 16 and annex 9 ('Decree establishing the National Force Support Authority (NFSA)'), pp. 67-70

n: Militia figure heading Tripoli's security agency held people who crossed it
org_label: Lotfi Harari and the Internal Security Agency, Tripoli
who: Lotfi Harari (formerly of the Ghenewa militia)
rank: Head of the Internal Security Agency, Tripoli
d: The UN Panel of Experts on Libya identified Lotfi Harari, head of the Internal Security Agency in Tripoli, as directly responsible for five cases of unlawful arrest and detention, enforced disappearance and degrading treatment in temporary facilities under the Agency's control. Harari came from the Ghenewa militia and was appointed deputy head of the Internal Security Service in September 2020. The Panel found he personally picked victims as punishment for behaviour that conflicted with the Agency's interests, that they were held up to 72 hours without any review, and that forced confessions were recorded and published. The Agency contested the findings, arguing that trial proceedings fall outside its mandate and that its leadership cannot be reduced to one person. It supplied no documentation, and the Panel reaffirmed its findings.
inside: A militia figure placed at the head of a state security agency used its detention powers against people who crossed the agency's own interests.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2024/914 (3 December 2024), annex 20, appendix B ('Violations of international human rights law committed in places of detention under the control of ISA-Tripoli'), pp. 106-107; S/2021/229, annex 6

n: Libya's eastern security agency closed election centres before the vote
rank: Internal Security Agency in the east
d: The UN Panel of Experts on Libya identified 16 incidents that obstructed or undermined the second round of Libya's municipal council elections in August 2025, and found that all of them involved perpetrators that were armed actors or security apparatuses operating under the de facto authority of armed groups. Among them, the Panel found that the Internal Security Agency in the east, in an organised, simultaneous and systematic manner, prevented the distribution of voter cards, confiscated cards already handed out, confiscated ballot boxes and closed election centres in Benghazi, Tobruq, Marj, Brak al-Shati, Sabha and Sirte in the days before the planned vote of 16 August 2025. In some cases the Agency arrived the night before or on the day, armed and threatening, to enforce the closures.
inside: A state security agency under the de facto authority of armed groups used its powers to stop the local elections in eastern Libya.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, S/2026/224 (24 March 2026), para. 47 and annex 15 ('Acts that obstruct or undermine the successful completion of the political transition in Libya'), paras. 3, 9 and 10, pp. 121-122

n: Janjaweed chief Ali Kushayb put in charge of a Sudanese police force
rank: Head of the central reserve police in Um Dafug, South Darfur
d: The UN Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic recorded, while tracing his movements in 2020, that Ali Kushayb is a former Janjaweed chief who was integrated into the Sudanese security forces in 2006 as head of the central reserve police in Um Dafug, South Darfur. The Janjaweed were militias that fought in Darfur. The Panel reported that he had left Sudan for the Central African Republic, reportedly facing arrest by the International Criminal Court, and was hosted in mid-February 2020 at the residence of the Sultan of Birao. He surrendered to the Court in 2020. On 6 October 2025 the Court found him guilty on 27 counts of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in West Darfur between August 2003 and March 2004.
inside: A militia commander was given command of a state police force in Darfur, putting the militia's own man in charge of policing where it operated.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on the Central African Republic, S/2020/662 (6 July 2020), para. 40 and footnotes 10 and 12; UN News, 6 October 2025, on the ICC judgment

n: Houthi trader made Yemen's assistant defence minister for logistics
rank: Assistant minister of defence for logistics, with the rank of major general; commander of the logistics support authority
d: The UN Panel of Experts on Yemen gathered information that Saleh Mesfer Saleh Alshaer was not a member of the Yemeni armed forces before the Houthis took power. It obtained copies of his passports giving his profession as worker in 2000 and trader in 2013, and noted that Houthi media presented him on 29 January 2018 as assistant minister of defence for logistics with the rank of major general. He was then appointed commander of the logistics support authority on 15 September 2018. A special criminal court in Sana'a also designated him judicial custodian of funds and assets taken from Houthi opponents, and the Panel said he is involved in widespread unlawful appropriation of their property without judicial due process.
inside: A trader with no prior service in the armed forces was given a Yemeni defence ministry post and a general's rank, running logistics for the movement.
cite: UN Panel of Experts on Yemen, S/2020/326 (28 April 2020), annex 26 ('Unlawful appropriation by major general Saleh Mesfer Alshaer network'), paras. 1-3

n: Houthi defence ministry's procurement director ran its arms shipments
rank: Director of procurement, Houthi-appointed ministry of defence
