He was sentenced on 18 March 2024 to 15 months in federal prison and three years of supervised release for his part in a conspiracy to smuggle contraband into the prison in exchange for money. The prosecutor said that corruption by any public official or law enforcement officer is unacceptable, and that Herrera had dishonoured the law he swore to uphold. The release does not name the facility, so the record places him at the seat of the federal district that prosecuted him.
inside: Payers bought a serving federal prison officer, who carried their goods through the gates as part of a wider conspiracy.
cite: United States v. Nickolas Carlos Herrera, D. Or., sentenced 18 March 2024; Department of Justice press release, 18 March 2024

n: A supplier's president paid a VA hospital buyer for orders never delivered
org_label: A medical supply company selling to the Jesse Brown VA Medical Center
who: The president of a medical supply company
rank: Procurement supervisor, Jesse Brown Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Chicago
d: The Jesse Brown Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Chicago is a public hospital, and its procurement supervisor decides which suppliers it orders from. Thomas E. Duncan, 40, held that post. He took kickbacks from the president of a medical supply company and in return steered orders to that company, orders the hospital paid for but never received. He pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and on 11 April 2024 was sentenced to seven years in federal prison and ordered to pay restitution of more than a million dollars. Under ruling 17 a public hospital reached through its own officers is a company rather than a ministry.
inside: A supplier paid the hospital's buyer, and the hospital paid for goods that the supplier never delivered.
cite: United States v. Thomas E. Duncan, N.D. Ill., guilty plea 2023, sentenced 11 April 2024; Department of Justice press release, 15 April 2024

n: A Californian inmate bought a state officer to bring in dental moulds and a grill
org_label: Contraband supply at Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility
who: Shawn Brown, an inmate of the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility
rank: Corrections officer, California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation
d: Shawn Brown was an inmate at the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility, a California state prison in San Diego. On 24 April 2024 he was sentenced to 30 months in prison for bribing a state corrections officer to smuggle contraband in to him, including dental moulds and an expensive bejewelled dental grill. A further consecutive sentence of 48 months was imposed for his part in a separate scheme to file fraudulent claims with the California Employment Development Department. The officer he paid was sentenced in the same case. The goods are unusual; the mechanism is the ordinary one.
inside: An inmate paid a state prison officer, and the officer carried what he had bought through the gates for him.
cite: United States v. Shawn Brown and a California corrections officer, S.D. Cal., sentenced 24 April 2024; Department of Justice press release, 24 April 2024

n: A transport firm paid 9,000 euros to kill a Romanian tax-fraud referral
org_label: An alternative passenger transport company in Bucharest
who: The two men running an alternative passenger transport company, through an intermediary
rank: Two antifraud inspectors and two service heads, ANAF Bucharest Regional Antifraud Directorate
d: Romania's tax administration ANAF has an antifraud directorate whose inspectors decide whether a company's irregularities become a criminal referral. In November 2024 two of its Bucharest inspectors, Marin Marius-Eduard and Aurica Costica, inspected a company in alternative passenger transport and found a series of irregularities. The men running that company asked, through an intermediary, to be spared criminal liability. A service head, Ivan Ionut-Bogdan, promised to approach a colleague, Istrati Bogdan, who headed the service the two inspectors reported to; Istrati then promised that for 9,000 euros he could get them to resolve the inspection favourably and not file the criminal referral. Prosecutors sent the case to court on plea agreements, announced 15 January 2026.
inside: A company bought the chain of command above the inspectors examining it, so the criminal referral against it was never filed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1575, 15 January 2026, on plea agreements in the case opened by communication 732/VIII/3 of 30 October 2025

n: A Romanian officer let a firm choose which price it paid to avoid a fine
org_label: A company inspected on environmental compliance in Constanta county
who: The general director of a company that had failed an environmental inspection
rank: Police officer, Constanta County Police Inspectorate, Environmental Crime Investigation Service
d: On 3 November 2025 Simineanu Florin, a police officer of the Constanta County Police Inspectorate with the power to record and penalise environmental breaches, carried out a general environmental inspection at a company in the county and found a series of irregularities. He wrote up a report of findings without imposing any fine and told the company's general director to put the problems right. On 12 November he asked that director for 20,000 lei or, alternatively, 25,000 lei, the choice being the director's, because he had not applied the penalties the law provided for what he had found. He received the money on 28 November. Prosecutors sent the case to court on a plea agreement, and on 12 January 2026 the court convicted him and imposed three years' imprisonment suspended over a three-year supervision term, with disqualification.
inside: A company bought the officer who had just inspected it, and the fines the law required were never imposed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 551, 16 January 2026, on the plea agreement in the case opened by communication 850/VIII/3 of 3 December 2025; conviction recorded in communication 253, 12 January 2026

n: A tax-evasion suspect paid a Romanian economic crime chief over his own case
org_label: A business under investigation for tax evasion in Giurgiu county
who: A person under investigation for tax evasion, a witness in the bribery case
rank: Chief commissioner, Giurgiu County Police Inspectorate, Economic Crime Investigation Service
d: Ciulei Adrian held the rank of chief commissioner in the Economic Crime Investigation Service of the Giurgiu County Police Inspectorate, the unit that builds tax evasion cases. Between December 2024 and December 2025, while handling such a case, he is alleged to have demanded and received money from a person involved in it, in five separate acts. Prosecutors sent him for trial in preventive detention, announced on 22 January 2026. Buying the outcome of your own case from inside the force investigating it is the shape ruling 3 of this map puts in scope.
inside: A tax-evasion suspect paid the police officer building the case against him, five times over, from inside the unit investigating it.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 389, 22 January 2026, on the indictment in the case opened by communication 884/VIII/3 of 5 December 2025

n: A Romanian mayor demanded 200,000 lei from a company director
org_label: A commercial company dealing with Dragușeni commune
who: The administrator of a commercial company, a witness in the case
rank: Mayor of the commune of Dragușeni, Botoșani county
d: Nechita Eugen was mayor of the commune of Draguseni in Botosani county, in north-eastern Romania. Between October 2024 and February 2025, at intervals, he is alleged to have demanded 200,000 lei as a bribe from the administrator of a commercial company and to have received 90,000 lei of it in three instalments, in connection with the performance of his duties as mayor. Prosecutors sent him for trial in preventive detention on 10 February 2026. Under ruling 21 of this map a commune mayor administers a government rather than sitting in an assembly, which places the case in the cabinet class.
inside: A company's owner paid the mayor in instalments, so the commune's decisions on his business were settled by the payments.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 380, 10 February 2026, on the indictment in the case opened by communication 392/VIII/3 of 26 June 2025

n: A company paid 50,000 euros for the Romanian tax office's creditor vote
org_label: A company in insolvency seeking a new reorganisation plan
who: The representative of a company in insolvency, through an insolvency practitioner
rank: Head of legal service and executive legal director, Bucharest Regional Directorate of Public Finances, ANAF
d: When a Romanian company goes into insolvency the tax administration ANAF is often its largest creditor, so how ANAF votes at the creditors' meeting decides whether a reorganisation plan can be changed. Between May and June 2022 Topan Octavian-Ciprian, head of a legal service at ANAF's Bucharest Regional Directorate of Public Finances, is alleged to have demanded 50,000 euros, through an insolvency practitioner, from the representative of a company in insolvency. He let it be understood that through his post and his relations with the directorate's executive legal director and with officials of its Mid-Sized Taxpayers Administration he could get them to issue a letter making ANAF vote for the change. Prosecutors opened the penal action against him and the executive legal director, Popovici Tatiana, on 30 March 2026.
inside: A company in insolvency paid for the state's vote as its biggest creditor, bought from inside the tax directorate that cast it.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 214/I-36, 30 March 2026

n: A Romanian welfare directorate leaked its buying terms to one bidder
who: The administrator of SC Best Oil Sorama SRL
rank: Director general of the Arges social assistance directorate and the vice-president of Arges County Council
d: The Arges General Directorate for Social Assistance and Child Protection was buying five buildings to house vulnerable adults, under two projects for protected housing and a respite centre. From January 2023 its director general Eftime Tatiana, the vice-president of Arges County Council Nicolaescu Marius-Florinel, and a third official, Gogoase Adela, are alleged to have passed the administrator of SC Best Oil Sorama SRL information not meant to be public and obtained in the course of their duties: the technical specifications of the buildings to be bought, the price that would be offered for each, the period in which the purchases would be made and the method of acquisition. Prosecutors sent them for trial, announced 8 April 2026.
inside: One bidder was given the directorate's own price, specifications and timing in advance, so it knew what to offer before anyone else.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1172, 8 April 2026, on the indictment in the case opened by communication 1126/VIII/3 of 4 December 2023

n: Company owners paid a Romanian antifraud inspector to stand his colleagues down
org_label: Several Romanian commercial companies under tax inspection
who: Administrators of several commercial companies, paying directly and through intermediaries
rank: Senior fiscal antifraud inspector, National Agency for Fiscal Administration (ANAF)
d: Dimitriu Andrei-Petru was a senior fiscal antifraud inspector at Romania's tax administration, ANAF. Between January and May 2025 he is alleged to have demanded various sums and received for himself 52,800 lei and 3,000 euros from the administrators of several commercial companies, both directly and through intermediaries. In return he was to use the influence he let it be understood he had over his fellow ANAF officials, so that they would not carry out acts that fell within their duties. The charge is influence peddling rather than simple bribery, which is the shape this corpus most often takes: the inspector sells not his own decision but his colleagues'.
inside: Company owners paid an antifraud inspector to work on his colleagues, so the duties they owed the state went unperformed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication of 8 May 2026 on the indictment

n: A tax-evasion suspect paid 50,000 lei to a Bucharest economic crime chief
org_label: A business under investigation for tax evasion in Bucharest
who: A person under investigation as a suspect in a tax evasion case
rank: Chief commissioner of judicial police, Sector 3 Police, Economic Crime Investigation Service
d: Sirbu Catalin-George was a judicial police officer with the rank of chief commissioner in the Economic Crime Investigation Service of Sector 3 Police in Bucharest. In May 2026 he is alleged to have demanded 50,000 lei from a person under investigation as a suspect in a tax evasion case, in return for exercising his duties favourably on certain investigative steps and for making other steps in the file partial. He received the money on 28 May 2026, and anticorruption prosecutors recorded the offence as it happened. Ruling 3 of this map puts buying the outcome of your own case in scope.
inside: A tax-evasion suspect paid the officer handling his file to steer the investigation, and was caught handing the money over.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 294, 29 May 2026

n: A contractor paid a Romanian mayor 500,000 lei to release road payments
org_label: A contractor on the Mihalaseni local roads contract
who: The administrator of the company holding an 11.65m lei roads contract
rank: Mayor of the commune of Mihalaseni, Botosani county
d: In 2023 the commune of Mihalaseni in Botosani county signed a works contract worth 11,654,162.34 lei to modernise local roads. Between April 2024 and 2 April 2025 its mayor, Chelariu Claudiu Daniel, is alleged to have repeatedly demanded a total of 550,000 lei as a bribe from the company's administrator, and to have received 500,000 lei of it, in connection with his duties over the payments due under that contract. Prosecutors sent him for trial on four counts of taking a bribe in continuous form, announced on 5 June 2026. The mechanism is the commonest in this corpus: the official who signs the payment sells the signature.
inside: A road contractor paid the mayor half a million lei, because the mayor decided when the contract's money was released.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 371, 5 June 2026, on the indictment

n: A Romanian officer sold influence over a colleague and a magistrate
org_label: A commercial company whose administrator was approached
who: The administrator of a commercial company, approached through an intermediary
rank: Subcommissioner, Olt County Police Inspectorate, Economic Crime Investigation Service
d: Georgescu Iulian Alexandru was a police subcommissioner in the Economic Crime Investigation Service of the Olt County Police Inspectorate. In early October 2024 and again in February 2025 he is alleged to have demanded money from the administrator of a commercial company, through an intermediary: first an unspecified sum, then 4,000 to 5,000 euros, finally raised to 6,000 euros. He let it be understood that he had influence over another police officer, a colleague of his, and over a magistrate, and promised to intervene with them. He was detained for 24 hours on 30 April 2026 and prosecutors sent the case to court, announced on 23 June 2026.
inside: A company owner was sold access to a police colleague and a judge by the officer claiming to hold sway over both.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications of 30 April 2026 and 669, 23 June 2026

n: A businessman promised 1.5m euros for a 21m lei Romanian VAT refund
org_label: A commercial company seeking a VAT refund
who: A businessman administering the company that would receive the refund
rank: Senior inspector, Timisoara Regional Directorate of Public Finances, ANAF
d: A VAT refund is paid out by Romania's tax administration ANAF after its officials approve the claim. On 4 December 2025 Crainic Ion-Dacian, a senior inspector at ANAF's Timisoara Regional Directorate of Public Finances, is alleged to have accepted directly a businessman's promise of 1,500,000 euros. In return he was to work on the ANAF Timisoara officials he let it be understood he had influence over, so that they would approve a VAT refund worth about 21,000,000 lei to the company the businessman represented. Prosecutors opened the penal action against both for influence peddling, announced on 3 September 2026. The promised bribe is the largest single figure in the Romanian releases the map has read.
inside: A businessman offered 1.5m euros to have the tax office approve his own 21m lei refund, bought through an inspector's pull with colleagues.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 619, 3 September 2026

n: Smugglers paid 200 euros a run to cross a Romanian border post from Ukraine
org_label: A smuggling operation moving goods from Ukraine through Racovat
who: A smuggler paying per crossing to use a particular officer's shift
rank: Customs workers, Iasi Regional Customs Directorate, Racovat border crossing
d: The Racovat crossing in Botosani county is a Romanian border post on the frontier with Ukraine, staffed in shifts by customs workers of the Iasi Regional Customs Directorate. Between October 2024 and January 2025 Fediuc Loredana, a customs worker there, is alleged to have repeatedly received 200 euros at a time from one man so that he could cross the post on her shift carrying goods that were prohibited or over the legal limit, brought in from Ukraine, without the required documents and without the legal measures being applied. Prosecutors also opened the penal action against a second customs worker at the same post, Pomparau Octavian Alexandru, in an update of 17 November 2026.
inside: A smuggler bought a particular officer's shift at the border post, so his loads crossed whenever she was on duty.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1913, 22 September 2026, with the update of 17 November 2026

n: A water-works contractor paid a Romanian mayor 15,000 euros as a first instalment
org_label: A contractor on the Slanic-Moldova water supply works
who: The representative of the company holding the water supply contract
rank: Mayor of the town of Slanic-Moldova, Bacau county
d: In 2025 the town hall of Slanic-Moldova in Bacau county signed a services contract worth 1,464,349.43 lei with a commercial company, for emergency works to restore the town's drinking water supply from its drain. On 23 July 2026 the mayor, Moraru Benone, is alleged to have received 15,000 euros from that company's representative as a bribe, described by prosecutors as a first instalment, in connection with the contract. Prosecutors opened the penal action and detained him for 24 hours from 27 October 2026. A first instalment implies the rest was still to come when the arrangement was stopped.
inside: The contractor repairing a town's water supply paid its mayor, in instalments, over the contract he controlled.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 396, 28 October 2026

n: An inspected company paid 3,000 lei to narrow a Romanian tax inspection
org_label: A commercial company under unannounced tax inspection
who: The administrator of the company being inspected
rank: Antifraud inspector, ANAF Bucharest Regional Antifraud Directorate
d: In October 2025 Nistor Constantin, an antifraud inspector at ANAF's Bucharest Regional Antifraud Directorate, carried out an unannounced operational inspection at a commercial company and found several irregularities in its activity. He is alleged to have then demanded 3,000 lei from the company's administrator as a bribe, so that he would limit the inspection to certain aspects only and not take it further. The sum is small and the mechanism is exact: what was bought was not a decision but the scope of the examination, which is cheaper and harder to see.
inside: A company paid the inspector examining it to look at less, so the inspection stopped before it reached what mattered.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1360, 9 December 2025

n: Developers paid Mangalia's mayor 622,233 euros for planning documents
org_label: Developers seeking Mangalia planning documents and council decisions
who: Parties seeking urban planning documents and local council decisions, paying directly and through an intermediary
rank: Mayor of the municipality of Mangalia
d: A Romanian mayor issues the urban planning documents that decide what may be built, and can put items before the local council. Between 2022 and 2025 Radu Cristian, mayor of the Black Sea municipality of Mangalia, is alleged to have demanded and received a total of 622,233 euros, both directly and through an intermediary, in connection with issuing such planning documents, with initiating local council decisions, and with other matters belonging to his office. Prosecutors sent him for trial on two counts of taking a bribe in continuous form, together with money laundering and incitement to misuse a company's assets, announced on 18 December 2025.
inside: Developers paid the mayor 622,233 euros, and the planning permissions and council motions followed the money.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 709, 18 December 2025, on the indictment

n: A county council president put his group on the state water company's board
org_label: An organised group around the president of Brasov County Council
who: An organised criminal group formed to take control of the county water company's resources
rank: Two placed members of the board of administration of SC Compania Apa Brasov SA
d: SC Compania Apa Brasov SA is the state-owned water company for the Brasov region, and A.D.I.D.A.J. Brasov is the public authority that supervises it. Between 20 March 2024 and 18 September 2025 Serban Todorica Constantin, vice-president and then president of Brasov County Council and president of A.D.I.D.A.J., is alleged to have formed an organised criminal group with Dragomir Liviu, Cocos Liviu and Top Ferghete Floriana Carmen, joined later by two others, to take control of the resources the water company managed. He is alleged to have rigged the appointment procedure to install Cocos and Top Ferghete on the company's board of administration, by first employing Dragomir at the supervising authority and then naming him president of the commission that selected that board.
inside: A group captured the commission that picks a state water company's board, then put two of its own members on that board.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1289, 23 December 2025, on the indictment, which also charges SC Ewora Resurse Umane SRL

n: A company owner paid a Romanian town hospital manager 15,000 euros
org_label: A commercial company dealing with Cernavoda Town Hospital
who: The administrator of a commercial company, paying through an intermediary
rank: Manager of Cernavoda Town Hospital, Constanta county
d: Cernavoda Town Hospital in Constanta county is funded from the budget of the Cernavoda local authority, and under ruling 17 a public hospital reached through its own officers is a company rather than a ministry. In January 2025, on a prior agreement, its manager Sponoche Marius Ion is alleged to have demanded 30,000 euros, through an intermediary named as a suspect in the case, from the administrator of a commercial company, and to have received 15,000 euros of it on 11 February 2025. Prosecutors opened the penal action against him for taking a bribe.
inside: A supplier paid the hospital's manager through a go-between, so what the hospital decided on his business was settled in advance.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 512, 11 February 2025

n: Businessmen paid Romania's maritime ports directors up to 100,000 euros
org_label: Businesses operating in the Port of Constanta
who: Several businessmen and company representatives operating in the Port of Constanta
rank: Technical director and commercial director, C.N. Administratia Porturilor Maritime S.A. Constanta
d: C.N. Administratia Porturilor Maritime S.A. Constanta is the Romanian state company that runs the country's maritime ports, including Constanta, the largest on the Black Sea. Between 2024 and 2025 several businessmen and company representatives are alleged to have promised and handed its technical director, Chirila Florin-Laurentiu, and its commercial director, Visan George-Gabriel, sums of money ranging from 2,000 to 100,000 euros, along with other goods, in return for support and help in developing the businesses they ran in the port area. Prosecutors opened the penal action against both directors for taking bribes, announced on 25 February 2025.
inside: Port businesses paid the two directors who ran the state ports company, and the help they needed came from inside it.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1349, 25 February 2025

n: A Romanian customs chief ran a bribe-collection system on Port Constanta imports
org_label: Importers using Port Constanta South Agigea, through customs brokers
who: Importers of goods through Port Constanta South Agigea, paying via customs brokers
rank: Head of the Constanta South border customs office, a customs inspector and a courier
d: In 2024 an organised criminal group formed inside the Constanta South border customs office, made up of its head, Cadir Sunai, the customs inspector Oprea Marius and Petcu Dorel-Emanuel. Its purpose was to collect bribes from importers bringing goods through Port Constanta South Agigea, taken through customs brokers, in exchange for performing the office's duties by speeding up customs clearance. Cadir is alleged to have designated Oprea to collect the money from importers and Petcu to take it and move it to places of safety. The collection ran from 13 June to 12 September 2024. Five customs inspectors at the same border office were separately convicted on 17 February 2025, each receiving three years suspended.
inside: The head of a border customs office organised his own staff to collect payments from importers, with a courier to move the cash.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 952, 4 March 2025, with the separate convictions of five customs inspectors at the same office recorded on 17 February 2025

n: A Romanian health director took a building plot as her bribe
org_label: A company leasing premises to the Olt Public Health Directorate
who: The administrator of a company holding a lease contract with the directorate
rank: Executive director, Olt County Public Health Directorate
d: In April 2021, while a lease contract was running between the Olt County Public Health Directorate and a company administered by a man named in the case as P.S.A., the directorate's executive director Ionita Elena is alleged to have accepted from him, as a bribe, a plot of land of 612 square metres in the town of Slatina, in an area with property development potential, so that the lease would run smoothly. Prosecutors also found that between 2023 and 2024 she signed the payment ordinances and ordered rent paid to a commercial company in sums that were not in the budget the Health Ministry had approved, causing a loss. She was charged with abuse of office in continuous form and two counts of taking a bribe. A bribe paid in land rather than cash is unusual in this corpus and harder to trace than a transfer.
inside: A landlord paid the health directorate's own director in development land, and the contract she oversaw ran smoothly for him.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 866, 7 April 2025

n: A farmer paid to be given the state compensation he was already owed
org_label: A farming company owed state compensation
who: A farmer, representative of a commercial company owed compensation by the Romanian state
rank: Executive director, Tulcea Sanitary Veterinary and Food Safety Directorate
d: The Romanian state pays compensation to farmers whose animals are culled in disease control, and it is paid out in instalments by the county sanitary veterinary and food safety directorate. In December 2024 the executive director of the Tulcea directorate, Tuchila Mitica, is alleged to have demanded 50,000 euros from a farmer representing a commercial company, and to have received 25,000 euros of it through an intermediary that month, with a further 11,000 euros on 15 April 2025. What the money bought was the payment of the compensation instalments the state already owed the farmer. He was placed in preventive detention on 16 April 2025.
inside: A farmer had to pay 25,000 euros, then 11,000 more, to the official who released the compensation the state already owed him.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 329, 17 April 2025 and 734, 10 June 2025

n: Six Romanian customs officials collected from shopping-centre traders
org_label: Traders in Bucharest and Ilfov commercial centres
who: Several businessmen operating in commercial centres in Bucharest and Ilfov county
rank: Six customs officials, and an intermediary selling influence over the border police
d: Between July and August 2023, while carrying out inspections, six Romanian customs officials named as Teianu Nicolae-Stefan, Cernat Alexandru, Marin Marius, Vulcan Marian-Vladimir, Gheorghe Demetrius and Urluceanu Ion are alleged to have demanded and received from several businessmen trading in commercial centres in Bucharest and Ilfov county a total of 52,600 lei, 5,000 US dollars, 5,600 euros and other benefits. In the same case Stamatescu Razvan-Cosmin is alleged to have accepted a businessman's promise of 10,000 US dollars for trafficking the influence he claimed to have over border police officers, so that they would not perform their duties.
inside: Six customs officials took payments from the traders they were inspecting, and a go-between sold the border police on top.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 851, 2 July 2025

n: A company promised a million euros for influence over Romania's tax officials
org_label: A commercial company with business before ANAF
who: A company administrator named in the case as G.F.M.
rank: Senior inspector, Bucharest Regional Directorate of Public Finances, ANAF
d: In the first half of 2023 Sirbu Florin, a senior inspector at ANAF's Bucharest Regional Directorate of Public Finances, is alleged to have accepted a promise from a company administrator named in the case as G.F.M. of 1,000,000 euros, and between September and October 2023 to have actually received from him more than 1,000,000 lei, on the claim that he had influence over officials of that directorate. Prosecutors charged him with influence peddling, false declarations, and using or allowing access to information not meant to be public. The promised figure is among the largest in the Romanian releases the map has read.
inside: A company promised a tax inspector a million euros for his pull with the colleagues who would decide its affairs.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 558, 7 July 2025

n: A Romanian commune mayor took 145,000 lei across six bribery counts
org_label: Companies seeking contracts from Troianul commune
who: Representatives of several commercial companies seeking commune contracts
rank: Mayor of the commune of Troianul, Teleorman county
d: Between 2021 and 2025 Neagu Ionel, mayor of the commune of Troianul in Teleorman county, is alleged to have demanded and received from the representatives of several commercial companies a total of 145,000 lei, in return for awarding contracts preferentially or for buying goods from a particular company. Prosecutors recorded six counts of taking a bribe against him and continued the investigation against five further individual suspects. The pattern across this corpus is that the commune, not the ministry, is where most of these arrangements sit, because one signature there controls the whole procurement.
inside: Companies paid a commune mayor in instalments across four years, and the commune's contracts and purchases went to them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 853, 8 August 2025

n: A contractor paid a Romanian mayor to speed his public works payments
org_label: A contractor on Mihai Eminescu commune's public works
who: The de facto administrator of a company holding commune contracts
rank: Mayor of the commune of Mihai Eminescu, Botosani county
d: Between July 2022 and March 2025 Gireada Dumitru-Verginel, mayor of the commune of Mihai Eminescu in Botosani county, demanded and received for himself and for others money, goods and other benefits from the de facto administrator of a company, in connection with his duties: facilitating the award of public procurement contracts, and carrying through and speeding up the approval of payments on public works contracts. Prosecutors sent him for trial on five counts of taking a bribe in continuous form on 11 November 2025, and on 5 November 2025 a court convicted him and imposed three years' imprisonment suspended over a four-year supervision term.
inside: A contractor paid the mayor both to win the commune's contracts and to have the money on them released faster.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 643, 11 November 2025 and 238, 5 November 2025 on the conviction

n: Driving instructors bought rigged licence exams from a police group in Suceava
org_label: Driving schools and instructors buying passes in Suceava
who: Driving instructors and others paying on candidates' behalf
rank: Examining agents of the Suceava driving licence and vehicle registration service
d: The SPCRPCIV is the Romanian public service that runs driving tests and vehicle registration, and its examining agents decide who passes the practical test. From January 2020 a group of examining agents at the Suceava service joined an organised criminal group set up by chief commissioner Obreja Radu-Ionut and agent Perijoc Gheorghe-Ionel, structured on several tiers, whose purpose was to rig the practical driving examinations in exchange for money taken as bribes. Gabor Alexandru, Blindu Cristian, Pascal Anamaria and Popa Cristian are among those charged as members. Blindu is alleged to have used part of the proceeds to buy a luxury car worth 41,500 euros, registered in another person's name but for himself.
inside: A group inside the driving test service sold passes, so who could legally drive was decided by who paid its examiners.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 677, 8 January 2024 and 832, 15 July 2024

n: Five Arad examiners took 200 to 400 euros a pass through driving instructors
org_label: Driving schools and instructors buying passes in Arad
who: Candidates paying through driving instructors or other trusted intermediaries
rank: Five police examiners of the Arad driving licence and vehicle registration service
d: Prosecutors in Timisoara completed a case on corruption in the issue of driving licences by the Arad public community service for driving licences and vehicle registration. Five of its police examiners are alleged to have received from a number of people, through intermediaries who were driving instructors or other trusted persons, sums of between 200 and 400 euros each, in connection with rigging the practical driving examinations so that candidates obtained a licence. The money reached the five officers from the intermediaries rather than from the candidates directly, which is what kept the arrangement running.
inside: Driving instructors collected from candidates and paid the state examiners, so licences were issued to drivers who had not passed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 146/VIII/3, 15 February 2024

n: Twenty-one Romanian border officers took up to 600 euros a coach
org_label: Passenger transport operators running between Moldova and the EU
who: Operators carrying passengers from Moldova into EU countries and back
rank: Twenty-one police agents at the Nadlac I and Nadlac II border crossings
d: Nadlac I and Nadlac II are Romanian crossings on the border with Hungary, which for passengers travelling from Moldova is the entry to the rest of the European Union. Between August 2022 and January 2023 twenty-one police agents stationed there are alleged to have repeatedly demanded and received sums of up to 600 euros from the operators carrying those passengers, in return for not applying the legal measures where non-EU citizens had overstayed their permitted time in the Union. Prosecutors completed the investigation and sent the case to court. The number of officers is the finding: this was not individuals but the posts themselves.
inside: Coach operators paid the officers at two border crossings, so passengers who had overstayed in the EU passed without consequence.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 439, 26 March 2024

n: A Bucharest hospital manager took 5 to 10 per cent of every invoice he paid
org_label: Suppliers under contract to Clinical Hospital CF No. 2 Bucharest
who: Several businessmen in contractual relations with the hospital
rank: Manager of Clinical Hospital CF No. 2, Bucharest
d: Between September 2022 and March 2024 Bucur Serban, manager of Clinical Hospital CF No. 2 in Bucharest, is alleged to have demanded and received money from several businessmen in contractual relations with the hospital, calculated as a variable percentage of between 5 and 10 per cent of the pre-VAT value of every invoice the hospital paid that supplier. Prosecutors recorded six counts of taking a bribe, five of them in continuous form, and one of using his office to favour particular people. A standing rate on every invoice, rather than a payment for a particular decision, is what makes this a system rather than an incident.
inside: Every invoice the hospital paid carried a cut of 5 to 10 per cent back to the manager who signed it off.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 545, 12 July 2024

n: A beach trader paid a municipal company's director to work the town hall
org_label: A beach bar and sunbed business at Saturn-Venus
who: A businessman trading on the beach, with a bar and sunbed rental
rank: Director of SC Goldterm SA, the company owned by Mangalia Local Council
d: SC Goldterm SA is a commercial company belonging to Mangalia Local Council on the Romanian Black Sea coast. Between 2023 and 2024 its director, Colgiu Dorinel, is alleged to have demanded and received 15,000 euros, equivalent to 75,000 lei, in several instalments from a businessman whose premises lay beside the Saturn and Venus beaches and whose trade was selling on the beach, running a bar and renting sunbeds. What the money bought was for Colgiu to intervene with officials of Mangalia Town Hall and of the Mangalia Local Police on his behalf. Prosecutors sent him for trial on three counts of influence peddling.
inside: A beach trader paid the director of the council's own company to work on the town hall and the local police for him.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 835, 8 October 2024, on the indictment

n: A sitting Romanian senator charged over buying influence with 60,000 euros
org_label: Parties seeking a favourable outcome through the trademarks office
who: A person who paid 150,000 lei of a 60,000 euro demand
rank: Director general of the State Office for Inventions and Trademarks, with a sitting senator
d: In 2022 a man named in the case as M.R.M., at the instigation of Eugen Pirvulescu, then and still a senator in Romania's Parliament, and with the help of a further suspect and of Burcescu Marian-Catalin, then director general of the State Office for Inventions and Trademarks, is alleged to have demanded 60,000 euros from a person, of which that person handed over 150,000 lei, the equivalent of 30,000 euros. M.R.M. let it be understood that he had influence over another person. Prosecutors charged the senator with incitement to the offence of buying influence. A sitting member of parliament and the head of a national office in one arrangement is the shape this corpus most rarely produces.
inside: A sitting senator is accused of setting up the purchase of influence, with the head of the national trademarks office helping it along.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 441, 11 October 2024

n: A lawyer offered 5,000 euros to downgrade his smuggling clients' charge
org_label: A qualified smuggling operation run by two Moldovan citizens
who: Two Moldovan citizens under investigation for qualified smuggling, through their chosen lawyer
rank: Police officer, Dolj County Police Inspectorate, Economic Crime Investigation Service
d: In early October 2024 a lawyer of the Olt Bar, acting as chosen defence counsel for two Moldovan citizens under investigation by the Dolj County Police Inspectorate's Economic Crime Investigation Service for qualified smuggling, is alleged to have offered 5,000 euros as a bribe to a police officer, so that the officer would change the legal classification of what his clients had done. Prosecutors opened the penal action against the lawyer for giving a bribe. The route is worth recording: the payment to the investigating force came through the defendants' own advocate, which is how it reached the file rather than the client.
inside: A smuggling pair's own lawyer offered the investigating officer money to reclassify the charge against them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 402, 15 October 2024

n: An accountant sold access to Romania's trade registry to strike off a company
org_label: A company seeking to be struck off the trade register
who: The administrator of a company that wanted to be removed from the register
rank: Officials of the Trade Register Office attached to the Bucharest Tribunal
d: The Trade Register Office attached to the Bucharest Tribunal records which companies exist and which have been struck off, and striking a company off ends the obligations attached to it. In January 2024 a chartered accountant named in the case as G.M., directly and through a co-defendant, Nae Nicoleta-Lucia, is alleged to have demanded 10,000 euros from the administrator of a company, of which he received 5,000 euros, in order to get officials of that office to facilitate the company's removal from the register by going round the legal rules. Prosecutors sent him for trial for influence peddling in continuous form and for forging documents under private signature.
inside: A company paid through its accountant to have the state registry strike it off outside the rules, bought from officials inside the office.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 636, 25 October 2024, on the indictment

n: A sports firm paid a Romanian hospital's buyer for two direct contracts
who: The administrator of SC Bracoma Sport SRL
rank: Economist, public procurement and contracting service, Brasov County Emergency Clinical Hospital
d: A direct public procurement contract is awarded without a competition, which puts the whole decision in the hands of the officer who prepares it. On 14 May 2020 the Brasov County Emergency Clinical Hospital awarded SC Bracoma Sport SRL two such contracts worth 571,094 lei between them. In July 2020 Teodorescu Gheorghe Sorin, an economist in the hospital's public procurement, supply and contracting service, is alleged to have received 50,000 lei from that company's administrator in exchange for having awarded them preferentially. Prosecutors sent him for trial for taking a bribe. Under ruling 17 a public hospital reached through its own officers is a company.
inside: A supplier paid the hospital's procurement officer, and two no-competition contracts worth 571,094 lei went to it.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication of 15 January 2025 on the indictment

n: A contractor paid two Bacau hospital officials a first instalment of 2,000 euros
org_label: A contractor on the Bacau pneumology hospital works
who: A businessman holding the maintenance and sanitation contract
rank: Two officials of the Bacau Pneumology Hospital
d: In February 2024, while a contract was running for maintenance and sanitation works in the basement and food block of the Bacau Pneumology Hospital, two of the hospital's officials, Alexa Dragos-Constantin and Pralea Doru-Ion, are alleged to have demanded 20,000 lei from the businessman holding it, of which each received 1,000 euros as a first instalment of the sum originally demanded. The money was to favour his interests. Prosecutors also opened the penal action against the businessman for giving a bribe, which is how both sides of these arrangements reach the file.
inside: A contractor paid two hospital officials in instalments to have his interests favoured on the works he was already doing.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 449, 23 February 2024

n: Businessmen and hospital managers paid a Romanian health insurance chief
org_label: Companies and health units contracting with the Maramures Health Insurance House
who: Several businessmen and hospital managers whose contracts the house decided
rank: Director general and executive director of contractual relations, Maramures Health Insurance House
d: A Romanian county health insurance house holds the contracts through which public money reaches hospitals, clinics and suppliers, so whoever runs it decides which of them are paid. Between September and December 2023 its director general in Maramures, Prodan Carmen Eleonora, and the executive director of its contractual relations directorate, Stretea Camelia Rodica, are alleged to have received undue benefits and sums not yet quantified from several businessmen and hospital managers, for their duties in concluding those contracts and seeing them run smoothly. Eight counts of bribery were recorded against Prodan, three of them in continuous form, and the investigation continued against others.
inside: Suppliers and hospital managers paid the two officials who decided which contracts the county's health money went to.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 486, 12 January 2024

n: A Romanian mayor asked for half a pavement contractor's profit and a house
org_label: A contractor on the Zanesti pavement works
who: The administrator of the company holding the pavement contract
rank: Mayor of the commune of Zanesti, Neamt county
d: In 2023 the commune of Zanesti in Neamt county had a contract running for repairs and the extension of its pavements, worth 3,015,980.63 lei before VAT. From April to the end of that year Filip Ioan is alleged to have demanded from the company's administrator a sum amounting to roughly half the profit on the contract, for signing it, letting it run smoothly and settling the works. He is also alleged to have received other benefits from the same administrator, including the building of a house. Prosecutors placed three further defendants under judicial control. Half the profit is a share rather than a bribe, which is a different arrangement from a fee for one signature.
inside: The mayor took about half the contractor's profit on a three-million-lei job, and had a house built for him as well.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1120, 12 November 2025

n: Two people paid 12,000 euros for porter jobs at a Romanian hospital
org_label: Candidates buying posts at Radauti Municipal Hospital
who: Two people paying to be given porter posts at the hospital
rank: Interim manager and a senior nurse, Radauti Municipal Hospital
d: At the start of 2023 Luta Vlad-Vasile, a senior nurse in the emergency admissions unit of Radauti Municipal Hospital in Suceava county, is alleged to have demanded and received 6,000 euros each from two people, to intervene with the hospital's interim manager so that they would be given porter posts there. The interim manager, Sima Flaviu-Emanuel, received 12,000 euros in total from the two through the nurse. A recruitment competition was organised for the posts. The map codes paying applicants as a crime group on the convention set by its South African Home Affairs and Samoan passport records.
inside: Two outsiders paid 12,000 euros to the hospital's own manager and were given jobs inside it through a competition they had bought.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 994, 28 October 2025

n: A Botosani hospital manager took 11,000 euros and gold for jobs inside it
org_label: Candidates and staff buying posts and favours at the Mavromati hospital
who: Hospital employees and candidates in the hospital's own recruitment competitions
rank: Manager of the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital, Botosani
d: Between December 2021 and July 2022 Caba Doina, manager of the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital in Botosani, is alleged to have repeatedly received a total of 11,000 euros, together with gold jewellery valued at more than 22,000 lei, directly or through intermediaries, from the hospital's own employees and from candidates sitting the competitions and examinations the hospital organised, in connection with her duties. Prosecutors recorded twelve counts of taking a bribe in continuous form against her, with a further count of using or allowing access to information not meant to be public.
inside: The hospital's manager sold the posts and favours inside it, taking cash and gold from candidates and from her own staff.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1183, 24 September 2026

n: A later manager of the same Botosani hospital sold a hiring and a transfer
org_label: Candidates and staff buying posts at the Mavromati hospital
who: Three people, two of them her own subordinates
rank: Manager of the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital, Botosani
d: In October and December 2023 Adascalitei Monica-Delia, by then manager of the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital in Botosani, is alleged to have received sums of between 5,000 and 10,000 lei, directly or through intermediaries, from three people of whom two were her own subordinates. The payments were to approve the hiring of a person as a doctor with limited competences, to approve a transfer into the hospital from a medical unit at Saveni, and to exercise the influence she claimed over her subordinates so that they would deal with a particular party. She was presented to the Suceava Tribunal with a proposal for 30 days' preventive arrest on 20 March 2024. This is a different manager of the same hospital, in a different year, from the record above.
inside: The hospital's manager sold a doctor's post and a transfer into the hospital, taking the money from her own staff.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 476, 20 March 2024

n: Botosani hospital examiners handed candidates the exam papers
org_label: Candidates buying posts at the Mavromati hospital
who: Candidates for hospital posts who were given the questions in advance
rank: Head nurse, coordinating nurse and a third member of the hospital's examination commissions
d: Between 2020 and 2022 Titiliuc Mirela, Surugiu Anca and Anichei Claudiu held positions on the examination commissions set up at the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital in Botosani to fill posts of electrician, unskilled worker supervising dangerous psychiatric patients, debutant nurse on a fixed term, and orderly. Surugiu and Anichei are alleged to have supplied certain candidates with the questions the commission had set for the competition, so that those candidates would pass. Two counts of taking a bribe were recorded against Titiliuc. This is the third separate prosecution at this hospital that the map holds.
inside: Candidates were given the commission's own questions before the test, and took jobs inside the hospital on the strength of them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 642, 16 January 2024

n: Seven people paid 49,500 euros for jobs in a Romanian ambulance service
org_label: Candidates buying posts in the Dolj ambulance service and a railway hospital
who: Nine people who were asked, and seven who paid, for posts for themselves or relatives
rank: General manager of the Dolj County Ambulance Service, and an official of the Craiova Railway Clinical Hospital
d: Between September and October 2024 Gavan Constantin is alleged to have demanded a total of 65,500 euros from nine people and received 49,500 euros from seven of them, directly or through others, claiming influence over his son-in-law Gingioveanu Cristian, general manager of the Dolj County Ambulance Service, and his daughter Gingioveanu Aurelia Maria, who held a decision-making post at the Craiova Railway Clinical Hospital. What the payers wanted was jobs for themselves, for relatives or for others as ambulance drivers or nurses at those two health units. The Panel of charges records that the general manager then acted through Gavan and a further intermediary.
inside: Seven outsiders paid nearly 50,000 euros and were put into driver and nurse posts inside a county ambulance service.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 619, 1 November 2024 and 1397, 17 February 2026

n: A lawyer sold a move from porter to nurse at a Romanian hospital
org_label: A person buying a nursing post at Caracal Municipal Hospital
who: A person paying to be moved from a porter's post to a nurse's post
rank: Officials of Caracal Municipal Hospital, and the president of a local authority
d: On 15 October 2025 a lawyer of the Olt Bar, named in the case as R.R.N., is alleged to have demanded money of an amount he did not then specify from a person, in order to exercise the influence he claimed to have over officials of Caracal Municipal Hospital and over the president of a local authority, so that the person would be moved from a porter's post to a nurse's post at the hospital. He promised to use the same influence for a further matter. Prosecutors opened the penal action for two counts of influence peddling in continuous form and detained him for 24 hours.
inside: A nursing post inside a public hospital was offered for sale through a lawyer claiming pull with its officials.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 657, 24 October 2025 and 826, 19 November 2025

n: Anatomy staff at a Romanian medical faculty took money from resit students
org_label: Students buying passes in anatomy resits
who: Students enrolled in two anatomy resit sessions
rank: Two university assistants in the anatomy department, Faculty of Medicine, Ovidius University Constanta
d: Between May and September 2026 Talpes Raluca, a university assistant in the anatomy department of the Faculty of Medicine at Ovidius University in Constanta, with duties assessing and grading students and a seat on one of the department's examination commissions, is alleged to have demanded and repeatedly received money from students enrolled in the two anatomy resit sessions held from 6 to 12 July and 1 to 6 September 2026. The money came through three co-defendants, among them a second university assistant, Batuhan Omeroglu. Fifteen counts of taking a bribe in continuous form were recorded against her. Under ruling 17 a university, which sells a service, is a company.
inside: Students bought their anatomy passes from the assistants who graded them and sat on the examining commission.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 617, 5 September 2026

n: A Romanian exam chair sold the pharmacist-specialist papers in advance
who: A resident pharmacist sitting the specialist examination
rank: President of the examination commission for the pharmacist-specialist title, Dunarea de Jos University Galati
d: Dumitriu Buzia Olimpia was a professor at the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy of Dunarea de Jos University in Galati, president of the examination commission for the pharmacist-specialist title, and coordinator of the pharmacy residency group. Ahead of the residency examination due in November 2024 she is alleged to have accepted, on 10 October 2024, the promise of 9,200 euros from a resident pharmacist who was a candidate, and on 15 October to have supplied that candidate with the examination papers in advance, so that candidates entered for the examination would pass fraudulently and obtain the specialist title.
inside: The chair of the examining commission sold the papers in advance, so pharmacists obtained a specialist title they had not earned.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1101, 30 December 2025

n: A military hospital neurosurgeon took money for sick notes and scans
org_label: Patients buying medical certificates and referrals
who: Nine patients paying for sick leave certificates and referrals
rank: Head of neurosurgery, Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital, Bucharest
d: A medical certificate of unfitness for work is a document that carries an entitlement, which is why ruling 4 of this map treats an official paid to issue documents as infiltration. On 25 August 2024 and between April and May 2025 Colonel Mitrica Marian, head of neurosurgery and a senior neurosurgeon at the Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital in Bucharest, is alleged to have received sums of between 100 and 1,000 lei from nine patients, in connection with granting sick leave certificates and with recommending paraclinical investigations, specialist consultations and surgery. Prosecutors record that some of the certificates he drew up were not warranted. Nine counts of taking a bribe in continuous form were charged.
inside: Patients paid the head of a hospital department for sick notes, some of which the prosecutors say were not warranted at all.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 680, 20 June 2025

n: A Bucharest power plant director took 10,000 euros from a contractor
org_label: A businessman buying officers of two state-majority companies
who: A businessman who paid in cash and through bank transfers justified by simulated economic operations
rank: Director of the Bucharest South thermoelectric plant, a works site of the state-majority company Electrocentrale Bucuresti
d: Electrocentrale Bucuresti, known as ELCEN, is majority state owned and supplies the capital's heating. Prosecutors allege that a businessman gave one person a total of 533,375 lei in cash and through bank transfers justified by simulated economic operations, in connection with influence he claimed to hold over the leadership of two majority state-owned companies, and gave 10,000 euros directly to Ecobescu Adrian Dorin, director of the Bucharest South thermoelectric plant, a works site of ELCEN, in connection with an act that would have fallen within his official duties. A state-majority company's public procurement by tender opened in July 2023 forms a further part of the charges.
inside: A contractor's money reached the director of the plant itself and, through an intermediary, the leadership of two state-owned companies.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 266, 17 April 2024

n: A company gave a Romanian heating utility director a container and a generator
org_label: A company holding contracts with the Brasov heating service
who: Representatives of a company that held works and services contracts with the utility
rank: Director of the Brasov Local Public Heating Service
d: Between 2018 and 2023 Marin Ionut Mircea, director of the Brasov Local Public Heating Service, is alleged to have demanded and received goods as bribes worth 270,710.19 lei in total from representatives of a company, among them a modular container fitted with a lavatory and an electricity generator. Prosecutors say the goods were given so that the contracts the heating service had concluded with the businessmen's company would run smoothly. Precautionary measures were ordered over several of his assets and the file went to the Brasov Tribunal with a proposal to keep them. A separate set of charges against the same director concerns direct-award procurements run as a formality.
inside: A supplier's container and generator went to the director who decided whether its own contracts with the utility ran smoothly.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 388, 25 June 2024

n: A woman sold hospital and border police jobs in northern Romania
org_label: People buying jobs for themselves and their relatives
who: Several people who paid for jobs for themselves or for relatives
rank: Leadership of the Sighetu Marmatiei Municipal Hospital and of the General Inspectorate of the Border Police
d: Between 15 September 2023 and 10 July 2024 a woman identified as D.C. is alleged to have demanded and received sums from several different people, directly or through a second defendant, in order to trade on influence she let them believe she held over officials in the leadership of certain institutions, among them the General Inspectorate of the Border Police and the Sighetu Marmatiei Municipal Hospital. In exchange she is said to have promised those people that they or their relatives would be employed at those institutions. The prosecutors' order recorded 42,700 euros and 1,800 lei demanded; the indictment records 32,700 euros and 1,800 lei. From four people she is alleged to have demanded between 3,500 and 4,000 euros each.
inside: Buyers were promised that they or their relatives would be hired inside a municipal hospital and the border police.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 431, 12 July 2024 and 509, 22 August 2024

n: A Romanian MP and hospital surgeon took money from 45 patients
org_label: Patients and relatives paying a hospital surgeon
who: Forty-five patients and relatives, twenty-seven of whom are suspects for giving a bribe
rank: Specialist doctor in the operating block of the Dimitrie Castroian Municipal Hospital in Husi, and a deputy in the Romanian Parliament
d: Between 3 April and 12 July 2024 Tataru Nelu, a specialist doctor in the operating block of the Dimitrie Castroian Municipal Hospital in Husi and at the same time a deputy in the Romanian Parliament, is alleged to have received as bribes sums generally between 100 and 500 lei, along with foodstuffs, from 45 patients and relatives, in connection with his official duties as a specialist doctor: surgical operations, patient consultations and the issuing of medical prescriptions. Fifty-seven separate counts of taking a bribe in continuous form were recorded. Prosecutors say the investigation also covers a further 27 people who are suspects for giving a bribe.
inside: Patients paid the surgeon inside the hospital for operations, consultations and prescriptions that were his official duty.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 603, 10 October 2024

n: A railway hospital manager took goods for hiring a man's partner as a nurse
org_label: A family buying a nursing post at the Craiova railway hospital
who: A woman and her son, who wanted his partner hired as a nurse
rank: Manager of the Craiova Railway Clinical Hospital
d: On 19 October 2024, after her husband acted as intermediary, Gingioveanu Aurelia-Maria, manager of the Craiova Railway Clinical Hospital, is alleged to have received various goods from Raducanu Ionica-Melania and her son, so that the son's partner would be employed at that hospital as a nurse. In a separate strand of the same file, a man identified as M.A. is alleged to have demanded 24,000 euros in total from two witnesses between September and October 2024, receiving 12,000 euros from them and 60,000 lei as the leu equivalent of a further 12,000 euros, promising to intervene with people who held decision-making power. The map holds a separate prosecution reaching the same hospital through the manager's father.
inside: Goods passed to the hospital's own manager, and a nursing post inside it followed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 619, 1 November 2024

n: A woman sold hospital, prison and border posts in western Romania
org_label: A man buying jobs for himself and his circle
who: One man who paid for a job for himself and for jobs for friends and relatives
rank: Leadership of hospital units, Arad County Council, Arad Penitentiary and border police formations
d: Between 2019 and 2023 a woman is alleged to have demanded 108,500 euros in total from one witness and received 78,500 euros, letting him believe she held influence over people in the leadership of the Arad County Council, over the leadership of hospital units and over a member of the European Parliament, and that she would arrange his employment as an accountant in a hospital unit, the employment of his friends and relatives in hospitals, at Arad Penitentiary, at the Nadlac border police sector and at the border police formation of Traian Vuia international airport in Timisoara, and two European funding awards for his family. An earlier order in the same case recorded 94,500 euros demanded and 64,500 received. She was caught in the act in February 2023.
inside: One buyer's money was to place him and his circle inside hospitals, a penitentiary and two border police units.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 85, 7 February 2023 and 133, 2 March 2023

n: 926 people bought Romanian Covid vaccination certificates without being vaccinated
who: 926 people who paid for certificates without being vaccinated
rank: A family doctor in Dolj county authorised to carry out Covid-19 vaccination
d: Between October 2021 and January 2022 Vatan Venera Ecaterina, a family doctor in Dolj county authorised to carry out Covid-19 vaccination, is alleged with the help of several other people to have demanded and received sums from 926 people, for whom she arranged vaccination attestations and certificates without their having been vaccinated. Of the sums the intermediaries demanded from each of the 926, prosecutors say 200 lei per person, 185,200 lei in all, went to the doctor, who then entered those people in the National Electronic Register of Vaccinations. The charges record 926 counts each of taking a bribe, computer forgery and deception.
inside: The buyers' names were entered in the state's own vaccination register, which is what made the certificates work.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 94, 13 February 2023

n: A Romanian anticorruption commissioner sold an ambulance service nursing post
org_label: A person buying a nursing post at the Dambovita ambulance service
who: A witness who paid to be hired and then made permanent as a nurse
rank: Chief police commissioner in the General Anticorruption Directorate
d: Between April and May 2021 Andronache Radu, a chief police commissioner in Romania's General Anticorruption Directorate, is alleged to have demanded 10,000 euros for himself from a witness and to have actually received 2,000 euros, in order to exercise an influence he claimed to hold over several people with decision-making power in Bucharest, in the Dambovita County Council and in the Targoviste County Emergency Hospital, so that the witness would be employed and then made permanent in the post of nurse at the Dambovita County Ambulance Service. A second count of influence peddling, demanded from the same witness, runs from April 2021 to June 2022.
inside: The buyer was to be hired and then made permanent as a nurse inside a county ambulance service.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 113, 22 February 2023

n: An Oradea nurse sold seven people permanent hospital contracts
org_label: Seven people buying nursing and orderly posts
who: Seven people who paid between 1,500 and 13,500 euros each
rank: Nurse at the Dr Gavril Curteanu Municipal Clinical Hospital in Oradea, later at the Bihor County Emergency Clinical Hospital
d: Between 2020 and 2022, during the Covid-19 pandemic, Craciun Sorin Ioan, a nurse at the Dr Gavril Curteanu Municipal Clinical Hospital in Oradea and later at the Bihor County Emergency Clinical Hospital after the first was taken over by the second, is alleged to have demanded and received from seven people sums between 1,500 and 13,500 euros, 29,500 euros in total, along with other undue benefits. He is said to have let them believe he held influence over decision-makers in the leadership of those two hospitals and to have promised he would get them to arrange open-ended employment contracts in their names, for posts of nurse and orderly. Seven counts were charged.
inside: Seven buyers were promised permanent nurse and orderly contracts inside the two hospitals.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 335, 24 May 2023

n: A Bucharest hospitals chief sold the Colentina manager's post for 20,000 euros
org_label: A manager-candidate and two contractors of the Bucharest hospitals administration
who: A man who wanted the Colentina hospital manager's post, and companies holding contracts with the administration
rank: Director general of the Administration of Hospitals and Medical Services of Bucharest
d: In April 2023 Pluta Cristian, director general of the Administration of Hospitals and Medical Services of Bucharest, is alleged to have received 50,000 lei from a defendant identified as S.I. so that contracts the institution he led had concluded with two companies would run smoothly and their invoices be paid on time. On 19 June 2023 he is alleged to have received 20,000 euros from Cristescu George Mirel for the support he had given him in taking the post of manager of the Colentina Clinical Hospital in Bucharest. Prosecutors say Pluta had earlier put a proposal to Bucharest City Hall that formed the basis of Cristescu's appointment to that post.
inside: One payment bought the manager's chair at a city hospital; the other bought smooth running of the administration's own contracts.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 574, 19 September 2023 and 748, 6 December 2023

n: A Romanian mayor took 10,000 euros towards a doctor's post at the town hospital
org_label: A person buying a doctor's post for a relative
who: A witness paying for a relative to be hired as a doctor
rank: Mayor of the town of Mioveni, Arges county
d: In the autumn of 2022 Georgescu Ion, mayor of the town of Mioveni in Arges county, is alleged to have accepted from a witness the promise of 30,000 euros, of which he is said to have received a first instalment of 10,000 euros in December 2022, in order to exercise influence he claimed to hold over decision-makers in the leadership of the Mioveni Town Hospital, so that they would order the employment of a relative of the witness in a doctor's post. Under the agreement the rest of the money was to be handed to the mayor after that person was actually taken on at the medical unit.
inside: The buyer's relative was to be given a doctor's post inside the town hospital once the rest of the money was paid.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 605, 5 October 2023 and 767, 18 December 2023

n: A village mayor took 2,000 euros for a sanatorium nursing post that never came
org_label: Two people buying a nursing post for a relative
who: Two people paying for a relative to be hired as a nurse
rank: Mayor of the commune of Draguseni, Botosani county
d: During 2020 Nechita Eugen, mayor of the commune of Draguseni in Botosani county, is alleged to have demanded and received 2,000 euros from two people, in order to exercise influence he claimed to hold over decision-makers in the leadership of the Podriga Neuropsychiatry Sanatorium in the same county, so that they would order the employment of a relative of those people in a nurse's post. Prosecutors record that the promise was never carried out, the post having been filled by transfer by another person. The mayor was informed of his procedural standing and the accusations in December 2023. The map holds a separate prosecution of the same mayor for a bribe demanded from a company administrator four years later.
inside: The money was taken for a nursing post inside a state sanatorium, which another candidate got by transfer instead.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 771, 21 December 2023

n: A Romanian ambulance service rigged the exam that made Covid hires permanent
org_label: Temporary ambulance staff buying permanent posts
who: Staff hired without competition during the alert state who wanted open-ended posts
rank: Interim general manager of the Neamt County Ambulance Service, and three subordinates
d: Between 2 and 18 May 2022 the Neamt County Ambulance Service held an examination to fill open-ended posts, for staff who had been taken on without competition into fixed-term execution posts during the alert state or periods of epidemiological and biological risk, under Health Ministry order 1168 of 2022. Prosecutors allege that Morenciu Dan Dorin, the service's interim general manager, acting directly or through his subordinates Andronache Gladior, Preda Elena and Rozoschi Maria Luminita, took bribes in that context. Twenty-two separate counts of taking a bribe in continuous form were recorded against him.
inside: Temporary staff paid to come out of the exam with permanent posts inside the county ambulance service.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 662, 25 October 2022

n: Three resident doctors paid 2,000 euros each for a periodontology title
org_label: Three resident doctors buying the specialist title
who: Three resident doctors sitting the periodontology specialist examination
rank: Dental surgeon and associate professor at the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy, Dunarea de Jos University Galati, residency programme coordinator and president of the examination commission
d: Between 10 September and 14 November 2021 Sincar Dorina Cerasella, a dental surgeon and associate professor at the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy of Dunarea de Jos University in Galati, residency programme coordinator and president of the examination commission, is alleged to have demanded 2,000 euros directly from each of three resident doctors who were candidates in the specialist examination in periodontology. She is said to have maintained that through the influence she held over the other two members of the examination commission she would get them to help the three residents pass fraudulently and so obtain the title of periodontology specialist. One of the three residents is a co-defendant.
inside: The chair of the commission sold passes through the two colleagues who graded alongside her.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 146, 4 March 2022 and 299, 26 April 2022

n: A military hospital surgery chief took money and jewellery from patients
org_label: Patients paying for operations and specialist examinations
who: Several people who paid for operations and examinations for themselves or those close to them
rank: Head of General Surgery II at the Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital, an active officer with the rank of colonel
d: During 2022 Savulescu Alexandru-Florin, head of the General Surgery II section at the Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital in Bucharest and an active military officer with the rank of colonel, is alleged to have received undue benefits consisting of money and jewellery from several people, in connection with surgical operations and specialist examinations carried out on them or on people close to them. He was placed under judicial control with obligations that included not communicating by any route with the people named in the order and not carrying out the activity in the course of which the alleged acts were committed.
inside: Patients paid the head of the surgical section inside a state military hospital for the operations he performed there.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 579, 19 September 2022

n: A Brasov infectious diseases hospital bought equipment it did not need
who: A businessman whose company supplied the equipment, and his firm as a defendant
rank: Manager of the Brasov Infectious Diseases Hospital
d: This file was split off from a larger prosecution. It concerns the alleged fraudulent award, by the leadership of the Brasov Infectious Diseases Hospital, of a contract to a businessman's company for medical equipment that was overvalued and was not needed. In exchange, prosecutors say, people with sway and influence over the hospital's leadership received sums of money from the favoured firm's legal representative. Ionescu Ramona Delia, the hospital's manager at the time, was sent for trial for abuse of office where the public official obtained an undue benefit for herself or another. SC Chantel Sante SRL was sent for trial in the same case.
inside: The supplier's money reached people with sway over the hospital's leadership, and the hospital bought equipment it had no use for.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 211, 26 March 2021

n: A Harghita hospital ran formal tenders so one firm would win
org_label: A medical equipment supplier favoured in the tenders
who: The legal representative of the firm that was designated the winner
rank: People in the leadership of Odorheiu Secuiesc Municipal Hospital, Harghita county
d: The case concerns the alleged fraudulent award, by people in the leadership of Odorheiu Secuiesc Municipal Hospital in Harghita county, of contracts under which the medical unit bought overvalued medical equipment and products, some of which did not meet conformity conditions and some of which were not needed at all. To award those preferential contracts, paid for out of public money, prosecutors say the hospital ran formal procedures designed to designate a particular firm the winner. In exchange, people in the hospital's leadership or with influence over it received money from the favoured firm. Charges included complicity in abuse of office in continuous form and giving a bribe.
inside: Tenders at the hospital were run as a formality so that one supplier's firm would be named the winner.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 270, 27 April 2021

n: An MP was offered public leadership posts to miss a no-confidence vote
who: A member of parliament and the director general of a municipal transport company
rank: A deputy in the Romanian Parliament who was asked to stay away from the vote
d: On 1 October 2021, with a censure motion to withdraw confidence from the Romanian government about to be debated and voted on, Sandru Cosmin, a deputy in the Romanian Parliament, and Bitea Nicolae-Florin, director general of the Timisoara Public Transport Company, are alleged to have promised another deputy the appointment of people close to him to leadership posts in public institutions. To get that favour, prosecutors say, the deputy was asked to be absent from the joint sitting of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate on 5 October 2021 at which the motion was to be taken. Both were made suspects for giving a bribe.
inside: The price of a vote in parliament was the right to name people to the leadership of public institutions.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 647, 14 October 2021

n: Detroit's mayor took over a million dollars from people seeking city business
org_label: Contractors seeking city business and pension fund work
who: A city contractor and others seeking business with the city or its pension funds
rank: Mayor of Detroit, previously a member of the Michigan House of Representatives
d: A federal jury convicted Kwame Kilpatrick, mayor of Detroit and previously a member of the Michigan House of Representatives, his father Bernard Kilpatrick and city contractor Bobby Ferguson on racketeering, extortion, bribery, fraud and tax charges.
