Prosecutors established that during his time as mayor Kwame and Bernard Kilpatrick solicited and accepted payments and property valued at over one million dollars from people seeking business with the city or with its General Retirement System and its Police and Fire pension funds. Kwame Kilpatrick also took cash kickbacks of over 250,000 dollars from his own fundraising director. He was sentenced to 28 years.
inside: Contractors' money bought city business and work for the pension funds that hold Detroit employees' retirement savings.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Michigan, 11 March 2013 and 10 October 2013

n: A Detroit council member took 15,000 dollars and free auto body work
who: A local business owner who paid cash and gave free auto body work
rank: Sitting member of the Detroit City Council
d: A federal grand jury indicted Gabriel Leland, a sitting member of the Detroit City Council, on one count of conspiracy to commit bribery and two counts of bribery. The indictment alleges that from May to August 2017 Leland conspired with Elisa Grubbs, a campaign worker, to solicit and accept bribes consisting of 15,000 dollars in cash and free auto body work from a local business owner. Leland is charged with taking a 7,500 dollar cash bribe on 4 August 2017, four days before the primary election for the Detroit City Council. The US Attorney said a sitting member of the council engaging in bribery badly undermines faith in local government.
inside: A business owner's cash and free bodywork reached a sitting member of the city council days before his primary.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Michigan, Detroit City Council Member Indicted for Taking Bribes

n: Marijuana permit seekers paid 70,000 dollars to a Baldwin Park councilman
who: A former Compton city councilman acting as a consultant, and his consulting client
rank: Member of the Baldwin Park City Council
d: A former Compton city councilman was arrested on a federal grand jury indictment alleging that he and his consulting client paid 70,000 dollars in bribes to a member of the Baldwin Park City Council in exchange for that official's votes and support for commercial marijuana permits. Prosecutors say Baldwin Park City Councilman Ricardo Pacheco began soliciting bribes from businesses seeking marijuana development agreements and related permits in the city. Pacheco pleaded guilty in June 2020 to one count of bribery for accepting tens of thousands of dollars, including 20,000 dollars in cash from a Baldwin Park police officer working at the FBI's direction, in exchange for his political support of the police association's contract with the city.
inside: The permit applicants' money bought a councilman's votes on the marijuana agreements they were applying for.
cite: US Attorney, Central District of California, Former Local Politician Arrested on Indictment Alleging $70,000 in Bribes

n: A contractor paid Markham's mayor 80,000 dollars to be the only bid presented
who: The president of a contracting firm that held city work
rank: Mayor of Markham from 2001 to 2017, and the Markham City Council
d: A federal judge in Chicago sentenced a contractor to more than three years in prison for paying bribes to the mayor of Markham in order to keep and expand his firm's business with the south suburb. Jarigese was president of Tower when he paid more than 80,000 dollars in bribes to Markham mayor David Webb Jr. The prosecutor said that by bribing Webb, Jarigese rigged the system, so that Tower's uncompetitive and unchallenged proposals were the only option presented to the Markham City Council. Webb, mayor from 2001 to 2017, pleaded guilty and admitted taking part in the scheme. A business owner was also sentenced for lying to federal agents about what he knew of it.
inside: The council voting on city contracts was shown only this firm's proposals, because its president was paying the mayor.
cite: US Attorney, Northern District of Illinois, Contractor Sentenced to More Than 3 Years in Prison for Paying Bribes to South Suburban Mayor

n: An Eagle Pass city manager paid a county commissioner for a landfill contract
who: A city manager running a private management firm on the side
rank: A Maverick County commissioner
d: FBI agents arrested Hector Chavez Sr, the Eagle Pass city manager, on federal bribery and obstruction charges over what prosecutors called a pay-to-play scheme involving a Maverick County landfill contract. The indictment alleges that from about May to June 2012 Chavez, doing business as Chace Management, paid a total of approximately 20,000 dollars in bribes to a Maverick County commissioner. The commissioners court is the elected body that awards the county's contracts. The same investigation produced charges against a former Maverick County justice of the peace over two county construction contracts.
inside: A private management firm's money reached a member of the elected body that awards the county's contracts.
cite: US Attorney, Western District of Texas, Eagle Pass City Manager Indicted by Federal Grand Jury

n: A businessman and four Crystal City officials ran a contracts kickback scheme
who: Ngoc Tri Nguyen, a businessman who admitted his role in the scheme
rank: City councilmen, a mayor pro-tem and the mayor of Crystal City
d: Former Crystal City councilman Gilbert Urrabazo pleaded guilty to a federal charge in connection with a bribery and kickback scheme involving city contracts. Former mayor pro-tem Rogelio Mata, former city councilman Roel Mata and businessman Ngoc Tri Nguyen have all admitted their roles in the same scheme. Former city attorney and city manager William James Jonas and former Crystal City mayor Ricardo Lopez remained under a superseding indictment at the time. Nearly the whole elected government of the small Texas city was charged in one case.
inside: A contractor's kickbacks reached councilmen, the mayor pro-tem and the mayor who voted the city's contracts.
cite: US Attorney, Western District of Texas, Former Crystal City Councilman Pleads Guilty to Role in Bribery and Kickback Scheme

n: A mayor paid a school board president to lift Reading's donation cap
org_label: A mayor's re-election campaign and its consultants
who: A mayor, his special assistant and his campaign manager
rank: President of Reading City Council, and the president of the Reading School Board
d: A jury found former Reading mayor Vaughn Spencer guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit federal program bribery and honest services wire fraud, nine counts of bribery and one count of honest services wire fraud. Spencer, his special assistant Eron Lloyd and his campaign manager Michael Fleck conspired to pay an 1,800 dollar bribe to Reading School Board president Rebecca Acosta, who was running for district justice, in exchange for her help and that of her husband, City Council president Francisco Acosta, in persuading Reading City Council to repeal a local ordinance setting an annual limit on individual campaign contributions. Spencer wanted to keep contributions he had already received above the limit.
inside: The council was paid to repeal the ordinance capping donations, so the mayor could keep money already given above it.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Pennsylvania, Former Reading Mayor Vaughn Spencer Convicted of Bribery and Wire Fraud

n: A law firm paid a Texas district judge for favourable rulings
who: An Austin attorney and his law firm, helped by a former state legislator
rank: Judge of the 404th Judicial District Court, Cameron County, and the county district clerk's office
d: A federal jury convicted Austin attorney Marc Garrett Rosenthal of conspiring to bribe a state district judge, bribe witnesses in state and federal cases, file fraudulent personal injury cases and deprive the citizens of Cameron County, Texas, of an elected official's honest services. Evidence showed that from November 2005 to December 2009 Rosenthal, directly or through former state legislator and attorney Jose Santiago Solis, paid money and other considerations to Judge Abel Corral Limas of the 404th Judicial District Court, which produced favourable rulings for the firm's clients. Rosenthal also had the random case assignment system at the Cameron County District Clerk's Office manipulated so cases landed in courts the firm preferred, and paid witnesses to give false testimony.
inside: The firm's money reached the judge hearing its cases and the clerk's system that decided which judge got them.
cite: US Attorney, Western District of Texas, 22 February 2013 and 4 December 2013

n: An Arkansas judge cut a 5.2 million dollar verdict against a care business
org_label: A Conway, Arkansas care business and its owner
who: A Conway business and its owner, the defendant in the negligence case
rank: Elected circuit judge, Twentieth Judicial District, Second Division, Arkansas
d: A former Arkansas state circuit judge pleaded guilty to accepting a bribe in exchange for reducing a negligence jury verdict against a Conway business, during his campaign to be elected to the Arkansas Court of Appeals. Michael A. Maggio admitted that in 2013, as the elected circuit judge presiding over a civil matter in Faulkner County Circuit Court, he handled a claim by a decedent's estate that the business, its owner and others had neglected and mistreated the man, leading to his death in their care. On 16 May 2013 a jury awarded 5.2 million dollars in damages against the business. The business then moved for a new trial or remittitur, and Maggio announced his appeals court candidacy weeks later.
inside: The judge hearing the case took money and cut the damages the jury had awarded against the business.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Arkansas, Former Judge Pleads Guilty to Bribery

n: A repair firm bribed Postal Service managers for vehicle work
org_label: Auto repair and maintenance companies owned by Ibrahim Issa
who: The owner of numerous auto repair and maintenance companies in the New York area
rank: Managers of United States Postal Service Vehicle Maintenance Facilities
d: Ibrahim Issa, who owned and operated numerous auto repair and maintenance companies in the New York area and elsewhere, was found guilty by a federal jury of bribery of public officials and tax fraud and sentenced to 60 months in prison. From about 2012 to August 2016 he paid bribes to United States Postal Service Vehicle Maintenance Facility managers in order to obtain work repairing and maintaining Postal Service vehicles, providing cash, gifts, lavish meals and trips in exchange for that work. As a result of some of those bribes, prosecutors said, Issa received millions of dollars in fees from the Postal Service. He was also convicted of conspiring to evade federal income taxes for his companies.
inside: Cash, meals and trips reached the managers who decide which firms repair the Postal Service's own vehicles.
cite: US Attorney, Southern District of New York, Owner of Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Companies Sentenced to 5 Years in Prison

n: A consultant routed monthly fees into Mississippi's prisons chief's bank account
org_label: Sentinel Offender Services, AJA Management and Health Assurance
who: A Biloxi consultant paid monthly by firms holding state and county corrections contracts
rank: Commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Corrections, and a Harrison County supervisor
d: Robert Simmons of Biloxi was sentenced to 87 months in prison for a kickback scheme in which he paid money to the commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Corrections and to a Harrison County supervisor in exchange for contracts with the state and county. From 2012 to August 2014 Simmons was paid 4,000 dollars a month as a consultant for Sentinel Offender Services, which held an MDOC contract to help monitor offenders on probation or parole, and deposited 1,400 dollars of each month's pay directly into the bank account of commissioner Christopher Epps. AJA Management, which managed the construction of two 40,000,000 dollar prison expansions, paid Simmons 10,000 dollars a month, part of which went to the commissioner every month.
inside: Part of each consulting fee went straight into the bank account of the man who awarded the contracts.
cite: US Attorney, Southern District of Mississippi, Biloxi Businessman Sentenced for Kickback Scheme

n: A Philadelphia councilman drew a union salary and voted its interests
who: The business manager of Local 98 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers
rank: Member of Philadelphia City Council for the 6th councilmanic district
d: A federal jury convicted John Dougherty, business manager of Local 98 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, and Philadelphia city councilmember Robert Henon of conspiracy to commit honest services fraud and multiple counts of honest services wire fraud. Evidence at trial showed that Henon received a salary and other things of value from Dougherty and in exchange used his seat on City Council to serve Dougherty's interests. The convictions rested on schemes the prosecutors labelled L&I/CHOP, Plumbing Code/Building Trades, Towing, Comcast and Soda Tax. A further count against Henon, and his bribery conviction, rested on a 5,000 dollar campaign contribution written on a Communications Workers of America account.
inside: A councilman sat on City Council while drawing a union salary, and used the seat on the union's business.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Pennsylvania, Local 98 Leader John Dougherty, Philadelphia City Councilmember Robert Henon Found Guilty

n: A Dallas developer was convicted of bribing two council members, then cleared
who: The president of a Dallas real estate development company
rank: Two members of Dallas City Council
d: A federal jury convicted Ruel Hamilton, president of AmeriSouth Realty Group, of one count of conspiracy and two counts of bribery of an agent of a local government receiving federal funds, for bribing two former Dallas City Council members, Carolyn Davis and Dwaine Caraway. The prosecutor said Hamilton had used money to bend elected officials to his will and that the office would not let a kickback culture fester at City Hall. The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals vacated that conviction in an opinion handed down on 23 August 2022 and remanded the case for further proceedings, so the finding against him no longer stands.
inside: A developer's payments reached two sitting council members, on a conviction an appeals court later vacated.
cite: US Attorney, Northern District of Texas, Real Estate Developer Convicted of Bribery, with the 23 August 2022 Fifth Circuit update

n: Maverick County's Precinct One commissioner picked his own bid winners
org_label: Private contractors holding Maverick County construction contracts
who: Private contractors who submitted inflated bids, including a county probation officer working as a general contractor
rank: Maverick County Precinct One commissioner
d: Maverick County Precinct One commissioner Eliaz Maldonado pleaded guilty to receiving a bribe, and Javier Gonzalez, a Maverick County probation officer and general contractor, pleaded guilty to paying one. Court records show that in 2010 and 2011 Maldonado, through his employees, manipulated the bidding process to guarantee that contractors he chose won Maverick County construction contracts. Those contractors cashed the cheques the county issued them and then made cash payments to Maldonado. They had submitted inflated bids so there would be enough money to do the work, make a profit and pay the bribe. The contracts involved more than 100,000 dollars of county funds, and Maldonado received between 500 and 3,500 dollars at least twelve times.
inside: The commissioner steered the county's construction contracts to contractors who paid him back in cash.
cite: US Attorney, Western District of Texas, Two Eagle Pass Residents Enter Guilty Pleas

n: A third Maverick County precinct ran the same inflated-bid scheme
org_label: Contractors chosen for Precinct 3 county contracts
who: Private contractors, among them an Eagle Pass businessman who had been a justice of the peace
rank: Maverick County Precinct 3 commissioner
d: Jose Luis Rosales, former Maverick County Precinct 3 commissioner and an Eagle Pass school district teacher, pleaded guilty to receiving a bribe, and Cesar Iracheta, a former Maverick County justice of the peace and businessman, pleaded guilty to paying a bribe to an agent of an organisation receiving federal funds. Rosales admitted that during 2012 he manipulated the bidding process to guarantee that individuals he chose won Maverick County construction contracts, with the contractors cashing the county's cheques and then paying him in cash out of inflated bids. Rosales was sentenced to 66 months and ordered to pay 14,185.72 dollars in restitution; Iracheta to 94 months and 81,607.80 dollars.
inside: A third precinct commissioner picked the winners of county construction contracts and was paid out of the inflated bids.
cite: US Attorney, Western District of Texas, 8 December 2015 and 24 May 2016

n: Developers paid a Michigan mayor over 40,000 dollars for foreclosed properties
org_label: Two real estate developers, one the owner of Dominick's Market
who: Two real estate developers seeking tax-foreclosed properties for redevelopment
rank: Mayor of the City of Taylor, and the manager of its Community Development department
d: Jeffrey Baum, former manager of the City of Taylor's Community Development department and former treasurer of Mayor Richard Sollars' campaign fund, pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit bribery with Sollars and two real estate developers, Shady Awad and Hadir Altoon. Baum admitted accepting thousands of dollars in cash bribes for himself and over 40,000 dollars in cash payments to Sollars, in connection with the city's Right of First Refusal programme, which lets Taylor acquire tax-foreclosed properties from Wayne County for redevelopment. Court records say that between 2017 and 2019 Baum also helped Sollars take money from his own campaign by handing him blank campaign cheques signed as treasurer.
inside: Developers' cash reached the mayor and the official who ran the programme deciding who got the city's foreclosed properties.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Michigan, City of Taylor Official Pleads Guilty to Accepting Bribes

n: A medical school senate president took 10,000 euros to create a post
org_label: A hospital doctor buying a university teaching post
who: A doctor at a Bucharest hospital who wanted a university assistant post
rank: President of the University Senate, director of Department 10 Surgery and head of General Surgery, Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy
d: On 18 December 2018 Beuran Mircea, president of the University Senate, director of Department 10 Surgery, head of the General Surgery discipline, doctoral supervisor and professor of general surgery at the Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Bucharest, accepted and received 10,000 euros from a doctor at a Bucharest hospital, in connection with acts that fell within his official duties. Prosecutors say he took the money both to propose that the university advertise a fixed-term post of university assistant in general surgery, and in connection with the witness taking up that post. A later communication puts the money and goods received at over 10,000 euros.
inside: The post itself was created and then filled at the buyer's request, by the man who chaired the university's senate.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 125, 13 February 2020 and 331, 29 April 2020

n: A hospital manager took 7 percent of an operating theatre contract
org_label: A company holding the operating theatre contract
who: Representatives of the company that won the design and works contract
rank: Manager of the Dr Constantin Opris County Emergency Hospital in Baia Mare
d: Between November 2019 and 28 February 2020 Pintea Sorina, manager of the Dr Constantin Opris County Emergency Hospital in Baia Mare, Maramures county, is alleged to have demanded and received through an intermediary, from representatives of a commercial company, two instalments she was not entitled to: 10,000 euros on 20 December 2019 and 120,000 lei on 28 February 2020. Prosecutors say the sums represented 7 percent of the value of a public procurement contract for the design and execution of works fitting out an operating block for cardiovascular and thoracic surgery and the spaces adjoining it, which the hospital had concluded with that company in 2019.
inside: The hospital's own manager took a fixed percentage of the contract she had awarded for its operating theatre.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 188, 29 February 2020 and 336, 30 April 2020

n: Fundeni staff fed suppliers the institute's own procurement plan
org_label: Medical equipment suppliers to the Fundeni Clinical Institute
who: Businessmen who went on to sign equipment and product contracts with the institute
rank: Two officials of the Fundeni Clinical Institute, Bucharest
d: Prosecutors allege that Grigore Emilia and Parvulescu Adrian unlawfully gave businessmen information not intended for publication, so that those businessmen could conclude several contracts for medical equipment and products with the Fundeni Clinical Institute in Bucharest. The information is said to have included data about a competing firm, the framework agreement the institute had signed with that competitor, the institute's medical equipment requirements and its public procurement plan. It was handed over both before the procurement procedures were organised and while they were running, between July 2015 and February 2016. The contracts were then signed, and the award documentation was drawn up accordingly.
inside: Suppliers held the institute's procurement plan and its rival's contract before bidding on its tenders.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 413, 2 June 2020

n: A state drug company's director asked 760,000 euros for a Covid kit contract
org_label: A private firm supplying Covid protective equipment
who: An intermediary representing a private company that wanted the supply contract
rank: Director general of the state company Compania Nationala Unifarm SA
d: Unifarm is Romania's state pharmaceutical supply company. Prosecutors allege that as its director general, Ionel Eugen Adrian demanded 760,000 euros from an intermediary acting for a commercial company, so that Unifarm would award that company a contract to supply equipment protecting against Covid-19 infection: 250,000 coveralls and 3 million surgical masks. The contract was concluded with a private firm in the first half of March 2020, in breach of the provisions of Law 98 of 2016 on public procurement. He was charged with taking a bribe, abuse of office with the obtaining of undue benefits, complicity in influence peddling, instigating intellectual forgery and using his position for someone's benefit.
inside: The state company that buys the country's medicines awarded a pandemic supply contract after its director asked for a cut.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 486, 23 June 2020

n: A ten percent commission on an airport maintenance contract
org_label: A firm holding a maintenance and repairs contract at Baneasa airport
who: The administrator of a firm that had invoiced works under the contract
rank: Director of the Operational Directorate at Baneasa - Aurel Vlaicu airport
d: Between February and April 2020 a private individual, helped by Mitrut Bogdan Ion, director of the Operational Directorate at Baneasa - Aurel Vlaicu airport, is alleged to have demanded and received from a firm's administrator 5,000 lei and 25,000 euros. Prosecutors say those sums represented a commission of 10 percent of the total the firm had invoiced for a series of works carried out under a maintenance and repairs contract concluded with the National Bucharest Airports Company. The 25,000 euros is said to have been handed over on 14 April 2020, when the offence was caught in the act. The director was charged with complicity in influence peddling.
inside: A tenth of everything the firm invoiced the state airports company went back through its own operations director.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 505, 1 July 2020

n: A water authority deputy took 100,000 lei to release a contractor's payments
org_label: A company holding three river works contracts
who: Two businessmen whose company had carried out river regularisation and flood defence works
rank: Deputy director general of the Mures Basin Water Administration
d: On 8 November 2019 Bratanovici Cristian is alleged to have received 100,000 lei in Targu Mures from one of two businessmen. Prosecutors say the deputy director general took the money in connection with acts falling within his official duties, concerning the arrangement of financing so that works the businessmen's company had carried out under three contracts with the Mures Basin Water Administration would be paid. The contracts covered the regularisation of the Gurasada stream in Hunedoara county and flood defence works on the Aries river and its tributaries protecting the town of Campeni and other localities. Both businessmen were charged with giving a bribe.
inside: The money bought the release of financing for the contractor's own river works, from the authority that ordered them.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 509, 2 July 2020

n: Five Romanian forestry officials signed off planting that paid them percentages
org_label: A company contracted for forestry services
who: Representatives of a company paid for planting, crop maintenance, clearing and cleaning works
rank: Head of the Comanesti forest district of the National Forest Administration Romsilva, and four district chiefs
d: Between 2015 and 2020 five officials of the Comanesti forest district in Bacau, part of the National Forest Administration Romsilva, are alleged to have demanded and received money from a company's representatives in return for confirming that forestry works had been carried out: planting, crop maintenance, clearing and cleaning. Pâslaru Aurel, the district head, is said to have asked for 3 percent of the pre-tax value of the invoices the company was to issue and to have received 210,000 lei; when the offence was caught in the act on 23 July 2020 he was found with 10,000 lei. The four district chiefs asked for the direct labour value of works in their own districts, with two of them receiving 995,370 lei and 980,750 lei.
inside: The officials who certify that trees were planted were paid a share of every invoice they signed off.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 586, 3 August 2020

n: Sixteen women paid a state burns hospital's manager for cosmetic surgery
org_label: Sixteen patients paying for cosmetic operations
who: Sixteen women who paid to have cosmetic operations in a state hospital
rank: Senior doctor and manager of the Clinical Emergency Hospital for Plastic Surgery and Burns, Bucharest
d: Between January 2013 and January 2014 Stan Vitalie, a senior doctor and the manager of the Clinical Emergency Hospital for Plastic Surgery and Burns in Bucharest, is alleged to have demanded and received from 16 female patients sums of between 1,100 and 2,700 euros, to carry out various cosmetic operations on them in that state hospital. Prosecutors say he admitted those patients under the pretext of conditions requiring surgical correction, and in exchange for the money performed the cosmetic surgery. Sixteen counts of taking a bribe were recorded against him.
inside: Private cosmetic operations were done inside a state burns hospital, on admissions written up as something else.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 650, 28 August 2020

n: A Bucharest hospital manager paid 648,193 lei to a co-defendant's companies
org_label: Companies administered by the manager's co-defendant
who: A businessman whose companies received the hospital's payments
rank: Manager and credit officer of the Nicolae Malaxa Clinical Hospital, Bucharest
d: Prosecutors allege that Secureanu Florin-Adrian breached the duties set out for him in primary legislation when, as manager of the Nicolae Malaxa Clinical Hospital in Bucharest and the officer authorising its spending, he ordered payments totalling 648,193 lei to be made between 2009 and 2016 out of the hospital's funds to several commercial companies, among them companies administered by his co-defendant in the case. The money is said to have been paid both in the context of commercial operations and otherwise, and the co-defendant was charged alongside him.
inside: The hospital's own spending officer sent its funds to companies run by the man charged with him.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 763, 29 September 2020

n: A businessman promised a minister 5 million dollars over Hidroelectrica deals
org_label: Firms holding electricity supply contracts with Hidroelectrica
who: A businessman whose firms held supply contracts with the state hydropower company
rank: The then minister of regional development and tourism
d: Hidroelectrica is Romania's state hydropower company. In the summer and autumn of 2011 a defendant identified as B.R.I. is alleged to have conveyed to the then minister of regional development and tourism a businessman's promise to give him 5,000,000 dollars, so that the minister would exercise his influence to keep the contracts the businessman's firms held with Hidroelectrica on the price and quantity of energy already negotiated. In a related strand, between November 2011 and February 2012 B.R.I. is said to have handed something to the former minister through an intermediary. He entered a plea agreement for complicity in buying influence.
inside: The payment was to hold in place the price and volume the firms were already getting from the state hydropower company.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 561, 27 July 2020

n: An Austrian rail builder paid 10 percent of every state payment it received
who: The director of the Austrian company's Romanian representative office
rank: A secretary of state in the Transport Ministry, and officials of the Finance and Transport ministries
d: Between 2005 and 2014 Romanian officials, or people with influence over them, are alleged to have received about 20 million euros from an Austrian company, so that contracts for rehabilitating sections of railway would be signed and their invoices paid, and so that outstanding VAT on another line the same company had already rebuilt would be paid. The money was a percentage of each payment the Romanian state made, handed over as the builder itself collected from the national railway company CFR. Between 2009 and 2013 Hornegger Josef, director of the company's Romanian office, helped negotiate and pay a commission of 10 percent of what it collected. Dascalu Constantin, a secretary of state in the Transport Ministry, allegedly received 1,114,000 euros.
inside: A tenth of every payment the state railway made to the builder went back to the officials who released it.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 253, 15 March 2019

n: A transport minister's adviser took 9.4 million lei to unblock railway payments
org_label: An Italian construction company and Team Delta Proiect SRL
who: A representative of a construction company owed money for railway works
rank: Personal adviser to the minister of transport, and officials of the Transport Ministry
d: During 2012, while serving as adviser to the minister of transport, Szechely Mihaela Vasilica demanded money from a representative of a construction company and between 2012 and 2015 received 9,410,375.7 lei through Team Delta Proiect, a firm she controlled. In exchange she promised that, through the influence her post as the minister's personal adviser gave her over Transport Ministry officials, she would get them to make the ministry allocate CFR SA the money it owed the company. Part of the commission, 1,011,550 euros, was transferred to Belgian consultancy firms and then used to pay for advertising in the 2012 parliamentary election campaign. The file came from a Belgian request for judicial assistance.
inside: The adviser's fee released the state railway's debts to the company, and part of it paid for election advertising.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 309, 8 April 2019 and 713, 21 August 2019

n: A psychiatric hospital lab chief took 3.5 percent of a supplier's invoices
org_label: A company holding contracts with the Obregia psychiatric hospital
who: Representatives of a company whose invoices the hospital paid
rank: Senior doctor and head of the medical analysis laboratory, Professor Doctor Alexandru Obregia Psychiatry Clinical Hospital
d: Between 29 August 2014 and 19 June 2015, in the course of contracts between the Professor Doctor Alexandru Obregia Psychiatry Clinical Hospital in Bucharest and a commercial company, Postolache Elena, a senior doctor and head of the hospital's medical analysis laboratory, is alleged to have received 102,200 lei in three instalments from the company's representatives. Prosecutors say that sum represented 3.5 percent of the pre-VAT value of the invoices the company issued and the hospital paid. She was charged with taking a bribe in continuous form.
inside: The head of the laboratory took a fixed share of every invoice the hospital paid its supplier.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 1021, 11 November 2019 and 1053, 19 November 2019

n: A military hospital surgeon told a patient 200 lei was too little
who: A patient's husband, who handed over the money before surgery
rank: Senior ear, nose and throat doctor at the Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital, an active officer with the rank of colonel
d: On 29 November 2018 Vracioiu Radu Viorel, a senior ear, nose and throat doctor at the Dr Carol Davila Central Military Emergency University Hospital in Bucharest and an active military officer with the rank of colonel, received 500 lei from a witness in connection with carrying out a surgical operation on the witness's wife, and the offence was caught in the act. Two days earlier, before the operation, prosecutors say the doctor had reproached the patient that the 200 lei she intended to hand him was too small a sum. He was charged with two counts of taking a bribe and with instigating the giving of a bribe.
inside: The surgeon named his own price to a patient inside a state military hospital before operating on her.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 245, 14 March 2019

n: Four sitting Toledo council members were charged with selling their votes
org_label: Local business owners seeking council votes
who: Local business owners who paid cash, cheques, money orders and other things of value
rank: Four sitting members of Toledo City Council
d: A federal grand jury sitting in Cleveland returned a 13-count indictment charging four sitting Toledo City Council members and one local attorney over a bribery and extortion scheme. The indictment alleges the scheme encouraged soliciting and accepting cash, cheques, money orders or other things of value from local business owners in exchange for the council members' votes on City Council. The US Attorney said elected officials are elected by the people to serve the people, not their own financial interests. Four of the nine seats on the council were held by people charged in the same case.
inside: Business owners' cash reached four of the nine council members whose votes decided their matters.
cite: US Attorney, Northern District of Ohio, Five Indicted in Toledo City Council Bribery and Extortion Scheme

n: An Arkansas senator drew retainers from a charity and an orthodontist
org_label: Preferred Family Healthcare Inc and an orthodontic chain
who: Executives and employees of a Missouri health care charity, and an orthodontist who owned clinics across Arkansas
rank: Member of the Arkansas State Senate
d: Former Arkansas state senator Jeremy Hutchinson was sentenced to 46 months for accepting multiple bribes and tax fraud. Court documents say he was hired as outside counsel by Dr Benjamin Burris, an orthodontist who owned clinics across Arkansas, and in exchange for payments and legal work pushed legislation beneficial to Burris, with the legal work provided to conceal the arrangement. In a separate strand he accepted bribes in the form of monthly legal retainers and other things of value from employees and executives of Preferred Family Healthcare, a Springfield, Missouri health care charity, and in exchange gave the charity favourable legislative and official action. The charity agreed in 2022 to pay more than 8 million dollars in forfeiture and restitution.
inside: A retainer on a senator's law practice bought the legislation and official action his payers wanted.
cite: US Attorney, Eastern District of Arkansas, Former Arkansas State Senator Sentenced for Bribery and Tax Fraud

n: A Cincinnati councilman took 15,000 dollars through a two-week-old nonprofit
org_label: Investors in two city development projects
who: Investors in real estate development projects, and an associate who held the nonprofit
rank: Member of Cincinnati City Council
d: Jeffrey Pastor, a Cincinnati city councilman, was sentenced to 24 months for honest services wire fraud after receiving a 15,000 dollar cash bribe in return for official action advancing development projects in the city. Court documents say that in September 2018 Pastor and an associate flew to Miami on a private plane to meet investors about a real estate development project, a trip he never paid for or disclosed. During it he explained that he would ensure favourable action by the city for the project and could be paid through his associate's nonprofit entity, which had been incorporated two weeks earlier. Pastor said the purpose of that entity was to sanitise the money. He admitted accepting things of value over two projects between June 2018 and January 2019.
inside: The payment was routed through a nonprofit set up two weeks before, in return for the city's favourable action.
cite: US Attorney, Southern District of Ohio, 7 June 2023 and 21 December 2023

n: Contractors seeking city help rebuilt a Chicago alderman's home
org_label: Construction contractors seeking city assistance for a ward development
who: Construction contractors on a development project in the alderman's own ward
rank: Alderman of a Far South Side ward, City of Chicago, and her chief of staff
d: A federal grand jury indicted City of Chicago alderman Carrie M. Austin and her chief of staff, Chester Wilson Jr, on bribery offences for allegedly conspiring to receive home improvements from construction contractors who were seeking city assistance for a development project in Austin's Far South Side ward. Austin was charged with one count of conspiring to use interstate facilities to promote bribery, two counts of using those facilities to promote bribery, and one count of wilfully making materially false statements to the FBI. Wilson was charged with the same bribery counts and one count of theft of government funds.
inside: The contractors who wanted the city's help on a ward project did the work on the ward alderman's own house.
cite: US Attorney, Northern District of Illinois, City of Chicago Alderman and Her Chief of Staff Indicted on Federal Bribery Charges

n: A transport secretary of state took 5.3 million euros on an Otopeni top-up
org_label: An international company holding the Otopeni modernisation contract
who: The representative of the Romanian branch of the company executing the works
rank: Secretary of state and vice-president of the Technical-Economic Council in the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, with the Henri Coanda airport company under his coordination
d: Anton Marin was a secretary of state and vice-president of the Technical-Economic Council in Romania's Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, with the national company running Henri Coanda airport at Otopeni under his coordination. Prosecutors say he accepted a promise from, and then received from, the representative of the Romanian branch of the international company executing the Otopeni modernisation contract a total of 22,760,654 lei, about 5.3 million euros at the exchange rate of the time, as a commission of 3.5 percent of the amount by which the works contract was to be topped up. The money was for approving the investment documentation, the funding note and the draft government decision on updated technical and economic indicators. Government Decision 852 of 2009 was then adopted.
inside: The commission was a share of the increase itself, paid to the official who signed off the increase.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 9, 8 January 2018

n: A health quality authority paid 13.7 million lei on overvalued service deals
org_label: Three companies supplying archiving and other services
who: Representatives of three service companies, two of whom paid the percentages
rank: Three officials of the National Authority for Quality Management in Health
d: Between 2 December 2010 and 5 August 2011 Dan Romulus Serban, Oana Mihaela Alexandrescu-Duca and Aracsia Magdalena Bentia concluded with three commercial companies, in breach of the law and in some cases at overvalued prices, two service contracts, an addendum and a framework agreement, covering purchases that included the electronic archiving of documents. Alexandrescu-Duca is alleged to have demanded from two of the suppliers' representatives 100,000 euros plus 20 percent of a contract worth 5,127,965 lei and 6 percent of a 1,012,000 lei addendum to it, and to have received 100,000 euros and 1,080,000 lei in instalments. The National Authority for Quality Management in Health joined the case as a civil party for 13,718,426 lei.
inside: The suppliers' percentages went to the officials who signed their contracts at the prices they set.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 20, 11 January 2018

n: An MP asked 5 percent of the water funds a contractor was waiting for
org_label: A company holding contracts with the river basin administrations
who: The representative of a company waiting for its river basin contracts to be funded
rank: Deputy in the Romanian Parliament and county organisation president of a political party
d: On 31 July 2015 Arsene Ionel, a deputy in the Romanian Parliament and president of the Neamt county organisation of a political party, demanded from a company's representative 5 percent of the 60,000,000 lei that the National Administration Apele Romane was to allocate so the company could complete the contracts it had running with the river basin administrations. A second influence peddling count against him concerns 100,000 euros received during 2013 to use influence he let it be believed he held over people in the leadership of the National Integrity Agency, over a conflict of interest finding.
inside: The fee was a share of the state water funds the contractor needed to finish the work it had already started.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 103, 14 February 2018 and 135, 22 February 2018

n: A Danube ports company director sold sailor and mechanic jobs
org_label: People buying sailor and mechanic posts
who: Five people who paid for posts for themselves or others
rank: Director of the National Company Administration of the Maritime Danube Ports
d: Between June 2017 and 17 April 2018 Ciubrei Luigi Marius, director of the National Company Administration of the Maritime Danube Ports, is alleged to have demanded and received through an intermediary, Tarau Constantin, a total of 2,700 euros from five people, so that some of them would be employed at the company he led in posts of sailor and mechanic. From two of them he received 1,000 euros to take one on as a sailor. The sums the buyers actually paid were much larger, because the intermediary and others kept a commission of between 100 and 600 euros each, with Tarau keeping 1,500 euros in all. The last payment, 500 euros, was made on 17 April 2018 when the offence was caught in the act.
inside: Crew posts at the state company that runs Romania's maritime Danube ports were sold by its own director.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 309, 18 April 2018 and 385, 18 May 2018

n: Prison staff paid a military hospital doctor for medical retirement
org_label: Arad Penitentiary staff buying medical retirement
who: Penitentiary staff who wanted to retire early on medical grounds
rank: Senior doctor and head of the Internal Medicine section, Timisoara Military Clinical Emergency Hospital, and a nurse
d: From November 2016 staff at Arad Penitentiary grew increasingly interested in ending their service through medical retirement, where the pension was roughly equal to the salary. Between 26 September and 15 October 2018 Posiar Eugen Silviu, head of the Internal Medicine section at the Timisoara Military Clinical Emergency Hospital, received 3,400 lei in total from two people who wanted to retire that way, and demanded 300 lei more and an unspecified sum to get the hospital's expert commission to decide in their favour. To make it appear they had qualifying conditions, prosecutors say the doctor and nurse Iliuta Elena Corina entered untrue details in their medical files, including fictitious admissions and supposed procedures. 156,950 euros and 6,480 lei were seized from him.
inside: Fictitious admissions and procedures were written into the files, and the hospital's expert commission signed the retirements off.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 848, 18 October 2018 and 936, 12 November 2018

n: A Bucharest district mayor was promised a million euros for building permits
org_label: A company registered in another EU country
who: Representatives of a company registered in an EU country, developing a property project
rank: Mayor of Bucharest sector 6
d: Between 2006 and 2007 Poteras Constantin Cristian, mayor of Bucharest sector 6, demanded 1,000,000 euros from the representatives of a company registered in an EU country, and on 31 July 2007 received 250,000 euros from them. Prosecutors say the money was demanded and received in exchange for exercising his official powers over the issuing of the permits needed to develop a property project. The money was sought while he held the office that issued those permits.
inside: The developer's money went to the mayor whose office issued the permits its project needed.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1083, 28 December 2018

n: A ministry official took 5 percent of a Tulcea flood defence contract
org_label: A company seeking the flood defence works
who: The representative of a company that wanted to be named executor of the works
rank: Deputy secretary general of the Ministry of Environment and Forests, reaching the minister and the leadership of the national water administration
d: In August 2010, as deputy secretary general of the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Para Lorant accepted a promise relayed through an intermediary from a company's representative: in exchange for money he would use his influence with the environment minister and the leadership of the National Administration Apele Romane so that the company would be named executor of flood embankment works in Tulcea county, a contract worth 5 million lei. On 3 September 2010 he received 250,000 lei through the intermediary, the equivalent of 5 percent of the sum allocated to the works. He also took hotel stays in Mamaia worth 18,376 lei and a trip to Vienna worth 4,485 lei from a subordinate, paid through companies.
inside: Five percent of the contract bought the company its selection as executor of the state's flood defences.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 527, 28 June 2017

n: A Hidroelectrica lab chief required subcontracts to his own firm
org_label: A maintenance contractor at hydropower sites
who: The administrator of a company seeking maintenance contracts at hydropower sites
rank: Head of the hydrotechnical structures monitoring laboratory, SC Hidroelectrica Bistrita branch
d: In early 2010 Catana Neculai, head of the laboratory monitoring the behaviour of hydrotechnical structures at the Bistrita branch of Hidroelectrica, let it be understood that he held influence with employees of that branch and of the affiliated companies Hidroserv Bistrita and Hidroserv Slatina. He demanded of a company's administrator that, in exchange for being awarded maintenance contracts at hydropower sites, part of the works be subcontracted to a company he controlled directly. Between 2010 and 2012 that company signed six contracts with the two Hidroserv companies, with the Bistrita branch as final beneficiary, collecting 2,368,784 lei for interior and exterior rehabilitation, bank protection and vegetation clearance.
inside: The price of a maintenance contract at the state hydropower sites was a subcontract to the official's own firm.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 630, 4 August 2017

n: A Romanian prosecutor asked 260,000 euros from the man he was investigating
org_label: A businessman under investigation for tax evasion and money laundering
who: A businessman who was a suspect in the prosecutor's own case file
rank: Prosecutor in the Criminal Investigation and Forensics Section of the Prosecutor's Office attached to the High Court of Cassation and Justice
d: In December 2016 Ceort Catalin Nicolae, a prosecutor in the Criminal Investigation and Forensics Section of the Prosecutor's Office attached to Romania's High Court of Cassation and Justice, is alleged to have demanded 260,000 euros indirectly, through a co-defendant, from a businessman who was being investigated for tax evasion and money laundering in a criminal file the prosecutor was himself handling. The money was sought in connection with adopting a favourable solution for that man in the case. On 27 December 2016 the intermediary received 30,000 euros from the businessman, and the offence was caught in the act.
inside: The man under investigation was asked to buy the outcome from the prosecutor running his own file.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 139, 22 February 2017

n: A court clerk sold two murder defendants' relatives a favourable verdict
who: A relative of two people on trial for murder
rank: Former court clerk at the Bistrita Nasaud Tribunal, reaching its magistrates
d: Between September 2016 and February 2017 Feher Veronica, using her standing as a former court clerk at the Bistrita Nasaud Tribunal, demanded and received 100,000 lei and food products from a relative of two people who had been sent for trial for murder. Prosecutors say she gave that person the impression that she held influence over the magistrates of the Bistrita Nasaud Tribunal who were charged with hearing the case, so as to obtain a favourable outcome for the two defendants. Two counts of influence peddling in continuous form were charged against her.
inside: A former clerk sold access to the magistrates of her old court while they were hearing a murder trial.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communications 141, 24 February 2017 and 291, 14 April 2017

n: Furniture for a court president's home, then a tender ruling for the giver
org_label: A businessman's company bidding for public contracts
who: A businessman whose company's cases were before the court
rank: Judge and president of the Constanta Court of Appeal
d: Between November and December 2012 Stanciu Nicolae, a judge and president of the Constanta Court of Appeal, demanded and received from Costea Vasile furniture worth 14,815.03 lei, delivered to the magistrate's home on 21 December 2012. In exchange he promised to use the influence his position as court president gave him over the magistrates who would handle the cases concerning the businessman's company, so that it would obtain favourable outcomes. Prosecutors say the promise was carried out during 2014, when the court decided a case brought by the company's competitors over a public procurement procedure: the complaints were rejected and the contract stayed with Costea's firm. The furniture was left out of the judge's 2013 asset declaration.
inside: Rivals' complaints about a tender were thrown out by the court whose president had taken the winner's furniture.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1, 3 January 2018

n: Candidates paid for eligible places on a Romanian county council list
org_label: A party's Brasov county branch and its election campaign
who: Candidates for the 2012 local elections who paid for list places
rank: President of Brasov County Council and president of a party's county branch, with county councillors and mayors
d: The case concerns corruption offences between 2010 and 2013 by Cancescu Aristotel Adrian, president of Brasov County Council and at the same time president of a political party's county branch, and by people around him including county councillors and mayors. Prosecutors allege undue benefits were taken from the award and running of public procurement contracts by the county council and by local authorities in the county, and that money was taken to fund the party branch's election campaign by demanding payment from candidates in the 2012 local elections in return for an eligible place on the county councillor list. The sums demanded for a place ranged from 15,000 to 220,000 lei.
inside: Seats on the county council were sold as places on the party list, at prices up to 220,000 lei.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 509, 21 June 2017

n: A hospital manager wrote tender terms only his two suppliers could meet
org_label: A laundry contractor and a funeral services concessionaire
who: Representatives of two companies, one running the outsourced laundry and one the funeral services concession
rank: Manager of the Sf Apostol Andrei County Emergency Clinical Hospital, Constanta
d: Between 2010 and December 2014 Capatina Danut, manager of the Sf Apostol Andrei County Emergency Clinical Hospital in Constanta, demanded commissions from the representatives of two companies: 10 percent of the invoices one of them collected from the hospital under a contract outsourcing its laundry, and 18 to 20 percent of the investments to be made under a funeral services concession held by the other. He received 663,083 lei in total through an intermediary. Prosecutors say the money was taken both to rig the award procedures and to write into the specifications and procurement documents qualification requirements that only the favoured firms could meet.
inside: The tender terms were drafted so that only the two firms paying commissions could qualify.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1035, 20 December 2017

n: A judicial panel took forest land off Romsilva and gave it to a claimant
org_label: A land restitution claimant and the lawyers acting for him
who: A claimant to forest and agricultural land, assisted by a lawyer of the Covasna Bar
rank: A panel of judges of the Covasna Tribunal
d: On 17 April 2012, following a prior arrangement and at the request of Adam Ioan, a panel of judges at the Covasna Tribunal that included Ordog Lorand Andras allowed an appeal in land fund matters and reconstituted property rights over a large area of forest and agricultural land in Bacau county in favour of Sturdza Paltin-Gheorghe, and against the National Forest Administration Romsilva. Ordog Melinda, a lawyer of the Covasna Bar, was indicted for complicity in taking a bribe in connection with that decision.
inside: A bought appeal ruling moved a large area of state forest into private hands.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1079, 28 December 2017

n: A contractor sponsored a mayor's football club with 3 percent of its contract
org_label: A construction company working on the Siret river
who: The director of a construction company holding a Hidroelectrica works contract
rank: Mayor of Piatra Neamt and vice-president of a political party, reaching Hidroelectrica's leadership
d: In early 2010 Stefan Gheorghe, mayor of Piatra Neamt and vice-president of a political party, asked the director of a construction company to sponsor the football club FC Ceahlaul Piatra Neamt with 3 percent of what the company would collect under a contract with the Bistrita hydropower branch of Hidroelectrica for hydro works on the Siret river. In exchange he promised to intervene with officials in the leadership of Hidroelectrica, the state-majority company that allocated the funds, so the investment's financing would continue. Between 2010 and 2011 the club and the company signed seven advertising contracts, nine invoices were issued and 998,000 lei was paid, with no evidence the advertising was delivered.
inside: The money for continued state funding of the works arrived as football sponsorship, through seven advertising contracts.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 1073, 28 December 2017

n: A county councillor asked 500,000 lei for party pull over coal haulage
org_label: A haulier bidding for coal transport contracts
who: A businessman and two others trying to win the haulage contracts through a company he controlled
rank: County councillor in Hunedoara County Council, claiming influence over a party's central leadership
d: In the summer of 2010 CET Bacau and Electrocentrale Oradea were about to sign contracts to transport coal bought from the National Coal Company Oltenia, and Mazilu Gabriela, Mazilu Ovidiu and a businessman tried to win them through a company he controlled. The businessman approached Simota Alin, then a county councillor in Hunedoara County Council, who told him that through the influence he held with a political party's central leadership he could secure the contracts, since the mayors of Bacau and Oradea belonged to the same party at the time. Simota asked him for 500,000 lei, saying the money would be used by the party, and the Mazilus agreed to the demand.
inside: The route to two state heating companies' haulage contracts ran through a party's central leadership.
cite: Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, communication 802, 5 October 2017

n: Bucharest customs inspectors were convicted of taking cash at warehouse checks
org_label: Companies whose goods the inspectors were checking
who: Representatives of commercial companies, among them a trader and the firm J&G TB SRL
rank: Customs inspectors and customs workers of the Bucharest Regional Customs Directorate
d: A colleague's denunciation to the anticorruption prosecutors stated that he and others in the Bucharest Regional Customs Directorate had taken money from company representatives so as not to perform their duties properly. On 9 February 2024, during a check at warehouses near Metro Voluntari in Ilfov county, three of them received 300 dollars from a trader. On 12 February 2024, at a check on the firm J&G TB SRL, customs workers received 4,500 lei, of which the inspectors kept 1,000 lei each and 1,500 lei went on to two others. The court convicted one of them of taking a bribe in continuous form, sentencing him to 2 years and 10 months and barring him from holding a post in the Romanian Customs Authority.
inside: Cash changed hands inside the customs directorate's own car during the checks it was carrying out.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13329

n: 5,000 euros kept a woman's hospital laboratory job in Botosani
org_label: A couple buying a permanent laboratory post
who: A man who paid for his wife to stay in her post on an open-ended contract
rank: Staff of the analysis laboratory at the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital, Botosani
d: In the spring of 2022 an intermediary passed 5,000 euros, in instalments of 1,500 and 3,500 euros, from one man to a second man, so that the first man's wife would stay employed on an open-ended contract at an analysis laboratory in the Mavromati County Emergency Hospital in Botosani. She had been taken on there during the pandemic. The court accepted a guilty plea agreement and convicted the recipient of influence peddling, sentencing him to 1 year and 10 months with the sentence suspended under supervision. This is a fourth separate prosecution reaching the same hospital that the map holds.
inside: The payment was to turn a pandemic hire at the hospital laboratory into a permanent post.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13330

n: An environment inspector let a chemicals firm trade without a permit
org_label: SC I.L. SRL, a chemicals maker and wholesaler
who: A company making and wholesaling chemical products
rank: Commissar of the National Environmental Guard, Cluj County Commissariat
d: On 7 October 2020 and 10 November 2021 a commissar of the National Environmental Guard's Cluj County Commissariat carried out inspections at a chemicals company and found it held no valid environmental permit. The court found he took no measures against the company and allowed it to carry on, harming the Guard's legitimate interest in seeing the law observed and producing an undue benefit for the firm, which was able to continue selling chemical products without a permit, some of them expired, from October 2020 into 2022. He denied the offences and was tried in the ordinary procedure. The judgment on appeal was published by the anticorruption prosecutors.
inside: The inspector who found the firm had no permit wrote nothing down, and it kept selling chemicals for two more years.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13374

n: Invigilators handed a Romanian school-leaver the exam answers
org_label: A candidate buying a pass in the national baccalaureate
who: A candidate sitting the written Romanian language and literature paper
rank: Members of the invigilation commission at a national college examination centre, Mures county
d: On 26 June 2023, sitting the written Romanian language and literature paper of the national baccalaureate at an examination centre in a national college in Mures county, a candidate used information not intended for publication by copying onto his examination sheet the contents of a draft carrying the answers to the paper. The court found that the draft had been handed to him by members of the invigilation commission. He was convicted under article 12 of Law 78 of 2000, which covers using information not meant to be public, or giving unauthorised people access to it, to obtain money, goods or other undue benefits.
inside: The staff supervising the examination passed the candidate the worked answers during the paper.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13380

n: Two suppliers each paid 5 percent of a railway hospital's invoices
org_label: Two companies in commercial relations with the CF No 2 hospital
who: The representatives of two supplier companies, each paying a percentage of its own invoices
rank: Manager and spending officer of the CF No 2 Clinical Hospital, Bucharest
d: On 7 April and 3 May 2023 the representative of one supplier handed the manager and spending officer of the CF No 2 Clinical Hospital in Bucharest about 9,100 lei, which the court recorded as 5 percent of the pre-VAT value of invoices the hospital had paid that spring. On 21 March 2023 the representative of a second supplier handed the same manager about 4,300 lei, again 5 percent of the pre-VAT value of three invoices the hospital had paid. In both cases the money went to the manager in connection with his official duties, specifically the smooth running of the contracts and the payment of the invoices. Both payers were convicted on guilty plea agreements.
inside: Each supplier returned a twentieth of every invoice to the hospital manager who authorised its payment.
cite: Judgments published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case documents 13402 and 13410

n: A man sold five families medical jobs across a Romanian county
org_label: Five people buying medical jobs for themselves or relatives
who: Five people who paid for jobs in the medical field for themselves or family members
rank: Doctors and officials with managerial duties at hospital units across Dolj county
d: Between October 2021 and February 2022 a man demanded a total of 22,500 euros from five different people and received from them 12,500 euros and 30,000 lei. The individual amounts ranged from 1,500 euros, paid so one payer's wife would be hired, to 6,000 euros. He was to intervene with doctors and officials holding managerial duties at hospital units in Dolj county, relying on an influence he claimed to hold over them, so that those who paid or their family members would be employed in the medical field. The court convicted him and precautionary seizure was ordered over his present and future property up to the sums received.
inside: Five families paid to be placed inside the county's hospitals, through a man claiming pull with their managers.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13440

n: 70,000 euros for an aviation authority permit to build
org_label: P.E. SRL, a company wanting to build
who: A man paying for a company's building approval
rank: Director general of the Romanian Civil Aeronautical Authority
d: Between June 2023 and July 2024 a defendant demanded 33,500 euros for another person, and then demanded and received 70,000 euros for himself and another, from the same payer. The court found he let the payer believe he held influence with the director general of the Romanian Civil Aeronautical Authority, and promised he would get that official to issue an approval needed to build a property for a company. The authority's approval is required where a construction would affect airspace or airport operations. He was convicted of influence peddling in continuous form.
inside: The approval the building needed sat with the aviation authority's director general, and access to him was sold.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13387

n: 350,000 euros for a land registration at a Romanian cadastre office
org_label: A claimant seeking registration of title
who: A man who wanted a property entered in the land register
rank: Officials of the Ilfov county office of cadastre and land registration
d: In January 2020 a defendant demanded 350,000 euros from a witness. The court found he not only promised to use influence with officials of the Ilfov county office of cadastre and land registration but pressed the witness to believe he had already intervened with them, guaranteeing several times that the registration had in fact been settled and that only the document proving it remained to be collected. The prosecutor said the evidence, which included witness statements, ambient interceptions and documents, showed the offence was committed in the form of demanding rather than receiving.
inside: Entering a property in the land register was offered for sale, with the buyer told it had already been arranged.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13395

n: An environment commissar asked 10,000 lei to drop what his check found
who: A representative of the company whose activity was being checked
rank: Environment commissar with powers to find and sanction administrative offences, and a colleague
d: On 6 February 2025, at about nine in the morning, an environment commissar carrying out his duties of inspecting a company's environmental activity demanded 10,000 lei at the company's premises, for himself and for a colleague, in connection with the two of them not carrying out their duty to sanction the irregularities the check had found. The following morning, near his workplace, he received 5,000 lei from the colleague. The court convicted him. The commissar held the power both to record administrative offences and to penalise them.
inside: The money reached the commissar who held the power to penalise, for not penalising what his own check had found.
cite: Judgment published by the Directia Nationala Anticorruptie, case document 13602
